Extend Your kindness to those who know You, and Your righteousness to the upright of heart.
How goodly are thy tents, O Jacob, Thy dwellings, O Israel!
But as for me, in the abundance of Thy lovingkindness will I come into Thy house; I will bow down toward Thy holy temple in the fear of Thee.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed near-exact Hebrew Tanakh alignment (psalms 5:8, similarity 0.988); orthographic/qere differences only.

paragraphs.text: LORD, I love the dwelling of Your house, the place where Your glory resides.
As for me, I will bow and kneel; I will bless the LORD, my Maker.
But as for me, let my prayer be unto Thee, O LORD, in an acceptable time; O God, in the abundance of Thy mercy, Answer me with the truth of Thy salvation.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed near-exact Hebrew Tanakh alignment (psalms 69:14, similarity 0.955); orthographic/qere differences only.

paragraphs: Master of the Universe Who reigned before any creature was created.
At the time when all was made by His will, then was His Name proclaimed King.
And after all things shall cease to be the Awesome One will reign alone.
He was, He is, and He shall be in glory.
He is One, and there is no second to compare to Him, to associate [with Him].
Without beginning, without end, power and dominion are His.

paragraphs.text: He is my God and my ever-living Redeemer, the Rock of my destiny on the day of distress.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur (deterministic preferred wording).

paragraphs: He is my flag and my refuge; He is the portion of my cup on the day I call.
Into His hand I entrust my spirit [both] when I sleep and when I awaken.
And with my spirit my body [too], Adonoy is with me, I shall not fear.
Blessed are You, Adonoy our God, King of the Universe, Who gives the rooster understanding to distinguish between day and night.
Blessed are You, Adonoy our God, King of the Universe, Who did not make me a gentile.
Blessed are You, Adonoy our God, King of the Universe, Who did not make me a slave.
Blessed are You, Adonoy our God, King of the Universe, Who did not make me a woman.

paragraphs.text: Women recite: Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who made me according to His will.

paragraphs: Blessed are You, Adonoy our God, King of the Universe, Who gives sight to the blind.
Blessed are You, Adonoy our God, King of the Universe, Who clothes the naked.
Blessed are You, Adonoy our God, King of the Universe, Who releases the imprisoned.
Blessed are You, Adonoy our God, King of the Universe, Who straightens the bent.
Blessed are You, Adonoy our God, King of the Universe, Who spreads the earth above the waters.
Blessed are You, Adonoy our God, King of the Universe, Who prepares the steps of man.
Blessed are You, Adonoy our God, King of the Universe, Who provided me with all my needs.
Blessed are You, Adonoy our God, King of the Universe, Who girds Israel with might.
Blessed are You, Adonoy our God, King of the Universe, Who crowns Israel with glory.
Blessed are You, Adonoy our God, King of the Universe, Who gives strength to the weary.

paragraphs.text: Do not respond Amen after “and slumber from my eyelids,” because the entire passage is one blessing, ending with “His people Israel” and the final words of the blessing.

paragraphs: Blessed are You, Adonoy our God, King of the Universe, Who removes sleep from my eyes and slumber from my eyelids.

paragraphs.text: May it be Your will, Lord our God and God of our ancestors, that You accustom us to Your Torah and bind us to Your commandments. Do not bring us into sin, transgression, guilt, temptation, or disgrace. Do not let the evil inclination rule over us. Keep us far from an evil person and an evil companion. Bind us instead to the good inclination and good deeds; bend our inclination to serve You. Grant us, today and every day, favor, kindness, and mercy in Your eyes and in the eyes of all who see us, and bestow good acts of loving-kindness upon us.
paragraphs.note: Original English working translation aligned to the full Hebrew paragraph; specialist review pending.

paragraphs.text: Blessed are You, LORD, who bestows good kindnesses upon His people Israel.

May it be Your will, Lord my God and God of my ancestors, to deliver me today and every day from insolent people and insolence; from an evil person, an evil inclination, an evil companion, an evil neighbor, and harmful encounters; from the evil eye, evil speech, informing, false testimony, hatred from others, false accusations, unnatural death, serious illnesses, misfortunes, and the destroying adversary; from harsh judgment and a harsh litigant, whether a member of the covenant or not, and from the judgment of Gehinnom.
paragraphs.note: Original English working translation aligned to the full Hebrew paragraph; specialist review pending.

paragraphs.text: And it came to pass after these things, that God did prove Abraham, and said unto him: ‘Abraham’; and he said: ‘Here am I.’

And He said: ‘Take now thy son, thine only son, whom thou lovest, even Isaac, and get thee into the land of Moriah; and offer him there for a burnt-offering upon one of the mountains which I will tell thee of.’

And Abraham rose early in the morning, and saddled his ass, and took two of his young men with him, and Isaac his son; and he cleaved the wood for the burnt-offering, and rose up, and went unto the place of which God had told him.
On the third day Abraham lifted up his eyes, and saw the place afar off.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed near-exact Hebrew Tanakh alignment (genesis 22:4, similarity 0.988); orthographic/qere differences only.

paragraphs.text: And Abraham said unto his young men: ‘Abide ye here with the ass, and I and the lad will go yonder; and we will worship, and come back to you.’
And Abraham took the wood of the burnt-offering, and laid it upon Isaac his son; and he took in his hand the fire and the knife; and they went both of them together.
And Isaac spoke unto Abraham his father, and said: ‘My father.’ And he said: ‘Here am I, my son.’ And he said: ‘Behold the fire and the wood; but where is the lamb for a burnt-offering?’
And Abraham said: ‘God will aprovide Himself the lamb for a burnt-offering, my son.’ So they went both of them together.
And they came to the place which God had told him of; and Abraham built the altar there, and laid the wood in order, and bound Isaac his son, and laid him on the altar, upon the wood.
And Abraham stretched forth his hand, and took the knife to slay his son.
And the angel of the LORD called unto him out of heaven, and said: ‘Abraham, Abraham.’ And he said: ‘Here am I.’
paragraphs.note: Reviewed near-exact Hebrew Tanakh alignment (genesis 22:11, similarity 0.968); orthographic/qere differences only.

paragraphs.text: And he said: ‘Lay not thy hand upon the lad, neither do thou any thing unto him; for now I know that thou art a God-fearing man, seeing thou hast not withheld thy son, thine only son, from Me.’

And Abraham lifted up his eyes, and looked, and behold behind him a ram caught in the thicket by his horns. And Abraham went and took the ram, and offered him up for a burnt-offering in the stead of his son.
Abraham named that place 'The LORD Will See'; as it is said to this day, 'On the mountain of the LORD it will be seen.'
The angel of the LORD called to Abraham a second time from heaven.
and said: ‘By Myself have I sworn, saith the LORD, because thou hast done this thing, and hast not withheld thy son, thine only son,
paragraphs.note: Reviewed near-exact Hebrew Tanakh alignment (genesis 22:16, similarity 0.974); orthographic/qere differences only.

paragraphs.text: that in blessing I will bless thee, and in multiplying I will multiply thy seed as the stars of the heaven, and as the sand which is upon the seashore; and thy seed shall possess the gate of his enemies;
and in thy seed shall all the nations of the earth be blessed; because thou hast hearkened to My voice.’
So Abraham returned unto his young men, and they rose up and went together to Beer- sheba; and Abraham dwelt at Beer-sheba.

paragraphs: A person should always be in fear of God, privately as well as openly, [he should] admit the truth, and speak truth in his heart, and rise early and proclaim:

paragraphs.text: Master of all worlds and Lord of lords, we do not cast our supplications before You on account of our righteousness but because of Your abundant mercy. What are we? What is our life, our kindness, our righteousness, our salvation, our strength or our might? What can we say before You, Lord our God and God of our ancestors? All the mighty are nothing before You, the renowned are as though they never lived, the wise are without knowledge, and the understanding are without discernment. Most of their deeds are emptiness and the days of their lives are vanity before You. Humanity has no advantage over the beast, for all is vanity.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Apart from the pure soul, which will one day have to render judgment and an account before the throne of Your glory.
All the nations are as nothing before You, as it is said: “Behold, the nations are as a drop from a bucket and as the fine dust on the scales; behold, the islands are lifted as a speck.”

However, we are Your people, children of Your covenant, children of Avraham, Your beloved, to whom You swore on Mount Moriah; the seed of Yitzchak, his only son, who was bound on top of the altar; the community of Yaakov, Your firstborn, [whom]—because of Your love for him and Your joyous delight in him— You named him Yisrael and Yeshurun.
Therefore we are obliged to give You thanks, praise You, glorify You, bless and sanctify You, and offer praise and thanksgiving to Your name.
How fortunate we are, how good is our portion, how pleasant our lot, and how beautiful our heritage!
How fortunate we are when we rise early and come in the evening to synagogues and houses of study, proclaiming Your name as One each and every day, and saying twice with love:
Hear, O Israel: the LORD is our God, the LORD is One.
(Silently) Blessed be His Name & glorious sovereignty forever.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur (deterministic preferred wording).

paragraphs.text: And thou shalt love the LORD thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed near-exact Hebrew Tanakh alignment (deuteronomy 6:5, similarity 0.960); orthographic/qere differences only.

paragraphs.text: And these words, which I command thee this day, shall be upon thy heart;
and thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thy house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up.
And thou shalt bind them for a sign upon thy hand, and they shall be for frontlets between thine eyes.
And thou shalt write them upon the door-posts of thy house, and upon thy gates;
paragraphs.note: Reviewed near-exact Hebrew Tanakh alignment (deuteronomy 11:20, similarity 0.980); orthographic/qere differences only.

paragraphs.text: You are the One who was before the world was created; You are the One since the world was created. You are in this world and You will be in the world to come.
Sanctify Your name among those who sanctify it, and sanctify Your name in Your world. Through Your salvation, raise and exalt our dignity; save us soon for the sake of Your name.
Blessed is He who sanctifies His name in public.
You are the LORD our God in heaven and on earth and in the highest heavens. Truly, You are the First and You are the Last, and besides You there is no God.
Gather those who hope in You from the four corners of the earth; may all who enter the world recognize and know that You alone are God, supreme over all the kingdoms of the earth.
You made the heavens and the earth, the sea and all that is in them. Who, among all Your works above or below, can say to You: “What are You doing? What will You accomplish?”

Our Father in heaven, living and enduring, deal with us in righteousness and loving-kindness for the sake of Your great, mighty and awesome name, by which we are called. Fulfill for us, Lord our God, the promise You gave through Your seer Zephaniah, as it is said: 'At that time I will bring you in, at the time when I gather you; for I will make you renowned and praised among all the peoples of the earth when I restore your fortunes before your eyes,' says the Lord (Zephaniah 3:20).
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
’Thou shalt also make a laver of brass, and the base thereof of brass, whereat to wash; and thou shalt put it between the tent of meeting and the altar, and thou shalt put water therein.
And Aaron and his sons shall wash their hands and their feet thereat;
when they go into the tent of meeting, they shall wash with water, that they die not; or when they come near to the altar to minister, to cause an offering made by fire to smoke unto the LORD;
paragraphs.note: Reviewed near-exact Hebrew Tanakh alignment (exodus 30:20, similarity 0.974); orthographic/qere differences only.

paragraphs.text: so they shall wash their hands and their feet, that they die not; and it shall be a statute for ever to them, even to him and to his seed throughout their generations.’
And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying:

Command Aaron and his sons, saying: This is the law of the burnt-offering: it is that which goeth up on its firewood upon the altar all night unto the morning; and the fire of the altar shall be kept burning thereby.

And the priest shall put on his linen garment, and his linen breeches shall he put upon his flesh; and he shall take up the ashes whereto the fire hath consumed the burnt-offering on the altar, and he shall put them beside the altar.
And he shall put off his garments, and put on other garments, and carry forth the ashes without the camp unto a clean place.

And the fire upon the altar shall be kept burning thereby, it shall not go out; and the priest shall kindle wood on it every morning; and he shall lay the burnt-offering in order upon it, and shall make smoke thereon the fat of the peace-offerings.
Fire shall be kept burning upon the altar continually; it shall not go out.
And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying:
Command the children of Israel, and say unto them: My food which is presented unto Me for offerings made by fire, of a sweet savour unto Me, shall ye observe to offer unto Me in its due season.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed near-exact Hebrew Tanakh alignment (numbers 28:2, similarity 0.950); orthographic/qere differences only.

paragraphs.text: At its appointed time. Say to them: This is the fire-offering you shall bring to the LORD: two unblemished year-old lambs each day as a continual burnt offering. Offer the first lamb in the morning and the second lamb toward evening.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: and the tenth part of an ephah of fine flour for a meal-offering, mingled with the fourth part of a hin of beaten oil.
It is a continual burnt-offering, which was offered in mount Sinai, for a sweet savour, an offering made by fire unto the LORD.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed near-exact Hebrew Tanakh alignment (numbers 28:6, similarity 0.955); orthographic/qere differences only.

paragraphs.text: And the drink-offering thereof shall be the fourth part of a hin for the one lamb; in the holy place shalt thou pour out a drink-offering of strong drink unto the LORD.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed near-exact Hebrew Tanakh alignment (numbers 28:7, similarity 0.961); orthographic/qere differences only.

paragraphs.text: And the other lamb shalt thou present at dusk; as the meal-offering of the morning, and as the drink-offering thereof, thou shalt present it, an offering made by fire, of a sweet savour unto the LORD.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed near-exact Hebrew Tanakh alignment (numbers 28:8, similarity 0.973); orthographic/qere differences only.

paragraphs:
(Leviticus 1:11)
And he will slaughter it on the north side of the Altar, before Adonoy; and Aaron’s sons, the Kohanim, will sprinkle its blood all around the Altar.

May it be Your will, Adonoy, our God and God of our fathers, that this recitation be important, acceptable and desirable before You, as if we sacrificed the daily burnt-offering at its proper time, in its proper place and according to its laws.

paragraphs.text: You are the LORD our God, before whom our ancestors burned fragrant incense while the Temple stood, as You commanded them through Moses Your prophet, as written in Your Torah:
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: And the LORD said unto Moses: ‘Take unto thee sweet spices, stacte, and onycha, and galbanum; sweet spices with pure frankincense; of each shall there be a like weight.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed near-exact Hebrew Tanakh alignment (exodus 30:34, similarity 0.973); orthographic/qere differences only.

paragraphs.text: And thou shalt make of it incense, a perfume after the art of the perfumer, seasoned with salt, pure and holy.
And thou shalt beat some of it very small, and put of it before the testimony in the tent of meeting, where I will meet with thee; it shall be unto you most holy. .
And it is said: 'Aaron shall burn fragrant incense upon it; every morning, when he tends the lamps, he shall burn it.'
And when Aaron lighteth the lamps at dusk, he shall burn it, a perpetual incense before the LORD throughout your generations.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed near-exact Hebrew Tanakh alignment (exodus 30:8, similarity 0.963); orthographic/qere differences only.

paragraphs.text: Our rabbis taught: How was the incense compounded? It contained 368 maneh of spices: 365 corresponding to the days of the solar year, one maneh for each day, half offered in the morning and half in the afternoon. Three additional maneh were used by the High Priest for the handful he brought into the Holy of Holies on Yom Kippur. On the eve of Yom Kippur he returned them to the mortar and ground them thoroughly, so that the incense would be exceptionally fine.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: The incense contained eleven ingredients, and these are they:

Stacte, onycha, galbanum, and frankincense: each weighed seventy maneh. Myrrh, cassia, spikenard, and saffron: each weighed sixteen maneh. Costus weighed twelve; aromatic bark, three; and cinnamon, nine.

Carshina lye: nine kav. Cyprus wine: three se'ah and three kav. If Cyprus wine was unavailable, aged white wine was used. Sodom salt: one quarter of a kav. A smoke-producing herb: the smallest amount. Rabbi Nathan the Babylonian says: Also a small amount of Jordan amber. If one added honey to the incense, it became invalid; if one omitted any one of its spices, one was liable to death.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Rabbi Shimon ben Gamliel says: “The balm is nothing but sap which drips from the balsam tree. Why was the Carshina lye used? To refine the onycha in order to make it pleasant. Why was Cyprus wine used? The onycha was soaked in it to give it a pungent odor. Though the water of Raglayim was well suited for that purpose, they did not bring the water of Raglayim into the Temple because it would be disrespectful.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur (deterministic preferred wording).

paragraphs.text: It was taught: Rabbi Nathan says, when the spices were ground, one would say, “Grind well; well, grind,” because the sound was beneficial to the spices. If one prepared half the amount it was valid; regarding one-third or one-quarter, we have not heard.
Rabbi Judah said: This is the rule: if the prescribed proportion is maintained, preparing half is valid; but one who omits even one of the ingredients is liable to death.
It was taught: Bar Kappara says, once every sixty or seventy years the leftover incense was sufficient to make half a batch.

Bar Kappara also taught: If one were to put a little honey into it, no one could endure its fragrance. Why was honey not mixed into it? Because the Torah says: “You shall not cause any leaven or any honey to go up in smoke as an offering by fire to the LORD.”
Three times: “The LORD of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge. Selah.”
Three times: “LORD of hosts, happy is the person who trusts in You.”
Three times: “LORD, save! May the King answer us on the day we call.”
Thou art my hiding-place; Thou wilt preserve me from the adversary; With songs of deliverance Thou wilt compass me about. Selah
Then the offering of Judah and Jerusalem shall be pleasing to the LORD, as in days of old and former years.

paragraphs: Abbaye listed the order of the [daily] Altar service based on tradition, and according to the opinion of Abba Shaul: the [arranging on the Altar of the] great Pyre precedes the second pyre [from which live coals are taken] for the incense-offering; the second pyre of the incense-offering [is arranged] before the placement of two logs [on the large pyre] the placement of the two logs precedes the removal of the ashes from the inner Altar; the removal of the ashes from the inner Altar precedes the cleaning of five lamps [of the Menorah]; the cleaning of the five lamps precedes [sprinkling] the blood of the daily-offering; the blood of the daily-offering precedes the cleaning of the [remaining] two lamps; the cleaning of the two lamps precedes the incense-offering; the incense-offering precedes [burning] the limbs [of the daily-offering]; burning the limbs [precedes] the meal-offering; the meal-offering [precedes] the baking-pan-offering; the baking-pan-offerings [precede] the wine libations; the wine-libations [precede] the Mussaf-offering; the Mussaf-offering [precedes] the two bowls of frankincense; and the two bowls of frankincense precede the daily afternoon-offering, for it is said, (Leviticus 6:5) And [the Kohein] shall arrange on it the burnt-offering, and burn on it the fat of the peace-offerings. Therewith complete all the offerings [of the day.]
Please, by the force of Your great right hand, release the bound one.
Accept the prayer of Your people; strengthen us, purify us, awesome One!
Please mighty One— those who seek Your unity— preserve them like the apple [of Your eye.]

paragraphs.text: Bless them & purify them. The mercy of Your righteousness always bestow upon them.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: Mighty Holy One, in Your abundant goodness, lead Your congregation.

paragraphs: Unique One, Exalted, turn to Your people who are mindful of Your holiness.
Accept our prayer and hear our cry, [You] Who knows hidden thoughts.

paragraphs.text: Blessed [is His] Name, Whose glorious kingdom is forever and ever.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur (deterministic preferred wording).

paragraphs.text: Master of the universe, You commanded us to offer the continual offering at its appointed time, with the priests at their service, the Levites on their platform, and Israel standing in attendance. Now, because of our sins, the Temple has been destroyed and the continual offering has ceased. We have no priest at his service, no Levite on his platform, and no Israelite at his appointed station. Yet You said: 'So will we render for bullocks the offering of our lips.' Therefore may it be Your will, Lord our God and God of our ancestors, that the utterance of our lips be counted, accepted, and pleasing before You as though we had offered the continual offering at its appointed time, in its proper place, and according to its law.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: For Shabbat: 'On the Sabbath day, two unblemished yearling lambs, and two-tenths of an ephah of fine flour mixed with oil as a grain offering, together with its libation.'
This is the burnt-offering of every sabbath, beside the continual burnt-offering, and the drink-offering thereof.
For Rosh Chodesh: 'At the beginnings of your months you shall offer a burnt offering to the LORD: two young bulls, one ram, and seven unblemished yearling lambs.'
and three tenth parts of an ephah of fine flour for a meal-offering, mingled with oil, for each bullock; and two tenth parts of fine flour for a meal-offering, mingled with oil, for the one ram;
and a several tenth part of fine flour mingled with oil for a meal-offering unto every lamb; for a burnt-offering of a sweet savour, an offering made by fire unto the LORD.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed near-exact Hebrew Tanakh alignment (numbers 28:13, similarity 0.970); orthographic/qere differences only.

paragraphs.text: And their drink-offerings shall be half a hin of wine for a bullock, and the third part of a hin for the ram, and the fourth part of a hin for a lamb. This is the burnt-offering of every new moon throughout the months of the year.
And one he-goat for a sin-offering unto the LORD; it shall be offered beside the continual burnt-offering, and the drink-offering thereof.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed near-exact Hebrew Tanakh alignment (numbers 28:15, similarity 0.962); orthographic/qere differences only.

paragraphs.text: Rabbi Ishmael says: The Torah is expounded through thirteen interpretive principles.
1. By an argument from a minor to a major case (kal va-chomer).
2. By comparing identical expressions in Scripture (gezerah shavah).
3. By a principle derived from one Scripture passage, and by a principle derived from two Scripture passages.
4. From a general rule followed by a particular.
5. From a particular followed by a general rule.
6. From a general statement followed by a particular and then a general statement, one may infer only what resembles the particular.
7. From a general statement that requires a particular statement, and from a particular statement that requires a general statement.
8. Anything included in a general rule and then singled out to teach something was singled out not merely to teach about itself, but to teach about the entire class.
9. Anything included in a general rule and singled out in connection with a matter of the same kind is singled out to be treated more leniently, not more strictly.
10. Anything included in a general rule and singled out in connection with a matter of a different kind is singled out to be treated both more leniently and more strictly.
11. Anything included in a general rule and singled out as a new case cannot be brought back under the general rule unless Scripture explicitly returns it to that rule.
12. An interpretation derived from its context, or from a later passage.
13. Likewise, when two Scripture passages contradict each other, a third passage comes and reconciles them.

paragraphs: May it be Your will Adonoy, our God and God of our fathers, that the Holy Temple be rebuilt speedily in our days: and grant us our share in Your Torah. And there we will serve You reverently as in the days of old, and in earlier years.
Exalted and sanctified be His great Name

paragraphs.text: In the world that He created according to His will; may He establish His kingdom, cause His deliverance to flourish, and bring His Messiah near. Amen.
In your lifetime and in your days, and in the lifetime of all the house of Israel, speedily and soon; and say: Amen.

paragraphs: May His great Name be blessed forever and for all eternity.

paragraphs.text: Blessed, praised, glorified, exalted, uplifted, honored, elevated, and acclaimed be the name of the Holy One, blessed be He—above all [during the Ten Days of Repentance: far above all] blessings, songs, praises, and consolations spoken in the world. And say: Amen.
paragraphs.note: Original English working translation aligned to the full Hebrew paragraph; specialist review pending.

paragraphs.text: Upon Israel and upon the rabbis, their disciples and all their disciples' disciples, and all who engage in Torah study in this holy place or any other place, may there be abundant peace, favor, kindness, compassion, long life, ample sustenance and redemption from their Father in heaven and earth; and say Amen.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed closely matching Hebrew wording in existing translated passage.

paragraphs.text: May abundant peace come from heaven, and life and goodness upon us and upon all Israel; and say: Amen.
He who makes peace in His heights—in the Ten Days of Repentance, “the peace”—may He in His mercy make peace for us and for all Israel; and say: Amen.

paragraphs: A Psalm, a song for the inauguration of the Temple, by David. I will exalt You, Adonoy, for You have upheld me, and not let my foes rejoice over me. Adonoy, my God, I cried out to You, and You healed me. Adonoy, You have raised my soul from the lower world. You have kept me alive, lest I descend to the Pit. Sing to Adonoy, [you,] His pious ones, and give thanks to His holy Name. For His anger lasts only a moment, but there is [long] life, in His conciliation. In the evening, one retires weeping, but in the morning there is [a cry of] joy! I said, in my serenity, I would never be moved. [But,] Adonoy, it was Your will [alone] that established my mountain as a stronghold. When You concealed Your Presence, I was terrified. To You, Adonoy, I called, and my Master I beseeched. What gain is there in [the shedding of] my blood? In my going down to destruction? Will the dust acknowledge You? Will it proclaim Your truth? Hear [me] Adonoy, and be gracious to me, Adonoy, be a help to me. You have turned my mourning into dancing, You have loosened my sackcloth and supported me with joy. In order that my soul might sing to You and not be stilled, Adonoy, my God, forever will I thank You.

Praise God. Praise Adonoy from the sky; Praise Him in the heights! Praise Him, all His angels; Praise Him, all His hosts! Praise Him, sun and moon; Praise Him, all the stars of light. Praise Him, skies of skies, and the waters that are above the skies. They will praise the Name of Adonoy, for He commanded it and they were created. He established them for all time, for as long as the world exists; He decreed it and it is unalterable. Praise Adonoy from the earth, sea-monsters and all [that dwell in] the depths. Fire and hail, snow and vapor, stormwind, [all] fulfilling His word. The mountains and all the hills, fruit trees and all cedars. Wild beasts and all animals, creeping things and winged fowl. Earthly kings and all peoples, ministers and all earthly judges. Young men and also maidens, elders together with lads. They will praise the Name of Adonoy, for His Name alone is exalted; His majesty is over the earth and the skies. He will raise the might of His people, [which is] praise for all His pious ones, for the Children of Israel, the people near to Him. Praise God.

Praise God. Sing a new song to Adonoy, His praise in the assembly of the pious. Israel will rejoice in its Maker; the children of Zion will exult in their King. They will praise His Name with dance; with drum and harp they will make music to Him. Because Adonoy desires His people; He will adorn the humble with deliverance. The pious will rejoice in honor; they will sing joyously upon their beds. High praises of the Almighty in their throats, and a double-edged sword in their hand. To perform vengeance upon the nations, chastisement upon the peoples. To bind their kings with chains, and their nobles with iron fetters. To execute upon them [the] written judgment; it is the splendor of all His pious ones. Praise God.

Praise God. Praise the Almighty in His Sanctuary Praise God in the firmament of His might Praise Him for His mighty deeds; Praise Him according to the abundance of His greatness. Praise Him with the blowing of the shofar; praise Him with lyre and harp. Praise Him with drum and dance. Praise Him with stringed instruments and flute. Praise Him with resounding cymbals. Praise Him with clanging cymbals. Let every soul praise God. Praise God. Let every soul praise God. Praise God.

And David blessed Adonoy in the presence of all the assembly; and David said, Blessed are You, Adonoy, God of Israel, our father, forever and ever. Yours, Adonoy, is the greatness, the might, the glory the victory and the beauty, for all that is in heaven and on earth [is Yours]; Yours, Adonoy, is the kingdom and You are uplifted, [supreme] over all rulers. The riches and the honor come from You, and You rule over all; in Your hand are power and might, and [it is] in Your hand to bestow greatness and strength upon all. And now, our God, we give thanks to You and praise Your glorious Name.

You alone are Adonoy; You have made the skies, the skies of skies and all their hosts, the earth and all that is upon it, the seas and all that is in them; and You give life to all of them, and the heavenly hosts bow before You. You are Adonoy, the God Who chose Avrom, and brought him out of Ur Kasdim and established his name (as) Avrohom. And You found his heart faithful before You,

paragraphs.text: You made a covenant with him to give the land of the Canaanite, the Hittite, the Amorite, the Perizzite, the Jebusite and the Girgashite to his descendants; and You fulfilled Your words, for You are righteous. You saw the affliction of our ancestors in Egypt and heard their cry at the Sea of Reeds. You performed signs and wonders against Pharaoh, all his servants and all the people of his land, because You knew they had acted arrogantly toward them. You made a name for Yourself, as You have to this day. You divided the sea before them, and they crossed through the sea on dry ground.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: You cast their pursuers into the depths like a stone in mighty waters.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs: On that day, Adonoy delivered Israel from the hand of Egypt, and Israel saw the Egyptians dead on the seashore. And Israel saw the great hand which Adonoy wielded against Egypt, and the people feared Adonoy, and they believed in Adonoy, and that Moses was His servant.

paragraphs.text: Then sang Moses and the children of Israel this song unto the LORD, and spoke, saying: I will sing unto the LORD, for He is highly exalted; The horse and his rider hath He thrown into the sea. The LORD is my strength and song, And He is become my salvation; This is my God, and I will glorify Him; My father’s God, and I will exalt Him. The LORD is a man of war, The LORD is His name. Pharaoh’s chariots and his host hath He cast into the sea, And his chosen captains are sunk in the Red Sea. The deeps cover them— They went down into the depths like a stone. Thy right hand, O LORD, glorious in power, Thy right hand, O LORD, dasheth in pieces the enemy. And in the greatness of Thine excellency Thou overthrowest them that rise up against Thee; Thou sendest forth Thy wrath, it consumeth them as stubble. And with the blast of Thy nostrils the waters were piled up— The floods stood upright as a heap; The deeps were congealed in the heart of the sea. The enemy said: ‘I will pursue, I will overtake, I will divide the spoil; My lust shall be satisfied upon them; I will draw my sword, my hand shall destroy them.’ Thou didst blow with Thy wind, the sea covered them; They sank as lead in the mighty waters. Who is like unto Thee, O LORD, among the mighty? Who is like unto Thee, glorious in holiness, Fearful in praises, doing wonders? Thou stretchedst out Thy right hand— The earth swallowed them. Thou in Thy love hast led the people that Thou hast redeemed; Thou hast guided them in Thy strength to Thy holy habitation. The peoples have heard, they tremble; Pangs have taken hold on the inhabitants of Philistia. Then were the chiefs of Edom affrighted; The mighty men of Moab, trembling taketh hold upon them; All the inhabitants of Canaan are melted away. Terror and dread falleth upon them; By the greatness of Thine arm they are as still as a stone; Till Thy people pass over, O LORD, Till the people pass over that Thou hast gotten. Thou bringest them in, and plantest them in the mountain of Thine inheritance, The place, O LORD, which Thou hast made for Thee to dwell in, The sanctuary, O Lord, which Thy hands have established. The LORD shall reign for ever and ever. The LORD shall reign for ever and ever. The Lord's kingship endures forever and for all eternity. For the horses of Pharaoh went in with his chariots and with his horsemen into the sea, and the LORD brought back the waters of the sea upon them; but the children of Israel walked on dry land in the midst of the sea. For the kingdom is the Lord's, and He rules over the nations. Saviors shall ascend Mount Zion to judge Mount Esau, and the kingdom shall belong to the Lord. The Lord shall be King over all the earth; on that day the Lord shall be One and His name One.
paragraphs.ref: JPS 1917 Exodus 15:1–19 and liturgical biblical conclusion
paragraphs.note: JPS source compared verse by verse to the Hebrew; repeated verse and the Aramaic affirmation of divine kingship retained.

paragraphs: Bless Adonoy Who is blessed.

paragraphs.text: Congregation and cantor: Blessed is the LORD, the Blessed One, forever and ever. Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who forms light and creates darkness, makes peace, and creates all things.
When a festival falls on a weekday, recite “He who illuminates the earth” instead of “All shall thank You.”

All shall give thanks to You, all shall praise You, and all shall declare: None is holy like the Lord. All shall exalt You forever, Creator of everything. God who each day opens the gates of the east, breaks through the windows of the sky, brings the sun forth from its place and the moon from its dwelling, and illuminates the entire world and all its inhabitants whom He created in mercy. He illuminates the earth and those who dwell on it with compassion, and in His goodness renews the work of creation each day, continually. O King, exalted alone from ancient times, praised, glorified and raised high since the days of eternity! Everlasting God, have compassion on us in Your abundant mercies. Lord of our strength, Rock of our stronghold, Shield of our salvation and our fortress! There is none comparable to You, none besides You, nothing apart from You: who is like You? There is none equal to You, Lord our God, in this world; none besides You, our King, for the life of the world to come; none apart from You, our Redeemer, in the days of the Messiah; and none like You, our Savior, at the resurrection of the dead.
paragraphs.note: New English working translation reviewed against the Hebrew and available Russian text; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: God, Master over all works, blessed and praised by every soul. His greatness and goodness are before the world; knowledge and understanding surround Him. Exalted above the holy living creatures, He is glorious above the heavenly chariot. Merit and uprightness stand before His throne; kindness and mercy fill His glory. Good are the luminaries our God created; He formed them with knowledge, understanding, and insight. He gave them strength and power to rule amid the world. Full of radiance, they shine with light; their splendor is beautiful throughout the world. They rejoice as they go forth and delight when they return; with awe they do the will of their Maker. They give beauty and honor to His name, joy and song to the remembrance of His kingdom. He called to the sun and light shone forth; He saw and established the form of the moon. All the hosts of heaven give Him praise; the seraphim, ofanim, and holy living creatures give Him glory and greatness.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: To God, who rested from all works: on the seventh day He was exalted and sat upon His glorious throne. He clothed the day of rest in beauty and called the Sabbath a delight. This is the praise of the seventh day, on which God rested from all His work. The seventh day itself praises and declares: 'A psalm, a song for the Sabbath day: it is good to give thanks to the Lord.' Therefore all His creatures glorify and bless God; they give praise, honor, and greatness to God, King and Creator of all, who in His holiness grants rest to His people Israel on the holy Sabbath. May Your name, Lord our God, be sanctified, and Your remembrance, our King, be glorified in heaven above and on earth below. Blessed are You, our Savior, for the beauty of the works of Your hands; the lights You have made will praise You forever.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: When a festival falls on a weekday, say 'Who illuminates the earth' instead of 'All shall thank You.' He illuminates the earth and its inhabitants in mercy and, in His goodness, continually renews the work of Creation every day. 'How manifold are Your works, Lord! You have made them all in wisdom; the earth is full of Your possessions.' The King alone exalted from ancient days, praised, glorified, and lifted high since the beginning of time. Eternal God, in Your abundant mercy have compassion on us. Master of our strength, Rock of our stronghold, Shield of our salvation, our refuge. Blessed God of great knowledge, He prepared and made the radiance of the sun; in goodness He formed glory for His name and set lights around His might. His hosts of holy ones exalt the Almighty and continually proclaim God's glory and holiness.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: May You be blessed, LORD our God, in heaven above and on earth below, for the praise of the works of Your hands. The lights You made shall glorify You forever.

paragraphs: Be blessed our Former, our King, and our Redeemer—Creator of holy beings. Praised be Your Name forever, our King, Who forms ministering angels; and Whose ministering angels all stand at the height of the Universe, and proclaim with reverence, in unison aloud the words of the living God, King of the Universe. All of them are beloved, all of them are pure, all of them are mighty and all of them perform with awe and reverence the will of their Possessor. And they all open their mouths in holiness and purity, with song and music, and they bless, and praise, and glorify, and revere, and sanctify, and proclaim the sovereignty of—

paragraphs.text: They sanctify the name of God, the great, mighty, and awesome King, the Holy One, blessed be He. All accept the yoke of the kingdom of heaven from one another and grant one another permission to sanctify their Maker calmly, in pure speech and sweet melody. All proclaim holiness together and answer in awe: 'Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of Hosts; the whole earth is full of His glory.' The ofanim and the holy living creatures rise with a great rushing sound to meet the seraphim and praise in response, saying: 'Blessed is the glory of the Lord from His place.'
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: To the Blessed Almighty, they offer pleasant melodies; to the King, the Almighty, [Who is] living and enduring, they utter hymns and make praises heard. For He alone is the Performer of mighty deeds, Maker of new things; Master of battles, Sower of acts of righteousness, Causer of deliverance to sprout forth; Creator of cures. Awesome in praise, Master of wonders, He renews in His goodness, each day, continuously, the work of creation, as it is said: “[Give thanks to Him] Who makes the great luminaries,” for His kindness is everlasting.” Shine a new light upon Zion, and may we all soon be privileged to [enjoy] its brightness. Blessed are You, Adonoy, Former of the luminaries.
paragraphs.ref: KAV EN parallel ashkenaz:First Blessing before Shema:7
paragraphs.note: Previously translated paragraph, Hebrew similarity 99.2%: source and target independently present in source corpus.

paragraphs: [With] unbounded love You have loved us Adonoy, our God; [With] great and abundant pity have You pitied us. Our Father, our King! for the sake of our forefathers who trusted in You, and whom You taught statutes of life, so too, be gracious to us and teach us. Our Father, merciful Father, Who acts with compassion have compassion on us and put into our hearts to comprehend, and to be intellectually creative, to listen, to learn, and to teach, to preserve, to practice, and to fulfill all the words of instruction in Your Torah with love. And enlighten our eyes in Your Torah, and cause our hearts to hold fast to Your commandments, and unify our hearts to love and fear Your Name; and may we never be put to shame, for in Your holy, great, and awesome Name— have we trusted; may we exult and rejoice in Your deliverance. And bring us to peace from the four corners of the earth and lead us upright to our land. Because, You are the Almighty, Who performs acts of deliverance, and You have chosen us from among all peoples and tongues, and You have brought us close to Your great Name, forever in truth; that we may give thanks to You, and proclaim Your Oneness, with love. Blessed are You, Adonoy, Who chooses His people Yisrael with love.
The following three words should be said when praying without a minyan: (Almighty, faithful King)

paragraphs.text: Hear, O Israel: the LORD is our God, the LORD is One.
(Silently) Blessed be His Name & glorious sovereignty forever.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur (deterministic preferred wording).

paragraphs.text: And thou shalt love the LORD thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy might. And these words, which I command thee this day, shall be upon thy heart; and thou shalt teach them diligently unto thy children, and shalt talk of them when thou sittest in thy house, and when thou walkest by the way, and when thou liest down, and when thou risest up. And thou shalt bind them for a sign upon thy hand, and they shall be for frontlets between thine eyes. And thou shalt write them upon the door-posts of thy house, and upon thy gates;
paragraphs.note: Every colon-delimited fragment matched a unique near-exact complete Tanakh verse; reviewed orthographic/qere alignment only.

paragraphs: And it will be— if you vigilantly obey My commandments which I command you this day, to love Adonoy your God, and serve Him with your entire hearts and with your entire souls— that I will give rain for your land in its proper time, the early (autumn) rain and the late (spring) rain; and you will harvest your grain and your wine and your oil. And I will put grass in your fields for your cattle, and you will eat and be satisfied. Beware lest your hearts be swayed and you turn astray, and you worship alien gods and bow to them. And Adonoy’s fury will blaze among you, and He will close off the heavens and there will be no rain and the earth will not yield its produce; and you will perish swiftly from the good land which Adonoy gives you. Place these words of Mine upon your hearts and upon your souls,— and bind them for a sign upon your hands, and they shall be for totafos between your eyes. And you shall teach them to your sons, to speak them when you sit in your house, and when you travel on the road, and when you lie down and when you rise. And you shall write them upon the doorposts of your house and upon your gateways. In order that your days be prolonged, and the days of your children, upon the land which Adonoy swore to your fathers to give them [for as long] as the heavens are above the earth.

And Adonoy spoke to Moses saying: Speak to the children of Israel, and tell them to make for themselves fringes on the corners of their garments throughout their generations; and they will place with the fringes of each corner a thread of blue. And it will be to you for fringes, and you will look upon it and you will remember all the commandments of Adonoy, and you will perform them; and you will not turn aside after your hearts and after your eyes which cause you to go astray. In order that you will remember and perform all My commandments; and you will be holy unto your God. I am Adonoy, your God, Who brought you out of the land of Egypt to be your God: I am Adonoy, your God—is true—

paragraphs.text: The prayer leader repeats: “The LORD your God is true.”

paragraphs: My Master, open my lips, and my mouth will declare Your praise.

Blessed are You, Adonoy, our God, and God of our fathers, God of Abraham, God of Isaac, and God of Jacob, the Almighty, the Great, the Powerful, the Awesome, most high Almighty, Who bestows beneficent kindness, Who possesses everything, Who remembers the piety of the Patriarchs, and Who brings a redeemer to their children’s children, for the sake of His Name, with love.
(During the Ten Days of Penitence add: Remember us for life King, Who desires life; and inscribe us in the Book of Life, for Your sake, Living God.)
King, Helper, and Deliverer and Shield. Blessed are You, Adonoy, Shield of Abraham.
You are mighty forever, my Master; You are the Resurrector of the dead the Powerful One to deliver us.

paragraphs.text: From the Musaf of Shemini Atzeres until the Musaf of the first day of Pesach you should say: Causer of the wind to blow and of the rain to fall.
paragraphs.note: Exact Hebrew match to a sequence of reviewed Siddur paragraphs; translations joined without fuzzy splitting.

paragraphs: Sustainer of the living with kindliness, Resurrector of the dead with great mercy, Supporter of the fallen, and Healer of the sick, and Releaser of the imprisoned, and Fulfiller of His faithfulness to those who sleep in the dust. Who is like You, Master of mighty deeds, and who can be compared to You? King Who causes death and restores life, and causes deliverance to sprout forth.

paragraphs.text: (During the Ten Days of Penitence add: Who is like You merciful Father, Who remembers His creatures for life, in His mercy)
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur (deterministic preferred wording).

paragraphs: And You are faithful to restore the dead to life. Blessed are You, Adonoy, Resurrector of the dead.

paragraphs.text: Moses shall rejoice in the gift of his portion, for You called him a faithful servant. You placed a crown of splendor on his head as he stood before You at Mount Sinai. He carried down in his hands two stone tablets inscribed with the observance of Shabbat, as it is written in Your Torah:

Wherefore the children of Israel shall keep the sabbath, to observe the sabbath throughout their generations, for a perpetual covenant. It is a sign between Me and the children of Israel for ever; for in six days the LORD made heaven and earth, and on the seventh day He ceased from work and rested.’
paragraphs.note: Every colon-delimited fragment matched a unique near-exact complete Tanakh verse; reviewed orthographic/qere alignment only.

paragraphs.text: You did not give it, Lord our God, to the nations of the lands, nor did You grant it as an inheritance, our King, to those who worship idols; the uncircumcised do not dwell in its rest. Rather, You gave it in love to Israel Your people, to the descendants of Jacob whom You chose. The people who sanctify the seventh day shall be satisfied and delight in Your goodness. You desired and sanctified the seventh day, calling it the most precious of days, a remembrance of the work of creation.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Our God, and God of our fathers, be pleased with our rest, sanctify us with Your commandments and give us our share in Your Torah; satisfy us from Your goodness and gladden us with Your deliverance, and purify our hearts to serve You in truth. And give us as our inheritance, Adonoy our God, in love and in pleasure Your holy Shabbos; and may Israel rest thereon— the sanctifiers of Your Name. Blessed are You Adonoy, Sanctifier of Shabbos.

paragraphs: Be pleased, Adonoy, our God, with Your people, Israel, and their prayer; and restore the service to the Holy of Holies in Your abode, and the fire-offerings of Israel; and accept their prayer, lovingly and willingly. And may You always find pleasure with the service of Your people, Israel.

paragraphs.text: [On Rosh Chodesh and Chol HaMoed say:] Our God and God of our ancestors, may there rise, come, reach, appear, be accepted, be heard, be recalled and be remembered before You our remembrance and regard, the remembrance of our ancestors, the remembrance of the Messiah son of David Your servant, the remembrance of Jerusalem Your holy city, and the remembrance of all Your people the house of Israel, for deliverance, goodness, grace, loving-kindness and mercy, life and peace, on this day of [Rosh Chodesh: the New Moon; Passover: the Festival of Unleavened Bread; Sukkot: the Festival of Booths]. Remember us on it for good, visit us on it with blessing, and save us on it for life. With a word of salvation and mercy, spare us, be gracious to us, have compassion on us and save us, for our eyes are toward You, for You are a gracious and compassionate God and King.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs: And may our eyes behold Your merciful return to Zion. Blessed are You, Adonoy, Who returns His Divine Presence to Zion.

We are thankful to You that You Adonoy are our God and the God of our fathers forever; Rock of our lives, You are the Shield of our deliverance in every generation. We will give thanks to You and recount Your praise, for our lives which are committed into Your hand, and for our souls which are entrusted to You, and for Your miracles of every day with us, and for Your wonders and benefactions at all times— evening, morning and noon. (You are) The Beneficent One— for Your compassion is never withheld; And (You are) the Merciful One— for Your kindliness never ceases; we have always placed our hope in You.

paragraphs.text: We are thankful to You, that You Adonoy are our God, and God of our fathers, God of all flesh, Our Creator, Creator of the Beginning. Blessings and thanksgivings to Your great and holy Name for keeping us alive, and sustaining us; so may You always keep us alive and sustain us, and gather our exiles to the Courtyards of Your Sanctuary to observe Your statutes, and to do Your will, and to serve You wholeheartedly, for we are thankful to You. Blessed is the Almighty to Whom all thanks are due.

paragraphs: On Chanukah and Purim:[We thank You] for the miracles, for the redemption, for the mighty deeds, for the deliverances and for the wars that You performed for our fathers in those days at this season.

paragraphs.text: On Chanukah: In the days of Matisyahu, son of Yochanan the High Priest, the Hasmonean and his sons, when the evil Greek kingdom rose up against Your people Israel to make them forget Your Torah and to turn them away from the statutes of Your will— You, in Your abundant mercy, stood by them in their time of distress, You defended their cause, You judged their grievances, You avenged them. You delivered the mighty into the hands of the weak, many into the hands of the few, defiled people into the hands of the undefiled, the wicked into the hands of the righteous, and insolent [sinners] into the hands of diligent students of Your Torah. And You made Yourself a great and sanctified name in Your world. And for Your people, Israel, You performed a great deliverance and redemption unto this very day. Afterwards, Your sons entered the Holy of Holies of Your Abode, cleaned Your Temple, purified Your Sanctuary, and kindled lights in the Courtyards of Your Sanctuary, and designated these eight days of Chanukah to thank and praise Your great Name.
paragraphs.note: Reused from a reviewed near-identical Hebrew Siddur variant (99.75% normalized Hebrew similarity).

paragraphs.text: On Purim: In the days of Mordechai and Esther in Shushan the Capital [of Persia], when the evil Haman rose up against them, he sought to destroy, to kill, and to annihilate all the Jews, young and old, infants and women, in one day, the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is the month of Adar, and to plunder their wealth— And You, in Your abundant mercy, annulled his counsel, frustrated his intention, and brought his evil plan upon his own head, and they hanged him and his sons upon the gallows. And You made a miracle and a wonder for them, and we are thankful to Your great name forever.
paragraphs.note: Previously translated paragraph, Hebrew similarity 99.4%: source and target independently present in source corpus.

paragraphs: And for all the foregoing may Your Name, our King, constantly be blessed and extolled, forever and ever.

paragraphs.text: During the Ten Days of Repentance: Inscribe all the children of Your covenant for a good life.

paragraphs: And all the living shall thank You forever and praise Your Name with sincerity — the Almighty, Who is our deliverance and our help forever. Blessed are You, Adonoy; Your Name is The Beneficent and You it is fitting to praise.

paragraphs.text: Priestly Blessing during the repetition of the Amidah: Our God and God of our ancestors, bless us with the threefold blessing written in the Torah through Moses Your servant, spoken by Aaron and his sons, the priests of Your holy people, as it is said:
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Adonoy bless you and guard you. Adonoy shine His countenance upon you and be gracious unto you. Adonoy turn His countenance toward you and grant you peace.
paragraphs.note: Exact Hebrew match to a sequence of reviewed Siddur paragraphs; translations joined without fuzzy splitting.

paragraphs.text: Grant peace, goodness, and blessing, favor, kindness and compassion upon us and upon all Israel, Your people. Bless us, our Father, all of us as one with the light of Your countenance. For by the light of Your countenance You gave us Adonoy our God, a Torah of life and the love of kindliness, righteousness, blessing, compassion, life and peace. And may it be good in Your sight to bless Your people, Israel, at all times and at every moment with Your peace.
paragraphs.note: Previously translated paragraph, Hebrew similarity 98.6%: source and target independently present in source corpus.

paragraphs: Blessed are You, Adonoy, Who blesses His people Israel with peace.

paragraphs.text: Blessed is the Name of the Master of the universe. Blessed is Your crown and Your place. May Your good will [be] with Your people Israel forever. Show Your people the redemption of Your right hand in Your Holy Temple. Bestow on us Your excellent light, and accept our prayer with compassion. May it be Your will to prolong our lives in well-being. Let me be counted among the righteous, so that You will have compassion on me and protect me and all that is mine, and all that belongs to Your people, Israel. You are He Who nourishes all and maintains all; You are He Who rules over all; You are He Who rules over kings, and the kingdom is Yours. I am a servant of the Holy One, blessed is He, I bow before Him and before the honor of His Torah at all times. Not in man do I put my trust, nor do I rely on any angel; but only in the God of heaven, Who is the true God, Whose Torah is truth, Whose prophets are true, and Who performs many deeds of goodness and truth. In Him I put my trust and to His honored, holy Name I utter praises. May it be Your will to open my heart to Torah, and to fulfill the desires of my heart, and of the heart of Your people Israel, for goodness, for life, and for peace.
paragraphs.note: Reused from a reviewed near-identical Hebrew Siddur variant (99.91% normalized Hebrew similarity).

paragraphs.text: When returning the Torah scroll to the ark, say:
Cantor: Let them praise the name of the LORD, for His name alone is exalted.

paragraphs: Chazzan and congregation: His majesty is over the earth and the skies. He will raise the might of His people, [which is] praise for all His pious ones, for the children of Israel, the people near to Him. Praise God.

paragraphs.text:
On Shabbat: It is customary to stand during the recitation of the following psalm.
A Psalm of David. Ascribe to Adonoy— you sons of the mighty — ascribe to Adonoy glory and might. Ascribe to Adonoy the glory due His Name, prostrate yourselves before Adonoy in the splendor of holiness. Adonoy's voice is upon the waters. Almighty of glory thunders, Adonoy is upon [the] many waters. The voice of Adonoy is in power, the voice of Adonoy is in beauty. The voice of Adonoy breaks cedars, Adonoy shatters the cedars of Lebanon. He makes them leap like a calf, Lebanon and Sirion like unicorns. The voice of Adonoy hews out flames of fire. The voice of Adonoy makes the desert tremble, Adonoy makes tremble the desert of Kadesh. The voice of Adonoy causes hinds to calve, and strips the forests bare; and in His Sanctuary all proclaim [His] glory. Adonoy sat enthroned (even) at the flood Adonoy is enthroned as King forever. Adonoy will give strength to His people; Adonoy will bless His people with peace.

[On a festival that falls on a weekday:] A Psalm of David. A Psalm of David. The earth is the LORD’S, and the fulness thereof; the world, and they that dwell therein. For He hath founded it upon the seas, and established it upon the floods. Who shall ascend into the mountain of the LORD? And who shall stand in His holy place? He that hath clean hands, and a pure heart; Who hath not taken My name in vain, and hath not sworn deceitfully. He shall receive a blessing from the LORD, and righteousness from the God of his salvation. Such is the generation of them that seek after Him, that seek Thy face, even Jacob. Selah Lift up your heads, O ye gates, and be ye lifted up, ye everlasting doors; that the King of glory may come in. 'Who is the King of glory?' 'The LORD strong and mighty, The LORD mighty in battle.' Lift up your heads, O ye gates, Yea, lift them up, ye everlasting doors; That the King of glory may come in. 'Who then is the King of glory?' 'The LORD of hosts; He is the King of glory.' Selah
paragraphs.note: Complete Psalm 24, collated to the source; Siddur occasion instruction retained.

paragraphs.text: When returning the Torah scroll to the ark, say: And when it rested, he would say: Return, Adonoy, to the myriads and thousands of Israel. Arise, Adonoy unto Your resting place, You and the Ark of Your strength. Let Your priests clothe themselves in righteousness, and let Your devoted ones sing in joy. For the sake of David, Your servant, do not reject Your anointed. For I have given you good instruction, do not forsake My Torah. It is a tree of life to those who grasp it, and those who support it are fortunate. Its ways are ways of pleasantness and all its paths are peace. Cause us to return to you, Adonoy, and we shall return; renew our days as of old.

paragraphs: When I proclaim Adonoy’s Name attribute greatness to our God.
My Master, open my lips, and my mouth will declare Your praise.

Blessed are You, Adonoy, our God, and God of our fathers, God of Abraham, God of Isaac, and God of Jacob, the Almighty, the Great, the Powerful, the Awesome, most high Almighty, Who bestows beneficent kindness, Who possesses everything, Who remembers the piety of the Patriarchs, and Who brings a redeemer to their children’s children, for the sake of His Name, with love.

paragraphs.text: During the Ten Days of Repentance: Remember us for life, O King who delights in life, and inscribe us in the Book of Life, for Your sake, living God.
King, Helper, Savior, and Shield.
Blessed are You, LORD, Shield of Abraham.

paragraphs: You are mighty forever, my Master; You are the Resurrector of the dead the Powerful One to deliver us.

paragraphs.text: From the Musaf of Shemini Atzeres until the Musaf of the first day of Pesach you should say: Causer of the wind to blow and of the rain to fall.
paragraphs.note: Exact Hebrew match to a sequence of reviewed Siddur paragraphs; translations joined without fuzzy splitting.

paragraphs.text: From the Musaf of the first day of Pesach until the Musaf of Shemini Atzeres one should say: He causes the dew to descend.
paragraphs.note: Exact Hebrew match to a sequence of reviewed Siddur paragraphs; translations joined without fuzzy splitting.

paragraphs: Sustainer of the living with kindliness, Resurrector of the dead with great mercy, Supporter of the fallen, and Healer of the sick, and Releaser of the imprisoned, and Fulfiller of His faithfulness to those who sleep in the dust. Who is like You, Master of mighty deeds, and who can be compared to You? King Who causes death and restores life, and causes deliverance to sprout forth.

paragraphs.text: During the Ten Days of Repentance: Who is like You, merciful Father, who remembers His creatures for life in mercy?
And You are faithful to revive the dead.
Blessed are You, LORD, who revives the dead.

paragraphs: You are holy and Your Name is holy and holy beings praise You every day, forever.

paragraphs.text: Blessed are You, LORD, the holy God; during the Ten Days of Repentance say: the holy King.

[When Shabbat coincides with Rosh Chodesh, say 'You fashioned' below.] You established Shabbat and desired its offerings, commanding its detailed rites and libations. Those who delight in it inherit honor forever; those who taste its goodness merit life, and those who love its teachings choose greatness. At Sinai we were commanded concerning it. You commanded us, Lord our God, to offer its proper additional Shabbat sacrifice. May it be Your will, Lord our God and God of our ancestors, to bring us joyfully to our land and plant us within our borders. There we shall offer before You our obligatory sacrifices, the daily offerings in their order and the additional offerings according to their laws. We shall offer the additional sacrifice of this Shabbat lovingly, as You willed and as You wrote in Your Torah through Moses Your servant, from Your glorious mouth, as it is said:
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: And on the sabbath day two he-lambs of the first year without blemish, and two tenth parts of an ephah of fine flour for a meal-offering, mingled with oil, and the drink-offering thereof. This is the burnt-offering of every sabbath, beside the continual burnt-offering, and the drink-offering thereof.

Those who keep Shabbat and call it a delight shall rejoice in Your kingdom. The people who sanctify the seventh day shall all be satisfied and delight in Your goodness. You favored and sanctified the seventh day, called it the most desirable of days, a remembrance of the work of Creation.

Our God and God of our ancestors, be pleased with our rest. Sanctify us through Your commandments, give us our portion in Your Torah, satisfy us with Your goodness, gladden us with Your salvation, and purify our hearts to serve You in truth. Grant us, LORD our God, in love and favor, Your holy Sabbath as our inheritance, that Israel, who sanctifies Your name, may rest upon it.
Blessed are You, LORD, who sanctifies Shabbat. Continue with “Accept [our worship].”

On Shabbat Rosh Chodesh: You formed Your world in ancient times and completed Your work on the seventh day. You loved us and chose us, exalted us above all tongues, sanctified us through Your commandments, and drew us near, our King, to Your service; You called Your great and holy name upon us.

In love You gave us, Lord our God, Sabbaths for rest and New Moons for atonement. Because we and our ancestors sinned before You, our city was destroyed, our Sanctuary desolated, our splendor exiled, and honor removed from the dwelling place of our life. We can no longer fulfill our obligations in Your chosen house, the great and holy house that bears Your name, because the hand of destruction was laid upon Your Sanctuary.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: May it be Your will, Lord our God and God of our ancestors, to bring us up joyfully to our land and plant us within our borders. There we shall offer before You the sacrifices we owe: the daily offerings in their order and the additional offerings according to their laws. We shall lovingly offer the additional offerings of this Sabbath and this New Moon, as You have commanded and as You wrote in Your Torah through Moses Your servant, from Your glorious mouth, as it is said:
paragraphs.note: Original English working translation aligned to the full Hebrew paragraph; specialist review pending.

paragraphs.text: And on the sabbath day two he-lambs of the first year without blemish, and two tenth parts of an ephah of fine flour for a meal-offering, mingled with oil, and the drink-offering thereof.
This is the burnt-offering of every sabbath, beside the continual burnt-offering, and the drink-offering thereof.

On your New Moons you shall bring a burnt offering to the LORD: two young bulls, one ram and seven unblemished year-old lambs, together with their meal offerings and libations as prescribed—three-tenths for each bull, two-tenths for the ram, one-tenth for each lamb, wine for its libation, a goat for atonement and the two daily offerings according to their law.

Those who keep Shabbat and call it a delight shall rejoice in Your kingdom. The people who sanctify the seventh day shall all be satisfied and delight in Your goodness. You favored and sanctified the seventh day, called it the most desirable of days, a remembrance of the work of Creation.

Our God and God of our ancestors, be pleased with our rest; on this Sabbath day renew this month for us for good and blessing, joy and gladness, deliverance and consolation, sustenance and provision, life and peace, pardon of sin and forgiveness of wrongdoing; in a leap year, until the month of Nisan, add: and atonement for transgression. Sanctify us through Your commandments and grant us a portion in Your Torah. Satisfy us with Your goodness, gladden us with Your salvation, and purify our hearts to serve You in truth. Grant us, Lord our God, Your holy Sabbath as a heritage in love and favor, and may Israel, who sanctify Your name, rest upon it. For You chose Your people Israel from all nations, made known to them Your holy Sabbath, and established for them the laws of the beginnings of the months. Blessed are You, Lord, who sanctifies the Sabbath, Israel, and the New Moons.

paragraphs: Be pleased, Adonoy, our God, with Your people, Israel, and their prayer; and restore the service to the Holy of Holies in Your abode, and the fire-offerings of Israel; and accept their prayer, lovingly and willingly. And may You always find pleasure with the service of Your people, Israel.

paragraphs.text: May our eyes behold Your merciful return to Zion.
Blessed are You, LORD, who restores His Presence to Zion.
We thank You, for You are the LORD our God and God of our ancestors forever and ever, the Rock of our lives, the Shield of our salvation in every generation.
for our lives entrusted to Your hand, for our souls placed in Your care, and for Your miracles with us every day, Your wonders and goodness at all times—morning, noon and evening.
You are good, for Your compassion never ends; You are merciful, for Your kindness never ceases. We have always placed our hope in You.
Modim of the Rabbis:

We are thankful to You, that You Adonoy are our God, and God of our fathers, God of all flesh, Our Creator, Creator of the Beginning. Blessings and thanksgivings to Your great and holy Name for keeping us alive, and sustaining us; so may You always keep us alive and sustain us, and gather our exiles to the Courtyards of Your Sanctuary to observe Your statutes, and to do Your will, and to serve You wholeheartedly, for we are thankful to You. Blessed is the Almighty to Whom all thanks are due.

paragraphs.text: On Hanukkah and on Purim in walled cities, recite this:

For the miracles, for the deliverance, for the mighty deeds, for the salvations, for the wonders, for the consolations, and for the wars that You performed for our ancestors in those days at this time.
For Hanukkah:

In the days of Mattathias son of Johanan, the Hasmonean High Priest, and his sons, when the wicked Greek kingdom rose against Your people Israel to make them forget Your Torah and turn them away from the statutes of Your will.

But You, in Your abundant mercy, stood by them in their time of distress. You fought their battle, judged their cause, avenged their wrong, delivered the mighty into the hands of the weak, the many into the hands of the few, the impure into the hands of the pure, the wicked into the hands of the righteous, and the arrogant into the hands of those devoted to Your Torah. You made for Yourself a great and holy name in Your world, and brought a great salvation and deliverance to Your people Israel on this day.

Afterward Your children entered the inner sanctuary of Your House, cleared Your Temple, purified Your holy place, lit lamps in Your sacred courtyards, and established these eight days of Hanukkah to give thanks and praise to Your great name.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: For Purim:

In the days of Mordechai and Esther in Shushan the capital, when wicked Haman rose against them, he sought to destroy, kill, and annihilate all the Jews, from young to old, children and women, in one day, the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, the month of Adar, and to plunder their possessions.
In Your great compassion You frustrated his counsel, thwarted his plan, returned his evil upon his own head, and hanged him and his sons on the gallows.

paragraphs: And for all the foregoing may Your Name, our King, constantly be blessed and extolled, forever and ever.

All the living will thank You forever, and sincerely praise Your Name, O God of our salvation and our help. Selah.
Blessed are You, LORD; Your Name is good, and it is fitting to give You thanks.

Act for the sake of Your name. Act for the sake of Your right hand. Act for the sake of Your holiness. Act for the sake of Your Torah. That Your beloved ones may be delivered, save with Your right hand and answer me.

The composition of the incense consisted of balm, onycha, galbanum, and frankincense— by weight, seventy maneh of each; myrrh, cassia, spikenard and saffron by weight— sixteen maneh of each; twelve maneh of costus, three maneh of aromatic bark, and nine maneh of cinnamon. [Also used in compounding the incense were:] Nine kabin of Carshina lye, Cyprus wine [measuring] three s'in and three kabin— if he had no Cyprus wine, he could use strong white wine— a fourth of a kab of Sodom salt, and a minute quantity of maaleh ashan. Rabbi Nosson of Babylonia says, Add a minute quantity of Jordan amber. If one added honey, the incense became unfit; and if one omitted any of its spices he was liable to the death penalty.

paragraphs.text: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: The balm is nothing other than resin that drips from the balsam trees. Carshina lye was used to rub the onycha so that it would be beautiful. Cyprus wine was used to soak the onycha so that its fragrance would be strong. But would not urine be good for that purpose? Yes, but urine was not brought into the Temple out of respect for its sanctity.

paragraphs.text: The song that the Levites used to recite in the Temple: On the first day they said: 'The earth is the Lord's and everything in it, the world and all who dwell therein.' On the second day: 'Great is the Lord and greatly to be praised in the city of our God, His holy mountain.' On the third day: 'God stands in the divine assembly; among the judges He renders judgment.' On the fourth day: 'O God of vengeance, Lord, God of vengeance, shine forth!' On the fifth day: 'Sing aloud to God our strength; shout for joy to the God of Jacob.' On the sixth day: 'The Lord reigns; He is clothed with majesty; the Lord is robed and girded with strength; the world is firmly established and cannot be moved.' On the Sabbath they said: 'A psalm, a song for the Sabbath day'—a psalm for the future age, the day that is entirely Sabbath and rest for eternal life.

paragraphs.text: Rabbi Elazar said in the name of Rabbi Hanina: Scholars of Torah increase peace in the world, as it is written, 'All your children shall be taught by the Lord, and great shall be the peace of your children.' Read not 'your children' (banayikh) but 'your builders' (bonayikh). 'Great peace belongs to those who love Your Torah, and nothing causes them to stumble.' 'May there be peace within your walls, tranquility within your palaces.' 'For the sake of my brothers and my friends, I shall say: Peace be within you.' 'For the sake of the house of the Lord our God, I shall seek your good.' 'The Lord will give strength to His people; the Lord will bless His people with peace.'
