paragraphs: It is our obligation to praise the Master of all, to ascribe greatness to the Creator of the [world in the] beginning: that He has not made us like the nations of the lands, and has not positioned us like the families of the earth; that He has not assigned our portion like theirs, nor our lot like that of all their multitudes. For they prostrate themselves to vanity and nothingness, and pray to a god that cannot deliver. But we bow, prostrate ourselves, and offer thanks before the Supreme King of Kings, the Holy One blessed is He, Who spreads the heavens, and establishes the earth, and the seat of His glory is in heaven above, and the abode of His invincible might is in the loftiest heights. He is our God, there is nothing else. Our King is true, all else is insignificant, as it is written in His Torah: And You shall know this day and take into Your heart that Adonoy is God in the heavens above and upon the earth below; there is nothing else.

paragraphs.text: Therefor, we will hope to You L·rd, our G·d to see speedily the glory of Your Might - to remove abominable idolatry from the earth & the false gods be utterly terminated, to repair the world with the Kingship of the Al·mighty. And all living flesh will call in Your Name to turn back to You all the wicked of the earth. They will recognize & will know, all the inhabitants of the earth, that to You that every knee shall bow down, & every tongue. Before you they will kneel & bow down & give honor to Your glorious name & they will all accept the yolk of Your Kingship. And Reign upon them speedily forever & ever. For the Kingship, it is Yours. And forevermore reign in glory. Like it is written in your Torah, “The L·rd will reign forever & ever.” And it is said “and it will be the L·rd will Be King upon all of the earth. On that day the L·rd will be One (ie, only He will be worshiped) & His name One.” And in Your Torah, L·rd, Our G·d, it is written saying “Hear Oh Israel, the L·rd is our G·d the L·rd is One.”

Be not afraid of sudden terror, Neither of the destruction of the wicked, when it cometh; Take counsel together, and it shall be brought to nought; Speak the word, and it shall not stand; For God is with us. Even to old age I am the same, and even to hoar hairs will I carry you; I have made, and I will bear; yea, I will carry, and will deliver.

paragraphs.text: The children of Israel shall keep the Sabbath, observing the Sabbath throughout their generations as an everlasting covenant. Between Me and the children of Israel it is an eternal sign; for in six days the LORD made heaven and earth, and on the seventh day He ceased and rested.

Remember the Sabbath day, to sanctify it. Six days you shall labor and do all your work, but the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God; you shall not do any work—you, your son, your daughter, your male servant, your female servant, your livestock, or the stranger within your gates. For in six days the LORD made heaven and earth, the sea and all within them, and rested on the seventh day; therefore the LORD blessed the Sabbath day and sanctified it.

paragraphs.text: Blessed is God Most High, who gave us rest,
redemption for our souls from burden and sighing.
He will seek out Zion, the banished city;
how long will the groaning soul remain afflicted?
Those who keep Shabbat, son and daughter alike, will be pleasing to God like a meal offering on a griddle.
Rider upon the highest heavens, King of all worlds,
He prepared His people to rest amid pleasant things,
with agreeable foods and many kinds of delicacies,
with garments of honor and a family feast.
Those who keep Shabbat, son and daughter alike, will be pleasing to God like a meal offering on a griddle.
Happy is everyone who awaits a twofold reward
from the One who shelters all, who dwells in the thick cloud.
They shall merit an inheritance upon mountain and plain,
an inheritance and rest, as the sun dawns upon them.
Those who keep Shabbat, son and daughter alike, will be pleasing to God like a meal offering on a griddle.
Whoever observes the Sabbath according to its law, without desecrating it,
shows a worthy love for the holiness that is their portion.
And whoever fulfills the obligations of the day is fortunate:
an offering is sent to God, the Lord who formed them.
Those who keep Shabbat, son and daughter alike, will be pleasing to God like a meal offering on a griddle.
My Rock called it the delight of days;
happy are the wholehearted if they keep it.
A fitting crown is fashioned upon their heads,
for the eternal Rock rested His spirit upon them.
Those who keep Shabbat, son and daughter alike, will be pleasing to God like a meal offering on a griddle.

paragraphs: Remember the Sabbath day to sanctify it.

paragraphs.text: For their dignity is lifted up like a crown upon their head;
therefore let each person give their soul
delight and joy to anoint it with gladness.
Those who keep Shabbat, son and daughter alike, will be pleasing to God like a meal offering on a griddle.
Holy to you is the Sabbath Queen;
she enters your homes to leave a blessing.
In all your dwellings you shall do no work,
neither your sons nor your daughters, nor servants, male or female.
Those who keep Shabbat, son and daughter alike, will be pleasing to God like a meal offering on a griddle.
Author: Rabbi Baruch ben Samuel of Mainz.
If I keep the Sabbath, God will keep me; it is an everlasting sign between Him and me.

paragraphs.text: It is forbidden to pursue one's business or set out on journeys,
or even to speak of one's everyday needs,
of commerce, or even affairs of kings.
I will study God's Torah, and it will make me wise.
In it my soul will always find rest.
Behold, for the first generation my Holy One gave
a sign, providing a double portion of bread on the sixth day.
Thus each Friday He will double my food.
God inscribed a statute in His law for His chosen ones:
to arrange the showbread before Him on this day.
Fasting on it is also prohibited by the sages,
except on the Day of Atonement for my sins.
It is a day of honor, a day of delights:
bread, good wine, meat, and fish.
Those who mourn on it turn away from its purpose,
for it is a day of joy, and You make me rejoice.
The one who desecrates it by work faces destruction.
Therefore I will cleanse my heart as with lye;
I will pray to God at evening and morning,
at Musaf and at Minchah, and He will answer me.
Author: Rabbi Abraham ibn Ezra.
But as for me, let my prayer be unto Thee, O LORD, in an acceptable time; O God, in the abundance of Thy mercy, Answer me with the truth of Thy salvation.

paragraphs.text: You are good, for Your compassion never ends; You are merciful, for Your kindness never ceases. We have always placed our hope in You.
Modim of the Rabbis:

We are thankful to You, that You Adonoy are our God, and God of our fathers, God of all flesh, Our Creator, Creator of the Beginning. Blessings and thanksgivings to Your great and holy Name for keeping us alive, and sustaining us; so may You always keep us alive and sustain us, and gather our exiles to the Courtyards of Your Sanctuary to observe Your statutes, and to do Your will, and to serve You wholeheartedly, for we are thankful to You. Blessed is the Almighty to Whom all thanks are due.
paragraphs.note: Reused from a reviewed near-identical Hebrew Siddur variant (99.76% normalized Hebrew similarity).

paragraphs.text: On Hanukkah and on Purim in walled cities, recite this:

paragraphs: [We thank You] for the miracles for the redemption, for the mighty deeds, for the deliverances, for the wonders for the consolations and for the wars that You performed for our fathers in those days at this season.

paragraphs.text: For Hanukkah:

In the days of Mattathias son of Johanan, the Hasmonean High Priest, and his sons, when the wicked Greek kingdom rose against Your people Israel to make them forget Your Torah and turn them away from the statutes of Your will.
paragraphs.note: Previously translated paragraph, Hebrew similarity 100.0%: source and target independently present in source corpus.

paragraphs.text: But You, in Your abundant mercy, stood by them in their time of distress. You fought their battle, judged their cause, avenged their wrong, delivered the mighty into the hands of the weak, the many into the hands of the few, the impure into the hands of the pure, the wicked into the hands of the righteous, and the arrogant into the hands of those devoted to Your Torah. You made for Yourself a great and holy name in Your world, and brought a great salvation and deliverance to Your people Israel on this day.

Afterward Your children entered the inner sanctuary of Your House, cleared Your Temple, purified Your holy place, lit lamps in Your sacred courtyards, and established these eight days of Hanukkah to give thanks and praise to Your great name.
For Purim:

In the days of Mordechai and Esther in Shushan the capital, when wicked Haman rose against them, he sought to destroy, kill, and annihilate all the Jews, from young to old, children and women, in one day, the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, the month of Adar, and to plunder their possessions.
In Your great compassion You frustrated his counsel, thwarted his plan, returned his evil upon his own head, and hanged him and his sons on the gallows.

paragraphs: And for all the foregoing may Your Name, our King, constantly be blessed and extolled, forever and ever.

paragraphs.text: During the Ten Days of Repentance add: 'And inscribe all the children of Your covenant for a good life.'
All the living will thank You forever, and sincerely praise Your Name, O God of our salvation and our help. Selah.
Blessed are You, LORD, whose name is good and to whom thanksgiving is fitting.

Grant peace, goodness, and blessing, favor, kindness and compassion upon us and upon all Israel, Your people. Bless us, our Father, all of us as one with the light of Your countenance. For by the light of Your countenance You gave us Adonoy our God, a Torah of life and the love of kindliness, righteousness, blessing, compassion, life and peace. And may it be good in Your sight to bless Your people, Israel, at all times and at every moment with Your peace.
paragraphs.note: Previously translated paragraph, Hebrew similarity 98.9%: source and target independently present in source corpus.

paragraphs.text: During the Ten Days of Repentance: In the Book of Life, blessing, peace, good livelihood, deliverance and comfort, may we and all Your people, the House of Israel, be remembered and inscribed before You for a good life and for peace.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs: Blessed are You, Adonoy, Who blesses His people Israel with peace.
May the words of my mouth and the thoughts of my heart be acceptable before You, Adonoy, my Rock and my Redeemer.

paragraphs.text: My God, guard my tongue from evil and my lips from speaking deceit. Before those who curse me, let my soul be silent, and let my soul be like dust to all. Open my heart to Your Torah, and let my soul pursue Your commandments. As for all who plan evil against me, swiftly frustrate their counsel and confound their designs.

Act for the sake of Your name. Act for the sake of Your right hand. Act for the sake of Your holiness. Act for the sake of Your Torah. That Your beloved ones may be delivered, save with Your right hand and answer me.

paragraphs: May the words of my mouth and the thoughts of my heart be acceptable before You, Adonoy, my Rock and my Redeemer.

paragraphs.text: He who makes peace in His heights (during the Ten Days of Repentance: 'the peace'), may He make peace for us and for all Israel; and say: Amen.
May it be Your will, LORD our God and God of our ancestors, that the Temple be rebuilt speedily in our days; and grant us our portion in Your Torah.
There we shall serve You in awe, as in days of old and former years.
On days when Tachanun is not recited on weekdays, and on the Shabbatot of the Four Special Torah Portions, Tzidkatkha is omitted.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and Thy law is truth.
Thy righteousness also, O God, which reacheth unto high heaven; Thou who hast done great things, O God, who is like unto Thee?
paragraphs.note: Reviewed near-exact Hebrew Tanakh alignment (psalms 71:19, similarity 0.988); orthographic/qere differences only.

paragraphs.text: Thy righteousness is like the mighty mountains; Thy judgments are like the great deep; Man and beast Thou preservest, O LORD.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed near-exact Hebrew Tanakh alignment (psalms 36:7, similarity 0.950); orthographic/qere differences only.

paragraphs: It is our obligation to praise the Master of all, to ascribe greatness to the Creator of the [world in the] beginning: that He has not made us like the nations of the lands, and has not positioned us like the families of the earth; that He has not assigned our portion like theirs, nor our lot like that of all their multitudes. For they prostrate themselves to vanity and nothingness, and pray to a god that cannot deliver. But we bow, prostrate ourselves, and offer thanks before the Supreme King of Kings, the Holy One blessed is He, Who spreads the heavens, and establishes the earth, and the seat of His glory is in heaven above, and the abode of His invincible might is in the loftiest heights. He is our God, there is nothing else. Our King is true, all else is insignificant, as it is written in His Torah: And You shall know this day and take into Your heart that Adonoy is God in the heavens above and upon the earth below; there is nothing else.

paragraphs.text: Therefor, we will hope to You L·rd, our G·d to see speedily the glory of Your Might - to remove abominable idolatry from the earth & the false gods be utterly terminated, to repair the world with the Kingship of the Al·mighty. And all living flesh will call in Your Name to turn back to You all the wicked of the earth. They will recognize & will know, all the inhabitants of the earth, that to You that every knee shall bow down, & every tongue. Before you they will kneel & bow down & give honor to Your glorious name & they will all accept the yolk of Your Kingship. And Reign upon them speedily forever & ever. For the Kingship, it is Yours. And forevermore reign in glory. Like it is written in your Torah, “The L·rd will reign forever & ever.” And it is said “and it will be the L·rd will Be King upon all of the earth. On that day the L·rd will be One (ie, only He will be worshiped) & His name One.” And in Your Torah, L·rd, Our G·d, it is written saying “Hear Oh Israel, the L·rd is our G·d the L·rd is One.”

Be not afraid of sudden terror, Neither of the destruction of the wicked, when it cometh; Take counsel together, and it shall be brought to nought; Speak the word, and it shall not stand; For God is with us. Even to old age I am the same, and even to hoar hairs will I carry you; I have made, and I will bear; yea, I will carry, and will deliver.
paragraphs.note: Every colon-delimited Hebrew fragment matched an exact complete bundled Tanakh verse; translations joined without fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: Bless the LORD, O my soul! LORD my God, You are exceedingly great; You are clothed in splendor and majesty.
Who coverest Thyself with light as with a garment, who stretchest out the heavens like a curtain;
Who layest the beams of Thine upper chambers in the waters, who makest the clouds Thy chariot, who walkest upon the wings of the wind;
Who makest winds Thy messengers, the flaming fire Thy ministers.
Who didst establish the earth upon its foundations, that it should not be moved for ever and ever;
Thou didst cover it with the deep as with a vesture; the waters stood above the mountains.
At Thy rebuke they fled, at the voice of Thy thunder they hasted away—
The mountains rose, the valleys sank down— Unto the place which Thou hadst founded for them;
Thou didst set a bound which they should not pass over, That they might not return to cover the earth.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed near-exact Hebrew Tanakh alignment (psalms 104:9, similarity 0.984); orthographic/qere differences only.

paragraphs.text: Who sendest forth springs into the valleys; They run between the mountains;
They give drink to every beast of the field, The wild asses quench their thirst. .
Beside them dwell the fowl of the heaven, From among the branches they sing.
Who waterest the mountains from Thine upper chambers; The earth is full of the fruit of Thy works.
Who causeth the grass to spring up for the cattle, And herb for the service of man; To bring forth bread out of the earth,
paragraphs.note: Reviewed near-exact Hebrew Tanakh alignment (psalms 104:14, similarity 0.988); orthographic/qere differences only.

paragraphs.text: And wine that maketh glad the heart of man, Making the face brighter than oil, And bread that stayeth man's heart.
The trees of the LORD have their fill, the cedars of Lebanon which He planted.
Wherein the birds make their nests; As for the stork, the fir-trees are her house.
The high mountains are for the wild goats; The rocks are a refuge for the conies.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed near-exact Hebrew Tanakh alignment (psalms 104:18, similarity 0.984); orthographic/qere differences only.

paragraphs.text: Who appointedst the moon for seasons; The sun knoweth his going down.
Thou makest darkness, and it is night, Wherein all the beasts of the forest do creep forth.
The young lions roar after their prey, And seek their food from God.
The sun ariseth, they slink away, And couch in their dens.
Man goeth forth unto his work And to his labour until the evening.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed near-exact Hebrew Tanakh alignment (psalms 104:23, similarity 0.980); orthographic/qere differences only.

paragraphs.text: How manifold are Thy works, O LORD! In wisdom hast Thou made them all; The earth is full of Thy creatures.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed near-exact Hebrew Tanakh alignment (psalms 104:24, similarity 0.960); orthographic/qere differences only.

paragraphs.text: Yonder sea, great and wide, Therein are creeping things innumerable, Living creatures, both small and great.
There go the ships; There is leviathan, whom Thou hast formed to sport therein.
All of them wait for Thee, That Thou mayest give them their food in due season.
Thou givest it unto them, they gather it; Thou openest Thy hand, they are satisfied with good.
Thou hidest Thy face, they vanish; Thou withdrawest their breath, they perish, And return to their dust.
Thou sendest forth Thy spirit, they are created; and Thou renewest the face of the earth.
May the glory of the LORD endure forever; may the LORD rejoice in His works.
Who looketh on the earth, and it trembleth; He toucheth the mountains, and they smoke.
I will sing to the LORD as long as I live; I will sing praise to my God while I have my being.
May my meditation be sweet to Him; I will rejoice in the LORD.
Let sinners cease out of the earth, and let the wicked be no more. Bless the LORD, O my soul. Hallelujah.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed near-exact Hebrew Tanakh alignment (psalms 104:35, similarity 0.968); orthographic/qere differences only.

paragraphs.text: Beloved of the soul, merciful Father, draw Your servant to Your will. [Then] Your servant will run like a deer; he will bow before Your splendor. To him, Your affections will be sweeter than the drippings of the honeycomb and all [other pleasant] tastes.

paragraphs: Splendid, Beautiful, Radiance of the world, my soul is lovesick for You. I beseech You, Almighty, please, heal her by showing her the pleasantness of Your radiance. Then she will be strengthened and healed and she will have everlasting joy.

paragraphs.text: Ancient One—let Your mercy be aroused, and please have pity upon Your beloved child; for it is long that I have yearned to behold soon the glory of Your strength. These my heart has desired, please have pity and do not conceal Yourself.

Reveal Yourself, please and spread over me, my Beloved, the shelter of Your peace, let the earth be illuminated from Your glory, we will exult and rejoice in You. Hasten, show [us Your] love, for the time has come, and be gracious unto us as in days of old.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed near-identical Hebrew reuse (>=97.2% normalized similarity) within the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: Behold, God is my salvation; I will trust, and will not be afraid; For GOD the LORD is my strength and song; And He is become my salvation.’

paragraphs.text: Therefore with joy shall ye draw water Out of the wells of salvation.
Salvation belongeth unto the LORD; Thy blessing be upon Thy people. Selah
The LORD of hosts is with us; The God of Jacob is our high tower. Selah
LORD of hosts, happy is the person who trusts in You.

paragraphs.text: Save, LORD; Let the King answer us in the day that we call.
The Jews had light and gladness, and joy and honour.
So may it be for us.
I will lift up the cup of salvation, And call upon the name of the LORD.

paragraphs: Blessed are You, Adonoy our God, King of the Universe, Creator of the fruit of the vine.

Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, Creator of the lights of fire.

paragraphs.text: Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who distinguishes between holy and ordinary, between light and darkness, between Israel and the nations, and between the seventh day and the six days of labor. Blessed are You, LORD, who distinguishes between holy and ordinary.

Hallelujah. Praise, O ye servants of the LORD, Praise the name of the LORD. Blessed be the name of the LORD From this time forth and for ever. From the rising of the sun unto the going down thereof The LORD'S name is to be praised. The LORD is high above all nations, His glory is above the heavens. Who is like unto the LORD our God, That is enthroned on high, That looketh down low Upon heaven and upon the earth? Who raiseth up the poor out of the dust, And lifteth up the needy out of the dunghill; That He may set him with princes, Even with the princes of His people. Who maketh the barren woman to dwell in her house As a joyful mother of children. Hallelujah.

When Israel came forth out of Egypt, The house of Jacob from a people of strange language; Judah became His sanctuary, Israel His dominion. The sea saw it, and fled; The Jordan turned backward. The mountains skipped like rams, The hills like young sheep. What aileth thee, O thou sea, that thou fleest? Thou Jordan, that thou turnest backward? Ye mountains, that ye skip like rams; Ye hills, like young sheep? Tremble, thou earth, at the presence of the Lord, At the presence of the God of Jacob; Who turned the rock into a pool of water, The flint into a fountain of waters.

[On Rosh Chodesh and on Chol HaMoed of Passover, the following section is omitted.] Not unto us, O LORD, not unto us, But unto Thy name give glory, For Thy mercy, and for Thy truth's sake. Wherefore should the nations say: 'Where is now their God?' But our God is in the heavens; Whatsoever pleased Him He hath done. Their idols are silver and gold, The work of men's hands. They have mouths, but they speak not; Eyes have they, but they see not; They have ears, but they hear not; Noses have they, but they smell not; They have hands, but they handle not; Feet have they, but they walk not; Neither speak they with their throat. . They that make them shall be like unto them; Yea, every one that trusteth in them. O Israel, trust thou in the LORD! He is their help and their shield! O house of Aaron, trust ye in the LORD! He is their help and their shield! Ye that fear the LORD, trust in the LORD! He is their help and their shield.
paragraphs.note: Public-domain JPS 1917 biblical passage; Hebrew text aligned, with Siddur-specific omission instruction.

paragraphs.text: The LORD hath been mindful of us, He will bless— He will bless the house of Israel; He will bless the house of Aaron. He will bless them that fear the LORD, Both small and great. The LORD increase you more and more, You and your children. Blessed be ye of the LORD Who made heaven and earth. The heavens are the heavens of the LORD; But the earth hath He given to the children of men. The dead praise not the LORD, Neither any that go down into silence; But we will bless the LORD From this time forth and for ever. Hallelujah.

[On Rosh Chodesh and on Chol HaMoed of Passover, the following section is omitted.] I love that the LORD should hear my voice and my supplications. Because He hath inclined His ear unto me, Therefore will I call upon Him all my days. The cords of death compassed me, And the straits of the nether-world got hold upon me; I found trouble and sorrow. But I called upon the name of the LORD: 'I beseech thee, O LORD, deliver my soul.' Gracious is the LORD, and righteous; Yea, our God is compassionate. The LORD preserveth the simple; I was brought low, and He saved me. Return, O my soul, unto Thy rest; For the LORD hath dealt bountifully with thee. For thou hast delivered my soul from death, Mine eyes from tears, And my feet from stumbling. I shall walk before the LORD In the lands of the living. I trusted even when I spoke: 'I am greatly afflicted.' I said in my haste: 'All men are liars.'
paragraphs.note: Public-domain JPS 1917 biblical passage; Hebrew text aligned, with Siddur-specific omission instruction.

paragraphs.text: How can I repay unto the LORD All His bountiful dealings toward me? I will lift up the cup of salvation, And call upon the name of the LORD. My vows will I pay unto the LORD, Yea, in the presence of all His people. Precious in the sight of the LORD Is the death of His saints. I beseech Thee, O LORD, for I am Thy servant; I am Thy servant, the son of Thy handmaid; Thou hast loosed my bands. I will offer to thee the sacrifice of thanksgiving, And will call upon the name of the LORD. I will pay my vows unto the LORD, Yea, in the presence of all His people; In the courts of the LORD’S house, In the midst of thee, O Jerusalem. Hallelujah.
O praise the LORD, all ye nations; Laud Him, all ye peoples. For His mercy is great toward us; And the truth of the LORD endureth for ever. Hallelujah.
Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good; His mercy endures forever.
So let Israel now say, For His mercy endureth for ever,
Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good; His mercy endures forever.
So let the house of Aaron now say, For His mercy endureth for ever.
Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good; His mercy endures forever.
So let them now that fear the LORD say, For His mercy endureth for ever.
Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good; His mercy endures forever.

Out of my straits I called upon the LORD; He answered me with great enlargement. The LORD is for me; I will not fear; What can man do unto me? The LORD is for me as my helper; And I shall gaze upon them that hate me. It is better to take refuge in the LORD Than to trust in man. It is better to take refuge in the LORD Than to trust in princes. All nations compass me about; Verily, in the name of the LORD I will cut them off. They compass me about, yea, they compass me about; Verily, in the name of the LORD I will cut them off. They compass me about like bees; They are quenched as the fire of thorns; Verily, in the name of the LORD I will cut them off. Thou didst thrust sore at me that I might fall; But the LORD helped me. The LORD is my strength and song; And He is become my salvation. The voice of rejoicing and salvation is in the tents of the righteous; The right hand of the LORD doeth valiantly. The right hand of the LORD is exalted; The right hand of the LORD doeth valiantly. I shall not die, but live, And declare the works of the LORD. The LORD hath chastened me sore; But He hath not given me over unto death. Open to me the gates of righteousness; I will enter into them, I will give thanks unto the LORD. This is the gate of the LORD; The righteous shall enter into it. I will give thanks unto Thee, for Thou hast answered me, And art become my salvation. I will give thanks unto Thee, for Thou hast answered me, And art become my salvation. The stone which the builders rejected Is become the chief corner-stone. The stone which the builders rejected Is become the chief corner-stone. This is the LORD’S doing; It is marvellous in our eyes. This is the LORD’S doing; It is marvellous in our eyes. This is the day which the LORD hath made; We will rejoice and be glad in it. This is the day which the LORD hath made; We will rejoice and be glad in it.

Please, LORD, save us!

Please, LORD, grant us success!

The LORD is God, and hath given us light; Order the festival procession with boughs, even unto the horns of the altar. The LORD is God, and hath given us light; Order the festival procession with boughs, even unto the horns of the altar. Thou art my God, and I will give thanks unto Thee; Thou art my God, I will exalt Thee. Thou art my God, and I will give thanks unto Thee; Thou art my God, I will exalt Thee. paragraphs: When I proclaim Adonoy’s Name attribute greatness to our God.
My Master, open my lips, and my mouth will declare Your praise.

paragraphs.text: Blessed are You, Adonoy, our God, and God of our fathers, God of Abraham, God of Isaac, and God of Jacob, the Almighty, the Great, the Powerful, the Awesome, most high Almighty, Who bestows beneficent kindness, Who possesses everything, Who remembers the piety of the Patriarchs, and Who brings a redeemer to their children’s children, for the sake of His Name, with love.
King, Helper, Savior, and Shield.
Blessed are You, LORD.
Shield of Abraham.

paragraphs: You are mighty forever, my Master; You are the Resurrector of the dead the Powerful One to deliver us.

paragraphs.text: From the Musaf of the first day of Pesach until the Musaf of Shemini Atzeres one should say: He causes the dew to descend.
paragraphs.note: Exact Hebrew match to a sequence of reviewed Siddur paragraphs; translations joined without fuzzy splitting.

paragraphs: Sustainer of the living with kindliness, Resurrector of the dead with great mercy, Supporter of the fallen, and Healer of the sick, and Releaser of the imprisoned, and Fulfiller of His faithfulness to those who sleep in the dust. Who is like You, Master of mighty deeds, and who can be compared to You? King Who causes death and restores life, and causes deliverance to sprout forth.

paragraphs.text: And You are faithful to revive the dead.
Blessed are You, LORD, who revives the dead.
(When the Chazzan repeats the Shemoneh Esrei, the Kedushah is said here)

paragraphs: We will hallow Your Name in the world, as they hallow it in the heavens above, as is written by the hand of Your prophet, And they called one to another, and said:

paragraphs: And in Your Holy Words it is written:
Adonoy will reign forever; Your God, Zion, throughout all generations! Praise God.

paragraphs.text: For the cantor: From generation to generation we shall proclaim Your greatness, and through all eternity we shall sanctify Your holiness. May Your praise, our God, never depart from our lips, for You are a great and holy God and King.

paragraphs.text: Blessed are You, LORD, the holy God (during the Ten Days of Repentance: the Holy King).

paragraphs: You are holy and Your Name is holy and holy beings praise You every day, forever.
Blessed are You, Adonoy, the Almighty, the Holy One.

paragraphs.text: You gave New Moons to Your people as a time of atonement throughout their generations, when they offered willing sacrifices before You and goats for sin offerings to atone for them. May they be a remembrance for all and deliverance for their souls from the enemy's hand. Establish a new altar in Zion, and upon it we shall offer the New Moon burnt offering and bring goat offerings with willing hearts. We shall all rejoice in the service of the Temple, and in the songs of David Your servant that resound in Your city and before Your altar. Bring them everlasting love, and remember the covenant of the ancestors for their children.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Bring us with singing to Zion, Your city, and with everlasting joy to Jerusalem, Your Sanctuary. There we shall present the offerings we owe—the daily offerings in their order and the additional offerings according to their rules. We shall lovingly bring and offer the additional offering of this New Moon, in accordance with Your will, as You wrote in Your Torah through Moses Your servant, from Your glorious mouth, saying:
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: And in your new moons ye shall present a burnt-offering unto the LORD: two young bullocks, and one ram, seven he-lambs of the first year without blemish;
paragraphs.note: Reviewed near-exact Hebrew Tanakh alignment (numbers 28:11, similarity 0.970); orthographic/qere differences only.

paragraphs.text: And their meal offerings and libations as prescribed: three-tenths of an ephah for each bull, two-tenths for the ram, one-tenth for each lamb, wine for its libation, one goat for atonement, and the two daily offerings according to their law.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Our God and God of our ancestors, renew this month upon us for goodness and blessing, gladness and joy, deliverance and consolation, livelihood and sustenance, life and peace, pardon for sin and forgiveness of wrongdoing. [In a leap year, until Nisan: and atonement for transgression.] For You have chosen Your people Israel from among all the nations and established for them the laws of the New Moons.
paragraphs.note: Original English working translation aligned to the full Hebrew paragraph; specialist review pending.

paragraphs.text: Blessed are You, LORD, who sanctifies Israel and the New Moons.

paragraphs: Be pleased, Adonoy, our God, with Your people, Israel, and their prayer; and restore the service to the Holy of Holies in Your abode, and the fire-offerings of Israel; and accept their prayer, lovingly and willingly. And may You always find pleasure with the service of Your people, Israel.

paragraphs.text: May our eyes behold Your merciful return to Zion.
Blessed are You, LORD, who restores His Presence to Zion.
We thank You, for You are the LORD our God and God of our ancestors forever and ever, the Rock of our lives, the Shield of our salvation in every generation.
for our lives entrusted to Your hand, for our souls placed in Your care, and for Your miracles with us every day, Your wonders and goodness at all times—morning, noon and evening.

paragraphs.text: For Hanukkah:

For by the light of Your countenance You gave us Adonoy our God, a Torah of life and the love of kindliness, righteousness, blessing, compassion, life and peace. And may it be good in Your sight to bless Your people, Israel, at all times and at every moment with Your peace.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed closely matching Hebrew wording in existing translated passage.

paragraphs: Blessed are You, Adonoy, Who blesses His people Israel with peace.
May the words of my mouth and the thoughts of my heart be acceptable before You, Adonoy, my Rock and my Redeemer.

paragraphs.text: My God, guard my tongue from evil and my lips from speaking deceit. Before those who curse me, let my soul be silent, and let my soul be like dust to all. Open my heart to Your Torah, and let my soul pursue Your commandments. As for all who plan evil against me, swiftly frustrate their counsel and confound their designs.

Act for the sake of Your name. Act for the sake of Your right hand. Act for the sake of Your holiness. Act for the sake of Your Torah. That Your beloved ones may be delivered, save with Your right hand and answer me.

paragraphs: May the words of my mouth and the thoughts of my heart be acceptable before You, Adonoy, my Rock and my Redeemer.

paragraphs.text: May the One who makes peace in His heights make peace for us and for all Israel; and say: Amen.
May it be Your will, LORD our God and God of our ancestors, that the Temple be rebuilt speedily in our days; and grant us our portion in Your Torah.
There we shall serve You in awe, as in days of old and former years.
Then the offering of Judah and Jerusalem shall be pleasing to the LORD, as in days of old and former years.
The Ark is opened:
Continue 'Blessed are You ...' through 'Savior and Shield.'
With His knowledge I shall utter riddles.
For this people, renew joy through dew.
Let dew gladden the valley and its grasses.
Those rejoicing in His shade are united.
May the dew, a sign of youth, protect the generations.
Blessed are You, LORD, Shield of Abraham.

paragraphs: You are mighty forever, my Master; You are the Resurrector of the dead the Powerful One to deliver us.

paragraphs.text: The depths yearn to serve as a footstool for His drops.
And every meadow of grass longs for it.
Remembering dew adds to the recital of His mighty deeds.
It is inscribed in the approach of the additional prayers.
May dew give life to the hollow places of the branches.
Our God and God of our ancestors:
Give dew to make Your land flourish.
Grant us blessing in Your joy.
Let grain and new wine abound when You bestow increase.
Restore the city You desire.
For dew:
Command the dew to bring a good and flourishing year.
Let the fruit of the earth be for glory and splendor.
The city that remains like a sheltering sukkah.
Set it as a crown in Your hand.
For dew:
May dew wave over a blessed land.
Satisfy us with blessing from the precious gifts of heaven.
To bring light out of darkness.
The vine has been drawn after You.
For dew:
May the dew bring forth the sweetness of the hills.
Nourish with Your abundance those whom You have chosen.
Rescue those favored by You from their prisons.
Let us make song sweet and raise our voices.
For dew:
Fill our storehouses with dew and abundance.
Will You now renew our days?
Establish our name in honor, as is fitting before You, O Beloved.
Make us a well-watered garden.
For dew:
May the dew bless our sustenance.
Let there be no leanness in our fertile places.
For the awe-inspiring people whom You led away like sheep,
Please bring forth Your favor for her.
For dew:
Cantor: For You are the LORD our God, who causes the wind to blow and brings down the dew.
For blessing and not for curse. Amen.
For life and not for death. Amen.
For plenty and not for hunger. Amen.
Who sustains the living, etc.

Af-Bri was appointed by name as the angel of rain.
To cover the sky with clouds, to pour forth and bring down rain.
Waters borne in clouds, to crown the valleys.
So that they not be held back by an unfulfilled decree.
Protect through them the faithful who ask for rain.
Blessed are You, LORD, Shield of Abraham.

paragraphs: You are mighty forever, my Master; You are the Resurrector of the dead the Powerful One to deliver us.

paragraphs.text: He labors to divide the rains from their streams.
To soften the face of the dry land through the precious stone’s brightness.
The waters You designated for Your majesty as a sign.
To give relief with their showers to every breathing soul.
Those who mention the might of rain ask that it give life.
Our God and God of our ancestors:
Remember the father who followed You like water.
You blessed him like a tree planted beside streams of water.
You sheltered him and rescued him from fire and water.
You remembered him on account of his descendants, upon all waters.
For his sake, do not withhold water.
Remember the one whose birth was foretold with “Let a little water be brought.”
You commanded his father to offer him, to pour out his blood like water.
He too took care to pour out his heart like water.
He dug and found wells of water.
By his merit, graciously grant abundant rain.
Remember the one who took his staff and crossed the waters of the Jordan.
He united his heart and rolled away the stone from the mouth of the well of water.
When he wrestled with a heavenly prince, mingled of fire and water.
Therefore You promised to be with him through fire and water.
For his sake, do not withhold water.
Remember the one drawn from the waters in a basket of reeds.
They said of him, “He drew water for us,” and he watered the flock.
When Your treasured people thirsted for water,
He struck the rock and waters came forth.
By his merit, graciously grant abundant rain.
Remember the appointed priest of the Temple who immersed five times in water.
He washed and sanctified his hands with water.
He proclaimed and sprinkled purifying water.
He was separated from the people who were impetuous like water.
For his sake, do not withhold water.
Remember the twelve tribes whom You led through the divided waters.
You made the bitter waters sweet for them.
Their descendants poured out their blood for You like water.
Turn toward us, for waters have surrounded our souls.
Through their righteousness, graciously grant abundant rain.
Cantor: For You are the LORD our God, who causes the wind to blow and brings down the rain.
For blessing and not for curse. Amen.
For life and not for death. Amen.
For plenty and not for hunger. Amen.
Who sustains the living, etc.

paragraphs.text: Every day will I bless Thee; And I will praise Thy name for ever and ever.
Great is the LORD, and highly to be praised; And His greatness is unsearchable.
One generation shall laud Thy works to another, And shall declare Thy mighty acts.
The glorious splendour of Thy majesty, And Thy wondrous works, will I rehearse.
They shall speak of the might of Your awesome deeds, and I shall recount Your greatness.

paragraphs.text: They shall utter the fame of Thy great goodness, And shall sing of Thy righteousness.

All Thy works shall praise Thee, O LORD; And Thy saints shall bless Thee.
They shall speak of the glory of Thy kingdom, And talk of Thy might;
To make known to the sons of men His mighty acts, And the glory of the majesty of His kingdom.
Thy kingdom is a kingdom for all ages, And Thy dominion endureth throughout all generations.
The LORD upholdeth all that fall, And raiseth up all those that are bowed down.

Thou openest Thy hand, And satisfiest every living thing with favour.

May He establish His kingdom, cause His deliverance to flourish, and hasten the coming of His Messiah. The congregation answers: Amen.

paragraphs.text: Blessed, praised, glorified, exalted, uplifted, honored, elevated and lauded be the name of the Holy One, blessed be He. The congregation answers: “Blessed be He.”

Thine, O LORD, is the greatness, and the power, and the glory, and the victory, and the majesty; for all that is in the heaven and in the earth is Thine; Thine is the kingdom, O LORD, and Thou art exalted as head above all.

'Forgive our iniquity and our sin, and take us as Your inheritance' (Exodus 34:9). Forgive us, our Father, for we have sinned; pardon us, our King, for we have transgressed (from the Amidah). 'For You, Lord, are good and ready to forgive, abundant in loving-kindness to all who call upon You' (Psalm 86:5).

paragraphs.text: 'Seek the Lord while He may be found; call upon Him while He is near' (Isaiah 55:6). 'Let the wicked abandon his way and the unrighteous man his thoughts; let him return to the Lord, who will have compassion on him, and to our God, who will abundantly pardon' (Isaiah 55:7). Lord, hear our voice; may Your ears attend to the sound of our supplications (adapted from Psalm 130:2). May our prayer be set before You like incense (adapted from Psalm 141:2).
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: As a father has compassion for his children, so may the Lord have compassion on us (adapted from Psalm 103:13). Lord of hosts, happy is the one who trusts in You (Psalm 84:13). Save us, Lord; may the King answer us on the day we call (Psalm 20:10).

paragraphs: You are Almighty, Slow to anger; You are called the Lord of Mercy, and You have taught us the way of repentance. Remember the greatness of Your mercy and kindness, this day and every day, for the descendants of Your loved ones. Turn to us with compassion for You are the Lord of Mercy. We approach Your Presence with supplication and prayer, as You made known to [Moses,] the modest one of old. Turn from Your fierce anger, as it is written in Your Torah: May we be sheltered and lodged in the shadow of Your wings, as on the day [of which it is said:] When Adonoy descended in the cloud. Remove [our] transgression, and blot out [our] iniquity, as on the day [of which it is said:] And He stood with him there. Give ear to our cry and listen to our speech, as on the day [of which it is said:] And He proclaimed in the Name, Adonoy And there it is said:
And Adonoy passed before him [Moses] and proclaimed:

paragraphs.text: The LORD, the LORD, a compassionate and gracious God, slow to anger, abundant in kindness and truth; preserving kindness for thousands, forgiving iniquity, transgression and sin, and cleansing. Forgive our iniquity and our sin, and take us as Your inheritance. Forgive us, our Father, for we have sinned; pardon us, our King, for we have transgressed. For You, O Lord, are good and forgiving, and abundant in kindness to all who call upon You.

For with the Lord is loving-kindness, and with Him is abundant redemption. Redeem Israel, O God, from all its troubles. He will redeem Israel from all its iniquities. The Lord redeems the souls of His servants; none who seek refuge in Him shall be condemned.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: As a father has compassion on his children, so may the LORD have compassion on us. Salvation belongs to the LORD; may Your blessing rest on Your people, selah. The LORD of Hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge, selah. LORD of Hosts, happy is the one who trusts in You. LORD, save us; may the King answer us on the day we call.

paragraphs: When the Torah is unrolled, the Reader says:

paragraphs.text: Pardon, we pray, the iniquity of this people according to the greatness of Your kindness, as You have forgiven this people from Egypt until now; and there it says:
Congregation:
And the LORD said: ‘I have pardoned according to thy word.

O my God, incline Thine ear, and hear; open Thine eyes, and behold our desolations, and the city upon which Thy name is called; for we do not present our supplications before Thee because of our righteousness, but because of Thy great compassions. O Lord, hear, O Lord, forgive, O Lord, attend and do, defer not; for Thine own sake, O my God, because Thy name is called upon Thy city and Thy people.’
paragraphs.note: Every colon-delimited fragment matched a unique near-exact complete Tanakh verse; reviewed orthographic/qere alignment only.

paragraphs.text: A penitential prayer arranged alphabetically; the author's name, Joseph, appears at the end.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Our God and God of our ancestors:

I recall the distress that overtook me: with three blows in this month He struck me, cut me down, confined me and crushed me, and even now they wear me out. On the eighth day of the month darkness came upon me from right and left; I ordained a fast for all three days. Then the Greek king compelled me to translate the Torah into Greek; plowmen plowed upon my back and drew long furrows. On the ninth I was enraged and covered with shame; the mantle of glory and splendor was taken from me. On this day the one who spoke beautiful sayings, Ezra the Scribe, was taken away. On the tenth the prophet, son of Buzi, was commanded: 'Write in a book of visions,' as a memorial for a wasting and despised people, 'this very day.' On the tenth day according to the count of months the enemy besieged the city. I shall raise mourning and lamentation with my mouth; a succession of disasters sets my heart aflame when a fugitive comes and says, 'The city has been struck.' Because of all this I put dust on my face; I opened my mouth over four calamities, as though an arrow had pierced my heart. Through these troubles I felt as though I had dug my grave. The Lord is righteous, for I rebelled against His word. I called upon Your name; You comfort me in my distress. See my affliction and hear the voice of my plea. Hear my supplication, hasten my deliverance; do not hide Your ear from my cry for relief. In the month of Tevet I suffered grievously and my paths were altered. I turned aside and sinned; may He show me goodness, the One who says to the sea, 'Thus far you may come.'
paragraphs.note: New English working translation reviewed against the Hebrew and available Russian text; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: God, the King, who sits upon a throne of mercy and acts with kindness, forgives the sins of His people, passing over each offense in turn. He grants abundant forgiveness to sinners and pardon to transgressors; He deals righteously with all flesh and spirit and does not repay them according to their wickedness. O God, You taught us to recite the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy. Remember for us today the covenant of the Thirteen Attributes, as You made them known to the humble one long ago. As it is written: The LORD descended in the cloud, stood with him there, and proclaimed the Name of the LORD.
And the LORD passed before him and proclaimed:

The LORD, the LORD, a compassionate and gracious God, slow to anger, abundant in kindness and truth; preserving kindness for thousands, forgiving iniquity, transgression and sin, and cleansing. Forgive our iniquity and our sin, and take us as Your inheritance. Forgive us, our Father, for we have sinned; pardon us, our King, for we have transgressed. For You, O Lord, are good and forgiving, and abundant in kindness to all who call upon You.

O God, the nations entered Your inheritance; they defiled Your holy sanctuary and reduced Jerusalem to ruins. O God, arrogant men rose up against us; an assembly of tyrants sought our lives, and they did not set You before them.

As a father has compassion on his children, so may the LORD have compassion on us. Salvation belongs to the LORD; may Your blessing rest on Your people, selah. The LORD of Hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge, selah. LORD of Hosts, happy is the one who trusts in You. LORD, save us; may the King answer us on the day we call.
An alphabetical penitential prayer signed with the author's name: Abraham son of Menachem, may he be strong.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Our God and God of our ancestors:

The cornerstone has become heaps of ruins and a plowed field; the heirs of the inheritance have become a laughingstock among the nations. My heart aches within me, worn out and broken; we remain as though fatherless, like orphans. Once delicate and refined, enclosed among roses, she now mourns, delivered into the hands of rebels. The faithful city has become like a widow; her countless descendants have been sold for no silver. Tender and delicate, worthy of royalty, her suffering has endured so many years and days. The house of Jacob has been given over to plunder, mockery and insult; the joyful city has become a place for planting vineyards. Made to drink the cup of staggering at the hands of the children of wrongdoing, she once was desired like a burnt offering and fragrant incense. She refused to abandon the Torah of her Father and found no rest by night or day. Awesome, Most High God! May favor come from You to defend Zion in the year of recompense. Renew our days as of old, O Dwelling, eternal God; make what is crimson white as wool, and stains white as snow. Strengthen us in awe of You and in keeping Your Torah; visit us with Your salvation, merciful God.
paragraphs.note: New English working translation reviewed against the Hebrew and available Russian text; specialist proofreading pending.

He grants abundant forgiveness to sinners and pardon to transgressors; He deals righteously with all flesh and spirit and does not repay them according to their wickedness. For You, O Lord, are good and forgiving, and abundant in kindness to all who call upon You.
A refrain whose opening letters spell the author's name: Abraham Isaac Ephraim, may he be strong.

paragraphs.text: My ancestors, when they trusted in the name of the God who is my Rock, grew great, prospered, and bore fruit. But from the time they were led astray and walked perversely with Him, they steadily declined until the tenth month. On the tenth day of the month the king of Babylon advanced, laid siege to the holy city, and the great destroyer drew near. My holy splendor was brought low and I was afflicted in chains; month after month, my lyre became an instrument of mourning.
paragraphs.note: Working English translation; liturgical proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: My ancestors: She, the firstborn of the beginning, became the first of those devoted to destruction; she invoked the names of other gods, and sin brought its consequence. She would not acknowledge the face of God and was swept away by the flood; anguish, like a woman in labor, rises now to the heights.
paragraphs.note: Working English translation; liturgical proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Our God brought a day of evil and siege; He commanded my enemies all around to besiege my children. That day my heart grew faint, without strength to restrain it, and He spoke to the prophet: Prophesy concerning the rebellious house.

From those who sit in the gate He removed the mantle; His anger burned like fire and He lifted away the crown. From Lebanon, the forest, He cast down its glory; the raging tempest makes the hair of my flesh stand on end.

You were compared to one exceedingly beautiful, but now are darkened. Through sin you stumbled and turned your heart backward. They struck at your rear and you were cut down, first and second time; you were not swaddled, and little balm remains.

The Rock is righteous and perfect, yet the burden of guilt grew weary. From the cherub to the threshold and the corner of the roof it departed, because of recorded sin; their outcry arose, for their evil was abundant like a fruit-bearing tree.

The One who measures deeds strengthened all who arose against me, for my days were filled with wicked acts. From the shame of my youth I forgot the kindnesses of the One who gives my bread, my water, my flax and my wool.

My attackers opened their mouths and swallowed my inheritance. They prevailed greatly over me, drinking and swallowing my blood. Foreigners besieged me and mistreated my brothers, crying, “Lay bare, lay bare!”—the children of Seir.

They said: “Come, let us destroy them and erase their memory.” Jealous and avenging God, repay them so they bear their ruin. Give them according to their deeds, and let their expectation end in shame, as one dreams of three white baskets.

My wound has not been softened and my bruises are grievous; my eyes have dimmed while gazing for my radiant Beloved. Has His anger still not subsided forever? Why has He done this, and why does His anger burn?

Merciful One, my God, do not abandon me forever. My mourning days have lengthened and my heart still sighs. Return, God, to Your dwelling; do not forsake Your place. End my days of mourning, for You will grant my reward.

LORD, the portion of my inheritance, hurry to help me. You have opened my sackcloth and girded me with gladness. Shine on my darkness with Your light; light the night of my longing, for You are my lamp.

From grief and groaning, God, redeem my soul. Grant respite to Your people, my King and my Holy One. Turn the fast of the fifth month, the fast of the fourth month, and the fast of the tenth month into gladness and joy.
My ancestors:

God, the King, who sits upon a throne of mercy and acts with kindness, forgives the sins of His people, passing over each offense in turn. He grants abundant forgiveness to sinners and pardon to transgressors; He deals righteously with all flesh and spirit and does not repay them according to their wickedness. O God, You taught us to recite the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy. Remember for us today the covenant of the Thirteen Attributes, as You made them known to the humble one long ago. As it is written: The LORD descended in the cloud, stood with him there, and proclaimed the Name of the LORD.
And the LORD passed before him and proclaimed:

The LORD, the LORD, a compassionate and gracious God, slow to anger, abundant in kindness and truth; preserving kindness for thousands, forgiving iniquity, transgression and sin, and cleansing. Forgive our iniquity and our sin, and take us as Your inheritance. Forgive us, our Father, for we have sinned; pardon us, our King, for we have transgressed. For You, O Lord, are good and forgiving, and abundant in kindness to all who call upon You.

Remember Your compassion, Lord, and Your loving-kindness, for they are everlasting. Remember us, Lord, with favor toward Your people; visit us with Your salvation. Remember Your congregation, which You acquired long ago, the tribe of Your inheritance which You redeemed—Mount Zion, where You dwelt. Remember, Lord, the love of Jerusalem; do not forget the love of Zion forever. You will arise and have mercy on Zion; for the time to favor her, the appointed time, has come. Remember, Lord, against the children of Edom the day of Jerusalem, when they said, 'Lay her bare, lay her bare, to her foundations!' Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel Your servants, to whom You swore by Yourself, saying You would multiply their descendants like the stars of heaven and give them the entire land as an eternal inheritance. Remember Your servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and do not regard this people's stubbornness, wickedness, or sin.
paragraphs.note: Original English working translation aligned to Hebrew; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Remember for us the covenant of the ancestors, as You said: 'I will remember My covenant with Jacob, and also My covenant with Isaac, and also My covenant with Abraham will I remember; and I will remember the land.'

Remember for us the covenant with those of old, as You said: 'I will remember for them the covenant with their ancestors whom I brought out of Egypt before the nations, to be their God; I am the Lord.' Treat us as You promised: 'Even when they are in their enemies’ land, I will not reject or abhor them to destroy them or break My covenant with them, for I am the Lord their God.' Restore our fortunes and have mercy upon us, as it is written: 'The Lord your God will restore your fortunes and have compassion on you and gather you again from all the peoples among whom He scattered you.' Gather our scattered ones, as it is written: 'Even if your dispersed are at the farthest edge of heaven, from there the Lord your God will gather you and take you.' Wipe away our transgressions like a cloud, as it is written: 'I have blotted out your transgressions like a cloud and your sins like a mist; return to Me, for I have redeemed you.' Erase our transgressions for Your own sake, as You said: 'I, I am He who blots out your transgressions for My own sake, and your sins I will not remember.' Make our sins white as snow and wool, as it is written: 'Come now, let us reason together, says the Lord: though your sins are scarlet, they shall be white as snow; though red like crimson, they shall become like wool.' Sprinkle pure water upon us and purify us, as it is written: 'I will sprinkle pure water upon you, and you shall be clean; from all your impurities and idols I will cleanse you.' Have mercy on us and do not destroy us, as it is written: 'For the Lord your God is a merciful God; He will not abandon or destroy you or forget His covenant with your ancestors, which He swore to them.' Circumcise our hearts to love Your name, as it is written: 'The Lord your God will circumcise your heart and the heart of your descendants to love the Lord your God with all your heart and soul, so that you may live.' Let us find You when we seek You, as it is written: 'You will seek the Lord your God from there, and find Him if you seek Him with all your heart and soul.' Bring us to Your holy mountain and gladden us in Your house of prayer, as it is written: 'I will bring them to My holy mountain and make them joyful in My house of prayer; their burnt offerings and sacrifices shall be accepted on My altar, for My house shall be called a house of prayer for all peoples.'
paragraphs.note: Original English working translation aligned to Hebrew; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Hear our voice, Lord our God; spare us and have mercy upon us, and receive our prayer with compassion and favor. Return us to You, Lord, and we shall return; renew our days as of old. Give ear to our words, Lord; understand our meditation. May the words of our mouths and the thoughts of our hearts be acceptable before You, Lord, our Rock and Redeemer. Do not cast us away from Your presence, nor take Your holy spirit from us. Do not cast us off in old age; when our strength fails, do not forsake us. Do not abandon us, Lord our God; do not be far from us. Show us a sign for good, that those who hate us may see it and be ashamed, for You, Lord, have helped and comforted us. For we hope in You, Lord; You will answer, Lord our God.
paragraphs.note: Original English working translation aligned to Hebrew; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs: Our God and God of our fathers, let our prayer come before you and do not ignore our supplication. For we are not so brazen-faced and stiff-necked to say to you, Adonoy, our God, and God of our fathers, We are righteous and have not sined. But, indeed, we and our fathers have sinned.

We have trespassed [against God and man, and we are devastated by our guilt]; We have betrayed [God and man, we have been ungrateful for the good done to us]; We have stolen; We have slandered. We have caused others to sin; We have caused others to commit sins for which they are called רְשָׁעִים, wicked; We have sinned with malicious intent; We have forcibly taken other’s possessions even though we paid for them; We have added falsehood upon falsehood; we have joined with evil individuals or groups. We have given harmful advice; We have deceived; We have mocked; We have rebelled against God and His Torah; We have caused God to be angry with us; We have turned away from God’s Torah; We have sinned deliberately; We have been negligent in our performance of the commandments; We have caused our friends grief; We have been stiff-necked, refusing to admit that the cause of our suffering is our own sins. We have committed sins for which we are called רָשָׁע [raising a hand to hit someone]. We have committed sins which are the result of moral corruption; We have committed sins which the Torah refers to as abominations; We have gone astray; We have led others astray.

paragraphs.text: We have turned away from Your commandments and Your good judgments, and it has not benefited us. Yet You are righteous in all that has come upon us, for You have acted faithfully while we have acted wickedly. We have done wrong and rebelled; therefore we have not been saved. Place in our hearts the resolve to abandon the way of wickedness and hasten salvation for us, as it is written through Your prophet: 'Let the wicked forsake his way and the unrighteous man his thoughts; let him return to the Lord, who will have compassion on him, and to our God, who will abundantly pardon.'
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Your righteous anointed one said before You: “Who can discern his errors? Clear me of hidden faults.” Cleanse us, Lord our God, of all our transgressions and purify us from all our impurities. Sprinkle clean water upon us and cleanse us, as it is written by Your prophet: “I will sprinkle clean water upon you, and you shall be clean; I will cleanse you from all your impurities and from all your idols.” Your people and inheritance hunger for Your goodness, thirst for Your kindness, and long for Your salvation. May they recognize and know that mercy and forgiveness belong to the Lord our God.
paragraphs.note: Working English translation; liturgical proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Your name is Merciful God; Your name is Gracious God. Your name is called upon us: Lord, act for the sake of Your name! Act for Your truth, Your covenant, Your greatness and splendor, Your teaching, Your majesty, Your promises, Your remembrance, Your kindness, Your goodness, Your unity, Your honor, Your instruction, Your kingship, Your eternity, Your mysteries, Your might, Your glory, Your righteousness, Your holiness, Your abundant mercies, Your Presence, and Your praise. Act for the sake of those who loved You and now dwell in the dust; for Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; for Moses and Aaron; for David and Solomon; for Jerusalem, Your holy city; for Zion, the dwelling of Your glory; for the desolation of Your Temple and the ruins of Your altar; for those killed because of Your holy name; for those slaughtered for affirming Your unity; for those who went through fire and water to sanctify Your name; for nursing infants who have not sinned; for weaned children who have not transgressed; and for the children who study in their teachers' houses. Act for Your own sake, if not for ours. Act for Your sake and save us.
paragraphs.note: Original English working translation aligned to Hebrew; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Answer us, Lord, answer us! Answer us, our God, our Father, our Creator, our Redeemer, our Seeker; answer us! Faithful God, ancient and kind, pure and upright, living and enduring, good and beneficent, knower of our nature, restrainer of anger, clothed in righteousness, King of kings of kings, awesome and exalted, forgiving and pardoning, answering in trouble, redeeming and rescuing, just and upright, near to those who call Him, compassionate and gracious, hearing the poor and supporting the innocent—answer us! God of our ancestors, God of Abraham, Fear of Isaac, Mighty One of Jacob, Helper of the tribes, Refuge of the mothers—answer us! Slow to anger, easily reconciled, answering in a time of favor, Father of orphans and Judge of widows—answer us!
paragraphs.note: Original English working translation aligned to Hebrew; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: May He who answered Abraham our father on Mount Moriah answer us. May He who answered Isaac his son when bound upon the altar answer us. May He who answered Jacob at Beth-El answer us. May He who answered Joseph in prison answer us. May He who answered our ancestors at the Sea of Reeds answer us. May He who answered Moses at Horeb answer us. May He who answered Aaron with the incense pan answer us. May He who answered Phinehas when he stood up among the congregation answer us. May He who answered Joshua at Gilgal answer us. May He who answered Samuel at Mizpah answer us. May He who answered David and his son Solomon in Jerusalem answer us. May He who answered Elijah on Mount Carmel answer us. May He who answered Elisha at Jericho answer us. May He who answered Jonah in the belly of the great fish answer us. May He who answered Hezekiah king of Judah in his illness answer us. May He who answered Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah in the fiery furnace answer us. May He who answered Daniel in the lions' den answer us. May He who answered Mordecai and Esther in the capital Shushan answer us. May He who answered Ezra in exile answer us. May He who answered all the righteous, devout, blameless and upright answer us.
paragraphs.note: Original English working translation aligned to Hebrew; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Merciful One who answers the poor, answer us. Merciful One who answers the brokenhearted, answer us. Merciful One who answers the humble of spirit, answer us. Merciful One, answer us. Merciful One, have pity. Merciful One, redeem. Merciful One, deliver. Merciful One, have mercy upon us, now, speedily, and in a time soon to come.
Forgive us, our Father, for in our great folly we have erred; pardon us, our King, for our sins are many.

paragraphs: You are Almighty, Slow to anger; You are called the Lord of Mercy, and You have taught us the way of repentance. Remember the greatness of Your mercy and kindness, this day and every day, for the descendants of Your loved ones. Turn to us with compassion for You are the Lord of Mercy. We approach Your Presence with supplication and prayer, as You made known to [Moses,] the modest one of old. Turn from Your fierce anger, as it is written in Your Torah: May we be sheltered and lodged in the shadow of Your wings, as on the day [of which it is said:] When Adonoy descended in the cloud. Remove [our] transgression, and blot out [our] iniquity, as on the day [of which it is said:] And He stood with him there. Give ear to our cry and listen to our speech, as on the day [of which it is said:] And He proclaimed in the Name, Adonoy And there it is said:
And Adonoy passed before him [Moses] and proclaimed:

paragraphs.text: The LORD, the LORD, a compassionate and gracious God, slow to anger, abundant in kindness and truth; preserving kindness for thousands, forgiving iniquity, transgression and sin, and cleansing. Forgive our iniquity and our sin, and take us as Your inheritance. Forgive us, our Father, for we have sinned; pardon us, our King, for we have transgressed. For You, O Lord, are good and forgiving, and abundant in kindness to all who call upon You.
I waited patiently for the LORD; He inclined to me and heard my cry. Indeed, in the path of Your judgments, LORD, we have waited for You; the desire of our soul is for Your name and remembrance.

As a father has compassion on his children, so may the LORD have compassion on us. Salvation belongs to the LORD; may Your blessing rest on Your people, selah. The LORD of Hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge, selah. LORD of Hosts, happy is the one who trusts in You. LORD, save us; may the King answer us on the day we call.

paragraphs.text: Pardon, we pray, the iniquity of this people according to the greatness of Your kindness, as You have forgiven this people from Egypt until now; and there it says:
Congregation:
And the LORD said: ‘I have pardoned according to thy word.

O my God, incline Thine ear, and hear; open Thine eyes, and behold our desolations, and the city upon which Thy name is called; for we do not present our supplications before Thee because of our righteousness, but because of Thy great compassions. O Lord, hear, O Lord, forgive, O Lord, attend and do, defer not; for Thine own sake, O my God, because Thy name is called upon Thy city and Thy people.’

paragraphs.text: A penitential poem arranged alphabetically; its closing acrostic gives the author's name as Menahem son of Rabbi Machir. May he live. Amen and amen.

Our God and God of our fathers! When a man rose against us, fear and trembling seized us. When he joined the deceitful kingdom, we nearly stumbled. They resolved to sell us, with no one to uphold us, and said: 'Come, let us wipe them out from among the nations, that the name of Israel be remembered no more.' My eyes grew weary looking heavenward; I cried to You while my enemies cursed: destroy their name and remnant, erase their name and let it perish. Entangle my oppressors in the very schemes of deceit they devised, for they said, 'The Lord does not see, nor does the God of Jacob understand.' He humbled and afflicted His scattered people, yet not from His heart, nor to destroy them. They had sinned before Him, and by the removal of a signet ring were handed over to calamity. Yet He fulfilled His good word before the eyes of the nations in order to raise them up: 'Yet even when they are in the land of their enemies, I will not reject them or abhor them so as to destroy them.' He hinted at the events to a people covered in dust and adorned with myrtle: it was written, 'I will surely hide My face,' yet the fragrant myrtle was planted. A tree was prepared for Haman's hanging, and 'instead of the thorn shall rise the cypress, and instead of the nettle shall rise the myrtle.' The one who listened to false words wrote an accusation and a decree of sorrow. He who erred in counting the appointed time dressed in royal robes, prepared to use the sacred vessels of the House hewn from stone; there the accuser appeared among them. The people in Shushan ate from the feast that brought them misfortune. The accuser opened his mouth to slander them and hand them over to one who was ready to purchase them. The Rock consented to the writing of the letter that would destroy their hope: 'I said, I would scatter them and erase their memory from among mankind.' The holy ministering angels wept bitterly and cried: 'Merciful One, look upon the covenant and do not break it by casting the people far away!' The Torah, Israel's inheritance, heard and dressed in the garments of widowhood and distress; she put her hand upon her head and went forth weeping and crying aloud. The Tishbite girded his loins with sackcloth and hurried to awaken those who slept in Machpelah—the three patriarchs. He urgently said to the shepherd: 'Why are you sleeping? Awake! Arise, call upon your God; perhaps God will remember us.' He told of the clay seal prepared for the accuser, and of what Nineveh teaches: repentance after a decree can turn wrath away. The son of Kish knocked at the doors of the study house, clothed himself in sackcloth and sat in ashes. He gathered the children before him; for three days they fasted and went hungry. The voice of Jacob weakened the arrogant one's hands, while his hands were spread in faith to God: 'Save me from disgrace, lest the enemy come and strike down mother together with children.' These and those—the children of my mighty ones and my teachers—all cried aloud, and their outcry rose to the Lord. The Lord heard their weeping and asked, 'What is this sound of a flock in My ears?' The shepherd replied, 'These are the holy little ones, the holy seed.' Lord, save those being led to death from the evil enemy! The Merciful One was filled with compassion and desired to mourn what had occurred; and when the King of Israel read the letter, He tore it up. The Jew gave over his children below, and their Father above; to each only a narrow space was left. The governor saw the double recompense, rejoiced, and spoke praise: 'He restored me to my position, and him he hanged.' Esther recorded the enactment to be read as praise and thanksgiving. In heaven they confirmed what the beloved people had accepted on earth. The miracle shall be celebrated as a sign, as in ancient days when wondrous deeds were proclaimed: 'At this time relief and deliverance shall arise for the Jews.'
paragraphs.note: New English working translation reviewed against the Hebrew and available Russian text; specialist proofreading pending.

O God, You taught us to recite the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy. Remember for us today the covenant of the Thirteen Attributes, as You made them known to the humble one long ago. And the LORD passed before him and proclaimed:
