Forgive our iniquity and our sin, and take us as Your inheritance. Forgive us, our Father, for we have sinned; pardon us, our King, for we have transgressed. For You, O Lord, are good and forgiving, and abundant in kindness to all who call upon You.

For with You is the fountain of life; in Your light we see light. Answer us when we call, God of our salvation. In our distress You made room for us; be gracious to us and hear our prayer. And now, may the power of the Lord be great, as You have spoken, saying:

As a father has compassion on his children, so may the LORD have compassion on us. Salvation belongs to the LORD; may Your blessing rest on Your people, selah. The LORD of Hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge, selah. LORD of Hosts, happy is the one who trusts in You. LORD, save us; may the King answer us on the day we call.
A penitential poem arranged alphabetically; its closing acrostic gives the author's name as Shimon son of Isaac.
Our God and God of our ancestors:

You are the God who performs wonders; among the nations You made known Your fearsome might. With Your hand You redeemed Your people from distress and struck their enemies with deadly plagues. When the enemy rose to stir up hostility and planned to destroy the tender shoots of Eden, he intended to weigh out ten thousand talents of silver for the king's treasuries. But You forestalled him: You commanded Your lambs to give their shekels beforehand. You know the future and anticipate schemes, preparing the means to extinguish the flame before it ignites and appointing those marked for death to life. A heavy veil of distress fell upon them because of their earlier service; branches and vines were consigned to cutting, snares surrounded them on every side, but their eyes turned toward You, and they sheltered in Your secret refuge. The pur, the lot, turned against their enemies; the gallows was prepared to receive the Agagite. You destroyed the veil cast over the nations and overthrew the peoples' discord and their arrogance. 'Peace and truth' were written everywhere; salvation became a strong rock and fortress. The destroyer was destroyed and caught in his own net; the slanderer was swept away, eradicated and crushed. They made feasts and established them for generations; they instituted the reading of the Scripture, and Heaven affirmed what was enacted below. The book records why these days were established. You stretched forth Your hand to forgive those who sinned; You appointed the Jew and Hadassah to bring deliverance. Their merit endures forever, and remembrance of their glory remains for those who were saved. Be zealous for Your awesome and holy name; look upon Your vineyard, ravaged and trampled. Gather our dispersed ones and let a new song be raised to You; establish them and give them life through the rebuilding of the Holy House. As You performed awesome wonders in those days, so perform for us the wondrous and lasting salvation. May we find atonement and comfort before You, God and King enthroned upon the throne of mercy.
paragraphs.note: New English working translation reviewed against the Hebrew and available Russian text; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: God, the King, who sits upon a throne of mercy and acts with kindness, forgives the sins of His people, passing over each offense in turn. He grants abundant forgiveness to sinners and pardon to transgressors; He deals righteously with all flesh and spirit and does not repay them according to their wickedness. O God, You taught us to recite the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy. Remember for us today the covenant of the Thirteen Attributes, as You made them known to the humble one long ago. As it is written: The LORD descended in the cloud, stood with him there, and proclaimed the Name of the LORD.
And the LORD passed before him and proclaimed:

The LORD, the LORD, a compassionate and gracious God, slow to anger, abundant in kindness and truth; preserving kindness for thousands, forgiving iniquity, transgression and sin, and cleansing. Forgive our iniquity and our sin, and take us as Your inheritance. Forgive us, our Father, for we have sinned; pardon us, our King, for we have transgressed. For You, O Lord, are good and forgiving, and abundant in kindness to all who call upon You.
A refrain arranged in reverse alphabetical order; its closing acrostic gives the author's name as Meshullam.

Though few in number, we have entreated You. Do not turn Your ear away from the cry of the brokenhearted; hear their pleading from Your heavenly dwelling. As in the days of Mordecai and Esther, the myrrh and myrtle, save Your children. You are enthroned amid the praises of Israel; You heed their cry and listen to their song. You prepare the cure before the blow, and devise good for those You have acquired, to settle them once more in their homes.
paragraphs.note: New English working translation reviewed against the Hebrew and available Russian text; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: When: The adversary and enemy sharpened his gaze; he opened his mouth to devour His afflicted ones. He devised a plan to destroy their multitudes, and inscribed a decree to annihilate His treasured people.

When: You took vengeance on the oppressors and kept account of the enemies; You repaid them according to the measure they plotted against Your beloved ones. The warrior and his sons were hanged on the gallows, strung up together like fish on a line.
When: The enemies had hoped to bring slaughter upon the besieged people; the decree was reversed and their corpses fell. Struck with terror and wrath, they were defeated and cast down.

Then may Your name be exalted and raised on high; Your splendor covers the heavens of heavens. The lowly, while they praise You, are given over to plunder, though Your praise fills the valley and all its bounds.

Understanding, defend us now and behold our distress. Rise in Your anger against the narrow-hearted oppressor. Master, we call to You from the straits: bring us out into the open and deliver us from distress.
Multiply forgiveness for us exceedingly. Hear our prayer and remove what is unworthy. Let those who press us make peace with us, and cast our sins into the depths. Do not withhold Your mercy from us.
When shall I...

God, the King, who sits upon a throne of mercy and acts with kindness, forgives the sins of His people, passing over each offense in turn. He grants abundant forgiveness to sinners and pardon to transgressors; He deals righteously with all flesh and spirit and does not repay them according to their wickedness. O God, You taught us to recite the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy. Remember for us today the covenant of the Thirteen Attributes, as You made them known to the humble one long ago. As it is written: The LORD descended in the cloud, stood with him there, and proclaimed the Name of the LORD.
And the LORD passed before him and proclaimed:

The LORD, the LORD, a compassionate and gracious God, slow to anger, abundant in kindness and truth; preserving kindness for thousands, forgiving iniquity, transgression and sin, and cleansing. Forgive our iniquity and our sin, and take us as Your inheritance. Forgive us, our Father, for we have sinned; pardon us, our King, for we have transgressed. For You, O Lord, are good and forgiving, and abundant in kindness to all who call upon You.

Remember Your compassion, Lord, and Your loving-kindness, for they are everlasting. Remember us, Lord, with favor toward Your people; visit us with Your salvation. Remember Your congregation, which You acquired long ago, the tribe of Your inheritance which You redeemed—Mount Zion, where You dwelt. Remember, Lord, the love of Jerusalem; do not forget the love of Zion forever. You will arise and have mercy on Zion; for the time to favor her, the appointed time, has come. Remember, Lord, against the children of Edom the day of Jerusalem, when they said, 'Lay her bare, lay her bare, to her foundations!' Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel Your servants, to whom You swore by Yourself, saying You would multiply their descendants like the stars of heaven and give them the entire land as an eternal inheritance. Remember Your servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and do not regard this people's stubbornness, wickedness, or sin.
paragraphs.note: Identical Hebrew passage to ashkenaz Ten of Tevet paragraph 43; verify typography and liturgical placement.

paragraphs.text: Remember for us the covenant of the ancestors, as You said: 'I will remember My covenant with Jacob, and also My covenant with Isaac, and also My covenant with Abraham will I remember; and I will remember the land.'

Remember for us the covenant with those of old, as You said: 'I will remember for them the covenant with their ancestors whom I brought out of Egypt before the nations, to be their God; I am the Lord.' Treat us as You promised: 'Even when they are in their enemies’ land, I will not reject or abhor them to destroy them or break My covenant with them, for I am the Lord their God.' Restore our fortunes and have mercy upon us, as it is written: 'The Lord your God will restore your fortunes and have compassion on you and gather you again from all the peoples among whom He scattered you.' Gather our scattered ones, as it is written: 'Even if your dispersed are at the farthest edge of heaven, from there the Lord your God will gather you and take you.' Wipe away our transgressions like a cloud, as it is written: 'I have blotted out your transgressions like a cloud and your sins like a mist; return to Me, for I have redeemed you.' Erase our transgressions for Your own sake, as You said: 'I, I am He who blots out your transgressions for My own sake, and your sins I will not remember.' Make our sins white as snow and wool, as it is written: 'Come now, let us reason together, says the Lord: though your sins are scarlet, they shall be white as snow; though red like crimson, they shall become like wool.' Sprinkle pure water upon us and purify us, as it is written: 'I will sprinkle pure water upon you, and you shall be clean; from all your impurities and idols I will cleanse you.' Have mercy on us and do not destroy us, as it is written: 'For the Lord your God is a merciful God; He will not abandon or destroy you or forget His covenant with your ancestors, which He swore to them.' Circumcise our hearts to love Your name, as it is written: 'The Lord your God will circumcise your heart and the heart of your descendants to love the Lord your God with all your heart and soul, so that you may live.' Let us find You when we seek You, as it is written: 'You will seek the Lord your God from there, and find Him if you seek Him with all your heart and soul.' Bring us to Your holy mountain and gladden us in Your house of prayer, as it is written: 'I will bring them to My holy mountain and make them joyful in My house of prayer; their burnt offerings and sacrifices shall be accepted on My altar, for My house shall be called a house of prayer for all peoples.'
paragraphs.note: Identical Hebrew passage to ashkenaz Ten of Tevet paragraph 45; verify typography and liturgical placement.

paragraphs.text: Hear our voice, Lord our God; spare us and have mercy upon us, and receive our prayer with compassion and favor. Return us to You, Lord, and we shall return; renew our days as of old. Give ear to our words, Lord; understand our meditation. May the words of our mouths and the thoughts of our hearts be acceptable before You, Lord, our Rock and Redeemer. Do not cast us away from Your presence, nor take Your holy spirit from us. Do not cast us off in old age; when our strength fails, do not forsake us. Do not abandon us, Lord our God; do not be far from us. Show us a sign for good, that those who hate us may see it and be ashamed, for You, Lord, have helped and comforted us. For we hope in You, Lord; You will answer, Lord our God.
paragraphs.note: Identical Hebrew passage to ashkenaz Ten of Tevet paragraph 46; verify typography and liturgical placement.

paragraphs: Our God and God of our fathers, let our prayer come before you and do not ignore our supplication. For we are not so brazen-faced and stiff-necked to say to you, Adonoy, our God, and God of our fathers, We are righteous and have not sined. But, indeed, we and our fathers have sinned.

We have trespassed [against God and man, and we are devastated by our guilt]; We have betrayed [God and man, we have been ungrateful for the good done to us]; We have stolen; We have slandered. We have caused others to sin; We have caused others to commit sins for which they are called רְשָׁעִים, wicked; We have sinned with malicious intent; We have forcibly taken other’s possessions even though we paid for them; We have added falsehood upon falsehood; we have joined with evil individuals or groups. We have given harmful advice; We have deceived; We have mocked; We have rebelled against God and His Torah; We have caused God to be angry with us; We have turned away from God’s Torah; We have sinned deliberately; We have been negligent in our performance of the commandments; We have caused our friends grief; We have been stiff-necked, refusing to admit that the cause of our suffering is our own sins. We have committed sins for which we are called רָשָׁע [raising a hand to hit someone]. We have committed sins which are the result of moral corruption; We have committed sins which the Torah refers to as abominations; We have gone astray; We have led others astray.

paragraphs.text: We have turned away from Your commandments and Your good judgments, and it has not benefited us. Yet You are righteous in all that has come upon us, for You have acted faithfully while we have acted wickedly. We have done wrong and rebelled; therefore we have not been saved. Place in our hearts the resolve to abandon the way of wickedness and hasten salvation for us, as it is written through Your prophet: 'Let the wicked forsake his way and the unrighteous man his thoughts; let him return to the Lord, who will have compassion on him, and to our God, who will abundantly pardon.' Your righteous anointed one said before You: 'Who can discern errors? Clear me from hidden faults.' Cleanse us, Lord our God, from all our transgressions and purify us from all our defilements. Sprinkle clean water upon us and purify us, as it is written through Your prophet: 'I will sprinkle clean water upon you and you shall be clean; from all your impurities and from all your idols I will cleanse you.' Your people and inheritance hunger for Your goodness, thirst for Your kindness, and long for Your salvation. May they recognize and know that mercy and forgiveness belong to the Lord our God.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Your name is Merciful God; Your name is Gracious God. Your name is called upon us: Lord, act for the sake of Your name! Act for Your truth, Your covenant, Your greatness and splendor, Your teaching, Your majesty, Your promises, Your remembrance, Your kindness, Your goodness, Your unity, Your honor, Your instruction, Your kingship, Your eternity, Your mysteries, Your might, Your glory, Your righteousness, Your holiness, Your abundant mercies, Your Presence, and Your praise. Act for the sake of those who loved You and now dwell in the dust; for Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; for Moses and Aaron; for David and Solomon; for Jerusalem, Your holy city; for Zion, the dwelling of Your glory; for the desolation of Your Temple and the ruins of Your altar; for those killed because of Your holy name; for those slaughtered for affirming Your unity; for those who went through fire and water to sanctify Your name; for nursing infants who have not sinned; for weaned children who have not transgressed; and for the children who study in their teachers' houses. Act for Your own sake, if not for ours. Act for Your sake and save us.
paragraphs.note: Identical Hebrew passage to ashkenaz Ten of Tevet paragraph 51; verify typography and liturgical placement.

paragraphs.text: Answer us, Lord, answer us! Answer us, our God, our Father, our Creator, our Redeemer, our Seeker; answer us! Faithful God, ancient and kind, pure and upright, living and enduring, good and beneficent, knower of our nature, restrainer of anger, clothed in righteousness, King of kings of kings, awesome and exalted, forgiving and pardoning, answering in trouble, redeeming and rescuing, just and upright, near to those who call Him, compassionate and gracious, hearing the poor and supporting the innocent—answer us! God of our ancestors, God of Abraham, Fear of Isaac, Mighty One of Jacob, Helper of the tribes, Refuge of the mothers—answer us! Slow to anger, easily reconciled, answering in a time of favor, Father of orphans and Judge of widows—answer us!
paragraphs.note: Identical Hebrew passage to ashkenaz Ten of Tevet paragraph 52; verify typography and liturgical placement.

paragraphs.text: May He who answered Abraham our father on Mount Moriah answer us. May He who answered Isaac his son when bound upon the altar answer us. May He who answered Jacob at Beth-El answer us. May He who answered Joseph in prison answer us. May He who answered our ancestors at the Sea of Reeds answer us. May He who answered Moses at Horeb answer us. May He who answered Aaron with the incense pan answer us. May He who answered Phinehas when he stood up among the congregation answer us. May He who answered Joshua at Gilgal answer us. May He who answered Samuel at Mizpah answer us. May He who answered David and his son Solomon in Jerusalem answer us. May He who answered Elijah on Mount Carmel answer us. May He who answered Elisha at Jericho answer us. May He who answered Jonah in the belly of the great fish answer us. May He who answered Hezekiah king of Judah in his illness answer us. May He who answered Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah in the fiery furnace answer us. May He who answered Daniel in the lions' den answer us. May He who answered Mordecai and Esther in the capital Shushan answer us. May He who answered Ezra in exile answer us. May He who answered all the righteous, devout, blameless and upright answer us.
paragraphs.note: Identical Hebrew passage to ashkenaz Ten of Tevet paragraph 53; verify typography and liturgical placement.

paragraphs.text: Merciful One who answers the poor, answer us. Merciful One who answers the brokenhearted, answer us. Merciful One who answers the humble of spirit, answer us. Merciful One, answer us. Merciful One, have pity. Merciful One, redeem. Merciful One, deliver. Merciful One, have mercy upon us, now, speedily, and in a time soon to come.
Forgive us, our Father, for in our great folly we have erred; pardon us, our King, for our sins are many.

paragraphs: You are Almighty, Slow to anger; You are called the Lord of Mercy, and You have taught us the way of repentance. Remember the greatness of Your mercy and kindness, this day and every day, for the descendants of Your loved ones. Turn to us with compassion for You are the Lord of Mercy. We approach Your Presence with supplication and prayer, as You made known to [Moses,] the modest one of old. Turn from Your fierce anger, as it is written in Your Torah: May we be sheltered and lodged in the shadow of Your wings, as on the day [of which it is said:] When Adonoy descended in the cloud. Remove [our] transgression, and blot out [our] iniquity, as on the day [of which it is said:] And He stood with him there. Give ear to our cry and listen to our speech, as on the day [of which it is said:] And He proclaimed in the Name, Adonoy And there it is said:
And Adonoy passed before him [Moses] and proclaimed:

paragraphs.text: The LORD, the LORD, a compassionate and gracious God, slow to anger, abundant in kindness and truth; preserving kindness for thousands, forgiving iniquity, transgression and sin, and cleansing. Forgive our iniquity and our sin, and take us as Your inheritance. Forgive us, our Father, for we have sinned; pardon us, our King, for we have transgressed. For You, O Lord, are good and forgiving, and abundant in kindness to all who call upon You.

Give Him no rest until He establishes Jerusalem and makes it a praise throughout the earth. For with You is the fountain of life; in Your light we see light. Our God, we are ashamed of our deeds and confounded by our sins.

As a father has compassion on his children, so may the LORD have compassion on us. Salvation belongs to the LORD; may Your blessing rest on Your people, selah. The LORD of Hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge, selah. LORD of Hosts, happy is the one who trusts in You. LORD, save us; may the King answer us on the day we call.

paragraphs: When the Torah is unrolled, the Reader says:

paragraphs.text: Pardon, we pray, the iniquity of this people according to the greatness of Your kindness, as You have forgiven this people from Egypt until now; and there it says:
Congregation:
And the LORD said: ‘I have pardoned according to thy word.

O my God, incline Thine ear, and hear; open Thine eyes, and behold our desolations, and the city upon which Thy name is called; for we do not present our supplications before Thee because of our righteousness, but because of Thy great compassions. O Lord, hear, O Lord, forgive, O Lord, attend and do, defer not; for Thine own sake, O my God, because Thy name is called upon Thy city and Thy people.’
paragraphs.note: Every colon-delimited fragment matched a unique near-exact complete Tanakh verse; reviewed orthographic/qere alignment only.

paragraphs.text: A selichah arranged in alphabetical acrostic order.
Our God and God of our ancestors:

We have come to You, Creator of spirits. Because of our many sins our sighs are heavy, the decrees are severe and the cries are multiplied, for on the seventeenth of Tammuz the Tablets were shattered. We were banished from the Chosen House; our sentence was signed and the decree issued, and light grew dim for us, for on the seventeenth of Tammuz the Torah was burned. Enemies destroyed our Temple, the Divine Presence withdrew from its place, and we were handed to the arrogant for destruction, for on the seventeenth of Tammuz an idol was set up in the Temple. We were scattered from city to city, our great and small alike were taken captive; our city became desolate and fire was kindled within it, for on the seventeenth of Tammuz the city wall was breached. The destroying enemy arrogantly stepped into our Sanctuary; bridegroom and bride were stripped of their ornaments. Because we provoked You, we were given over to annihilation, for on the seventeenth of Tammuz the daily offering ceased. All our glory and splendor disappeared; the enemy drew his sword against us to destroy us, and infants and sucklings were doomed to slaughter, for on the seventeenth of Tammuz burnt offerings and sacrifices ceased. We rebelled against the One who dwells on high and so were scattered to every region; our dancing turned to mourning, for on the seventeenth of Tammuz the offerings ended. We stumbled before You amid quarrels of tongues and so our tongues learned laments. We were left uncounted, for on the seventeenth of Tammuz our sins brought this upon us. We are scattered and find no relief; our groaning therefore grows. Rock, look upon us: our souls have sunk down; turn the seventeenth of Tammuz into rejoicing and gladness for us. We stiffened our necks, and our afflictions multiplied; therefore we were delivered to plunder and trampling. Look, Lord, and rescue us from distress; turn the seventeenth of Tammuz into joy and celebration. Hear us, You who dwell on high; gather our scattered ones from the ends of the earth, say to Zion 'Arise!' and turn the seventeenth of Tammuz for us into a day of salvation and comfort.
paragraphs.note: New English working translation reviewed against the Hebrew and available Russian text; specialist proofreading pending.

And the LORD passed before him and proclaimed:

Forgive our iniquity and our sin, and take us as Your inheritance. Forgive us, our Father, for we have sinned; pardon us, our King, for we have transgressed. For You, O Lord, are good and forgiving, and abundant in kindness to all who call upon You.

O God, keep not Thou silence; Hold not Thy peace, and be not still, O God. For, lo, Thine enemies are in an uproar; And they that hate Thee have lifted up the head. O LORD, Thou God to whom vengeance belongeth, Thou God to whom vengeance belongeth, shine forth.

The LORD of Hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge, selah. LORD of Hosts, happy is the one who trusts in You. LORD, save us; may the King answer us on the day we call.
An alphabetical penitential prayer signed with the name Menachem son of Rabbi Machir.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Our God and God of our ancestors! I weep bitterly because of the hand stretched against my city. When I treated Him with contempt in His House, betraying Him and misusing consecrated things, the Divine Presence withdrew, departing by ten stages, and ascended to the seventh heaven. The enemy regarded me as prey, oppressed and burned me in the fourth month. The appointed time came to crush the young men; exhaustion and distress doubled that month, while even His dwelling was like women weeping for Tammuz. My sin made me my own enemy in the month of Tammuz. Five traps were laid—the five calamities told of in Scripture—and on the seventeenth they overcame me. I was ensnared like a hapless bride under a wedding canopy of peace and success: I did not even wait six hours for my Shepherd, and the Tablets were broken. From His hand I lost my ornament, bracelet and necklace; on the day of His anger the troubles poured upon me because I had corrupted my ways. I stopped fulfilling the order of His service and the established rites on the altar; therefore the continual offering from the chamber of lambs ceased. The city was destroyed and scattered, poor and tempest-tossed; Zion was left without a pilot and was broken like a ship. She suffered double punishment for her sin, sigh after sigh. Enemies multiplied, and on this very day the city wall was breached for the second time. She was driven out like a fleeing gazelle with no one to shelter her. Enemies sharpened their tongues and handed her over like a sheep to strip off her wool and fat. She cried out over the precious treasure with which she had been crowned: the joy of her eyes was taken when the wicked Apostomos burned the Torah. He insulted the oppressed and brokenhearted; the fool mocked them aloud. They were humbled and abandoned in the darkness of the hiding of the Face; the enemy's hand completed the abomination when an idol was erected in the Temple in a time of distress. The wounded and exhausted children, descendants of the ancients, have borne troubles for many years, one after another. Struck as though by bees and scorpions that sting repeatedly, they think: 'Our hope has perished; expectation has gone out in the darkness.' Jealous God, who restrains wrath before those who stir Your jealousy, we await Your restoration of the ancient foundations, like plantings rooted in love. May the promise of truth and peace concerning the fasts be fulfilled: may they become forever days of joy, gladness and good festivals.
paragraphs.note: New English working translation reviewed against the Hebrew and available Russian text; specialist proofreading pending.

A refrain whose poetic meter is a long syllable, two short syllables, a long syllable and two short syllables; the author's name is Solomon.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Hear the captive delivered into the hands of Babylon and also of Seir. For so long he has groaned and pleaded to You like a small child. On the day the enemy prevailed and the city wall was breached, I bent low and wrung my hands; on a day of five calamities I was scattered. Through the sin of the golden calf I was deprived of the Tablets; the enemy also ended the continual offering and imprisoned me. An idol was set up in the perfected Sanctuary and bereft me of counsel; the meal offering ceased, and the enemy burned Your Torah in the fire.
paragraphs.note: New English working translation reviewed against the Hebrew and available Russian text; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Day: I tremble and quake exceedingly on the day the Almighty thrust me away. A serpent from the north swept me away like a raging stream. The light darkened, and Babylon rolled me up like a ball. The hunter stretched forth his hand, the goat and the shaggy-haired enemy.
paragraphs.note: New English working translation reviewed against the Hebrew and available Russian text; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Day: Glory of my heart and my refuge! Will Your anger smolder forever? Do You not see the exhausted people, for whom dawn has become like a furnace? Repair my breach through the son of Perez; gather the lily from the thornbush. Rebuild the House of Your dwelling; restore the bounds of Carmel and Bashan. Open Your eye and exact vengeance from the enemy and Edom; judge the speechless one, and then the one who harmed and kindled the fire shall repay. On the day the enemy prevailed and the city wall was breached.
paragraphs.note: New English working translation reviewed against the Hebrew and available Russian text; specialist proofreading pending.

Remember Your servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and do not regard this people's stubbornness, wickedness, or sin.

paragraphs.text: Remember for us the covenant of the ancestors, as You said: 'I will remember My covenant with Jacob, and also My covenant with Isaac, and also My covenant with Abraham will I remember; and I will remember the land.'

Remember for us the covenant with those of old, as You said: 'I will remember for them the covenant with their ancestors whom I brought out of Egypt before the nations, to be their God; I am the Lord.' Treat us as You promised: 'Even when they are in their enemies’ land, I will not reject or abhor them to destroy them or break My covenant with them, for I am the Lord their God.' Restore our fortunes and have mercy upon us, as it is written: 'The Lord your God will restore your fortunes and have compassion on you and gather you again from all the peoples among whom He scattered you.' Gather our scattered ones, as it is written: 'Even if your dispersed are at the farthest edge of heaven, from there the Lord your God will gather you and take you.' Wipe away our transgressions like a cloud, as it is written: 'I have blotted out your transgressions like a cloud and your sins like a mist; return to Me, for I have redeemed you.' Erase our transgressions for Your own sake, as You said: 'I, I am He who blots out your transgressions for My own sake, and your sins I will not remember.' Make our sins white as snow and wool, as it is written: 'Come now, let us reason together, says the Lord: though your sins are scarlet, they shall be white as snow; though red like crimson, they shall become like wool.' Sprinkle pure water upon us and purify us, as it is written: 'I will sprinkle pure water upon you, and you shall be clean; from all your impurities and idols I will cleanse you.' Have mercy on us and do not destroy us, as it is written: 'For the Lord your God is a merciful God; He will not abandon or destroy you or forget His covenant with your ancestors, which He swore to them.' Circumcise our hearts to love Your name, as it is written: 'The Lord your God will circumcise your heart and the heart of your descendants to love the Lord your God with all your heart and soul, so that you may live.' Let us find You when we seek You, as it is written: 'You will seek the Lord your God from there, and find Him if you seek Him with all your heart and soul.' Bring us to Your holy mountain and gladden us in Your house of prayer, as it is written: 'I will bring them to My holy mountain and make them joyful in My house of prayer; their burnt offerings and sacrifices shall be accepted on My altar, for My house shall be called a house of prayer for all peoples.'
paragraphs.note: Identical Hebrew passage to ashkenaz Ten of Tevet paragraph 45; verify typography and liturgical placement.

paragraphs.text: Hear our voice, Lord our God; spare us and have mercy upon us, and receive our prayer with compassion and favor. Return us to You, Lord, and we shall return; renew our days as of old. Give ear to our words, Lord; understand our meditation. May the words of our mouths and the thoughts of our hearts be acceptable before You, Lord, our Rock and Redeemer. Do not cast us away from Your presence, nor take Your holy spirit from us. Do not cast us off in old age; when our strength fails, do not forsake us. Do not abandon us, Lord our God; do not be far from us. Show us a sign for good, that those who hate us may see it and be ashamed, for You, Lord, have helped and comforted us. For we hope in You, Lord; You will answer, Lord our God.
paragraphs.note: Identical Hebrew passage to ashkenaz Ten of Tevet paragraph 46; verify typography and liturgical placement.

paragraphs: Our God and God of our fathers, let our prayer come before you and do not ignore our supplication. For we are not so brazen-faced and stiff-necked to say to you, Adonoy, our God, and God of our fathers, We are righteous and have not sined. But, indeed, we and our fathers have sinned.

We have trespassed [against God and man, and we are devastated by our guilt]; We have betrayed [God and man, we have been ungrateful for the good done to us]; We have stolen; We have slandered. We have caused others to sin; We have caused others to commit sins for which they are called רְשָׁעִים, wicked; We have sinned with malicious intent; We have forcibly taken other’s possessions even though we paid for them; We have added falsehood upon falsehood; we have joined with evil individuals or groups. We have given harmful advice; We have deceived; We have mocked; We have rebelled against God and His Torah; We have caused God to be angry with us; We have turned away from God’s Torah; We have sinned deliberately; We have been negligent in our performance of the commandments; We have caused our friends grief; We have been stiff-necked, refusing to admit that the cause of our suffering is our own sins. We have committed sins for which we are called רָשָׁע [raising a hand to hit someone]. We have committed sins which are the result of moral corruption; We have committed sins which the Torah refers to as abominations; We have gone astray; We have led others astray.

paragraphs.text: We have turned away from Your commandments and Your good judgments, and it has not benefited us. Yet You are righteous in all that has come upon us, for You have acted faithfully while we have acted wickedly. We have done wrong and rebelled; therefore we have not been saved. Place in our hearts the resolve to abandon the way of wickedness and hasten salvation for us, as it is written through Your prophet: 'Let the wicked forsake his way and the unrighteous man his thoughts; let him return to the Lord, who will have compassion on him, and to our God, who will abundantly pardon.' Your righteous anointed one said before You: 'Who can discern errors? Clear me from hidden faults.' Cleanse us, Lord our God, from all our transgressions and purify us from all our defilements. Sprinkle clean water upon us and purify us, as it is written through Your prophet: 'I will sprinkle clean water upon you and you shall be clean; from all your impurities and from all your idols I will cleanse you.' Your people and inheritance hunger for Your goodness, thirst for Your kindness, and long for Your salvation. May they recognize and know that mercy and forgiveness belong to the Lord our God.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Your name is Merciful God; Your name is Gracious God. Your name is called upon us: Lord, act for the sake of Your name! Act for Your truth, Your covenant, Your greatness and splendor, Your teaching, Your majesty, Your promises, Your remembrance, Your kindness, Your goodness, Your unity, Your honor, Your instruction, Your kingship, Your eternity, Your mysteries, Your might, Your glory, Your righteousness, Your holiness, Your abundant mercies, Your Presence, and Your praise. Act for the sake of those who loved You and now dwell in the dust; for Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; for Moses and Aaron; for David and Solomon; for Jerusalem, Your holy city; for Zion, the dwelling of Your glory; for the desolation of Your Temple and the ruins of Your altar; for those killed because of Your holy name; for those slaughtered for affirming Your unity; for those who went through fire and water to sanctify Your name; for nursing infants who have not sinned; for weaned children who have not transgressed; and for the children who study in their teachers' houses. Act for Your own sake, if not for ours. Act for Your sake and save us.
paragraphs.note: Identical Hebrew passage to ashkenaz Ten of Tevet paragraph 51; verify typography and liturgical placement.

paragraphs.text: Answer us, Lord, answer us! Answer us, our God, our Father, our Creator, our Redeemer, our Seeker; answer us! Faithful God, ancient and kind, pure and upright, living and enduring, good and beneficent, knower of our nature, restrainer of anger, clothed in righteousness, King of kings of kings, awesome and exalted, forgiving and pardoning, answering in trouble, redeeming and rescuing, just and upright, near to those who call Him, compassionate and gracious, hearing the poor and supporting the innocent—answer us! God of our ancestors, God of Abraham, Fear of Isaac, Mighty One of Jacob, Helper of the tribes, Refuge of the mothers—answer us! Slow to anger, easily reconciled, answering in a time of favor, Father of orphans and Judge of widows—answer us!
paragraphs.note: Identical Hebrew passage to ashkenaz Ten of Tevet paragraph 52; verify typography and liturgical placement.

paragraphs.text: May He who answered Abraham our father on Mount Moriah answer us. May He who answered Isaac his son when bound upon the altar answer us. May He who answered Jacob at Beth-El answer us. May He who answered Joseph in prison answer us. May He who answered our ancestors at the Sea of Reeds answer us. May He who answered Moses at Horeb answer us. May He who answered Aaron with the incense pan answer us. May He who answered Phinehas when he stood up among the congregation answer us. May He who answered Joshua at Gilgal answer us. May He who answered Samuel at Mizpah answer us. May He who answered David and his son Solomon in Jerusalem answer us. May He who answered Elijah on Mount Carmel answer us. May He who answered Elisha at Jericho answer us. May He who answered Jonah in the belly of the great fish answer us. May He who answered Hezekiah king of Judah in his illness answer us. May He who answered Hananiah, Mishael and Azariah in the fiery furnace answer us. May He who answered Daniel in the lions' den answer us. May He who answered Mordecai and Esther in the capital Shushan answer us. May He who answered Ezra in exile answer us. May He who answered all the righteous, devout, blameless and upright answer us.
paragraphs.note: Identical Hebrew passage to ashkenaz Ten of Tevet paragraph 53; verify typography and liturgical placement.

paragraphs.text: Merciful One who answers the poor, answer us. Merciful One who answers the brokenhearted, answer us. Merciful One who answers the humble of spirit, answer us. Merciful One, answer us. Merciful One, have pity. Merciful One, redeem. Merciful One, deliver. Merciful One, have mercy upon us, now, speedily, and in a time soon to come.

A Prayer of the afflicted, when he fainteth, and poureth out his complaint before the LORD. O LORD, hear my prayer, and let my cry come unto Thee. Hide not Thy face from me in the day of my distress; incline Thine ear unto me; in the day when I call answer me speedily. For my days are consumed like smoke, and my bones are burned as a hearth. My heart is smitten like grass, and withered; for I forget to eat my bread. By reason of the voice of my sighing My bones cleave to my flesh. I am like a pelican of the wilderness; I am become as an owl of the waste places. I watch, and am become like a sparrow that is alone upon the housetop. Mine enemies taunt me all the day; they that are mad against me do curse by me. For I have eaten ashes like bread, and mingled my drink with weeping, Because of Thine indignation and Thy wrath; for Thou hast taken me up, and cast me away. My days are like a lengthening shadow; and I am withered like grass. But Thou, O LORD, sittest enthroned for ever; and Thy name is unto all generations. Thou wilt arise, and have compassion upon Zion; for it is time to be gracious unto her, for the appointed time is come. For Thy servants take pleasure in her stones, and love her dust. So the nations will fear the name of the LORD, and all the kings of the earth Thy glory; When the LORD hath built up Zion, when He hath appeared in His glory; When He hath regarded the prayer of the destitute, And hath not despised their prayer. This shall be written for the generation to come; And a people which shall be created shall praise the LORD. For He hath looked down from the height of His sanctuary; From heaven did the LORD behold the earth; To hear the groaning of the prisoner; To loose those that are appointed to death; That men may tell of the name of the LORD in Zion, And His praise in Jerusalem; . When the peoples are gathered together, And the kingdoms, to serve the LORD. He weakened my strength in the way; He shortened my days. I say: 'O my God, take me not away in the midst of my days, Thou whose years endure throughout all generations. Of old Thou didst lay the foundation of the earth; And the heavens are the work of Thy hands. They shall perish, but Thou shalt endure; Yea, all of them shall wax old like a garment; As a vesture shalt Thou change them, and they shall pass away; But Thou art the selfsame, And Thy years shall have no end.
paragraphs.note: Public-domain JPS 1917 English aligned with the original Hebrew; any liturgical instructions are supplied by the project.

paragraphs.text: This piyyut was composed by Rabbi Judah Aryeh of Modena; his name is hinted at the beginning of each stanza.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Let this day be weighed against all my sins, and may they be diminished like the waning moon; today alone let the tally of my merits grow and blossom like a flowering bud.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: My heart's willful sin is surely known to Him, along with the threads of my wrongs and the veil of my wickedness. I know the judgment due me in scorching fire, for evil and shame are what I have woven from my crimes, going day after day after my gain, fleeing like an ignorant child from the house of study.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Indeed I drag my sin along with cords of emptiness. I have come and stand before You, my God, seeking a cure for the bitter venom of the serpent's bite; grieving, sorrowful, dwelling in affliction as upon rough-hewn stone, with hand, mouth and eye bereft of taste and fragrance.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Behold, You gave Your people the New Moons as a time of atonement for every generation. Turn the accuser away from those You love; therefore I come before You with their supplications. From the day before, when the time approaches, I return as one who belongs here and no longer as a stranger.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: In Your great kindness, my King, rise up and have mercy on Zion our sanctuary. Restore the glory of Your dwelling place of rest, where we shall offer our New Moon burnt offerings. God, send forth the bearer of our crown, for our hearts long to see its light.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Day:

paragraphs: To Him Who grants victory, a Psalm of David May Adonoy answer you on the day of distress; May the Name of Jacob’s God fortify you. May He send your help from the Sanctuary, and support you from Zion. May He remember all your meal-offerings, and accept your burnt sacrifices, Selah. May He grant you what your heart desires, and fulfill all your plans. We will sing at Your deliverance, and in the Name of our God, raise our banners; May Adonoy fulfill all your wishes. Now I know that Adonoy has delivered His anointed one, He will answer him from His holy heavens with the mighty deliverance of His right hand. Some [rely] upon chariots and some upon horses, but as for us, upon the Name of Adonoy, our God, we call. They have bowed down and fallen, but we have risen and stand firm. Adonoy, deliver [us], the King will answer us on the day we call.

paragraphs.text: Order of the offerings: say Ashrei, Half Kaddish, and pray the Amidah. After the cantor's repetition, begin here:
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Come, let us return to the Lord, for He has torn and He will heal us; He has struck and He will bind us up. After two days He will revive us; on the third day He will raise us up, and we shall live before Him. Not because of our righteousness do we place our supplications before You, but because of Your great mercies. Lord, hear! Lord, forgive! Lord, listen and act! Do not delay, for Your own sake, my God, because Your name is called upon Your city and Your people.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Congregation and cantor: Return us to You, LORD, and we shall return; renew our days as of old.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Three times:

God, the King, who sits upon a throne of mercy and acts with kindness, forgives the sins of His people, passing over each offense in turn. He grants abundant forgiveness to sinners and pardon to transgressors; He deals righteously with all flesh and spirit and does not repay them according to their wickedness. O God, You taught us to recite the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy. Remember for us today the covenant of the Thirteen Attributes, as You made them known to the humble one long ago. As it is written: The LORD descended in the cloud, stood with him there, and proclaimed the Name of the LORD.
And the LORD passed before him and proclaimed:

The LORD, the LORD, a compassionate and gracious God, slow to anger, abundant in kindness and truth; preserving kindness for thousands, forgiving iniquity, transgression and sin, and cleansing. Forgive our iniquity and our sin, and take us as Your inheritance. Forgive us, our Father, for we have sinned; pardon us, our King, for we have transgressed. For You, O Lord, are good and forgiving, and abundant in kindness to all who call upon You.

Please, Lord God of heaven, may our prayer be set before You as incense; bring forth our righteousness as light and our judgment as the noonday. Give ear to our words, Lord; understand our meditation. Answer us when we call, God of our righteousness. As a father has compassion on his children, so have compassion on us, Lord. Deliverance belongs to the Lord; Your blessing is upon Your people, Selah. The Lord of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our stronghold, Selah. Lord of hosts, happy is the one who trusts in You. Lord, save! May the King answer us on the day we call.
paragraphs.note: Working English translation; liturgical proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Pardon, please, the sin of this people according to Your great kindness, as You have forgiven this people from Egypt until now. And there it is said:
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: And the LORD said: ‘I have pardoned according to thy word.

O my God, incline Thine ear, and hear; open Thine eyes, and behold our desolations, and the city upon which Thy name is called; for we do not present our supplications before Thee because of our righteousness, but because of Thy great compassions. O Lord, hear, O Lord, forgive, O Lord, attend and do, defer not; for Thine own sake, O my God, because Thy name is called upon Thy city and Thy people.’
paragraphs.note: Every colon-delimited fragment matched a unique near-exact complete Tanakh verse; reviewed orthographic/qere alignment only.

paragraphs.text: A penitential prayer by Rabbi Mordechai son of Shabbethai Arukh; his name is hinted at the beginning of each stanza.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Our God and God of our ancestors:
Cantor: Accept my uplifted hands as a worthy evening offering; let my prayer rise like incense before You, in sincerity and uprightness. When I call, answer me, my Rock, before the day has turned.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Congregation: As the children of Israel bring the meal offering.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Cantor: May the words of my mouth be a pleasing fragrance before You, Rock of Ages. Receive the small measure of my flesh and blood in this fast in place of sacrificial fat and blood, and accept the thoughts of my heart that I have arranged this day [variant: over these many days] as a sweet offering.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Congregation: Like the sin offering, the guilt offering and the meal offering.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Cantor: Seek out those who seek You today, and make Yourself available to them through the words of their lips. Look favorably on their standing and purify them as silver refined seven times; accept their words as a lamb, one of the flock out of two hundred.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Congregation: From Israel's gift, as a meal offering.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Cantor: Regard my supplication as a wholly offered burnt offering; contend with those who accuse me. Bring forth my vindication like the light before the sun sets and evening falls; let everyone pour out the heart like water in prayer.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Congregation: The one who brings an offering shall present his sacrifice to the LORD as a meal offering.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Cantor: Jeshurun, Your people, will sing Your lovingkindness with good instruction; incline Your ear to them and hear, open Your eyes, and see how good it is to shelter at the gates of Your mercy.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Congregation: And he took from what had come into his hand a gift.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Cantor: In Your great mercy, hear my words, LORD, and understand my meditation. If I have found favor in Your eyes, ancient God of refuge, take from my hand the offering I brought You in supplication.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Congregation: When the offering was brought up.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Cantor: Almighty, we cannot fully comprehend Your mighty power. You accepted alike the soul of the one who offered much and of the one who offered little, when he returned; only let his heart be directed to You as he brings his offering.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Congregation: This is the law of the meal offering.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Cantor: When my altar and sanctuary stood in their place and within their bounds, the goats chosen by lot brought atonement for us. But now, because of our guilt—if the LORD had desired to kill us...
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Congregation: He took no burnt offering or meal offering from our hands.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Cantor: Your people speak supplications and seek pardon with a bitter heart. See them standing upon the rampart and keeping watch, pleading before You at the hour of the evening offering and awaiting atonement.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Congregation: For he said: I shall appease him with the gift.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Cantor: Rebuild Jerusalem, Your city, and all its surrounding towns; open the prisons of the oppressed and bring them into freedom. May their offerings once again be pleasing to the LORD as in days of old, and may You turn back to them with favor.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Congregation: Yet to turn toward the afternoon meal offering.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Cantor: Extend Your hand again to gather the scattered of Israel; shepherd them as a flock and bring them to a good pasture. He shall sit as a refiner and purify the children of Israel like gold and silver.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Congregation and cantor: They shall bring a meal offering to the LORD.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

He grants abundant forgiveness to sinners and pardon to transgressors; He deals righteously with all flesh and spirit and does not repay them according to their wickedness. So shall we offer the prayers of our lips in place of bulls. Let our prayer be set before You like incense, and the lifting of our hands like the evening offering. paragraphs: When the Torah is unrolled, the Reader says:

paragraphs.text: God of all flesh, Your people tremble in awe of You, always standing watch and awaiting the time of the evening offering.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Congregation: For he said: I shall appease him with the gift.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Cantor: Refuse, refuse to listen to our accusers. Though they howl in tumult, God, be not swept away; if You should keep a record of sins, they are indeed numerous.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Congregation: From where can one yet turn to the afternoon offering?
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Cantor: Israel, Your people, believes in You. Though You pushed them away with Your left hand, draw them close with Your right; they have come to seek Your presence.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Congregation: And he took from what had come into his hand a gift.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Cantor: Those who arrange their cries repay the bulls with the offerings of their lips. Accept them and cast all their sins into the depths of the sea; may their speech and song be sweet before You.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Congregation: Like the sin offering, the burnt offering, and the meal offering.
Cantor: In remembrance of the bull within, the inner and outer goats, may our words find favor before You and may our offering be as pleasing as a lamb, one of the flock out of two hundred.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Congregation: From Israel's gift, as a meal offering.

paragraphs.text: Cantor: See how our strength has failed and the exalted ones have bowed down. The faithful have vanished, and so we speak with a heavy mouth and halting lips.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Congregation: And the children of Israel sent an offering by his hand.
Cantor: Refine the words of my lips like the spreading dawn. Answer me and heal Your ruined altar; may the smoothness of my tongue be pleasant like oil to the crushed.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Congregation: The burnt offering and the meal offering.
Cantor: Count their house of prayer, where their whispered pleas are poured out, as the place where the priests once cooked the sin offering and the guilt offering.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Congregation: And those who bake the meal offering.

Cantor: May the LORD command His kindness; restore me upright to the beauty of my dwelling. Renew the glory and splendor of the place of Your sanctuary. Then He will sit as a refiner and purify the children of Levi.

paragraphs.text: God, the King, who sits upon a throne of mercy and acts with kindness, forgives the sins of His people, passing over each offense in turn. He grants abundant forgiveness to sinners and pardon to transgressors; He deals righteously with all flesh and spirit and does not repay them according to their wickedness. O God, You taught us to recite the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy. Remember for us today the covenant of the Thirteen Attributes, as You made them known to the humble one long ago. As it is written: The LORD descended in the cloud, stood with him there, and proclaimed the Name of the LORD.
And the LORD passed before him and proclaimed:

The LORD, the LORD, a compassionate and gracious God, slow to anger, abundant in kindness and truth; preserving kindness for thousands, forgiving iniquity, transgression and sin, and cleansing. Forgive our iniquity and our sin, and take us as Your inheritance. Forgive us, our Father, for we have sinned; pardon us, our King, for we have transgressed. For You, O Lord, are good and forgiving, and abundant in kindness to all who call upon You.

The Lord is good to all, and His compassion rests upon all His works. The Lord is good to those who wait for Him, to the soul that seeks Him. It is good to wait quietly for the salvation of the Lord. Better to take refuge in the Lord than to trust in a human being; better to take refuge in the Lord than to trust in princes. The Lord is good and upright, therefore He teaches sinners the way. The Lord is a stronghold in the day of distress and knows those who take refuge in Him. He knows our frame; He remembers that we are dust. The Lord is good; His steadfast love endures for ever, and His faithfulness through all generations. As a father has compassion on his children, so have compassion on us, Lord. Deliverance belongs to the Lord; Your blessing is upon Your people, Selah. The Lord of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge, Selah. Lord of hosts, happy is the person who trusts in You. Lord, save! May the King answer us on the day we call.
paragraphs.note: Working English translation; liturgical proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Daughter of my people, do not fall silent or cease crying out; instead of burnt offerings and fire offerings, prepare earnest supplication. They shall present a meal offering to the LORD in righteousness.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: A faithful prince of God, foremost among the mighty patriarchs, rose early at dawn and appointed hour to stand and offer my entreaties, in place of the regular offering, seeking favor for my sacrifices. He believed in the LORD, and it was counted to him as righteousness: those who bring offerings in righteousness to the LORD.

His only one was granted favor at the age of one hundred; bound on the stone altar, at the approach of evening he obtained mercy, and God turned His face toward him. The evening continual offering was established to seek the favor of its Master, like a man taking handfuls of finely powdered fragrant incense, bringing offerings in righteousness to the LORD.

The praying dweller in tents who lodged in the honored place raised up abundant sacrificial portions on approaching the house of offerings. Where no offering can be brought, I shall arrange praises in their stead, for to do justice and righteousness is chosen by the LORD more than sacrifice: those who bring offerings in righteousness to the LORD.

I have fallen silent, deprived of the service of the priests. How can I sing in captivity, when my faithful Levites have been gathered away? Yet in all this I thank Yah, for He is exalted in judgment; shame of face is ours, and righteousness is Yours. Those who bring an offering to the Lord shall offer it in righteousness. In place of sacrificial portions, may my prayer appear before You as I recount in order the service of the ministers who entered each chamber of the Temple. May they hear the herald who proclaims the vision: “To you who fear My name, the sun of righteousness shall arise.” Those who bring an offering to the Lord shall offer it in righteousness.
paragraphs.note: Working English translation; liturgical proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: God, the King, who sits upon a throne of mercy and acts with kindness, forgives the sins of His people, passing over each offense in turn. He grants abundant forgiveness to sinners and pardon to transgressors; He deals righteously with all flesh and spirit and does not repay them according to their wickedness. O God, You taught us to recite the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy. Remember for us today the covenant of the Thirteen Attributes, as You made them known to the humble one long ago. As it is written: The LORD descended in the cloud, stood with him there, and proclaimed the Name of the LORD.
And the LORD passed before him and proclaimed:

The LORD, the LORD, a compassionate and gracious God, slow to anger, abundant in kindness and truth; preserving kindness for thousands, forgiving iniquity, transgression and sin, and cleansing. Forgive our iniquity and our sin, and take us as Your inheritance. Forgive us, our Father, for we have sinned; pardon us, our King, for we have transgressed. For You, O Lord, are good and forgiving, and abundant in kindness to all who call upon You.
Afterward recite ten invocations of 'Merciful One,' corresponding to the Ten Utterances and the Ten Commandments.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Prayer leader and congregation:

Merciful One, remember for us the covenant of Abraham the beloved, for the sake of “And the Lord passed by.” Merciful One, remember for us the covenant of Isaac who was bound, for the sake of “And the Lord passed by.” Merciful One, remember for us the covenant of Jacob the perfect, for the sake of “And the Lord passed by.” Merciful One, remember for us the merit of Joseph the righteous, for the sake of “And the Lord passed by.” Merciful One, remember for us the covenant of Moses the prophet, for the sake of “And the Lord passed by.” Merciful One, remember for us the covenant of Aaron the priest, for the sake of “And the Lord passed by.” Merciful One, remember for us the covenant of Phinehas the zealous, for the sake of “And the Lord passed by.” Merciful One, remember for us the covenant of David the anointed, for the sake of “And the Lord passed by.” Merciful One, remember for us the prayer of Solomon the king, for the sake of “And the Lord passed by.” Merciful One, turn from Your anger, and let us not return empty-handed from before You.
paragraphs.note: Working English translation; liturgical proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: God, the King, who sits upon a throne of mercy and acts with kindness, forgives the sins of His people, passing over each offense in turn. He grants abundant forgiveness to sinners and pardon to transgressors; He deals righteously with all flesh and spirit and does not repay them according to their wickedness. O God, You taught us to recite the Thirteen Attributes of Mercy. Remember for us today the covenant of the Thirteen Attributes, as You made them known to the humble one long ago. As it is written: The LORD descended in the cloud, stood with him there, and proclaimed the Name of the LORD.
And the LORD passed before him and proclaimed:

The LORD, the LORD, a compassionate and gracious God, slow to anger, abundant in kindness and truth; preserving kindness for thousands, forgiving iniquity, transgression and sin, and cleansing. Forgive our iniquity and our sin, and take us as Your inheritance. Forgive us, our Father, for we have sinned; pardon us, our King, for we have transgressed. For You, O Lord, are good and forgiving, and abundant in kindness to all who call upon You.

Our God and God of our fathers, do not bring us to destruction; hold back Your hand in judgment. When accusation comes before You, do not erase our name from Your record. When You approach to examine and chastise, let Your mercy precede Your anger. When You behold the poverty of our deeds, bring Your own righteousness near. Teach us when we cry to You; command our salvation through the intercessor. Restore the captivity of the tents of the innocent; see how their entrances lie desolate. Remember what You declared: the testimony shall not be forgotten from the mouth of his descendants. Unseal the sealed testimony; place Your secret among those You teach. The navel, the rounded bowl—may the mixed wine never be lacking. O Yah, acknowledge those who know You; cast down the people who do not know You. For You will return the captives to the stronghold, prisoners of hope.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed parallel passage from the existing English Siddur.

paragraphs.text: The Great Confession by our teacher Rabbenu Nissim, of blessed memory.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Master of the universe! Before anything else, I have no mouth with which to answer and no boldness to lift my head, for my iniquities are more than can be counted and my sins are more numerous than any reckoning. They weigh upon me more heavily than a crushing burden. I confess before You, Lord my God, with head and body bowed, my strength broken and my power weakened, with a shattered heart and a humbled spirit, bowing low, bending the knee and prostrating myself, in trembling, fear, shaking, quaking, confusion, reverence and awe. Before You, Lord my God, I name only a portion of my evil deeds, my ugly ways and my corrupt actions. They cannot all be spoken; I lack the strength to distinguish them, the courage to reveal them, the ability to tell them all and the worthiness to enumerate them. And to beg forgiveness, mercy and atonement for them—what am I, and what is my life? I am vanity and nothingness, a worm and dust, earth and ashes. I am ashamed of my sins and disgraced by my transgressions; I have no defense as I confess before You. My iniquity is great, too heavy to bear; my offenses cannot be numbered. I am ashamed and confounded like a thief caught in the act. Master of the universe! Were I to begin listing and explaining my sins in detail, time itself would come to an end before they did. For which shall I beg? For which shall I plead? Which shall I confess—every one together or each separately, those concealed or revealed, the first or the last, the new or the old, the hidden or the known, those I remember or those I have forgotten? I know of myself that I have neither Torah nor wisdom, knowledge nor understanding, righteousness nor uprightness, nor deeds of mercy. I am foolish and do not know, ignorant and do not understand, a robber rather than faithful, guilty rather than vindicated, wicked rather than righteous, evil rather than good. I have committed every kind of evil deed and grave transgression. If You judge me according to my deeds, woe to me, woe to me, alas for me and my soul! If You purify me as silver is refined in the furnace, nothing will remain of me: I am like straw before fire and dry wood before flames, like silver dross upon a potsherd, like utter vanity in which nothing enduring is found. With what shall I appear before You, and what healing shall I seek? I have been like a stubborn and rebellious son, like a servant who rises against his master, like a student who argues with his teacher. What You declared pure I defiled; what You declared impure I considered pure. What You permitted I forbade, and what You forbade I permitted. What You loved I hated, and what You hated I loved. Where You were lenient I became strict, and where You were strict I became lenient. Those whom You brought near I drove away, and those whom You kept distant I brought close. And yet it was not my intention to provoke You to anger; nevertheless, with shameless audacity I have come to request Your forgiveness. I made my face like the face of a dog, displayed brazenness like that of a harlot, and approached You with a disgraced face, as it is written: 'You had the forehead of a harlot; you refused to be ashamed.' Master of the universe! I do not pray and confess for myself alone, but for myself and Your congregations standing before You. Though I am unworthy and undeserving even to confess for myself, much less on behalf of others, it is nonetheless Your way to be slow to anger, Your attribute to turn wrath away, and Your custom to show mercy to Your creatures—especially to those who return to You, acknowledge their wrongdoing before You, forsake their transgressions, repent of them and do not conceal them. For it is written, 'Whoever covers his transgressions shall not prosper, but whoever confesses and forsakes them shall obtain mercy,' and shall deliver his soul from the judgment of Gehinnom. Master of the universe! The order of Your righteous judgment is not like the order of human courts. Among people, when one demands repayment from another before a court or judge, the defendant may escape payment by denying the debt, but by admitting it he becomes obligated to pay. Your righteous judgment is not so: if a person denies, woe to him and woe to his soul; but if he confesses and abandons the sin, You have mercy on him. Master of the universe! Were it not for our sins and transgressions, we would have nothing of which to be ashamed and nothing to confess; it is impossible to seek forgiveness for a sin one has not committed. The strength of Your mercy becomes manifest precisely when You remove sins from those who fear You. Nor do I confess for myself alone, but for myself and all Your congregation. May it be Your will, Lord our God and God of our fathers, to forgive and pardon us all our iniquities and transgressions, and to atone for all our sins.
paragraphs.note: New English working translation reviewed against the Hebrew and available Russian text; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs: Our God and God of our fathers, let our prayer come before you and do not ignore our supplication. For we are not so brazen-faced and stiff-necked to say to you, Adonoy, our God, and God of our fathers, We are righteous and have not sined. But, indeed, we and our fathers have sinned.

paragraphs.text: We have trespassed [against God and man, and we are devastated by our guilt]; We have betrayed [God and man, we have been ungrateful for the good done to us]; We have stolen; We have slandered. We have caused others to sin; We have caused others to commit sins for which they are called רְשָׁעִים, wicked; We have sinned with malicious intent; We have forcibly taken other’s possessions even though we paid for them; We have added falsehood upon falsehood; we have joined with evil individuals or groups. We have given harmful advice; We have deceived; We have mocked; We have rebelled against God and His Torah; We have caused God to be angry with us; We have turned away from God’s Torah; We have sinned deliberately; We have been negligent in our performance of the commandments; We have caused our friends grief; We have been stiff-necked, refusing to admit that the cause of our suffering is our own sins. We have committed sins for which we are called רָשָׁע [raising a hand to hit someone]. We have committed sins which are the result of moral corruption; We have committed sins which the Torah refers to as abominations; We have gone astray; We have led others astray. We have turned away from Your commandments and from Your good laws, and we have gained nothing from it. And You are the Righteous One in all [punishment] that has come upon us; for You have acted truthfully and we have acted wickedly.
paragraphs.note: Exact Hebrew match to a sequence of reviewed Siddur paragraphs; translations joined without fuzzy splitting.

paragraphs.text: We are more guilty than any people, ashamed more than any generation. Rejoicing has vanished from us and our hearts grieve because of our sins; our cherished possession has been destroyed and our beauty removed. The dwelling of our Holy Temple is laid waste because of our sins. Our fortress has become a wilderness, the beauty of our land has passed to strangers, our strength to foreigners. And still we have not turned back from our wandering. How shall we dare to lift our faces and stiffen our necks, saying before You, Lord our God and God of our ancestors, 'We are righteous and have not sinned'? No: we and our ancestors have sinned. Before our eyes they plundered our labor; all we treasured has been taken. They put their yoke on us and we carried it on our shoulders; servants ruled over us and there was none to rescue us from their hands. Many troubles surrounded us. We called to You, Lord our God, but because of our sins You distanced Yourself from us. We turned away from following You, strayed and were lost. And still we have not turned back from our wandering. How shall we dare to lift our faces and stiffen our necks, saying before You, Lord our God and God of our ancestors, 'We are righteous and have not sinned'? No: we and our ancestors have sinned.
paragraphs.note: New English working translation reviewed against the Hebrew and available Russian text; specialist proofreading pending.
