Once.
HEAR, O ISRAEL: THE LORD OUR GOD, THE LORD IS ONE.
Three times softly.
Blessed [is His] Name, Whose glorious kingdom is forever and ever.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur (deterministic preferred wording).

paragraphs.text: Seven times.
The LORD, He is God!
The LORD reigns; the LORD has reigned; the LORD shall reign forever and ever.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Answer us, God of Abraham, answer us. Answer us, Dread of Isaac, answer us. Answer us, Mighty One of Jacob, answer us. Answer us, Shield of David, answer us. Answer us, God of the divine chariot, answer us. Answer us, You who answer in a time of favor, answer us. Answer us, You who answer in distress, answer us. Answer us, You who answer in a time of mercy, answer us. Answer us, merciful and gracious One, answer us. Merciful One, answer us! Merciful One, redeem us! Merciful One, fill Yourself with compassion toward us, all the members of our household, and all our brothers and sisters of the house of Israel. Bring us out from darkness into light for the sake of Your great name.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Full Kaddish, Aleinu, and Mourner's Kaddish.

For the Leader; upon the Gittith. A Psalm of David. O LORD, our Lord, How glorious is Thy name in all the earth! Whose majesty is rehearsed above the heavens. Out of the mouth of babes and sucklings hast Thou founded strength, Because of Thine adversaries; That Thou mightest still the enemy and the avenger. When I behold Thy heavens, the work of Thy fingers, The moon and the stars, which Thou hast established; What is man, that Thou art mindful of him? And the son of man, that Thou thinkest of him? Yet Thou hast made him but little lower than the angels, And hast crowned him with glory and honour. Thou hast made him to have dominion over the works of Thy hands; Thou hast put all things under His feet: Sheep and oxen, all of them, Yea, and the beasts of the field; The fowl of the air, and the fish of the sea; Whatsoever passeth through the paths of the seas. O LORD, our Lord, How glorious is Thy name in all the earth!
paragraphs.note: Complete bundled Tanakh passage aligned at 99.68% normalized Hebrew similarity; only orthographic/punctuation variation accepted.

paragraphs.text: Forgive us, our Father, for in our great folly we have erred; pardon us, our King, for our sins are many.

paragraphs: You are Almighty, Slow to anger; You are called the Lord of Mercy, and You have taught us the way of repentance. Remember the greatness of Your mercy and kindness, this day and every day, for the descendants of Your loved ones. Turn to us with compassion for You are the Lord of Mercy. We approach Your Presence with supplication and prayer, as You made known to [Moses,] the modest one of old. Turn from Your fierce anger, as it is written in Your Torah: May we be sheltered and lodged in the shadow of Your wings, as on the day [of which it is said:] When Adonoy descended in the cloud. Remove [our] transgression, and blot out [our] iniquity, as on the day [of which it is said:] And He stood with him there. Give ear to our cry and listen to our speech, as on the day [of which it is said:] And He proclaimed in the Name, Adonoy And there it is said:
And Adonoy passed before him [Moses] and proclaimed:

paragraphs.text: The LORD, the LORD, a compassionate and gracious God, slow to anger, abundant in kindness and truth; preserving kindness for thousands, forgiving iniquity, transgression and sin, and cleansing. Forgive our iniquity and our sin, and take us as Your inheritance. Forgive us, our Father, for we have sinned; pardon us, our King, for we have transgressed. For You, O Lord, are good and forgiving, and abundant in kindness to all who call upon You.

paragraphs: Psalm 137 is recited before Birkas Hamazon on weekdays in memory of the destruction of the Beis Hamikdash:

By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat and we also wept, when we remembered Zion. Upon the willows in its midst, we hung our harps. For there our captors demanded of us words of song, and our tormentors asked of us [with] mirth; Sing to us from the song[s] of Zion. How shall we sing the song of Adonoy on alien soil? If I ever forget you, Jerusalem, may my right hand forget [its movement]. May my tongue cleave to my palate, if I remember you not; if I set not Jerusalem above my highest joy. Remember, Adonoy, to the sons of Edom the day of Jerusalem, [it was they] who said, Raze it, raze it to its very foundation. Daughter of Babylon, you are the annihilated one; fortunate is he who will repay you for all you have done to us. Fortunate is he who will take and dash your little ones against the rock.
Psalm 126 is recited on Shabbos, Yom Tov and other festive occasions such as weddings, circumcisions or redemption of the first born.

A Song of Ascents. When Adonoy brings about the return to Zion we will have been like dreamers. Then will our mouths be filled with laughter, and our tongue with joyous song. Then will they say among the nations: ‘Adonoy has done great things for them.’ Adonoy had done great things for us; we will [then] rejoice. Adonoy! bring back our exiles like springs in the desert. Those who sow in tears will reap with joyous song. [Though] he walks along weeping, carrying the bag of seed, he will return with joyous song carrying his sheaves.
When three or more males, aged 13 or older eat together one of them leads the group in reciting the Birkas Hamazon.
The leader begins by saying:
“Gentlemen, let us say the blessing:
The others respond:
The Name of Adonoy will be blessed from now forever.
The leader repeats:
“The Name of Adonoy will be blessed from now forever.”
The leader continues: (the words “our God” are substituted for “Him” and “He” if ten males are in the group):
“With your permission our masters and teachers, Let us bless (our God,) Him, for we have eaten of His bounty.”
The others respond accordingly:
Blessed is (our God) He for we have eaten of His bounty and through His goodness we live.
One who did not eat, responds:
Blessed is (our God) He, and His Name constantly, forever and ever.
The leader repeats:
“Blessed is (our God) He for we have eaten of His bounty and through His goodness we live.”
Some add: Blessed is He and blessed is His Name.
FIRST BERACHA

Blessed are You, Adonoy our God, King of the Universe, Who nourishes the entire world with His goodness, with favor, with kindness, and with mercy. He provides food for all flesh, for His kindness endures forever. And through His great goodness, we have never lacked and we will not lack food forever and ever, for the sake of His great Name. For He is Almighty Who nourishes and maintains all, does good to all, and prepares nourishment for all His creatures which He has created. Blessed are You, Adonoy Who nourishes all.
SECOND BERACHA

We thank You, Adonoy, our God, for Your parceling out as a heritage to our fathers, a land which is desirable, good, and spacious; for Your bringing us out, Adonoy, our God, from the land of Egypt, and redeeming us from the house of bondage; for Your covenant which You sealed in our flesh; for Your Torah which You taught us; for Your statutes which You made known to us; for the life, favor, and kindness which You granted us; and for the provision of food with which You nourish and maintain us constantly, every day, at all times and in every hour.

On regular weekdays, continue, “For everything”. On Chanukah and Purim add עַל הַנִּסִּים. If you forgot to say עַל הַנִּסִּים, you may include it when you reach הָרַחֲמָן by saying: הָרַחֲמָן הוּא יַעֲשֶׂה־לָּנוּ נִסִים וְנִפְלָאוֹת כְּמוֹ שֶׁעָשָׂה לַאֲבוֹתֵינוּ בַּיָּמִים הָהֵם בַּזְּמַן הַזֶּה. and then continue on Chanukah with: בִּימֵי מַתִּתְיָהוּ, and on Purim with: בִּימֵי מָרְדְּכַי וְאֶסְתֵּר. If you reminded yourself before concluding the second blessing עַל הָאָרֶץ וְעַל הַמָּזוֹן, you may repeat it at that time and continue with the Birkas Hamazon.

[We thank You] for the miracles for the redemption, for the mighty deeds, for the deliverances, for the wonders for the consolations and for the wars that You performed for our fathers in those days at this season.
On Chanukah:

In the days of Matisyahu, son of Yochanan the High Priest, the Hasmonean and his sons, when the evil Greek kingdom rose up against Your people Israel to make them forget Your Torah and to turn them away from the statutes of Your will— You, in Your abundant mercy, stood by them in their time of distress, You defended their cause, You judged their grievances, You avenged them. You delivered the mighty into the hands of the weak, many into the hands of the few, defiled people into the hands of the undefiled, the wicked into the hands of the righteous, and insolent [sinners] into the hands of diligent students of Your Torah. And You made Yourself a great and sanctified name in Your world. And for Your people, Israel, You performed a great deliverance and redemption unto this very day. Afterwards, Your sons entered the Holy of Holies of Your Abode, cleaned Your Temple, purified Your Sanctuary, and kindled lights in the Courtyards of Your Sanctuary, and designated these eight days of Chanukah to thank and praise Your great Name.
On Purim:

In the days of Mordechai and Esther in Shushan the Capital [of Persia], when the evil Haman rose up against them, he sought to destroy, to kill, and to annihilate all the Jews, young and old, infants and women, in one day, the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is the month of Adar, and to plunder their wealth And You, in Your abundant mercy, annulled his counsel, frustrated his intention, and brought his evil plan upon his own head, and they hanged him and his sons upon the gallows.

For everything Adonoy, our God, We thank You and bless You. Blessed be Your Name through the mouth of all the living, constantly, forever, as it is written: When You have eaten and are satisfied, You will bless Adonoy, your God, for the good land which He has given to you. Blessed are You, Adonoy, for the land and for the food.
THIRD BERACHA

Have compassion, Adonoy, our God, on Israel, Your people, on Jerusalem, Your city, on Zion, the dwelling place of Your glory, on the kingship of the house of David, Your anointed; and on the great and holy House upon which Your Name is called. Our God, our Father tend us, nourish us, maintain us, sustain us, relieve us and grant us relief Adonoy, our God, speedily from all our troubles. Adonoy, our God—may we never be in need of the gifts of men nor of their loans, but only of Your hand which is full, open, holy and generous, so that we may not be shamed nor humiliated forever and ever.
On regular weekdays, continue, “Rebuild”. On Shabbos add:

May it please You, to strengthen us Adonoy, our God, through Your commandments, and through the commandment of the seventh day, this great and holy Sabbath. For this day is great and holy before You, to refrain from work on it and to rest on it with love, as ordained by Your will. And by Your will, grant us repose Adonoy, our God, that there be no distress, sorrow, or sighing on the day of our rest. Show us Adonoy, our God, the consolation of Zion, Your city, and the rebuilding of Jerusalem, city of Your Sanctuary, for You are the Master of deliverance and the Master of consolation.
On Rosh Chodesh and Yom Tov add:

Our God and God of our fathers, may there ascend, come, and reach, appear, be desired, and heard, counted and recalled our remembrance and reckoning; the remembrance of our fathers; the remembrance of the Messiah the son of David, Your servant; the remembrance of Jerusalem, city of Your Sanctuary; and the remembrance of Your entire people, the House of Israel, before You for survival, for well-being, for favor, kindliness, compassion, for life and peace on this day of:
Rosh Chodesh
the Festival of Matzos

paragraphs.text: On Shavuot: 'this festival of Shavuot.'

paragraphs: the Festival of Sukkos
the Festival of Shmini Atseres
Remembrance

paragraphs.text: For children who eat on Yom Kippur, say: 'the Day of Atonement.'

paragraphs: Remember us Adonoy, our God, on this day for well-being; be mindful of us on this day for blessing, and deliver us for life. In accord with the promise of deliverance and compassion, spare us and favor us, have compassion on us and deliver us; for to You our eyes are directed because You are the Almighty Who is King, Gracious, and Merciful.

If you forgot to say רְצֵה or יַעֲלֶה וְיָבֹא and became aware of it before starting the fourth blessing (הַטּוֹב וְהַמֵּטִיב), or even if you are in doubt, see below for the appropriate blessing. If you reminded yourself after you had already begun the fourth blessing and have said: בָּרוּךְ אַתָּה ה', then you must repeat the entire Birkas Hamazon. These laws apply only to Shabbos, and the Festival days of Pesach, Shavuos and Sukkos. On Chol Ha-Moed or on Rosh Chodesh days that do not fall on Shabbos, you need not repeat the Birkas Hamazon even though you began the blessing of הַטּוֹב וְהַמֵּטִיב.
Rebuild Jerusalem, city of the Holy Sanctuary, speedily, in our days. Blessed are You, Adonoy, Builder of Jerusalem in His mercy. Amein.
FOURTH BERACHA

Blessed are You, Adonoy our God, King of the Universe, the Almighty, our Father, our King, our Mighty One, our Creator, our Redeemer, our Maker, our Holy One, Holy One of Jacob, our Shepherd, Shepherd of Israel, the King, Who is good and beneficent to all. Every single day He has done good, does good, and will do good to us. He has rewarded us, He rewards us, He will reward us forever with favor, kindness, and compassion, relief, rescue, and success, blessing, deliverance, and consolation, maintenance, sustenance, compassion, life, peace, and everything good; and of all good things may He never deprive us.
The Merciful One will reign over us forever and ever.
The Merciful One will be blessed in heaven and on earth.
The Merciful One will be praised for all generations, He will be glorified through us forever and for all eternity; and He will be honored through us for time everlasting.
May the Merciful One maintain us with honor.
The Merciful One will break the yoke (of oppression) from our necks and lead us upright to our land.
May the Merciful One send us abundant blessing to this house, and upon this table at which we have eaten.
The Merciful One will send us Elijah the prophet, who is remembered for good, who will announce to us good tidings, deliverances, and consolations.
When eating at your parents’ table, say:
May the Merciful One bless my father, my teacher, the master of this house, and my mother, my teacher, the mistress of this house; them, their household, their children and all that is theirs.
When eating at your own table, say:
May the Merciful One bless me, my spouse, my children, and all that is mine;

Ours and all that is ours— just as our forefathers were blessed— Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob— In all things, “From everything,” and “With everything”; so may He bless us, all of us together, with a perfect blessing and let us say Amein.
A guest says:

May it be God’s will that the host should not be shamed and not humiliated not in this world nor in the World to Come. And he will be successful with all his possessions. May his properties prosper and be located close to town. May no evil force have power over his endeavors. May no opportunity present itself before him any matter of sin, nor thought of iniquity from now forever.

From on high, may there be invoked upon them and upon us, [the] merit to insure peace, And may we receive a blessing from Adonoy, and kindness from the God of our deliverance; and may we find favor and understanding in the eyes of God and man.
On Shabbos say:
May the Merciful One let us inherit the day which will be completely Shabbos and rest, for life everlasting.
On Rosh Chodesh say:
May the Merciful One renew for us this month for good and for blessing.
On Yom Tov say:
May the Merciful One let us inherit that day which is completely good.
On Rosh Hashono say:
May the Merciful One renew for us this year for good and for blessing.
On Sukkos say:
May the Merciful One raise up for us the fallen Tabernacle of David.

May the Merciful One make us worthy of the days of the Messiah and life of the World to Come. He who gives great deliverance to His king, (On Shabbos and Yom Tov say: He who is a tower of deliverance to His king,) and shows kindness to His anointed— to David and his descendants forever. He Who makes peace in His high heavens may He make peace for us and for all Israel, and say, Amein.

Fear Adonoy, [you] His holy ones, for those who fear Him suffer no deprivation. Young lions may feel want and hunger, but those who seek Adonoy, will not be deprived of any good thing. Give thanks to Adonoy, for He is good, for His kindness endures forever. You open Your hand and satisfy the desire of every living being. Blessed is the man who trusts in Adonoy, so that Adonoy is his security. I was young and I have grown old, yet I have never seen a righteous man forsaken, nor his children begging for bread. Adonoy will give strength to His people, Adonoy will bless His people with peace.
The following blessings are said in the event you forgot to say רְצֵה or יַעֲלֶה וְיָבֹא and reminded yourself before starting the fourth blessing, הַטּוֹב וְהַמֵּטִיב.
If you forgot to say רְצֵה on Shabbos:
Blessed are You, Adonoy our God, King of the Universe, Who gave Shabbosos for rest to His people Israel with love for a sign and a covenant. Blessed are You Adonoy, Sanctifier of Shabbos.
If you forgot to say יַעֲלֶה וְיָבֹא on Rosh Chodesh:
Blessed are You, Adonoy King of the Universe, Who gave Rosh Chodesh days to His people Israel for remembrance.
If you forgot to say יַעֲלֶה וְיָבֹא on Yom Tov:

Blessed are You, Adonoy our God, King of the Universe, Who gave Yomim Tovim to His people Israel for happiness and joy, this day of (name the Yom Tov). Blessed are You, Adonoy, Sanctifier of Israel and the seasons.
If a Yom Tov occurs on Shabbos and you forgot to say רְצֵה and יַעֲלֶה וְיָבֹא:

Blessed are You, Adonoy our God, King of the Universe, Who gave Shabbosos for rest to His people Israel with love, for a sign and a covenant, and Yomim Tovim for happiness and joy, this day of (name the Yom Tov.) Blessed are You, Adonoy, Sanctifier of Shabbos, Israel, and the seasons.
If you forgot to say יַעֲלֶה וְיָבֹא on Rosh Hashanah:
Blessed are You, Adonoy our God, King of the Universe, Who gave Festivals to His people Israel for remembrance.
If Rosh Hashanah occurs on Shabbos and you forgot to say רְצֵה and יַעֲלֶה וְיָבֹא:

Blessed are You, Adonoy our God, King of the Universe, Who gave Shabbosos for rest to His people Israel, with love for a sign and a covenant, and Yomim Tovim to Israel, for remembrance. Blessed are You, Adonoy, Sanctifier of Shabbos, Israel, and the Day of Remembrance.

paragraphs.text: Blessings over fragrances.
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who creates fragrant spices.
Blessings upon seeing extraordinary sights.
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who makes the works of Creation.
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who made the great sea.
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who remembers the covenant, is faithful to His covenant, and fulfills His word.
Blessings upon hearing news.
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, whose power and might fill the world.
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who is good and does good.
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, the true Judge.
Blessing on seeing a rainbow: One who sees a rainbow should recite this blessing, but should not stare at the rainbow.
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who remembers the covenant, is faithful to His covenant, and fulfills His word.
For lightning and thunder:
The custom is to bless without mentioning Hashem's name
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: Blessed is He who makes the works of Creation.
On thunder one blesses
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: Blessed is He whose power and might fill the world.
Blessings for commandments.
The Torah commands the construction of a parapet. It must be at least ten handbreadths high and strong enough to lean against. Before fixing it in place, recite:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who has sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us to make a parapet.

It is a positive commandment from the Torah to affix a mezuzah. And one must affix it to the right of one walking in through the space of the opening, in the handbreadth adjacent to the outside, at the beginning of the highest third of the height of the entrance (going upwards). And it should be erect lengthwise. Before he affixes it, he should recite the blessing:
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who has sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us to affix a mezuzah.
After affixing the mezuzah, kiss it and say: 'This is the gate of the LORD; the righteous shall enter through it.'
One who acquires metal or glass utensils from a non-Jew, or from a Jew when the utensils were made by a non-Jew, must immerse them before use. Before immersing them, recite:

Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who has sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us concerning the immersion of utensils. When immersing a single utensil, say 'utensil' in the singular.
Blessing for separating challah:
The minimum quantity of dough that requires the separation of challah is stated here as 977 dirhams of flour by weight. Before separating, recite:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who has sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us to separate challah as a priestly gift.
Then take a small portion and say: 'This is challah.'
Redemption of a firstborn donkey: A male firstborn donkey must be redeemed from the priest, as it says, 'You shall redeem the firstborn of a donkey with a lamb.' Before redeeming it, say:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who has sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us concerning the redemption of the firstborn donkey.
And recite Shehecheyanu.
The blessing over trees: Whoever sees fruit trees in bloom during the month of Nissan says:
And let the graciousness of the Lord our God be upon us; Establish Thou also upon us the work of our hands; Yea, the work of our hands establish Thou it.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed near-exact Hebrew Tanakh alignment (psalms 90:17, similarity 0.959); orthographic/qere differences only.

paragraphs.text: Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who has left nothing lacking in His world and created beautiful creatures and fine trees for the enjoyment of humanity.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: May it be Your will, Lord our God and God of our ancestors, to lead us in peace, guide our steps in peace, direct our journey in peace, support us in peace and bring us to our destination in life, joy and peace. [If returning immediately, add: and bring us back in peace.] Deliver us from the hand of every enemy, ambusher, robber, or dangerous animal on the road, and from all calamities that threaten the world. Grant us favor, kindness and compassion in Your sight and in the eyes of all who see us, for You are a God who hears prayer and supplication. Blessed are You, Lord, who hears prayer.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs: For His angels He will command in your behalf, to guard you in all your ways. Adonoy will guard your going and coming from now, forever.

paragraphs.text: Jacob went on his way, and angels of God met him. When Jacob saw them, he said [initials of the names Raphael, Uriel and Michael]: 'This is God's camp'; and he named the place Mahanaim.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs: Adonoy bless you and guard you.
Adonoy shine His countenance upon you and be gracious unto you.
Adonoy turn His countenance toward you and grant you peace.
Exalted and sanctified be His great Name

in the world which He created according to His will and may He rule His kingdom. In your lifetime and in your days, and in the lifetime of the entire House of Israel, speedily and in the near future— and say Amein.

paragraphs.text: [Amen. May His great name be blessed forever and to all eternity.]

May His great name be blessed forever and to all eternity. Blessed, praised, glorified, exalted, elevated, honored, raised high and lauded be the name of the Holy One, blessed be He. Blessed be He. [Amen.]
paragraphs.note: Identical unpointed Hebrew source across sections.

paragraphs.text: Beyond every blessing, song, praise, and consolation uttered in the world; and let us say: Amen. [Amen]

Upon Israel and upon the rabbis, their disciples and all their disciples' disciples, and all who engage in Torah study in this holy place or any other place, may there be abundant peace, favor, kindness, compassion, long life, ample sustenance and redemption from their Father in heaven and earth; and say Amen.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed closely matching Hebrew wording in existing translated passage.

paragraphs.text: May abundant peace come from heaven, and life upon us and upon all Israel; and say: Amen.
He who makes peace in His heavens, may He make peace for us and for all Israel, and say: Amen. [Amen.]

Magnified and sanctified be His great name in the world destined to be renewed, when He will revive the dead, raise them to everlasting life, rebuild the city of Jerusalem and perfect His Temple within it, uproot foreign worship from the earth, and restore the worship of heaven to its place. May the Holy One, blessed be He, reign in His kingship and glory [alternative version: may His deliverance spring forth and His Messiah draw near] in your lifetimes and your days and in the lifetime of all the house of Israel, speedily and soon; and say: Amen.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs: May His great Name be blessed forever and for all eternity.

paragraphs.text: Blessed, praised, glorified, exalted, elevated, honored, raised high and lauded be the name of the Holy One, blessed be He; above (during the Ten Days of Repentance: far above) all blessings, songs, praises and consolations uttered in the world; and say Amen.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Upon Israel and upon the rabbis, their disciples and all their disciples' disciples, and all who engage in Torah study in this holy place or any other place, may there be abundant peace, favor, kindness, compassion, long life, ample sustenance and redemption from their Father in heaven and earth; and say Amen.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: May abundant peace come from heaven, and life and goodness upon us and upon all Israel; and say: Amen.
He Who makes peace (Ten Days of Penitence: the peace) in His high heavens may He, in His mercy, make peace for us and for all Israel, —and say Amein.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur (deterministic preferred wording).

paragraphs.text: Our Father in heaven:
Rock and Redeemer of Israel,
bless the State of Israel,
the beginning of the flowering of our redemption.
Shield it beneath the wings of Your kindness;
spread over it Your canopy of peace.
Send Your light and truth to its leaders, ministers, and advisers,
and direct them with good counsel from before You.
Strengthen the hands of the defenders of our holy land;
grant them, our God, deliverance,
and crown them with victory.
Bring peace to the land
and everlasting joy to its inhabitants.
And as for our brothers and sisters, the whole House of Israel,
remember them in all the lands where they are scattered;
lead them swiftly, upright, to Zion Your city
and Jerusalem, the dwelling place of Your name,
as is written in the Torah of Moses Your servant (Deuteronomy 30:4–6):
Even if those of you who are dispersed are at the ends of heaven,
from there the LORD your God will gather you, and from there He will take you.
The LORD your God will bring you into the land your ancestors possessed, and you shall possess it;
He will do good to you and multiply you more than your ancestors.
The LORD your God will circumcise your heart and the heart of your descendants,
so that you may love the LORD your God with all your heart and all your soul.
For the sake of your life.
Unite our hearts to love and revere Your name
and to keep all the words of Your Torah.
Send us speedily the son of David, Your righteous Messiah,
to redeem those who await the end of Your salvation.
Reveal Yourself in the splendor of Your mighty majesty
to all inhabitants of Your world and land;
may every creature with breath in its nostrils declare:
The LORD, God of Israel, is King,
and His kingship rules over all!
Amen, selah.
May the One who blessed our ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob
bless the soldiers of the Israel Defense Forces,
who stand guard over our land and the cities of our God,
from the border of Lebanon to the desert of Egypt,
and from the Mediterranean Sea to the approach of the Arabah, on land, in the air, and at sea.
May the LORD cause the enemies who rise against us to be defeated before them.
May the Holy One, blessed be He, guard and rescue our soldiers from every trouble and distress, injury and illness.
May He send blessing and success in all the work of their hands;
may He subdue those who hate us before them and crown them with salvation and victory.
May the following verse be fulfilled for them:
For the LORD your God is the One who goes with you to fight for you against your enemies and to save you.
And let us say: Amen.
Kedushah for the cantor during the repetition of the Amidah:
We will revere and sanctify You in the manner of the holy seraphim, who sanctify Your name in holiness, as it is written through Your prophet: 'And one called to another and said ...'
Congregation and prayer leader: Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of hosts; the whole earth is filled with His glory.
Cantor: His glory fills the world. His ministers ask one another, 'Where is the place of His glory?' In response they say: 'Blessed ...'
Congregation and prayer leader: Blessed is the glory of the LORD from His place.
Cantor: From His place may He turn in mercy and favor the people who proclaim His name as One evening and morning, every single day; twice with love they say: Hear, O Israel.
Congregation and cantor: Hear, O Israel, the LORD is our God, the LORD is One.
Cantor: He is our God, He is our Father, He is our King and our Savior. In His mercy He will again proclaim before all living beings: 'To be your God.'
Congregation and prayer leader: I am the LORD your God.
Prayer leader: And in Your holy words it is written, saying:
Congregation and prayer leader: The LORD shall reign forever; your God, O Zion, throughout all generations. Hallelujah!

Cantor: From generation to generation we will declare Your greatness; throughout eternity we will sanctify Your holiness. Praise of You, our God, shall never depart from our mouths, for You are a great and holy God and King.
Blessed are You, LORD, the holy God; during the Ten Days of Repentance say: the holy King.
The Ark is opened:

Cantor: I shall make my melodies sweet and weave songs, for my soul yearns for You. Congregation: My soul longs to shelter in the shadow of Your hand and learn every secret of Your hidden mysteries. Cantor: When I speak of Your glory, my heart stirs with love for You. Congregation: Therefore I shall speak of Your exalted things and honor Your name with songs of love. Cantor: I shall tell of Your glory though I have not seen You; I shall describe and name You though I have not known You. Congregation: Through Your prophets, in the secret council of Your servants, You revealed images of the splendor of Your majestic glory. Cantor: They described Your greatness and strength according to the power of Your deeds. Congregation: They likened You not to Your essence but to Your acts. Cantor: They pictured You in a multitude of visions, though You are One in every image. Congregation: They beheld You both as an elder and as a young man, the hair of Your head both white and black. Cantor: As an elder on the day of judgment, as a young man on the day of battle, like a warrior skilled in war. Congregation: A helmet of salvation is upon His head; His right hand and holy arm brought Him victory. Cantor: His head is filled with the dew of light, His locks with drops of night. Congregation: He glorifies Himself through me, for He has desired me; He shall be a crown of beauty for me. Cantor: Pure gold, the finest gold, is the image of His head; on His forehead is inscribed the glory of His holy name. Congregation: For kindness and honor, for beauty and splendor, His people crowned Him with a diadem. Cantor: The tresses of His head are like those of youth, His curls are black. Congregation: The abode of righteousness is the beauty of His glory; may it rise above His joyful head. Cantor: May His chosen people be a crown and royal turban in His hand, a diadem of splendor. Congregation: Those whom He carries, He exalted with a crown and honored, because they are precious in His eyes. Cantor: His glory rests on me and my glory rests on Him; He is near to me when I call to Him. Congregation: White and ruddy, His clothing is red as He strides forth from Edom, treading the winepress. Cantor: He showed the knot of the tefillin to the humble one, and the likeness of the Lord was before his eyes. Congregation: He delights in His people, adorns the humble with salvation, and dwells amid their praises to be glorified. Cantor: The beginning of Your word is truth, proclaimed from the beginning; remember from generation to generation the people who seek You. Congregation: May my many songs be placed before You, and may my rejoicing draw near to You. Cantor: Let my praise be a crown upon Your head and my prayer rise like incense. Congregation: May the song of the poor be precious in Your eyes like the song sung at Your sacrifices. Cantor: May my blessing rise to the head of the One who sustains, who forms and creates, the mighty Righteous One. Congregation: In response to my blessing incline Your head to me and receive it like the finest fragrances. Cantor: May my words about You be pleasing to You, for my soul longs for You.
paragraphs.note: New English working translation reviewed against the Hebrew and available Russian text; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: This day is more honored than all other days, for on it the Rock of all worlds rested.
Six days shall you do your work,
but the seventh day is for your God;
on the Sabbath you shall do no work,
for He made everything in six days.
This day is more honored than all other days, for on it the Rock of all worlds rested.
It is the first among holy convocations,
a day of complete rest, a holy Sabbath;
therefore everyone sanctifies it over wine,
and the faithful break two loaves.
This day is more honored than all other days, for on it the Rock of all worlds rested.
Eat rich foods and drink sweet beverages,
for God gives to all who cling to Him
clothing to wear and a daily portion of bread,
meat, fish, and every delicacy.
This day is more honored than all other days, for on it the Rock of all worlds rested.
You shall lack nothing on it (variant wording) and you shall eat,
be satisfied, and bless
the LORD your God, who has loved you,
for He has blessed you above all nations.
This day is more honored than all other days, for on it the Rock of all worlds rested.
The heavens recount His glory,
and the earth, too, is full of His kindness.
See that His hand has made all these things,
for He is the Rock whose work is perfect.
This day is more honored than all other days, for on it the Rock of all worlds rested.
Author: Rabbi Yisrael the Convert, a righteous convert of the twelfth century.
The Sabbath day must never be forgotten;
its remembrance is like a pleasing fragrance.
On it the dove found rest,
and there those weary from their toil shall rest.
The dove found rest on it; there the weary find repose.
This day is honored by the faithful,
fathers and children who take care to observe it.
It is engraved on the two tablets of stone
by the One of great strength and mighty power.
The dove found rest on it; there the weary find repose.
They all entered the covenant together;
as one they said, 'We will do and we will hear.'
They opened their mouths and answered, 'The LORD is One.'
Blessed is He who gives strength to the weary.
The dove found rest on it; there the weary find repose.
He spoke in holiness on Mount Moriah:
'Remember and observe the seventh day.'
Fulfill all His precepts together;
strengthen your loins and summon courage.
The dove found rest on it; there the weary find repose.
May He remember the people who wandered like lost sheep
and attend to them by covenant and oath,
so that no evil befalls them,
as You swore at the waters of Noah.
The dove found rest on it; there the weary find repose.
Author: Rabbi Judah Halevi.
Keep My Sabbaths,
so that you may draw sustenance and be satisfied by the radiance of My blessings.
For you have entered into rest;
borrow on My account, My children, and delight in My delicacies.
Today is a Shabbat unto the LORD.
Proclaim freedom to the weary,
and I shall bestow My blessing.
Join one to another,
to celebrate the day of My gladness.
Wear garments of fine linen and scarlet,
and learn from My elders.
Today is Shabbat dedicated to the LORD; borrow on My account...
Make haste with the portion,
to carry out Esther's command;
and settle accounts with the One who acquired you,
to pay, to eat, and to leave something over.
Trust, My faithful ones,
and drink wine from My abundance.
Today is Shabbat dedicated to the LORD; borrow on My account...
Behold, this is a day of redemption:
if you observe the Sabbath,
you will be My treasured possession.
Stay overnight and only then depart,
and you will live in My presence
and fulfill what I have stored up.
Today is Shabbat dedicated to the LORD; borrow on My account...
Strengthen My city,
O God, Most High;
restore My dwelling,
amid joy and contemplation.
There My singers will sing,
My Levites and My priests;
and then you shall delight in the LORD.
Today is Shabbat dedicated to the LORD; borrow on My account...
Kedushah during the reader's repetition of the Amidah:
We shall sanctify Your name in the world just as the angels sanctify it in the highest heavens, as written by Your prophet:
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: And one called to another and said:
Congregation and prayer leader: Holy, holy, holy is the LORD of hosts; the whole earth is filled with His glory.
Prayer leader: Facing them, they say: Blessed...
Congregation and prayer leader: Blessed is the glory of the LORD from His place.
Prayer leader: And in Your holy words it is written, saying:
Congregation and prayer leader: The LORD shall reign forever; your God, O Zion, throughout all generations. Hallelujah!

Cantor: From generation to generation we shall proclaim Your greatness, and for all eternity we shall sanctify Your holiness. May praise of You, our God, never depart from our lips, for You are a great and holy God and King.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Blessed are You, LORD, the holy God (during the Ten Days of Repentance: the Holy King).

LORD our God, favor Your people Israel and heed their prayers. Restore the Temple service to the innermost sanctuary of Your House; receive the fire-offerings of Israel and their prayers lovingly and willingly, and may the worship of Your people Israel always be acceptable to You.
May our eyes behold Your merciful return to Zion.
Blessed are You, LORD, who restores His Presence to Zion.

We are thankful to You that You Adonoy are our God and the God of our fathers forever; Rock of our lives, You are the Shield of our deliverance in every generation. We will give thanks to You and recount Your praise, for our lives which are committed into Your hand, and for our souls which are entrusted to You, and for Your miracles of every day with us, and for Your wonders and benefactions at all times— evening, morning and noon. (You are) The Beneficent One— for Your compassion is never withheld; And (You are) the Merciful One— for Your kindliness never ceases; we have always placed our hope in You.
paragraphs.note: Previously translated paragraph, Hebrew similarity 99.6%: source and target independently present in source corpus.

paragraphs.text: Modim of the Rabbis:

We are thankful to You, that You Adonoy are our God, and God of our fathers, God of all flesh, Our Creator, Creator of the Beginning. Blessings and thanksgivings to Your great and holy Name for keeping us alive, and sustaining us; so may You always keep us alive and sustain us, and gather our exiles to the Courtyards of Your Sanctuary to observe Your statutes, and to do Your will, and to serve You wholeheartedly, for we are thankful to You. Blessed is the Almighty to Whom all thanks are due.
paragraphs.note: Previously translated paragraph, Hebrew similarity 99.3%: source and target independently present in source corpus.

paragraphs.text: For all of these, may Your name, our King, be blessed, exalted and raised on high always, forever and ever.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: All the living shall thank You forever and praise and bless Your name in truth, O God of our salvation and our help, Selah.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Blessed are You, LORD; Your Name is good, and it is fitting to give You thanks.

LORD our God, favor Your people Israel and heed their prayers. Restore the Temple service to the innermost sanctuary of Your House; receive the fire-offerings of Israel and their prayers lovingly and willingly, and may the worship of Your people Israel always be acceptable to You.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: In the cantor's repetition, add VeTe'erav ('May it be pleasing') here:
May our eyes behold Your merciful return to Zion.
Blessed are You, LORD, who restores His Presence to Zion.

We give thanks to You, for You are the Lord our God and the God of our ancestors forever and ever, the Rock of our lives and Shield of our salvation. From generation to generation we will thank You and recount Your praise: for our lives entrusted into Your hand, for our souls placed in Your care, and for Your miracles with us every day, and Your wonders and goodness at every moment—at evening, morning, and noon.
paragraphs.note: Original English working translation aligned to the full Hebrew paragraph; specialist review pending.

paragraphs.text: The Good One, for Your mercies have never ceased; the Merciful One, for Your kindnesses have never ended. In You we have always placed our hope.
Modim of the Rabbis:

We are thankful to You, that You Adonoy are our God, and God of our fathers, God of all flesh, Our Creator, Creator of the Beginning. Blessings and thanksgivings to Your great and holy Name for keeping us alive, and sustaining us; so may You always keep us alive and sustain us, and gather our exiles to the Courtyards of Your Sanctuary to observe Your statutes, and to do Your will, and to serve You wholeheartedly, for we are thankful to You. Blessed is the Almighty to Whom all thanks are due.
paragraphs.note: Previously translated paragraph, Hebrew similarity 98.8%: source and target independently present in source corpus.

paragraphs.text: For all this, may Your name, our King, be blessed, exalted and raised high continually, forever and ever.
All living beings will thank You forever and praise Your name in truth, O God of our salvation and our help, forever.
Blessed are You, LORD; Your Name is good, and it is fitting to give You thanks.

Be seated, be seated, exalted guests! Be seated, be seated, holy guests! Be seated, be seated, guests of faith! Fortunate is Israel's portion, as it is written: 'For the LORD's portion is His people; Jacob is the measure of His inheritance.'
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: May it be Your will, Lord my God and God of my ancestors, that Your Presence dwell among us and that You spread over us the sukkah of Your peace, through the merit of the commandment of sukkah that we fulfill, to unite the name of the Holy One, blessed be He, with His Presence in awe and love, joining Yod–Heh with Vav–Heh in complete unity for the sake of all Israel. Surround them with the radiance of Your holy and pure glory, spread above their heads as an eagle stirs its nest; from there may a current of life flow to Your servant, son of [name], and to Your maidservant. Through the merit of leaving my house to go outdoors and running in the path of Your commandments, may this be accounted to me as though I had gone into exile. Wash me thoroughly of my iniquity and cleanse me of my sin. For the sake of the supernal guests, the guests of faith, let Your ears attend to abundant blessings; provide the hungry and thirsty with reliable bread and water. Grant me the merit to sit and shelter in the secret shadow of Your wings at the hour I leave this world, and to find cover from the storm and rain when You rain snares upon the wicked. May this commandment of sukkah that I fulfill be reckoned as though I had carried it out with every detail, refinement and requirement, and all the commandments dependent on it. Grant us a good final sealing [of judgment] and allow us to live many days in the Holy Land, serving You and standing in awe before You. Blessed is the Lord forever. Amen and amen.

paragraphs.text: On the first night, when entering the sukkah before sitting down to eat, and every day before the meal, say the following:
I invite to my meal the exalted guests: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, Aaron, Joseph, and David.
On the first day, say:
I ask you, Abraham, my exalted guest, to sit with me; and with you, all the exalted guests: Isaac, Jacob, Moses, Aaron, Joseph, and David.
On the second day, say:
I ask you, Isaac, my exalted guest, to sit with me; and with you, all the exalted guests: Abraham, Jacob, Moses, Aaron, Joseph, and David.
On the third day, say:
I ask you, Jacob, my exalted guest, to sit with me; and with you, all the exalted guests: Abraham, Isaac, Moses, Aaron, Joseph, and David.
On the fourth day, say:
I ask you, Moses, my exalted guest, to sit with me; and with you, all the exalted guests: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Aaron, Joseph, and David.
On the fifth day, say:
I ask you, Aaron, my exalted guest, to sit with me; and with you, all the exalted guests: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, Joseph, and David.
On the sixth day, say:
I ask you, Joseph, my exalted guest, to sit with me; and with you, all the exalted guests: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, Aaron, and David.
On the seventh day, say:
I ask you, David, my exalted guest, to sit with me; and with you, all the exalted guests: Abraham, Isaac, Jacob, Moses, Aaron, and Joseph.
For Your sake, our God, save us, we pray! For Your sake, our Creator, save us, we pray!
For Your sake, our Redeemer, save us, we pray! For Your sake, O One who seeks us, save us, we pray!
A people guarded like the apple of Your eye,
Who reflects on the Torah that restores the soul,
Who completes the study of the laws of Shabbat,
Who seeks the obligation of Shabbat,
Who establishes the two-thousand-cubit Sabbath boundary,
And refrains from journeying on Shabbat,
Who observes “Remember” and “Guard” on Shabbat,
Who hastens to welcome the arrival of Shabbat,
Who prepares throughout the six days for Shabbat,
Who sits and waits until the Sabbath ends,
Who calls Shabbat a day of honor and delight,
Who changes garments and clothing for Shabbat,
Who prepares food and drink for Shabbat,
Who makes the Sabbath pleasant with delicacies,
Who observes the three Sabbath meals,
Who breaks bread over two loaves on Shabbat,
Who sets forth the four domains on Shabbat,
Who lights a lamp as commanded in honor of Shabbat,
Who recites the sanctification of the day on Shabbat,
Who prays the seven blessings on Shabbat,
Who calls seven people to the Torah according to the law on Shabbat,
Grant her inheritance in the day that is entirely Shabbat.
Save us, we pray!

Ani VaHo, please save us! As You saved Adam, the work of Your hands, sheltering him and granting him atonement and favor on the holy Shabbat; as You saved the marked people who awaited freedom, giving them understanding to choose the seventh day for rest; as You saved the people whom You led like a flock, setting for them a statute at Marah beside still waters; as You saved those You fed in the wilderness of Sin, who understood and gathered a double portion of bread on the sixth day; as You saved those You nurtured and taught to prepare, and showed them their Shepherd; as You saved those sustained by the delight of the preserved manna, whose appearance and fragrance did not change; as You saved those who completed the laws of Shabbat burdens and observed rest, domains and boundaries; as You saved those who heard the fourth commandment at Sinai—'Remember' and 'Keep'—to sanctify the seventh day; as You saved those commanded to circle Jericho seven times and besiege it even on Shabbat until it fell; as You saved Kohelet and his people in the everlasting House, celebrating seven days and another seven; as You saved those who returned from exile to redemption, reading Your Torah at the festival day after day; as You saved those gladdened by the renewed building of the Second Temple, who carried the lulav on all seven days in the Sanctuary; as You saved those who beat the willow even when it overrode Shabbat, bringing tall branches from Motza and setting them by the base of the altar; as You saved those who blessed the high branches and rejoiced with them and, as they departed, sang of Your beauty; as You saved those who give thanks and hope without wavering: We belong wholly to the Lord, and our eyes turn again toward the Lord; as You saved the people of the vineyard You planted, who circle with fresh greenery and cry 'Ani VaHo, please save us!'; as You saved the company of swift ministers serving on the day of rest when the Shabbat offering is doubled, the burnt offering and the meal offering; as You saved the Levites on their platform, who increased their song and recited 'A Psalm, a Song for the Sabbath Day'; as You saved those You comfort, who delight always in Your commandments: favor them and strengthen them, for in returning and resting they shall be saved; as You saved the returning tribes of Jacob: bring back and restore the captivity of Jacob's tents, please save us! As You saved those who observe the commandments and wait for salvation, O God of salvation, please save us!

paragraphs.text: Save Your people and bless Your heritage; shepherd them and carry them forever. May these words with which I have pleaded before the LORD be near the LORD our God day and night, that He may uphold the cause of His servant and His people Israel as each day requires, so that all the peoples of the earth may know that the LORD is God, and there is none else.
Full Kaddish.
For Your sake, our God, save us, we pray! For Your sake, our Creator, save us, we pray!
For Your sake, our Redeemer, save us, we pray! For Your sake, O One who seeks us, save us, we pray!

For the sake of Your truth; for Your covenant; for Your greatness and splendor; for Your law; for Your majesty; for Your promise; for Your remembrance; for Your kindness; for Your goodness; for Your unity; for Your glory; for Your instruction; for Your kingship; for Your eternity; for Your secret counsel; for Your might; for Your beauty; for Your righteousness; for Your holiness; for Your abundant mercies; for Your Divine Presence—save us, please! For the sake of Your praise—save us, please!

paragraphs.text: Ani va-Ho, save us, we pray.
As You saved the mighty ones in Lod among Your people, when You went forth to save Your people, so save us now, we pray.
As You saved the people who sought God's deliverance, so save us now, we pray.
As You saved the multitude of hosts, and with them the angels of the heavenly hosts, so save us now, we pray.
As You saved the pure ones from the house of bondage, when they were in the hands of their oppressors, O Gracious One, so save us now, we pray.
As You saved those submerged in the depths of the divided waters, while Your glory passed with them, so save us now, we pray.
As You saved the singing one, like a reed, so that he was rescued, and saved her whose source was marked out, so save us now, we beseech You.
As You saved through Your promise, 'I will bring you out,' and Your declared promise, 'I will bring you with Me,' so save us now, we pray.
As You saved those who circled the altar, bearing willow branches to encircle the altar, so save us now, we pray.

As You saved the congregations exiled to Babylon, sending forth Your mercy for their sake, so save us now, we pray.
As You saved the captive tribes of Jacob, so return once more and restore the captives of Jacob's tents; save us now, we pray.
As You saved those who keep the commandments and await deliverance, O God of salvation, save us now, we pray!
Ani va-Ho, save us, we pray.

I arrange my plea in the house of my supplication; in fasting I laid bare my wrongdoing. I sought You there to save me. Hear the voice of my cry; arise and save me. Remember and have mercy, my Savior; living God, delight in me again. In my groaning, hear my supplication; hasten, my Savior. Bring to an end those who condemn me so that I may be condemned no more. Hasten, God of my salvation, to save me for ever. Bear away the guilt of my wickedness and pass over my transgression. Turn toward me to save me, righteous Rock, my Savior. Accept my cry and exalt the horn of my deliverance. Almighty Savior, save us, please! Appear and save me; save us, please!

paragraphs.text: When it falls on Thursday:

The people of whom it is said, “I am a wall,” clear as the sun, exiled and rejected, likened to the palm tree, slain for Your sake and counted as sheep for slaughter; scattered among those who provoke her, yet embraced and attached to You, bearing Your yoke, unique in proclaiming Your oneness.
