Save humanity and beast, flesh, spirit and soul, sinew, bone and skin, likeness, image and form. Human glory resembles a breath; man is likened to the beasts that perish. Save the beauty of appearance and stature, the renewal of the face of the earth, the planting of living trees, the winepresses and standing grain, the vineyards and sycamores of the appointed world. Save the powerful rains that nourish it and revive what has been forgotten; the shrubs that raise it up, its delights that strengthen it, its flowers that make it flourish, its plants that bring down rain, its cool streams and abundant showers that sustain it, and its waters that lift it up. Save us, please! Save the earth suspended upon nothing; save us, please!
paragraphs.note: Working English translation; liturgical proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Add: O LORD, our Lord, How glorious is Thy name in all the earth! Whose majesty is rehearsed above the heavens.

Save the soil from the curse, cattle from miscarriage, the threshing floor from the cutting locust, grain from blight, possessions from disaster, food from confusion, olives from falling, wheat from grasshoppers, sustenance from swarming locusts, winepresses from crawling pests, vineyards from worms, late harvests from locusts, fine fruits from rustling devastation, lives from panic, plenty from consumption, flocks from poverty, fruits from scorching, sheep from destruction, harvests from curses, abundance from famine, and ears of grain from withering. Save us from every plague upon the produce of the earth; save us, please!
paragraphs.note: Working English translation; liturgical proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Add: The LORD is righteous in all His ways, And gracious in all His works.
For the sake of the steadfast one cast into the blazing fire, save us, we pray.
For the sake of the son bound upon wood and fire, save us, we pray.
For the sake of the mighty one who wrestled with the angel of fire, save us, we pray.
For the sake of those under the banners whom You guided with light and a cloud of fire, save us, we pray.
For the sake of the one who ascended on high, raised among the angels of fire, save us, we pray.
For the sake of the One who was to You like a prince among the angels of fire.
For the sake of the gift of the commandments given from the fire, save us, we pray.
For the sake of the covering of curtains by the cloud of fire, save us, we pray.
For the sake of the ceremony at the mountain upon which You descended in fire, save us, we pray.
For the sake of the beloved House which You loved from the heavens of fire, save us, we pray.
For the sake of the one who longed until the fire subsided, save us, we pray.
For the sake of the one who took a firepan and turned away the fury of fire, save us, we pray.
For the sake of the one who was zealous with great zeal amid the fire, save us, we pray.
For the sake of the one who waved his hand and stones of fire came down, save us, we pray.
For the sake of the One who placed a milk-white lamb as a whole burnt offering.
For the sake of the one who stood at the threshing floor and was accepted by fire, save us, we pray.
For the sake of the one who prayed in the Temple courtyard and fire descended, save us, we pray.
For the sake of the prophet who ascended in a chariot and horses of fire, save us, we pray.
For the sake of the holy ones cast into the fire, save us, we pray.
For the sake of the one who saw myriads upon myriads and rivers of fire, save us, we pray.
For the sake of the ruins of Your city, consumed by fire, save us, we pray.
For the sake of the descendants of the chiefs of Judah, make them like a vessel of fire, save us, we pray.

Yours, Lord, are the greatness, might, glory, victory and majesty, for everything in heaven and on earth is Yours. Yours, Lord, is the kingdom, and You are exalted above all as Head. The Lord shall be King over all the earth; on that day the Lord shall be One and His name One. In Your Torah it is written: 'Hear, O Israel: The Lord our God, the Lord is One.' Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom forever and ever.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Ani va-Ho, save us, we pray.
As You saved the mighty ones in Lod among Your people, when You went forth to save Your people, so save us now, we pray.
As You saved the people who sought God's deliverance, so save us now, we pray.
As You saved the multitude of hosts, and with them the angels of the heavenly hosts, so save us now, we pray.
As You saved the pure ones from the house of bondage, when they were in the hands of their oppressors, O Gracious One, so save us now, we pray.
As You saved those submerged in the depths of the divided waters, while Your glory passed with them, so save us now, we pray.
As You saved the singing one, like a reed, so that he was rescued, and saved her whose source was marked out, so save us now, we beseech You.
As You saved through Your promise, 'I will bring you out,' and Your declared promise, 'I will bring you with Me,' so save us now, we pray.
As You saved those who circled the altar, bearing willow branches to encircle the altar, so save us now, we pray.
As You saved through the wonders of the Ark when it was taken captive, afflicting Philistia in fierce anger until deliverance came, so save us now, we pray.
As You saved the congregations exiled to Babylon, sending forth Your mercy for their sake, so save us now, we pray.
As You saved the captive tribes of Jacob, so return once more and restore the captives of Jacob's tents; save us now, we pray.
As You saved those who keep the commandments and await deliverance, O God of salvation, save us now, we pray!
Ani va-Ho, save us, we pray.
Before lighting the candles, the following blessings are recited:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe.
Who has sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us to light the Hanukkah candle.
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe.
Who performed miracles for our ancestors in those days, at this season.
On the first night, add:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe.
Who has kept us alive, sustained us, and enabled us to reach this time.
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe.
For food made from the five grains: 'For the nourishment and sustenance.'
For wine: 'For the vine and the fruit of the vine.'
For fruit of the Seven Species: 'For the tree and the fruit of the tree.'

For the produce of the field and for the desirable, good and spacious land that You favored and granted as an inheritance to our ancestors, so that they might eat its fruit and be satisfied with its goodness. Have mercy, Lord our God, upon Israel Your people, upon Jerusalem Your city, upon Zion the dwelling place of Your glory, upon Your altar and upon Your Sanctuary. Rebuild Jerusalem, the holy city, speedily in our days. Bring us into it and let us rejoice in its rebuilding; may we eat of its fruit, be satisfied with its goodness, and bless You for it in holiness and purity. [On Shabbat: 'Favor and strengthen us on this Sabbath day.'] [On Rosh Chodesh: 'Remember us for good on this New Moon.'] [On Rosh Hashanah: 'Remember us for good on this Day of Remembrance.'] [On a festival or its intermediate days: 'Make us rejoice on the day of'—Passover: 'this Festival of Unleavened Bread'; Shavuot: 'this Festival of Weeks'; Sukkot: 'this Festival of Booths'; Shemini Atzeret: 'this Eighth Day, Festival of Assembly'—'on this holy convocation.'] For You, Lord, are good and do good to all, and we thank You for the land.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: For foods made from the five grains: 'And for the nourishment.'
For wine: 'and for the fruit of her vine' (outside Israel: 'and for the fruit of the vine').
For fruit of the Seven Species: 'and for her fruits' (outside Israel: 'and for the fruits').
Blessed are You, LORD, for the land.
For foods made from the five grains: 'And for the nourishment' (some also say 'and for the sustenance').
For wine: 'and for the fruit of her vine' (outside Israel: 'and for the fruit of the vine').
For fruit of the Seven Species: 'and for her fruits' (outside Israel: 'and for the fruits').

This blessing is recited after eating tree fruits other than the Seven Species, vegetables and other produce of the ground, after drinking other beverages, and after food that does not grow from the ground.
After eating, recite:

Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who creates many living beings and their needs, for all that You created to sustain the life of every living creature. Blessed is the Life of all worlds.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Mourner: May His great name be exalted and sanctified. [Congregation: Amen.]
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: In the world that He created according to His will, may He establish His kingdom in your lifetimes and days, and in the lifetime of the entire House of Israel, speedily and soon, and say: Amen. [Congregation: Amen.]
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Congregation and mourner: May His great name be blessed forever and to all eternity.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Mourner: Blessed, praised, glorified, exalted, elevated, honored, raised high and lauded be the name of the Holy One, blessed be He. [Congregation: Blessed be He.]
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Above all blessings [during the Ten Days of Repentance: far above all blessings], songs, praises and consolations uttered in the world; and say: Amen. [Congregation: Amen.]
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: May abundant peace come from heaven, and life upon us and upon all Israel; and say: Amen.
He who makes peace [during the Ten Days of Repentance: the peace] in His heights, may He make peace for us and for all Israel; and say: Amen. [Congregation: Amen.]
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: May His great name be exalted and sanctified. (Congregation: Amen.)
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: In the world that He will renew, when He revives the dead, raises them to eternal life, rebuilds the city of Jerusalem, perfects His Temple within it, uproots foreign worship from the land, restores heavenly worship to its place, and the Holy One, blessed be He, reigns in His glorious kingdom, brings forth salvation and draws His Messiah near. (Congregation: Amen.)
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: In your lifetime and in your days, and in the lifetime of all the house of Israel, speedily and soon; and say: Amen.
(Congregation: Amen. May His great name be blessed forever and to all eternity.)
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: May His great name be blessed forever and to all eternity. Blessed, praised, glorified, exalted, elevated, honored, raised high and lauded be the name of the Holy One, blessed be He. Congregation: Amen (or: Blessed be He).
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Beyond all blessings (during the Ten Days of Repentance: far beyond all blessings), songs, praises and consolations uttered in the world; and say: Amen. (Congregation: Amen.)
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: May abundant peace come from heaven, and life upon us and upon all Israel; and say: Amen.

(Step backward three steps.) He who makes peace (during the Ten Days of Repentance: the peace) in His heights—He (in the Edot HaMizrach custom, add: in His mercy) shall make peace for us and for all Israel; and say Amen. (Congregation: Amen.)
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: He shall proclaim freedom to son and daughter,
and protect you as the pupil of His eye.
May your name be pleasant and never cease;
sit and rest on the Sabbath day.
Seek out my dwelling and my sanctuary;
show me a sign of salvation.
Plant a choice vine in my vineyard;
heed the plea of the children of my people.
Tread the winepress in Bozrah,
and in Babylon (variant: Edom), which has grown mighty.
Shatter my enemies in anger and wrath;
hear my voice on the day I call.
O God, give the wilderness a mountain,
myrtle, acacia, cypress (variant: plane tree), and elm.
For the one who warns and the one who heeds,
grant peace flowing like a river.
Crush those who rise against me, living and zealous God;
make their hearts melt and bring them low (variant wording).
Then we shall open our mouths wide and fill them;
our tongues will sing Your praise.
Learn wisdom for your soul;
it will be a crown upon your head.
Keep the commandment of your Holy One (variant: your God);
observe the Sabbath, your holy day.
Author: Dunash ben Labrat.
This prayer is said every Friday night after the service, before leaving the synagogue.

Master of all worlds, Lord of all souls, Lord of peace: mighty King, blessed King, great King, King who speaks peace, glorious King, ancient King, pure King, everlasting living King, good and beneficent King, unique and singular King, majestic King, clothed in mercy, King of kings, exalted King, supporter of the fallen, Maker of creation, Redeemer and Rescuer, radiant King, holy King, high and lifted up, Hearer of prayer, King whose way is perfect.

I give thanks before You, LORD my God and God of my ancestors, for every kindness You have shown me and will yet show me, my household, and all Your creatures, the children of Your covenant. Blessed are Your holy and pure angels who do Your will. Lord of peace, King to whom peace belongs, bless me with peace. Remember me, my entire household, and all Your people, the house of Israel, for good life and for peace.

Supreme King over all the heavenly hosts, our Maker and Creator from the beginning, I entreat Your shining countenance: enable me and all my household to find favor and good understanding in Your eyes and in the eyes of every son of Adam and Eve, and all who see us, so that we may serve You. Grant that I welcome Sabbaths with great joy, with wealth and honor, and with few transgressions. Remove from me and from all Your people Israel every kind of sickness, ailment, poverty, want, and destitution. Give us a good inclination to serve You in truth, awe, and love, and let us be honored in Your eyes and in the eyes of all who see us, for You are the King of glory, and glory befits You.

Please, King of kings, command Your ministering angels, servants of the Most High, to attend me with compassion and bless me when they come to my home on our holy day. I have lit my candles, prepared my bed, and changed my garments in honor of the Sabbath. I have come into Your house to offer my supplication and ask You to remove my sighing. I testify that You made all creation in six days, and once, twice, and a third time I shall testify over my cup in joy, as You commanded me to remember the Sabbath and delight in it with the added soul You gave me. On this day I rest, as You commanded me to serve You. I recount Your greatness in song and set the LORD before me. Have mercy on me in exile and redeem me; awaken my heart to love You. Then I shall keep Your precepts and statutes without sorrow and pray in the fitting and proper manner.
Angels of peace, may your arrival be peaceful. Bless me with peace, pronounce a blessing upon my set table, and depart in peace, from now and forever. Amen, selah.
How beloved is your rest, O Sabbath Queen!
So we run to greet you: Come, O royal bride.
Put on beautiful garments to kindle the lamp with a blessing,
and let all labor cease: You shall do no work.
To delight in pleasures: geese, quail, and fish!
From the evening, prepare every kind of delicacy;
while it is yet day, ready the fattened fowl,
set out many dishes, and drink fragrant wines;
enjoy delicious treats at each of the three meals. To delight!
They shall inherit Jacob's portion, an inheritance without bounds.
Rich and poor shall honor it and merit redemption.
If you keep the Sabbath, you will be My treasured possession.
For six days you shall labor, and on the seventh let us rejoice. To delight!
Your business affairs are forbidden on it, as is reckoning accounts;
but you may ponder, and arrange a daughter's marriage.
You may teach a child a book or sing melodies,
and reflect on beautiful words everywhere. To delight!
Walk in a tranquil manner; call the Sabbath a delight.
Sleep is praiseworthy, when it refreshes the soul as is fitting.
Therefore my soul yearns for you, to rest in affection,
sheltered as among roses; son and daughter alike shall rest. To delight!
The Sabbath of rest is a foretaste of the world to come.
All who delight in it will merit abundant joy.
They shall be rescued from the birth pangs of the Messiah;
may our redemption spring forth and sorrow and sighing flee. To delight!
This day brings light and joy to Israel: the Sabbath of rest.
You commanded the precepts at the assembly at Sinai,
to keep the Sabbath and the festivals all my years,
to set a meal and offering before You: the Sabbath of rest.
A delight to the hearts of a broken nation,
an additional soul for those whose spirits ache;
for the troubled soul it removes sighing: the Sabbath of rest.
You sanctified it and blessed it above all days;
in six days You completed the work of the worlds.
On it the sorrowful found calm and safety: the Sabbath of rest.
O Awesome One, You commanded us to refrain from work;
if I keep the Sabbath I shall merit royal splendor.
I will bring a gift to the One I revere, a fragrant offering: the Sabbath of rest.
I will compose a song for You with melody and sweetness;
before the splendor of Your greatness my soul longs for You.
Fulfill Your promise to Your wholehearted treasured people: the Sabbath of rest.
Accept my prayer as You accepted Nahshon's offering;
make my day of rest resound with song and gladness,
beloved as the pupil of an eye, with abundant success: the Sabbath of rest.
We have hoped for Your salvation, O mighty LORD;
send the son of David, our king, to the Hebrews,
to proclaim freedom, relief, and rest: the Sabbath of rest.
Please, awesome Most High, look upon our affliction;
redeem us quickly, favor us and answer us.
Gladden our souls with light and joy: the Sabbath of rest.
Renew our Sanctuary; remember that it was destroyed.
Bestow Your goodness, our Savior, on the one in sorrow,
who sits on the Sabbath singing and praising: the Sabbath of rest.
Remember the holy day for our sake, by its precious merit;
guard us on this day and every day.
My radiant and awesome Beloved, bring relief: the Sabbath of rest.
Let Israel hear the voice of song and salvation;
when the vision of redemption comes, O Rock who makes salvation flourish,
let the light of my sun appear and shine continually: the Sabbath of rest.
My soul thirsts for God, for the living God;
my heart and flesh sing for joy to the living God.
The living God created me and said, 'As I live,
no human may see Me and live.'
He created all things with wisdom, counsel, and purpose,
though it remains hidden from the eyes of all living beings.
His glory is exalted above all; every mouth declares His majesty.
Blessed is He in whose hand is the soul of every living being.
He distinguished the descendants of the upright and taught them statutes
by which a person shall live when they are observed.
Who can claim to be righteous? Humanity is like fine dust.
Truly, no living person can be righteous before You.
The inclination of the heart is cunning, like the venom of a viper;
how, then, shall mortal flesh return?
Those who strayed may yet turn back from their ways
before they lie down in the house appointed for all the living.
For all Your acts of kindness, renew Your testimonies;
You open Your hand and satisfy every living being.
Remember the love of the ancients and revive those who sleep;
bring near the days when the son of Jesse shall live.
See how the true mistress is challenged by the speaking maidservant:
'No, your son is the dead one; mine is the living one.'
Have You not chosen Your portion from the beginning? Demand justice for its blood;
pour out wrath upon the head of the living goat.
Perhaps the hour has come to bring back those borne in guilt
to Your house, where one may behold Him and live.
I will spread out my hands to You and bow upon my face
when I open my mouth with 'The soul of every living being.'

Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who fashioned humanity with wisdom and created within the body openings and cavities. It is revealed and known before the throne of Your glory that if one of them should open when it ought to be closed, or close when it ought to be open, it would be impossible to exist and stand before You even for one moment.
Blessed are You, LORD, who heals all flesh and acts wondrously.

My God! the soul which You bestowed in me is pure; You created it, You formed it, You breathed it into me and You preserve it within me. You will eventually take it from me, and restore it in me in the time to come. So long as the soul is within me I give thanks to You, Adonoy my God, and God of my fathers, Lord of all creatures, Master of all souls.
Blessed are You, LORD, who restores souls to lifeless bodies.
For the cantor's repetition of the Amidah.

We shall sanctify Your name in the world as they sanctify it in the heavens above. As written by Your prophet: 'And one called to another and said: Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hosts; the whole earth is full of His glory.' Then, with a tremendous, mighty and powerful sound, they raise their voices opposite the seraphim, saying before them: 'Blessed is the glory of the Lord from His place.' From Your place, our King, appear and reign over us, for we await You. When will You reign in Zion? Soon, in our days, may You dwell there for all eternity. May You be magnified and sanctified in Jerusalem, Your city, in every generation and forever. May our eyes behold Your kingship, as was said in Your mighty songs through David, Your righteous anointed one: 'The Lord shall reign forever, your God, Zion, from generation to generation. Hallelujah!'
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: From generation to generation we shall declare Your greatness, and forever and ever we shall sanctify Your holiness. Your praise, our God, shall never depart from our mouths, for You are a great and holy God and King. Blessed are You, LORD, the holy God. During the Ten Days of Repentance conclude: the holy King.
You are holy and Your name is holy, and holy beings praise You every day forever. Blessed are You, LORD, the holy God. During the Ten Days of Repentance say instead: the holy King.

Before opening the ark, say: None is like You among the gods, O Lord, and none is like Your works. Your kingdom is a kingdom for all ages, and Your rule endures through every generation. The LORD reigns, the LORD has reigned, the LORD will reign forever. The LORD gives strength to His people; the LORD blesses His people with peace.
Merciful Father, in Your favor do good to Zion; rebuild the walls of Jerusalem. For in You alone we have placed our trust, O exalted King, Lord of worlds.

When the Holy Ark is opened, say: And it came to pass, when the Ark set forward, that Moses said: “Arise, O LORD, and let Your enemies be scattered, and let those who hate You flee before You.” For from Zion shall go forth the Torah, and the word of the LORD from Jerusalem. Blessed is He who gave the Torah to His people Israel in His holiness.

On a festival falling on a weekday, on Yom Kippur, and on Hoshana Rabbah, say: “The LORD, the LORD, compassionate and gracious God, slow to anger, abundant in kindness and truth, preserving kindness for thousands, forgiving iniquity, transgression and sin, and cleansing.” Repeat three times.

For the three pilgrimage festivals and Shemini Atzeret: Master of the universe, fulfill the petitions of my heart for good, bring about my worthy desire, and grant my request. Enable me, [name], and my wife, sons, daughters, and all my household to do Your will with a whole heart. Deliver us from the evil inclination and give us our portion in Your Torah. Grant that Your Presence may rest upon us. Cause a spirit of wisdom and understanding to shine upon us, and fulfill in us the verse: 'The spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him, a spirit of wisdom and understanding, a spirit of counsel and strength, a spirit of knowledge and fear of the Lord.'
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Therefore may it be Your will, Lord our God and God of our ancestors, to grant us the merit to do what is good in Your eyes and to walk uprightly before You. Sanctify us with Your holiness, that we may merit good and long lives and life in the world to come. Protect us from evil actions and from the troubled times that may come upon the world. Whoever trusts in the Lord shall be surrounded by kindness. Amen.
paragraphs.note: Original English working translation aligned to the full Hebrew paragraph; specialist review pending.

paragraphs.text: And as for me, may my prayer come before You, LORD, at a favorable time. O God, in Your great kindness answer me with Your faithful salvation. Repeat three times.
The cantor and congregation: Hear, O Israel, the LORD is our God, the LORD is One.
The cantor and congregation: Our God is One; great is our Lord; holy is His name. On Rosh Hashanah, Yom Kippur and Hoshana Rabbah add: and awesome is His name.
Cantor: Magnify the LORD with me, and together let us exalt His name.
Cantor: Magnify the LORD with me, and together let us exalt His name.
Congregation: Yours, LORD, are greatness, might, splendor, victory and majesty; for everything in heaven and on earth is Yours.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: The person called to the Torah blesses: Bless the LORD who is to be blessed.
The congregation responds: Blessed is the LORD, the Blessed One, forever and ever.
The person called repeats: Blessed is the LORD, the Blessed One, forever and ever.
The person then recites: Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who chose us from among all peoples and gave us His Torah. Blessed are You, LORD, Giver of the Torah.

After the Torah reading, the person called up blesses: Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who gave us the Torah of truth and planted eternal life within us. Blessed are You, LORD, giver of the Torah.
Birkat HaGomel: Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who bestows good upon those who are obligated, and who has bestowed every good upon me.
The congregation answers Amen, and then says: May He who has bestowed good upon you continue to bestow every good upon you, selah.

May He who blessed our ancestors Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob bless [name], son of [father’s name], who has reached thirteen years of age, has become obligated in the commandments, and has been called to the Torah to offer praise and thanks to the Blessed LORD for all the good He has bestowed upon him. May the Holy One, blessed be He, protect him and preserve his life, and direct his heart to remain wholehearted with the LORD, to walk in His ways and observe His commandments all his days. And let us say: Amen.

When a boy who has become bar mitzvah is called to the Torah, after he recites the concluding blessing his father says: 'Blessed is He who has released me from the punishment [for the deeds] of this one.'
The cantor takes the Torah scroll in his hands and says:

May it be Your will, Lord our God and God of our ancestors, to renew this month upon us for goodness and blessing. Grant us long lives: lives of peace, goodness, blessing, sustenance and bodily vigor; lives with reverence for heaven and fear of sin; lives without shame or humiliation; lives of wealth and honor; lives in which love of Torah and reverence for heaven dwell within us; lives in which the desires of our hearts are fulfilled for good. Amen, Selah.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: May He who performed miracles for our ancestors and redeemed them from slavery to freedom redeem us soon and gather our dispersed people from the four corners of the earth. All Israel are companions; and let us say: Amen.
Rosh Chodesh of [name of month] will be on [day of the week]. May it come for good upon us and upon all Israel.

May the Holy One, blessed be He, renew this month for us and for all His people, the House of Israel, wherever they dwell: for goodness and blessing, rejoicing and gladness, deliverance and consolation, good livelihood and sustenance, life and peace, good reports and glad tidings; in winter add: and rain in its proper season; for complete healing and an approaching redemption. And let us say: Amen.
Hope in the LORD; be strong and let your heart take courage, and hope in the LORD.

There is none holy like the Lord, for there is none besides You and no Rock like our God. For who is God besides the Lord, and who is a Rock except our God? There is none like our God, none like our Master, none like our King, none like our Savior. Who is like our God? Who is like our Master? Who is like our King? Who is like our Savior? Let us thank our God, thank our Master, thank our King, thank our Savior. Blessed be our God, blessed be our Master, blessed be our King, blessed be our Savior. You are our God, You are our Master, You are our King, You are our Savior. You are the One before whom our ancestors offered the incense of spices.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: A psalm of David. The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not lack anything.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: He makes me lie down in green pastures; He leads me beside still waters.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: He restores my soul; He guides me in paths of righteousness for His name's sake.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: 4. Even as I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no harm, for You are with me; Your rod and Your staff comfort me.
5. You set a table before me in the presence of my enemies; You anoint my head with oil, and my cup overflows.
6. Surely goodness and kindness will follow me all the days of my life, and I will dwell in the house of the LORD for many days.
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who has sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us to recite Hallel.

May all Your works praise You, Lord our God, and Your faithful ones, the righteous who do Your will, and all Your people, the house of Israel. With song may they thank, bless, praise, glorify, sing of, exalt, revere, sanctify and enthrone Your name, our King, continually. For it is good to give thanks to You and fitting to sing to Your name, for from everlasting to everlasting You are God.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Blessed are You, LORD, the King praised with songs of praise.

May it be Your will, LORD our God and God of our ancestors, that this blessing which — the priests say: “You commanded us”; the congregation says: “You commanded” — to bless Your people Israel should be a complete blessing, with no obstacle or sin in it, from now and forever.

May our plea be as acceptable to You [alternate: before You] as a burnt offering and sacrifice. Merciful One, in Your abundant mercy restore Your Presence to Zion, Your city, and the order of worship to Jerusalem.

Custom in many American congregations: May our eyes behold Your merciful return to Zion. There we shall worship You in reverence as in ancient days. Blessed are You, LORD, whom alone we shall worship with reverence.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: The Vilna Gaon's wording and the custom of the Land of Israel: There we shall worship You with reverence as in ancient days. May our eyes behold Your merciful return to Zion. Blessed are You, LORD, who restores His Presence to Zion.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: [Continue 'We give thanks' through 'to thank You.' Some have the custom that the priests quietly say:] May it be Your will, Lord our God and God of our ancestors, that this blessing which You commanded us [alternative: commanded] to bestow upon Your people Israel be a complete blessing, containing no stumbling block or sin, from now and forever.

paragraphs.text: The cantor says softly: Our God and God of our ancestors, bless us with the threefold blessing written in the Torah by Moses Your servant, spoken by Aaron and his sons—
Cantor, aloud: 'Kohanim!' ('Priests!')
The congregation responds: 'Your holy people, as it is said:'
The priests: Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who has sanctified us with Aaron's sanctity and commanded us to bless His people Israel with love.

The prayer leader prompts the priests one word at a time. A widespread custom is for the priests to chant before the end of each verse while the congregation quietly recites the prayer concerning a favorable dream. Some recite a different prayer before the final word “peace.” Supplications should not be said on Shabbat.
May the LORD bless you and protect you. (Congregation: Amen.)
May the LORD make His face shine upon you and be gracious to you. (Congregation: Amen.)
May the LORD lift His face toward you and grant you peace. (Congregation: Amen.)
The cantor immediately continues with Sim Shalom ('Grant peace') and the remainder of the prayer.

Some have the custom that the congregation says: Mighty One on high, enthroned in power, You are peace and Your name is peace. May it be Your will to grant us and all Your people, the House of Israel, life and blessing, guarding us in peace.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: The priests also say: Master of the Universe, we have done what You decreed upon us; now do for us as You promised: Look forth from Your holy dwelling, from heaven, and bless Your people Israel and the land You gave us, as You swore to our ancestors, a land flowing with milk and honey.

I am ready and prepared to fulfill the mitzvah of dwelling in the sukkah, as the Creator, blessed be His name, commanded me: “For seven days you shall dwell in booths; every native-born Israelite shall dwell in booths.”
So that your generations may know that I made the children of Israel dwell in booths when I brought them out of the land of Egypt.
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who has sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us concerning the taking of the lulav.
When blessing the lulav for the first time, also recite the Shehecheyanu blessing:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who has kept us alive, sustained us, and enabled us to reach this time.
Before eating bread, wash the hands and say: Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who has sanctified us by His commandments and commanded us concerning the washing of hands.
Over bread say: Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who brings forth bread from the earth.
Over dishes made from the five grains and over baked grain products say: Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who creates kinds of nourishment.
Over wine say: Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who creates the fruit of the vine.
Over fruit that grows on trees say: Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who creates the fruit of the tree.
Over produce of the ground say: Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who creates the fruit of the ground.

Over meat, fish, milk, eggs, cheese, truffles, mushrooms and similar foods, and over all drinks other than wine, one says: Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, by whose word everything came into being.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

May it be Your will Adonoy, my God, and God of my fathers, to consider [my fulfillment of] the mitzva of tzitzis before You as though I had fulfilled it in every detail, accurately and with full intent, and the 613 commandments that depend on it. Amein, Selah.
The commandment of the LORD is pure, enlightening the eyes.

On a festival, the cantor sings “God, in the might of Your strength”: God, mighty in Your strength, great in the glory of Your name, powerful forever, awesome in Your wondrous deeds; the King seated upon a high and exalted throne.

On Shabbat, the cantor begins with “He who dwells forever”: He who dwells forever, exalted and holy is His name. And it is written: “Sing joyfully, righteous ones, to the LORD; praise is fitting for the upright.”

By the mouths of the upright You will be praised; by the words of the righteous You will be blessed; by the tongues of the devout You will be exalted; and in the midst of the holy You will be sanctified.

In the assemblies of the multitudes of Your people, the house of Israel, Your name, our King, shall be glorified in song throughout every generation. For it is the duty of all creatures before You, Lord our God and God of our ancestors, to thank, praise, acclaim, glorify, exalt, honor, bless, elevate, and extol You—beyond all the songs and praises of David son of Jesse, Your servant, Your anointed one.

paragraphs.text: When the Torah scroll is lifted, look at its writing and say: “This is the Torah that Moses placed before the children of Israel, by the word of the LORD through Moses.”

Before reading the Haftarah, the reader says this blessing: Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who chose worthy prophets and took delight in their words spoken in truth. Blessed are You, LORD, who chooses the Torah, Moses His servant, Israel His people, and the prophets of truth and righteousness.

After reading the Haftarah, the reader recites these blessings: Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the universe, Rock of all worlds, righteous throughout all generations, the faithful God who speaks and acts, who promises and fulfills, whose every word is truth and justice.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: You are faithful, LORD our God, and Your words are faithful. Not one of Your words shall return unfulfilled, for You are a faithful and merciful God and King. Blessed are You, LORD, the God faithful in all His words.

paragraphs.text: Have mercy on Zion, for it is the home of our life; swiftly in our days bring salvation to her, humbled in spirit.
Blessed are You, LORD, who gladdens Zion with her children.

Bring us joy, Lord our God, through Elijah the prophet, Your servant, and through the kingdom of the house of David, Your anointed one. May he come speedily and gladden our hearts. No stranger shall sit upon his throne, nor shall others inherit his glory, for You swore to him by Your holy name that his lamp would never be extinguished. Blessed are You, Lord, Shield of David. [Up to this point is recited on public fast days and at the afternoon service of Yom Kippur.]

paragraphs.text: On Shabbat, including Shabbat during the intermediate days of Passover, say: For the Torah, the Temple service, the Prophets, and this Sabbath day that You, Lord our God, gave us for holiness and rest, for honor and splendor: for all these we thank You and bless You, Lord our God. May Your name be blessed by every living mouth always, forever and ever. Blessed are You, Lord, who sanctifies the Sabbath.

For all this we thank You and bless You, Lord our God. May Your name be blessed by every living mouth always, forever and ever. Blessed are You, Lord, who sanctifies the Sabbath, Israel and the festive seasons.

For all this we thank You and bless You, Lord our God. May Your name be blessed by every living mouth always, forever and ever. paragraphs.text: Today is the holy Shabbat, on which the Levites would say in the Temple: “A psalm, a song for the Sabbath day.”

It is good to thank Adonoy, and sing praise to Your Name, Most High. To relate Your kindliness in the morning, and Your faithfulness in the nights. Upon a ten-stringed instrument and lute, in meditation upon the harp. For You have given me joy, Adonoy, with Your deeds, at the work of Your hands I sing joyously. How great are Your works, Adonoy; how infinitely profound are Your thoughts. An empty-headed man cannot know, nor does a fool understand this: When the wicked bloom like grass, and all the evildoers blossom— it is so that they may be destroyed forever. But You will remain on high forever Adonoy. For behold, Your enemies, Adonoy; For behold, Your enemies shall perish; dispersed shall be all evildoers. You uplifted my horn like that of a unicorn; I am saturated with fresh oil. My eye has seen [the defeat of] those who spy on me; of the wicked who rise against me, my ears have heard [that they are doomed]. The righteous will blossom like a date palm, like a cedar in Lebanon, he will grow tall. Planted in the House of Adonoy, in the courtyards of our God they will blossom. They will still be fruitful in old age; they will be full of sap and freshness. To declare that Adonoy is upright; He is my Stronghold; in Whom there is no injustice.
paragraphs.ref: KAV EN parallel ashkenaz:Mizmor Shir L'Yom HaShabbat:1
paragraphs.note: Reviewed closely matching Hebrew wording in existing translated passage.

paragraphs.text: May it be Your will, LORD our God and God of our ancestors, that just as I have fulfilled the mitzvah and dwelt in this sukkah, so may I merit next year to dwell in the sukkah made from the Leviathan.
Rock, stronghold of my salvation, it is fitting to praise You.
Restore the house of my prayer, and there we shall offer thanksgiving.
When You prepare the downfall of the raging enemy,
Then I shall complete, with song and psalm, the dedication of the altar.
My soul was sated with suffering; my strength was exhausted by grief.
They embittered my life with hardship, under the bondage of the kingdom of Egypt.
Yet with His mighty hand He brought forth His treasured people.
Pharaoh’s army and all his troops sank like a stone into the deep.
He brought me to His holy sanctuary, yet even there I found no rest.
For an oppressor came and exiled me, because I served foreign gods.
I poured for myself a cup of poison; I nearly perished.
At Babylon’s end, through Zerubbabel, after seventy years I was saved.
The Agagite, son of Hammedatha, sought to cut down the lofty cypress.
But his plan became a snare and a trap for him, and his pride came to an end.
You raised up the head of the Benjaminite and erased the enemy’s name.
His many sons and all his possessions You hung upon the gallows.
The Greeks gathered against me in the days of the Hasmoneans.
They broke through the walls of my towers and defiled all the oils.
Yet from the remaining jars a miracle was wrought for the people likened to lilies.
The wise established eight days for songs and rejoicing.
Reveal Your holy arm and bring the end of deliverance near.
Avenge the blood of Your servants upon the wicked nation.
For the hour of our suffering has been prolonged, and the days of evil seem endless.
Drive away Edom into the shadow of darkness; raise up for us the seven shepherds.

Av HaRachamim is omitted on Shabbat when Tachanun would not be recited were it a weekday; also on the Shabbatot of the Four Special Torah Portions and on Shabbat Mevarchim. But when blessing the months of Iyar, Sivan or Av, it is recited even if there is a circumcision or bridegroom.

paragraphs.text: Father of compassion, who dwells on high: in His abundant mercy may He remember with compassion the devout, the upright, and the blameless holy communities who gave their lives for the sanctification of the Name. Beloved and cherished in their lives, they were not separated even in death; they were swifter than eagles and stronger than lions in doing the will of their Maker and the desire of their Rock. May our God remember them for good among the other righteous of the world and avenge the blood of His servants that has been shed, as it is written in the Torah of Moses, the man of God: 'Sing aloud, O nations, of His people; for He will avenge the blood of His servants, render vengeance to His foes, and make atonement for His land and His people.' And through Your servants the prophets it is written: 'And I shall hold as innocent their blood which I have not held innocent; and the Lord dwells in Zion.' And in the Holy Writings it says: 'Why should the nations say, Where is their God? Let the avenging of the spilled blood of Your servants be made known among the nations before our eyes.' And it says: 'For He who requires blood remembers them; He does not forget the cry of the humble.' And it says: 'He shall judge among the nations; He shall fill the places with dead bodies; He shall shatter the head over a wide land. He shall drink of the brook along the way; therefore He shall lift up his head.'
paragraphs.note: New English working translation reviewed against the Hebrew and available Russian text; specialist proofreading pending.

Arise, ______ son of _____, the Kohein, Blessed is He Who gave the Torah to His people, Israel, in His holiness.

paragraphs.text: MISHNAH I Where are the offerings slaughtered [in the Holy Temple?] The holiest of offerings are slaughtered on the north side [of the Altar]. The bullock and he-goat of Yom Kippur are slaughtered on the north side, and their blood is received in a sacred vessel, on the north side. Their blood must be thrown between the poles [of the Ark], and in front of the curtain and upon the Gold Altar; [omission of] any one of these applications prevents [atonement]. The remainder of the blood [in the vessel] he [the Kohein] would pour on the western base of the Outer Altar; [but] if he did not do so, it did not prevent [atonement].
paragraphs.ref: KAV EN parallel ashkenaz:Laws of Sacrifices:1

paragraphs.text: MISHNAH II The bullocks that are burned entirely, and the he-goats that are burned entirely, are slaughtered on the north side, and their blood is received in a sacred vessel, on the north side; their blood must be thrown in front of the curtain and upon the Gold Altar; [omission of] any one of these applications prevents [atonement]. The remainder of the blood [in the vessel] he [the Kohein] would pour on the western base of the Outer Altar; [but] if he did not do so, it did not prevent [atonement]. These [offerings] and those are burned at the place where the ashes were put.
paragraphs.ref: KAV EN parallel ashkenaz:Laws of Sacrifices:2

paragraphs.text: The communal and individual sin offerings. These are the communal sin offerings: the goats offered on New Moons and festivals. They are slaughtered on the north side of the altar; their blood is received in a sacred vessel in the north. Their blood requires four applications to the four horns of the altar. How is this done? The priest ascends the ramp, turns to the surrounding ledge, and comes to the southeastern horn, then the northeastern horn, then the northwestern horn [the source paragraph ends mid-sentence].
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: The western and southwestern sides: the remaining blood was poured out at the southwestern base of the altar. These offerings were eaten within the courtyard curtains by male priests, prepared in any manner, for one day and the following night until midnight.

A Prayer of Moses the man of God. Lord, Thou hast been our dwelling-place in all generations. Before the mountains were brought forth, Or ever Thou hadst formed the earth and the world, Even from everlasting to everlasting, Thou art God. Thou turnest man to contrition; And sayest: 'Return, ye children of men.' For a thousand years in Thy sight Are but as yesterday when it is past, And as a watch in the night. Thou carriest them away as with a flood; they are as a sleep; In the morning they are like grass which groweth up. In the morning it flourisheth, and groweth up; In the evening it is cut down, and withereth. For we are consumed in Thine anger, And by Thy wrath are we hurried away. Thou hast set our iniquities before Thee, Our secret sins in the light of Thy countenance. For all our days are passed away in Thy wrath; We bring our years to an end as a tale that is told. The days of our years are threescore years and ten, Or even by reason of strength fourscore years; Yet is their pride but travail and vanity; For it is speedily gone, and we fly away. Who knoweth the power of Thine anger, And Thy wrath according to the fear that is due unto Thee? So teach us to number our days, That we may get us a heart of wisdom. Return, O LORD; how long? And let it repent Thee concerning Thy servants. O satisfy us in the morning with Thy mercy; That we may rejoice and be glad all our days. Make us glad according to the days wherein Thou hast afflicted us, According to the years wherein we have seen evil. Let Thy work appear unto Thy servants, And Thy glory upon their children. And let the graciousness of the Lord our God be upon us; Establish Thou also upon us the work of our hands; Yea, the work of our hands establish Thou it.
paragraphs.ref: KAV EN parallel edot:Psalms for Shabbat:5
paragraphs.note: Previously translated paragraph, Hebrew similarity 99.3%: source and target independently present in source corpus.

paragraphs.text: He who dwells in the shelter of the Supreme One, under the protection of Shadai he will abide. I say of Adonoy, [He is] my refuge and my stronghold, my God in Whom I trust. For He will save you from the snare-trap, from destructive pestilence. With His wings He will cover you and beneath His wings, you will find refuge; His truth is a shield, a full shield. You will not fear the terror of night, nor the arrow that flies by day. The pestilence that prowls in darkness, nor the deadly plague that ravages at noon. A thousand will fall at your [left] side, and ten thousand at your [right] side but it shall not come near you. Only with your eyes will you behold and see the punishment of the wicked. For you [have proclaimed]: “Adonoy is my refuge,” the Supreme One you have made your dwelling. No evil shall befall you, and no plague shall come near your tent. For His angels He will command on your behalf— to guard you in all your ways. They will carry you upon their hands, lest you hurt your foot on a rock. You will tread upon lion and snake, you will trample young lion and serpent. Because he clings to Me with desire, I will save him; I will strengthen him, for he knows My Name. When he calls upon Me, I will answer him; I am with him in distress, I will free him and honor him. I will satiate him with longevity, and will let him see My deliverance. I will satiate him with longevity, and will let him see My deliverance.
paragraphs.note: Previously translated paragraph, Hebrew similarity 98.9%: source and target independently present in source corpus.

paragraphs.text: Praise God! for it is good to sing to our God; for [His] praise is pleasant, befitting. The builder of Jerusalem is Adonoy; the banished ones of Israel He will gather. [He is] the Healer of the broken-hearted and [also] binds up their wounds. He fixes the number of stars; He calls all of them by names. Great is our Master and abundant in power; His understanding is beyond reckoning. Adonoy causes the humble to stand firm; He casts down the wicked to the ground. Cry out to Adonoy in thanksgiving; sing to our God with the harp. [He] Who covers the heaven with clouds, Who prepares rain for the earth; Who causes grass to grow upon the hills. Who gives the animal its fodder; [also] to the young ravens which call. Not the power of the horse does He desire, nor the thighs of man does He want. Adonoy wants those who fear Him, those who hope for His kindliness. Jerusalem, praise Adonoy; Zion, extol your God. For He has fortified the bars of your gates; He has blessed your children in your midst. He established peace at your border; with prime wheat He satisfies you. He dispatches His command earthward; His word races swiftly. He provides snow like fleece, He scatters frost like ashes. He hurls His ice like crumbs; who can withstand His cold? He dispatches His word and melts them; He blows His wind, they flow as water. He declares His word to Jacob, His statutes and His laws to Israel. He did not do so to any [other] nation; and of His laws they were not informed. Praise God.
paragraphs.note: Previously translated paragraph, Hebrew similarity 98.5%: source and target independently present in source corpus.

paragraphs.text: Praised be Your Name forever, our King, Almighty the great and holy King in heaven and on earth. For to You it is fitting [to offer] Adonoy, our God, and God of our fathers, song and praise, glorification and hymns, [to proclaim Your] strength and dominion, victory, grandeur, and might, praise and glory, holiness and sovereignty, blessings and thanksgivings, from now and forever. Blessed are You, Adonoy, Almighty, King [Who is] great in [our] praise Almighty, of [to Whom we offer our] thanksgiving, Master of [Whom we praise for His] wonders, the Selector of song-hymns, You are the King, Almighty, Life of [all] the worlds.
paragraphs.note: Previously translated paragraph, Hebrew similarity 98.4%: source and target independently present in source corpus.

paragraphs.text: Blessed is the Name of the Master of the universe. Blessed is Your crown and Your place. May Your good will [be] with Your people Israel forever. Show Your people the redemption of Your right hand in Your Holy Temple. Bestow on us Your excellent light, and accept our prayer with compassion. May it be Your will to prolong our lives in well-being. Let me be counted among the righteous, so that You will have compassion on me and protect me and all that is mine, and all that belongs to Your people, Israel. You are He Who nourishes all and maintains all; You are He Who rules over all; You are He Who rules over kings, and the kingdom is Yours. I am a servant of the Holy One, blessed is He, I bow before Him and before the honor of His Torah at all times. Not in man do I put my trust, nor do I rely on any angel; but only in the God of heaven, Who is the true God, Whose Torah is truth, Whose prophets are true, and Who performs many deeds of goodness and truth. In Him I put my trust and to His honored, holy Name I utter praises. May it be Your will to open my heart to Torah, and to fulfill the desires of my heart, and of the heart of Your people Israel, for goodness, for life, and for peace.

paragraphs.text: May the Father of mercy have compassion on the people borne by Him, and may He remember the covenant with the patriarchs; may He rescue our souls from evil times; and may He rebuke the evil impulse from those who have been carried by Him; and may He graciously grant us eternal survival; and fulfill our requests in beneficent measure, [for] deliverance and compassion.

paragraphs.text: For the director of music. A psalm of David. The heavens declare the glory of God; the skies proclaim the work of his hands. Day after day they pour forth speech; night after night they reveal knowledge. They have no speech, they use no words; no sound is heard from them. Yet their voice goes out into all the earth, their words to the ends of the world. In the heavens God has pitched a tent for the sun. It is like a bridegroom coming out of his chamber, like a champion rejoicing to run his course. It rises at one end of the heavens and makes its circuit to the other; nothing is deprived of its warmth. The law of the Lord is perfect, refreshing the soul. The statutes of the Lord are trustworthy, making wise the simple. The precepts of the Lord are right, giving joy to the heart. The commands of the Lord are radiant, giving light to the eyes. The fear of the Lord is pure, enduring forever. The decrees of the Lord are firm, and all of them are righteous. They are more precious than gold, than much pure gold; they are sweeter than honey, than honey from the honeycomb. By them your servant is warned; in keeping them there is great reward. But who can discern their own errors? Forgive my hidden faults. Keep your servant also from willful sins; may they not rule over me. Then I will be blameless, innocent of great transgression. May these words of my mouth and this meditation of my heart be pleasing in your sight, Lord, my Rock and my Redeemer.

[A Psalm] of David; when he changed his demeanour before Abimelech, who drove him away, and he departed. I will bless the LORD at all times; His praise shall continually be in my mouth. My soul shall glory in the LORD; The humble shall hear thereof, and be glad. O magnify the LORD with me, And let us exalt His name together. I sought the LORD, and He answered me, And delivered me from all my fears. They looked unto Him, and were radiant; And their faces shall never be abashed. This poor man cried, and the LORD heard, And saved him out of all his troubles. The angel of the LORD encampeth round about them that fear Him, And delivereth them. O consider and see that the LORD is good; Happy is the man that taketh refuge in Him. O fear the LORD, ye His holy ones; For there is no want to them that fear Him. The young lions do lack, and suffer hunger; But they that seek the LORD want not any good thing. Come, ye children, hearken unto me; I will teach you the fear of the LORD. Who is the man that desireth life, and loveth days, That he may see good therein? Keep thy tongue from evil, And thy lips from speaking guile. Depart from evil, and do good; Seek peace, and pursue it. The eyes of the LORD are toward the righteous, And His ears are open unto their cry. The face of the LORD is against them that do evil, To cut off the remembrance of them from the earth. They cried, and the LORD heard, And delivered them out of all their troubles. The LORD is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart, And saveth such as are of a contrite spirit. Many are the ills of the righteous, But the LORD delivereth him out of them all. He keepeth all his bones; Not one of them is broken. Evil shall kill the wicked; And they that hate the righteous shall be held guilty. The LORD redeemeth the soul of His servants; And none of them that take refuge in Him shall be desolate.

Hallelujah. Praise ye the name of the LORD; Give praise, O ye servants of the LORD, Ye that stand in the house of the LORD, In the courts of the house of our God. Praise ye the LORD, for the LORD is good; Sing praises unto His name, for it is pleasant. For the LORD hath chosen Jacob unto Himself, And Israel for His own treasure. For I know that the LORD is great, And that our Lord is above all gods. Whatsoever the LORD pleased, that hath He done, In heaven and in earth, in the seas and in all deeps; Who causeth the vapours to ascend from the ends of the earth; He maketh lightnings for the rain; He bringeth forth the wind out of His treasuries. Who smote the first-born of Egypt, Both of man and beast. He sent signs and wonders into the midst of thee, O Egypt, Upon Pharaoh, and upon all his servants. Who smote many nations, And slew mighty kings: Sihon king of the Amorites, And Og king of Bashan, And all the kingdoms of Canaan; And gave their land for a heritage, A heritage unto Israel His people. O LORD, Thy name endureth for ever; Thy memorial, O LORD, throughout all generations. For the LORD will judge His people, And repent Himself for His servants. The idols of the nations are silver and gold, The work of men's hands. They have mouths, but they speak not; Eyes have they, but they see not; They have ears, but they hear not; Neither is there any breath in their mouths. They that make them shall be like unto them; Yea, every one that trusteth in them. O house of Israel, bless ye the LORD; O house of Aaron, bless ye the LORD; O house of Levi, bless ye the LORD; Ye that fear the LORD, bless ye the LORD. Blessed be the LORD out of Zion, Who dwelleth at Jerusalem. Hallelujah.

Rejoice in the LORD, O ye righteous, Praise is comely for the upright. Give thanks unto the LORD with harp, Sing praises unto Him with the psaltery of ten strings. Sing unto Him a new song; Play skilfully amid shouts of joy. For the word of the LORD is upright; And all His work is done in faithfulness. He loveth righteousness and justice; The earth is full of the lovingkindness of the LORD. By the word of the LORD were the heavens made; And all the host of them by the breath of His mouth. He gathereth the waters of the sea together as a heap; He layeth up the deeps in storehouses. Let all the earth fear the LORD; Let all the inhabitants of the world stand in awe of Him. For He spoke, and it was; He commanded, and it stood. The LORD bringeth the counsel of the nations to nought; He maketh the thoughts of the peoples to be of no effect. The counsel of the LORD standeth for ever, The thoughts of His heart to all generations. Happy is the nation whose God is the LORD; The people whom He hath chosen for His own inheritance. The LORD looketh from heaven; He beholdeth all the sons of men; From the place of His habitation He looketh intently Upon all the inhabitants of the earth; He that fashioneth the hearts of them all, That considereth all their doings. A king is not saved by the multitude of a host; A mighty man is not delivered by great strength. A horse is a vain thing for safety; Neither doth it afford escape by its great strength. Behold, the eye of the LORD is toward them that fear Him, Toward them that wait for His mercy; To deliver their soul from death, And to keep them alive in famine. Our soul hath waited for the LORD; He is our help and our shield. For in Him doth our heart rejoice, Because we have trusted in His holy name. Let Thy mercy, O LORD, be upon us, According as we have waited for Thee.

A Psalm, a song for the Shabbos day. It is good to thank Adonoy, and sing praise to Your Name, Most High. To relate Your kindliness in the morning, and Your faithfulness in the nights. Upon a ten-stringed instrument and lute, in meditation upon the harp. For You have given me joy, Adonoy, with Your deeds, at the work of Your hands I sing joyously. How great are Your works, Adonoy; how infinitely profound are Your thoughts. An empty-headed man cannot know, nor does a fool understand this: When the wicked bloom like grass, and all the evildoers blossom— it is so that they may be destroyed forever. But You will remain on high forever Adonoy. For behold, Your enemies, Adonoy; For behold, Your enemies shall perish; dispersed shall be all evildoers. You uplifted my horn like that of a unicorn; I am saturated with fresh oil. My eye has seen [the defeat of] those who spy on me; of the wicked who rise against me, my ears have heard [that they are doomed]. The righteous will blossom like a date palm, like a cedar in Lebanon, he will grow tall. Planted in the House of Adonoy, in the courtyards of our God they will blossom. They will still be fruitful in old age; they will be full of sap and freshness. To declare that Adonoy is upright; He is my Stronghold; in Whom there is no injustice.

Adonoy has begun His reign, with majesty He has clothed Himself; Adonoy clothed Himself, with strength He has girded Himself; He has firmly established the world, so that it cannot be moved. Your throne stands firm from of old, You are from eternity. The rivers have raised—Adonoy— the rivers have raised their voice, the rivers raise their raging waves. More than the roar of many waters, mightier than the breakers of the sea, mighty on high are You “Adonoy.” Your testimonies are extremely faithful; holiness is becoming to Your House, Adonoy,—for the length of days.

Fortunate are those who dwell in Your house; may they continue to praise You, Selah. Fortunate is the people whose lot is thus; fortunate is the people for whom Adonoy is their God. A praise by David! I will exalt You, my God, the King, and bless Your Name forever and ever. Every day I will bless You and extol Your Name forever and ever. Adonoy is great and highly extolled, and His greatness is unfathomable. One generation to another will praise Your works, and Your mighty acts they will declare. The splendor of Your glorious majesty, and the words of Your wonders I will speak. Of Your awesome might, they will speak, and Your greatness I will recount. Mention of Your bountifulness they will express, and in Your righteousness joyfully exult. Adonoy is gracious and merciful, slow to anger and great in kindliness. Adonoy is good to all, His mercy encompasses all His works. All Your works will thank You, Adonoy, and Your pious ones will bless You. Of the honor of Your kingship, they will speak, and Your might they will declare. To reveal to men His mighty acts, and the glorious splendor of His kingship. Your kingship is the kingship for all times, and Your dominion is in every generation. Adonoy supports all the fallen, and straightens all the bent. The eyes of all look expectantly to You, and You give them their food at its proper time. You open Your hand and satisfy the desire of every living being. Adonoy is just in all His ways and benevolent in all His deeds. Adonoy is near to all who call upon Him, to all who call upon Him in truth. The will of those who fear Him, He fulfills; He hears their cry and delivers them. Adonoy watches over all those who love Him, and will destroy all the wicked. Praise of Adonoy, my mouth will declare and all flesh will bless His holy Name forever and ever. And we will bless God from now forever. Praise God.

Praise God! My soul, praise Adonoy. I will praise Adonoy with my life; I will sing to my God as long as I live. Do not place your trust [even] in noble men, in man who has no [power of] deliverance. [When] his spirit departs, he returns to his earth; on that day his plans come to naught. Fortunate [is he] when the Almighty of Jacob is his help, whose expectation is on Adonoy, his God. He makes heaven and earth, the sea and all that is in them; He keeps His promises faithfully forever. He performs justice for the oppressed; He gives bread to the hungry; Adonoy releases the imprisoned. Adonoy gives sight to the blind; Adonoy straightens the bent. Adonoy loves the righteous. Adonoy protects strangers; the orphan and widow He enables to stand firm; and the way of the wicked He thwarts. Adonoy will reign forever; your God, Zion, throughout all generations. Praise God.

Blessed is Adonoy forever, Amein and Amein! Blessed is Adonoy from Zion, Who dwells in Jerusalem. Praise God. Blessed is Adonoy, God, God of Israel Who alone performs wonders. And blessed is the Name of His glory forever, and may His glory fill the whole earth. Amein and Amein!

On Shabbat Shuvah, this psalm is recited verse by verse. A Song of Ascents. Out of the depths I have called to You, Adonoy. My Master, hear my voice; let Your ears be attentive to the voice of my supplications. If You God should take account of iniquities, my Master, who could survive? For with You is forgiveness, in order that You be feared. I hope for Adonoy, my soul hopes; and for His word, I wait. My soul [waits] for my Master more than the watchman [waits] for the morning, [more than] the watchman [waits] for the morning. Wait, Israel, upon Adonoy, for with Adonoy there is loving-kindness, and with Him there is much redemption. And He will redeem Israel from all its iniquities.

Exalted and sanctified be His great Name in the world which He created according to His will and may He rule His kingdom. In your lifetime and in your days, and in the lifetime of the entire House of Israel, speedily and in the near future— and say Amein. May His great Name be blessed forever and for all eternity. Blessed and praised, glorified, and exalted and uplifted, honored and elevated and extolled be the Name of the Holy One, blessed is He; above (Ten Days of Penitence: far above) all the blessings and hymns, praises and consolations which we utter in the world—and say Amein.

May the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable before You, Lord, my Rock and my Redeemer. My God, guard my tongue from evil and my lips from speaking deceit. Let my soul be silent before those who curse me, and let my soul be like dust to all. Open my heart to Your Torah, and let my soul pursue Your commandments. As for all who plot evil against me, quickly nullify their counsel and frustrate their designs. Act for the sake of Your name; act for the sake of Your right hand; act for the sake of Your holiness; act for the sake of Your Torah. So that Your beloved may be rescued, save with Your right hand and answer me. May the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable before You, Lord, my Rock and my Redeemer. May He who makes peace [during the Ten Days of Repentance: 'the peace'] in His heights make peace upon us and upon all Israel; and say: Amen.

paragraphs.text: May it be Your will, Adonoy, our God, and the God of our Fathers that the Holy Temple be rebuilt speedily in our days, and grant us our share in Your Torah. And there we will serve You reverently as in the days of old, and in earlier years. And let Adonoy be pleased with the offerings of Judah and Jerusalem as in the days of old and in earlier years.

The Congregation responds: Yours, Adonoy, is the greatness, the might, the glory, the victory, and the beauty, for everything in heaven and on earth [is Yours]; Yours, Adonoy, is the kingdom, and You are uplifted over all rulers. Exalt Adonoy, our God, and prostrate yourselves at His footstool, Holy is He. Exalt Adonoy, Our God, and prostrate yourselves at His holy mountain for Adonoy, our God, is holy.

Blessed is He who spoke and the world came into being. Blessed is He. Blessed is He who made creation, who speaks and acts, who decrees and fulfills, who has compassion on the earth and on all creatures, who rewards those who revere Him, who lives forever and endures eternally, who redeems and rescues. Blessed is His name.

Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the universe: God, compassionate Father, praised by the mouth of His people, acclaimed and glorified by the tongues of His faithful servants. With the songs of David Your servant we praise You, Lord our God, in praises and melodies. We magnify, exalt, and glorify You and proclaim Your name, our King and our God, the One, the Life of all worlds. The great name of the King is praised and glorified forever. Blessed are You, Lord, King acclaimed in songs of praise.
paragraphs.note: Original English working translation aligned to the full Hebrew paragraph; specialist review pending.

paragraphs.text: The prayer leader places the Torah scroll on the reading platform and says: May He help, protect, and save all who trust in Him, and let us say: Amen. All: Ascribe greatness to our God and give honor to the Torah. Let the kohen come forward; let [name], son of [name], the kohen, stand. Blessed is He who gave the Torah to His people Israel in holiness.

[For the mother of a boy:] May the One who blessed our ancestors Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, Moses and Aaron, David and Solomon, and Sarah, Rebecca, Rachel and Leah, bless the mother [name], daughter of [name], and the son born to her at an auspicious time. As her husband, the child's father, pledges charity on their behalf, may the parents merit to bring him into the covenant of Abraham our father and raise him to Torah, marriage, and good deeds. And let us say: Amen.
paragraphs.note: Original English working translation aligned to the full Hebrew paragraph; specialist review pending.

paragraphs.text: [For the mother of a girl:] May the One who blessed our ancestors Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, Moses and Aaron, David and Solomon, and Sarah, Rebecca, Rachel and Leah, bless the mother [name], daughter of [name], and the daughter born to her at an auspicious time. Let the girl be named in Israel [name], daughter of [name]. As her husband, the child's father, pledges charity for them, may the parents merit to raise her to Torah, marriage, and good deeds. And let us say: Amen.
paragraphs.note: Original English working translation aligned to the full Hebrew paragraph; specialist review pending.

paragraphs.text: We kindle these lights because of the miracles, wonders, acts of deliverance, and battles that You performed for our ancestors in those days at this season, through Your holy priests. Throughout the eight days of Hanukkah these lights are sacred. We are not permitted to make ordinary use of them, but only to look at them, so that we may thank and praise Your great name for Your miracles, wonders, and salvation.
paragraphs.note: Original English working translation aligned to the full Hebrew paragraph; specialist review pending.

paragraphs.text: May His great name be exalted and sanctified [the Vilna Gaon's reading varies in vocalization]. (Amen.) In the world He created according to His will, may He establish His kingdom in your lifetimes and days and in the lifetime of the entire house of Israel, speedily and soon; and say, Amen. (Amen.) May His great name be blessed forever and throughout all eternity. Blessed, praised, glorified, exalted, uplifted, honored, raised high and extolled be the name of the Holy One, blessed be He. (Blessed be He.) Above every blessing, song, praise and consolation uttered in the world [during the Ten Days of Repentance: far, far above them]; and say, Amen. (Amen.) [Congregation: Receive our prayer with mercy and favor.] May the prayers and petitions of all Israel be accepted before their Father in heaven; and say, Amen. (Amen.) [Congregation: Blessed be the name of the Lord from now and forever.] May abundant peace from heaven and life be granted us and all Israel; and say, Amen. (Amen.) [Congregation: My help comes from the Lord, Maker of heaven and earth.] May He who makes peace [during the Ten Days of Repentance: the peace] in His heights make peace upon us and all Israel; and say, Amen. (Amen.)
