[Congregation: My help comes from the Lord, Maker of heaven and earth.] May He who makes peace [during the Ten Days of Repentance: the peace] in His heights make peace upon us and all Israel; and say, Amen. (Amen.)
paragraphs.note: Identical Hebrew passage to ashkenaz Kaddish Shalem paragraph 0; verify typography and liturgical placement.

paragraphs.text: O give thanks unto the LORD, for He is good, For His mercy endureth for ever. . O give thanks unto the God of gods, For His mercy endureth for ever. O give thanks unto the Lord of lords, For His mercy endureth for ever. To Him who alone doeth great wonders, For His mercy endureth for ever. To Him that by understanding made the heavens, for His mercy endureth for ever. To Him that spread forth the earth above the waters, For His mercy endureth for ever. To Him that made great lights, For His mercy endureth for ever; The sun to rule by day, For His mercy endureth for ever; The moon and stars to rule by night, For His mercy endureth for ever. To Him that smote Egypt in their first-born, For His mercy endureth for ever; And brought out Israel from among them, For His mercy endureth for ever; With a strong hand, and with an outstretched arm, For His mercy endureth for ever. To Him who divided the Red Sea in sunder, For His mercy endureth for ever; And made Israel to pass through the midst of it, For His mercy endureth for ever; But overthrew Pharaoh and his host in the Red Sea, For His mercy endureth for ever. To Him that led His people through the wilderness, For His mercy endureth for ever. To Him that smote great kings; For His mercy endureth for ever; And slew mighty kings, For His mercy endureth for ever. Sihon king of the Amorites, For His mercy endureth for ever; And Og king of Bashan, For His mercy endureth for ever; And gave their land for a heritage, For His mercy endureth for ever; Even a heritage unto Israel His servant, For His mercy endureth for ever. Who remembered us in our low estate, For His mercy endureth for ever; And hath delivered us from our adversaries, For His mercy endureth for ever. Who giveth food to all flesh, For His mercy endureth for ever. O give thanks unto the God of heaven, For His mercy endureth for ever.
paragraphs.note: Public-domain JPS 1917 biblical passage; Hebrew text aligned, with Siddur-specific omission instruction.

paragraphs.text: Let the living God be magnified and praised: He exists, and no time limits His existence. He is One, with a unity like no other; He is hidden, and His oneness has no end. He has neither body nor bodily form; His holiness cannot be compared. He preceded everything created, the First, whose beginning has no beginning. Behold, He is Master of the world and all that was formed, revealing His greatness and His kingship. He bestowed the abundance of His prophecy upon His treasured, glorious people. Never again has there arisen in Israel a prophet like Moses, who gazed upon His likeness. God gave His people the Torah of truth through His prophet, faithful in all His house. God will neither exchange His Torah nor replace it with another, ever. He watches and knows our secrets; from the beginning He sees the end of all things. He rewards a person with loving-kindness according to their deeds and gives the wicked the consequence of their wickedness. At the end of days He will send our Messiah to redeem those awaiting His salvation. In abundant mercy God will revive the dead; blessed forever be His name of praise.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Master of the universe, who reigned before any creature was formed; when all was made according to His will, then His name was called King. After all things cease to be, He alone will reign in awe. He was, He is, and He shall be in glory. He is One, without a second to be compared or joined to Him; without beginning or end, His are power and dominion. He is my God and my living Redeemer, the Rock of my portion in distress. He is my banner and my refuge, my allotted cup on the day I call. Into His hand I entrust my spirit when I sleep and when I wake; with my spirit, my body too. The Lord is with me; I shall not fear.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: [Mourner's Kaddish. Mourner:] Magnified and sanctified be His great name. [Congregation: Amen.] In the world He created according to His will, may He establish His kingdom in your lifetime, in your days, and in the lifetime of all the house of Israel, speedily and soon; and say, Amen. [Congregation: Amen.] [Mourner and congregation:] May His great name be blessed forever and to all eternity. [Mourner:] Blessed, praised, glorified, exalted, uplifted, honored, elevated and acclaimed be the name of the Holy One, blessed be He. [Congregation: Blessed be He.] Above every blessing [during the Ten Days of Repentance: far above every blessing], song, praise and consolation spoken in the world; and say, Amen. [Congregation: Amen.] May abundant peace from heaven and life be upon us and upon all Israel; and say, Amen. [Congregation: Amen.] May He who makes peace [during the Ten Days of Repentance: the peace] in His heights make peace upon us and all Israel; and say, Amen. [Congregation: Amen.]
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: [After the Haftarah blessings:] May deliverance arise from heaven: grace, kindness and mercy, long life, generous sustenance, heavenly help, bodily health, a clear light, and living descendants who endure and never cease from the words of Torah, for our masters and rabbis, the holy company in the land of Israel and in Babylonia, the heads of academies and the exilarchs, the heads of study houses and judges at the gates, their disciples and disciples' disciples, and all who occupy themselves with Torah. May the King of the world bless them, lengthen their lives, increase their days, and grant them many years. May they be redeemed and rescued from all distress and illness. May our Master in heaven be their help at every time and season. And let us say: Amen.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: [One praying alone at home does not say this Yekum Purkan or the following Mi Sheberach.] May salvation arise from heaven, with grace, kindness and mercy, long life, generous sustenance, heavenly help, bodily health, clear light, and living descendants who endure and do not cease from the words of Torah, for this entire holy congregation, elders with youngsters, children and women. May the King of the universe bless you, lengthen your lives, multiply your days and years, and rescue and deliver you from all distress and illness. May our Master in heaven be your help at all times and seasons. And let us say: Amen.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: [Blessing for the congregation:] May He who blessed our ancestors Abraham, Isaac and Jacob bless this entire holy congregation together with all holy communities—them, their wives, sons and daughters, and all they possess; those who dedicate synagogues for prayer, those who enter them to pray, those who provide lights for illumination, wine for Kiddush and Havdalah, bread for guests and charity for the poor, and all who faithfully serve the needs of the community. May the Holy One, blessed be He, reward them, remove every illness, heal their bodies, forgive all their sins, and send blessing and success to all the work of their hands together with all their brothers and sisters of Israel. And let us say: Amen.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: May He who blessed our ancestors Abraham, Isaac and Jacob bless [name], son or daughter of [name], who was called to the Torah for the honor of the Omnipresent, the Torah, and [on Shabbat: the Sabbath; on a festival: the festival; on Rosh Hashanah or Yom Kippur: the Day of Judgment]. In the merit of this, may the Holy One, blessed be He, protect and deliver this person from every trouble, distress, affliction and illness, and send blessing and success in all their endeavors. [On festivals: May they merit to make pilgrimage.] [On Rosh Hashanah and Yom Kippur: May they be inscribed and sealed for a good life on this Day of Judgment,] together with all their fellow Israelites. And let us say: Amen.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: [For a male patient:] May He who blessed our ancestors Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, Moses and Aaron, David and Solomon bless the sick person [name], son of [mother's name], because [donor's name] pledges charity on his behalf. In this merit may the Holy One, blessed be He, be filled with compassion to strengthen, heal, restore and sustain him, and speedily send complete healing from heaven to all his 248 limbs and 365 sinews, together with all the sick of Israel: healing of spirit and healing of body. [On Shabbat: Shabbat is a time to refrain from crying out, and healing is near to come.] [On a festival: The festival is a time to refrain from crying out, and healing is near to come.] Now, swiftly and soon. And let us say: Amen.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: [For a female patient:] May He who blessed our ancestors Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, Moses and Aaron, David and Solomon bless the sick person [name], daughter of [mother's name], because [donor's name] pledges charity on her behalf. In this merit may the Holy One, blessed be He, be filled with compassion to strengthen, heal, restore and sustain her, and speedily send complete healing from heaven to every limb and sinew of her body, together with all the sick of Israel: healing of spirit and healing of body. [On Shabbat: Shabbat is a time to refrain from crying out, and healing is near to come.] [On a festival: The festival is a time to refrain from crying out, and healing is near to come.] Now, swiftly and soon. And let us say: Amen.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: May He who blessed our ancestors Abraham, Isaac and Jacob, Joseph, Moses and Aaron, David and Solomon bless, safeguard and protect all those abducted, held captive or missing, together with our fellow Israelites who are in distress and captivity. Because the congregation prays on their behalf, may the Holy One, blessed be He, show them compassion, bring them out of darkness and the shadow of death, break their bonds, rescue them from their suffering, and return them quickly to the embrace of their families. Let them thank the Lord for His loving-kindness and for His wonders toward humankind. May the verse be fulfilled in them: 'The redeemed of the Lord shall return and come to Zion with song, and everlasting joy shall be upon their heads; they shall attain gladness and joy, and sorrow and sighing shall flee away.' And let us say: Amen.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: [Mourner's Kaddish. Mourner:] Magnified and sanctified be His great name. [Congregation: Amen.] In the world He created according to His will, may He establish His kingdom in your lifetime, in your days, and in the lifetime of all the house of Israel, speedily and soon; and say, Amen. [Congregation: Amen.] [Mourner and congregation:] May His great name be blessed forever and to all eternity. [Mourner:] Blessed, praised, glorified, exalted, uplifted, honored, elevated and acclaimed be the name of the Holy One, blessed be He. [Congregation: Blessed be He.] Above every blessing [during the Ten Days of Repentance: far above every blessing], song, praise and consolation spoken in the world; and say, Amen. [Congregation: Amen.] May abundant peace from heaven and life be upon us and upon all Israel; and say, Amen. [Congregation: Amen.] May He who makes peace [during the Ten Days of Repentance: the peace] in His heights make peace upon us and all Israel; and say, Amen. [Congregation: Amen.]
paragraphs.note: Identical Hebrew passage to ashkenaz Mourner's Kaddish paragraph 0; specialist review pending.

paragraphs.text: It is true, established, certain, right, faithful, beloved, cherished, precious, pleasant, awesome, mighty, proper, accepted, good and beautiful—this word is ours for ever and ever. True it is: our eternal God and King, the Rock of Jacob and Shield of our salvation, endures from generation to generation. His name endures, His throne is established, and His reign and faithfulness endure forever. His words are living and enduring, faithful and treasured throughout all ages and for all eternity.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: For our ancestors and for us, for our children and all our generations, for every generation of the descendants of Israel, Your servants, both the earliest and the latest, this good word stands forever and ever: truth and faithfulness, a decree that shall not pass. Truly You are the Lord our God and God of our ancestors, our King and the King of our ancestors, our Redeemer and the Redeemer of our ancestors, our Creator, the Rock of our salvation, our Deliverer and Rescuer. Your name has been so from eternity; there is no god besides You.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: From eternity You have been the help of our ancestors, the shield and deliverer of their children after them, in each and every generation. Your dwelling is in the heights of the world, yet Your judgments and righteousness reach the ends of the earth. Happy is the person who heeds Your commandments and takes Your Torah and word to heart. Truly You are the Lord of Your people, the mighty King who pleads their cause. Truly You are the first and the last; apart from You we have no king, redeemer or savior. From Egypt You redeemed us, Lord our God, and from the house of slavery You delivered us. You slew all their firstborn and redeemed Your own firstborn. You split the Sea of Reeds, drowned the arrogant, and led Your beloved through. The waters covered their enemies; not one of them remained. Therefore the beloved praised and exalted God, offering songs, hymns, praises, blessings and thanksgiving to the King, the living and enduring God, high and exalted, great and awesome, who humbles the proud and raises the lowly, frees captives, redeems the humble, helps the poor, and answers His people when they cry out to Him. Praises to the Most High God, blessed and praised is He. Moses and the children of Israel answered You in song with great joy, and all said: 'Who is like You among the mighty, Lord? Who is like You, glorious in holiness, awesome in praise, doing wonders?' The redeemed sang a new song to Your name on the seashore. Together they gave thanks, proclaimed Your kingship and said: 'The Lord shall reign forever and ever.' Rock of Israel, rise up to help Israel, and as You promised, redeem Judah and Israel. 'Our Redeemer, the Lord of hosts is His name, the Holy One of Israel.' Blessed are You, Lord, who redeemed Israel.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: May the glory of the Lord endure forever; may the Lord rejoice in His works. Blessed be the name of the Lord from this time forth and forevermore. From the rising of the sun to its setting, the name of the Lord is praised. High above all nations is the Lord; above the heavens is His glory. Lord, Your name endures forever, Your remembrance throughout all generations. The Lord established His throne in heaven, and His kingdom rules over all. Let the heavens rejoice and the earth be glad; let them proclaim among the nations: The Lord reigns. The Lord is King, the Lord was King, the Lord will reign forever and ever. The Lord is King for ever and ever; nations vanish from His earth. The Lord frustrates the counsel of nations and thwarts the designs of peoples. Many are the plans in a person's heart, but the counsel of the Lord shall stand. The counsel of the Lord stands forever, the thoughts of His heart throughout all generations. For He spoke and it came to be; He commanded, and it stood firm. For the Lord chose Zion and desired it for His dwelling. For the Lord chose Jacob for Himself, Israel as His treasured possession. For the Lord will not abandon His people nor forsake His heritage. He is compassionate, forgiving iniquity without destroying; again and again He turns back His anger and does not stir up His full wrath. Save us, Lord! May the King answer us on the day we call.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: O give thanks unto the LORD, call upon His name; Make known His doings among the peoples. Sing unto Him, sing praises unto Him; Speak ye of all His marvellous works. Glory ye in His holy name; Let the heart of them rejoice that seek the LORD. Seek ye the LORD and His strength; Seek His face continually. Remember His marvellous works that He hath done, His wonders, and the judgments of His mouth; O ye seed of Israel His servant, Ye children of Jacob, His chosen ones. He is the LORD our God; His judgments are in all the earth. Remember His covenant for ever, The word which He commanded to a thousand generations; [The covenant] which He made with Abraham, And His oath unto Isaac; And He established it unto Jacob for a statute, To Israel for an everlasting covenant; Saying: ‘Unto thee will I give the land of Canaan, The lot of your inheritance.’ When ye were but a few men in number, Yea, very few, and sojourners in it, And when they went about from nation to nation, And from one kingdom to another people, He suffered no man to do them wrong, Yea, for their sake He reproved kings: ’Touch not Mine anointed ones, And do My prophets no harm.’ Sing unto the LORD, all the earth; Proclaim His salvation from day to day. Declare His glory among the nations, His marvellous works among all the peoples. For great is the LORD, and highly to be praised; He also is to be feared above all gods. For all the gods of the peoples are things of nought; But the LORD made the heavens. Honour and majesty are before Him; Strength and gladness are in His place. Ascribe unto the LORD, ye kindreds of the peoples, Ascribe unto the LORD glory and strength. Ascribe unto the LORD the glory due unto His name; Bring an offering, and come before Him; Worship the LORD in the beauty of holiness. Tremble before Him, all the earth; The world also is established that it cannot be moved. Let the heavens be glad, and let the earth rejoice; And let them say among the nations: ‘The LORD reigneth.’ Let the sea roar, and the fulness thereof; Let the field exult, and all that is therein; Then shall the trees of the wood sing for joy, Before the LORD, for He is come to judge the earth. O give thanks unto the LORD; for He is good; For His mercy endureth for ever. And say ye: ‘Save us, O God of our salvation, And gather us together and deliver us from the nations, That we may give thanks unto Thy holy name, That we may triumph in Thy praise.’ Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, From everlasting even to everlasting. And all the people said: ‘Amen, ‘and praised the LORD. Exalt the Lord our God, and bow down at His footstool; holy is He. Exalt the Lord our God and bow down at His holy mountain, for holy is the Lord our God. He, being compassionate, forgives iniquity and does not destroy; many times He turns away His anger and does not stir up all His wrath. You, Lord, will not withhold Your mercies from me; may Your loving-kindness and truth continually preserve me. Remember Your mercies, Lord, and Your acts of loving-kindness, for they are from everlasting. Give strength to God, whose majesty is over Israel and whose strength is in the skies. Awesome is God from Your sanctuaries, the God of Israel, who gives strength and might to the people. Blessed be God. Lord, God of vengeance; God of vengeance, shine forth! Rise up, Judge of the earth; repay the arrogant according to their deserts. Salvation belongs to the Lord; upon Your people be Your blessing, Selah. The Lord of hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge, Selah. Lord of hosts, happy is the one who trusts in You. Save us, Lord; may the King answer us on the day we call. Save Your people and bless Your inheritance; shepherd them and carry them forever. Our soul has waited for the Lord; He is our help and our shield. For in Him our heart rejoices, because we have trusted in His holy name. May Your loving-kindness, Lord, be upon us, as we have waited for You. Show us Your loving-kindness, Lord, and grant us Your salvation. Arise as our help and redeem us for the sake of Your loving-kindness. I am the Lord your God, who brought you up from the land of Egypt; open your mouth wide and I will fill it. Happy is the people for whom this is so; happy is the people whose God is the Lord. But I have trusted in Your loving-kindness; my heart shall rejoice in Your salvation. I shall sing to the Lord, because He has dealt bountifully with me.
paragraphs.ref: JPS 1917 I Chronicles 16:8–36 plus source-aligned Psalms selections
paragraphs.note: Opening 29 verses verified against the bundled JPS Hebrew chapter; remaining psalm selections translated independently in source order.

paragraphs.text: From the first of Elul until after Shemini Atzeret, recite this Psalm: [A Psalm] of David. The LORD is my light and my salvation; whom shall I fear? The LORD is the stronghold of my life; of whom shall I be afraid? When evil-doers came upon me to eat up my flesh, Even mine adversaries and my foes, they stumbled and fell. Though a host should encamp against me, My heart shall not fear; Though war should rise up against me, Even then will I be confident. One thing have I asked of the LORD, that will I seek after: That I may dwell in the house of the LORD all the days of my life, To behold the graciousness of the LORD, and to visit early in His temple. For He concealeth me in His pavilion in the day of evil; He hideth me in the covert of His tent; He lifteth me up upon a rock. . And now shall my head be lifted up above mine enemies round about me; And I will offer in His tabernacle sacrifices with trumpet-sound; I will sing, yea, I will sing praises unto the LORD. Hear, O LORD, when I call with my voice, And be gracious unto me, and answer me. In Thy behalf my heart hath said: ‘Seek ye My face'; Thy face, LORD, will I seek. Hide not Thy face far from me; Put not Thy servant away in anger; Thou hast been my help; Cast me not off, neither forsake me, O God of my salvation. For though my father and my mother have forsaken me, The LORD will take me up. Teach me Thy way, O LORD; And lead me in an even path, Because of them that lie in wait for me. Deliver me not over unto the will of mine adversaries; For false witnesses are risen up against me, and such as breathe out violence. If I had not believed to look upon the goodness of the LORD In the land of the living!— Wait on the LORD; Be strong, and let thy heart take courage; Yea, wait thou for the LORD.
paragraphs.note: Public-domain JPS 1917 English aligned with the original Hebrew; any liturgical instructions are supplied by the project.

paragraphs.text: The soul of every living being shall bless Your name, Lord our God, and the spirit of all flesh shall always glorify and exalt Your remembrance, our King. From eternity to eternity You are God. Apart from You we have no King who redeems and saves, delivers and rescues, sustains and shows compassion in every time of trouble and distress. We have no King who helps and supports us but You. God of the first and last generations, God of every creature, Master of all creation, praised with abundant praises, who governs His world with kindness and His creatures with compassion! The Lord neither slumbers nor sleeps. He awakens those who sleep, rouses those who slumber, enables the mute to speak, frees the bound, supports the fallen and straightens those who are bent. You alone we thank. Even if our mouths were filled with song as the sea, our tongues with rejoicing as its countless waves, our lips with praise as the breadth of the heavens, our eyes shone like the sun and moon, our hands were outstretched like the eagles of heaven, and our feet were swift as deer, we could not thank You, Lord our God and God of our ancestors, nor bless Your name for even one of the thousands upon thousands, myriad myriads of benefits You have done for our ancestors and for us. You redeemed us from Egypt, Lord our God, and freed us from the house of slavery. In famine You fed us, in plenty You sustained us, from the sword You rescued us, from pestilence You delivered us, and from grave and enduring illnesses You raised us up. To this day Your mercies have helped us and Your kindness has not abandoned us. Do not forsake us, Lord our God, forever. Therefore the limbs You fashioned within us, the spirit and soul You breathed into our nostrils, and the tongue You placed in our mouth shall thank, bless, praise, glorify, exalt, revere, sanctify and proclaim the sovereignty of Your name, our King. For every mouth shall thank You, every tongue shall swear by You, every knee shall bend before You, every upright body shall bow before You, every heart shall fear You, and every inward part shall sing praise to Your name, as it is written: 'All my bones shall say: Lord, who is like You, who rescues the poor from one stronger than he, the poor and needy from one who robs him?' Who is like You, who is equal to You, who can be compared with You, great, mighty and awesome God, Most High God, Creator of heaven and earth? We will praise, glorify and exalt You and bless Your holy name, as it is said: 'Of David. Bless the Lord, O my soul; let all that is within me bless His holy name!'
paragraphs.note: New English working translation reviewed against the Hebrew and available Russian text; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: A redeemer shall come to Zion, and to those who turn from transgression in Jacob, says the Lord. 'As for Me, this is My covenant with them, says the Lord: My spirit which is upon you and My words which I have placed in your mouth shall not depart from your mouth, or from the mouths of your children, or from the mouths of your children's children, says the Lord, from now and forever.' But You are holy, enthroned upon the praises of Israel. They called to one another and said: 'Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of Hosts; the whole earth is full of His glory.' And they receive permission from one another and say: 'Holy in the highest heavens, the abode of His Presence; holy upon earth, the work of His might; holy for ever and ever is the Lord of Hosts, the whole earth is filled with the radiance of His glory.' A spirit lifted me up, and I heard behind me the sound of a great rushing: 'Blessed be the glory of the Lord from His place!' A spirit lifted me, and I heard behind me the voice of a mighty commotion of those who praise and say: 'Blessed be the glory of the Lord from the place of His Presence!' The Lord shall reign forever, your God, O Zion, through every generation. Hallelujah! May He establish His kingdom, reveal His salvation, and bring His Messiah near. May He save His people in your lifetime, in your days, and in the lifetime of all the house of Israel, swiftly and soon; and let us say: Amen. 'The Lord shall reign forever, your God, O Zion, through every generation. Hallelujah!' Lord, God of Abraham, Isaac and Israel, our ancestors, preserve this forever as the inclination of the hearts of Your people and direct their hearts toward You. He, the Merciful One, pardons wrongdoing and does not destroy; many times He turns back His anger and does not stir up all His wrath. For You, Lord, are good and forgiving, abundant in kindness toward all who call upon You. Your righteousness is righteousness forever, and Your Torah is truth. Grant truth to Jacob and kindness to Abraham, as You swore to our ancestors in days of old. Blessed be the Lord day by day; He bears our burdens, the God of our salvation, Selah. The Lord of Hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge, Selah. Lord of Hosts, happy is the person who trusts in You! Lord, save us; may the King answer us on the day we call. Blessed is our God, who created us for His glory, separated us from those who stray, and gave us the Torah of truth. May He open our hearts to His Torah, instill in us love and awe of Him, that we may do His will and serve Him wholeheartedly, so that we neither labor in vain nor bring forth children for turmoil. May it be Your will, Lord our God and God of our ancestors, that we keep Your statutes in this world and merit to live, to see, and to inherit goodness and blessing in the days of the Messiah and in the life of the world to come. 'That my soul may sing praise to You and not be silent; Lord my God, I will thank You forever.' Blessed is the person who trusts in the Lord and whose confidence is the Lord. Trust in the Lord forever, for in the Lord is an everlasting Rock. Those who hope in the Lord shall renew their strength, rise on wings like eagles, run and not grow weary, walk and not become faint. May the Lord our God help us and bless us, as He blessed our fathers Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, in everything, from everything, with everything. Thus may He bless us together with a complete blessing, and let us say: Amen. May the favor of the Lord our God be upon us; establish for us the work of our hands, and establish the work of our hands. May the name of the Lord be blessed from now and forever. 'The Lord desires, for the sake of His righteousness, to magnify the Torah and make it glorious.'
paragraphs.note: New English working translation reviewed against the Hebrew and available Russian text; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs: Prayers upon Awakening
Modeh Ani
When waking up from sleep, before washing hands, one should say:
I am thankful before You, living and enduring King, for you have mercifully restored my soul within me. Great is Your faithfulness.
Morning Blessings
After washing hands, but before drying them, one says this blessing (and if someone was awake all night - they do not make this blessing, but only wash):
Blessed are You, Hashem, our God, King of the universe, Who has sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us regarding the raising of hands [i.e., washing]:
Every time a person goes to the bathroom, they should afterwards [wash hands] and say the Asher Yatzar blessing:

Blessed are You, Hashem, our God, King of the Universe, Who formed man with wisdom and created many openings and cavities within him. It is obvious and known before Your throne of glory that if any one of them were closed or if one of any one them were opened, it would be impossible to exist for even an hour [i.e., a short while]. Blessed are You, Hashem, Who heals all flesh and does wondrous things.
The Alo-hai Neshama blessing should immediately follow the Asher Yatzar blessing

My God, the soul that you placed within me is pure. You created it, You formed it, You breathed it into me, and You preserve it within me. And in the future, You will take it from me and restore it in the Time to Come. All the time that this soul is within me, I am thankful before You, Hashem, my God and the God of my fathers, Ruler of all creation, Lord of all the souls. Blessed are You, Hashem, Who restores souls to dead bodies.
Blessed are You, Hashem, King of the Universe, Who gives the rooster [alt. heart] the understanding to distinguish between day and between night.
Blessed are You, Hashem, King of the Universe, Who gives sight to the blind.
Blessed are You, Hashem, King of the Universe, Who releases the bound.
Blessed are You, Hashem, King of the Universe, Who straitens the bent.
Blessed are You, Hashem, King of the Universe, Who clothes the naked.
Blessed are You, Hashem, King of the Universe, who gives strength to the weary.
Blessed are You, Hashem, King of the Universe, Who spreads the earth over the waters.
Blessed are You, Hashem, King of the Universe, Who prepares the steps of man.
On Tisha B'Av and Yom Kippur, the "Provided for me all my needs" blessing is not said. But for those who have the custom to say it then, they have whom to rely on.
Blessed are You, Hashem, King of the Universe, Who has provided for me all of my needs.
Blessed are You, Hashem, King of the Universe, Who girds Israel with might.
Blessed are You, Hashem, King of the Universe, who crowns Israel with glory.
Blessed are You, Hashem, King of the Universe, Who did not make me a gentile. (A woman says: gentile woman)
Blessed are You, Hashem, King of the Universe, Who did not make me a slave. (A woman says: maid-servant)...
A man blesses
Blessed are You, Hashem, King of the Universe, Who did not make me a woman.
A woman blesses without pronouncing Hashem's name and Kingship
Blessed is He Who made me according to His Will.

Blessed are You, Hashem, King of the Universe, Who removes the bonds of sleep from my eyes and the slumber from my eyelids. And may it be Your will, Hashem, my God and God of my fathers, that You accustom me in Your Torah and attach me to Your commandments. And do not bring me to sin, nor to iniquity, nor to be tested, nor to be disgraced. And distance me from the evil inclination and attach me to the good inclination. And compel my inclination to serve You. And grant me today, and everyday, grace, loving-kindness, and compassion in Your eyes and in the eyes of all who see me, and bestow upon me good kindnesses. Blessed are You, Hashem, Who bestows good kindnesses to His nation, Israel.

May it be the will, before You, Hashem, my God and the God of my fathers, that You spare me today and every single day, from the arrogant, and from arrogance, from an evil man, from the evil inclination, from an evil friend, from an evil companion, from a bad mishap, from the evil eye, from slander, from a difficult judgment, and from a difficult accuser, whether he is a Jew or whether he is not a Jew.
Blessings of the Torah
Blessed are You, Hashem, King of the Universe, Who has sanctified us with His commandments and has commanded us regarding the words of the Torah.

And sweeten for us, Hashem, our God, the words of Torah in our mouths and in the mouths of Your nation, the House of Israel. And let us and our offspring, and our offspring's offspring, and the offspring of Your nation, the House of Israel - all know Your name, learn Your Torah for its own sake. Blessed are You, Hashem, who teaches Torah to His nation Israel.
Blessed are You, Hashem, King of the Universe, who chose us from all the nations and gave us His Torah. Blessed are You, Hashem, Who gives the Torah.

Hashem spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to Aaron and to his sons, saying: So shall you bless the children of Israel. Say to them: May Hashem bless you and guard them. May Hashem illuminate His countenance upon you and be gracious to you. May Hashem lift His countenance toward you and give you peace. They shall place My name upon the children of Israel and I will bless them.

paragraphs.text: Order of Tikkun Chatzot (Midnight Lamentations).

For the sake of uniting the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Presence, in awe and love, and in love and awe, to unite the name Yod–Heh with Vav–Heh in perfect unity, in the name of all Israel: I am ready to recite Tikkun Rachel and Tikkun Leah. On the specified days recite Tikkun Leah; during the Three Weeks recite Tikkun Rachel, as our sages of blessed memory arranged for us, to repair their spiritual root (or one's own root) in the highest realm, to bring delight to our Maker and fulfill our Creator's will. 'May the favor of the Lord our God be upon us; establish the work of our hands for us; yes, establish the work of our hands.' Repeat this last verse twice.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Please, LORD our God and God of our fathers, may our prayer come before You, and do not ignore, our King, our supplication. For we are not so brazen and stiff-necked as to say before You, LORD our God and God of our fathers, that we are righteous and have not sinned. Rather, we have sinned, we have committed iniquity, we have transgressed — we, our fathers, and the members of our households. We have incurred guilt; we have betrayed; we have robbed; we have spoken slander and evil speech; we have acted perversely and wickedly; we have acted presumptuously; we have done violence; we have attached ourselves to falsehood and deceit; we have given evil counsel; we have lied; we have become angry; we have mocked; we have rebelled; we have disobeyed Your words; we have provoked; we have committed adultery; we have turned aside; we have committed iniquity; we have transgressed; we have damaged; we have oppressed; we have caused pain to father and mother; we have been stiff-necked; we have acted wickedly; we have corrupted; we have acted abominably; we have strayed and led others astray. We have turned away from Your commandments and Your good judgments, and it has not benefited us. You are righteous in all that has come upon us, for You have acted truthfully, while we have acted wickedly.
paragraphs.note: Kavvanah reviewed Siddur translation (2026).

paragraphs.text: What can we say before You, Dweller on high, and what can we recount before You, whose dwelling is in the skies? You know both the hidden and the revealed; You know the secrets of the world and the mysteries concealed within every living being. You search every innermost chamber and examine heart and conscience. Nothing is hidden from You, and nothing is concealed from Your eyes. May it be Your will, LORD our God and God of our ancestors, to pardon all our sins, atone for all our iniquities, and forgive all our transgressions.
Tikkun Rachel.

By the rivers of Babylon, there we sat and we also wept, when we remembered Zion. Upon the willows in its midst, we hung our harps. For there our captors demanded of us words of song, and our tormentors asked of us [with] mirth; Sing to us from the song[s] of Zion. How shall we sing the song of Adonoy on alien soil? If I ever forget you, Jerusalem, may my right hand forget [its movement]. May my tongue cleave to my palate, if I remember you not; if I set not Jerusalem above my highest joy. Remember, Adonoy, to the sons of Edom the day of Jerusalem, [it was they] who said, Raze it, raze it to its very foundation. Daughter of Babylon, you are the annihilated one; fortunate is he who will repay you for all you have done to us. Fortunate is he who will take and dash your little ones against the rock.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: A Psalm of Asaph. O God, the heathen are come into Thine inheritance; They have defiled Thy holy temple; They have made Jerusalem into heaps. They have given the dead bodies of Thy servants to be food unto the fowls of the heaven, The flesh of Thy saints unto the beasts of the earth. They have shed their blood like water Round about Jerusalem, with none to bury them. We are become a taunt to our neighbours, A scorn and derision to them that are round about us. How long, O LORD, wilt Thou be angry for ever? How long will Thy jealousy burn like fire? Pour out Thy wrath upon the nations that know Thee not, And upon the kingdoms that call not upon Thy name. For they have devoured Jacob, And laid waste his habitation. Remember not against us the iniquities of our forefathers; Let Thy compassions speedily come to meet us; For we are brought very low. Help us, O God of our salvation, for the sake of the glory of Thy name; And deliver us, and forgive our sins, for Thy name's sake. Wherefore should the nations say: 'Where is their God?' Let the avenging of Thy servants' blood that is shed Be made known among the nations in our sight. . Let the groaning of the prisoner come before Thee; According to the greatness of Thy power set free those that are appointed to death; And render unto our neighbours sevenfold into their bosom Their reproach, wherewith they have reproached Thee, O Lord. So we that are Thy people and the flock of Thy pasture Will give Thee thanks for ever; We will tell of Thy praise to all generations.
paragraphs.note: Every colon-delimited fragment matched a unique near-exact complete Tanakh verse; reviewed orthographic/qere alignment only.

paragraphs.text:
Remember, O LORD, what is come upon us; Behold, and see our reproach. Our inheritance is turned unto strangers, Our houses unto aliens. We are become orphans and fatherless, Our mothers are as widows. We have drunk our water for money; Our wood cometh to us for price. To our very necks we are pursued; We labour, and have no rest. We have given the hand to Egypt, And to Assyria, to have bread enough; Our fathers have sinned, and are not; And we have borne their iniquities. Servants rule over us; There is none to deliver us out of their hand. We get our bread with the peril of our lives Because of the sword of the wilderness. Our skin is hot like an oven Because of the burning heat of famine. They have ravished the women in Zion, The maidens in the cities of Judah. Princes are hanged up by their hand; The faces of elders are not honoured. The young men have borne the mill, And the children have stumbled under the wood. The elders have ceased from the gate, The young men from their music. The joy of our heart is ceased; Our dance is turned into mourning. The crown is fallen from our head; Woe unto us! for we have sinned. For this our heart is faint, For these things our eyes are dim; For the mountain of Zion, which is desolate, The foxes walk upon it. Thou, O LORD, art enthroned for ever, Thy throne is from generation to generation. Wherefore dost Thou forget us for ever, And forsake us so long time? Turn Thou us unto Thee, O LORD, and we shall be turned; Renew our days as of old. Thou canst not have utterly rejected us, And be exceeding wroth against us!
[Turn us unto Thee, O Lord, and we shall be turned; Renew our days as of old.] Turn Thou us unto Thee, O LORD, and we shall be turned; renew our days as of old.
paragraphs.note: Public-domain JPS 1917 English aligned with the original Hebrew; any liturgical instructions are supplied by the project.

paragraphs.text: Look down from heaven, and see, even from Thy holy and glorious habitation; Where is Thy zeal and Thy mighty acts, The yearning of Thy heart and Thy compassions, Now restrained toward me? For Thou art our Father; for Abraham knoweth us not, and Israel doth not acknowledge us; Thou, O LORD, art our Father, Our Redeemer from everlasting is Thy name. O LORD, why dost Thou make us to err from Thy ways, And hardenest our heart from Thy fear? Return for Thy servants’sake, The tribes of Thine inheritance. Thy holy people they have well nigh driven out, Our adversaries have trodden down Thy sanctuary.
paragraphs.note: Exact complete Hebrew passage matched to the bundled Tanakh; no fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: But now, O LORD, Thou art our Father; we are the clay, and Thou our potter, and we all are the work of Thy hand. Be not wroth very sore, O LORD, neither remember iniquity for ever; behold, look, we beseech Thee, we are all Thy people. Thy holy cities are become a wilderness, Zion is become a wilderness, Jerusalem a desolation. Our holy and our beautiful house, where our fathers praised Thee, is burned with fire; and all our pleasant things are laid waste. Wilt Thou refrain Thyself for these things, O LORD? Wilt Thou hold Thy peace, and afflict us very sore?
paragraphs.note: Exact complete Hebrew passage matched to the bundled Tanakh; no fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: During the Three Weeks, additional psalms are recited here at midday; they are not reproduced here.

I have set watchmen Upon thy walls, O Jerusalem, They shall never hold their peace Day nor night: ‘Ye that are the LORD’S remembrancers, Take ye no rest, And give Him no rest, Till He establish, And till He make Jerusalem A praise in the earth.’ The LORD hath sworn by His right hand, And by the arm of His strength: Surely I will no more give thy corn To be food for thine enemies; And strangers shall not drink thy wine, For which thou hast laboured; But they that have garnered it shall eat it, And praise the LORD, And they that have gathered it shall drink it In the courts of My sanctuary.
paragraphs.note: Exact complete Hebrew passage matched to the bundled Tanakh; no fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: Thou wilt arise, and have compassion upon Zion; for it is time to be gracious unto her, for the appointed time is come. For Thy servants take pleasure in her stones, and love her dust. The LORD doth build up Jerusalem, He gathereth together the dispersed of Israel;
paragraphs.note: Every colon-delimited Hebrew fragment matched an exact complete bundled Tanakh verse; translations joined without fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: Tikkun Leah.

For the Leader; Maschil of the sons of Korah. As the hart panteth after the water brooks, so panteth my soul after Thee, O God. My soul thirsteth for God, for the living God: 'When shall I come and appear before God?' My tears have been my food day and night, while they say unto me all the day: 'Where is Thy God?' These things I remember, and pour out my soul within me, how I passed on with the throng, and led them to the house of God, with the voice of joy and praise, a multitude keeping holyday. Why art thou cast down, O my soul? And why moanest thou within me? Hope thou in God; for I shall yet praise Him for the salvation of His countenance. O my God, my soul is cast down within me; therefore do I remember Thee from the land of Jordan, and the Hermons, from the hill Mizar. Deep calleth unto deep at the voice of Thy cataracts; all Thy waves and Thy billows are gone over me. By day the LORD will command His lovingkindness, and in the night His song shall be with me, even a prayer unto the God of my life. I will say unto God my Rock: 'Why hast Thou forgotten me? Why go I mourning under the oppression of the enemy?' As with a crushing in my bones, mine adversaries taunt me; while they say unto me all the day: 'Where is Thy God?' Why art thou cast down, O my soul? And why moanest thou within me? Hope thou in God; for I shall yet praise Him, the salvation of my countenance, and my God.

Be Thou my judge, O God, and plead my cause against an ungodly nation; O deliver me from the deceitful and unjust man. For Thou art the God of my strength; why hast Thou cast me off? Why go I mourning under the oppression of the enemy? O send out Thy light and Thy truth; let them lead me; Let them bring me unto Thy holy mountain, and to Thy dwelling-places. Then will I go unto the altar of God, unto God, my exceeding joy; And praise Thee upon the harp, O God, my God. Why art thou cast down, O my soul? And why moanest thou within me? Hope thou in God; for I shall yet praise Him, The salvation of my countenance, and my God.
paragraphs.note: Exact complete Hebrew passage matched to the bundled Tanakh; no fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: On days when Tachanun is omitted, do not recite this psalm.

For the Leader. A Psalm of David. The LORD answer thee in the day of trouble; The name of the God of Jacob set thee up on high; Send forth thy help from the sanctuary, And support thee out of Zion; Receive the memorial of all thy meal-offerings, And accept the fat of thy burnt-sacrifice; Selah Grant thee according to thine own heart, And fulfil all thy counsel. We will shout for joy in thy victory, And in the name of our God we will set up our standards; The LORD fulfil all thy petitions. Now know I that the LORD saveth His anointed; He will answer him from His holy heaven With the mighty acts of His saving right hand. Some trust in chariots, and some in horses; But we will make mention of the name of the LORD our God. They are bowed down and fallen; But we are risen, and stand upright. Save, LORD; Let the King answer us in the day that we call.
paragraphs.note: Exact complete Hebrew passage matched to the bundled Tanakh; no fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: A psalm of David: the earth is Adonoy’s and the fullness thereof, the inhabited world and those who dwell in it. For He founded it upon the seas, and established it upon rivers. Who may ascend the mountain of Adonoy, and who may stand in the place of His holiness? The clean of hands and the pure of heart, who has not borne My soul in vain, and has not sworn deceitfully. He will bear Adonoy’s blessing and righteousness from the God of his deliverance. This is the generation of those who seek Him, the seekers of Your Presence, [God of] Jacob, Selah. Lift up your heads, gates, and be uplifted [you] entranceways to eternity, so that the King of Glory may enter. Who is this King of Glory? Adonoy, strong and mighty; Adonoy, the Mighty One in battle. Lift up your heads, gates, and lift, entranceways to eternity, so that the King of Glory may enter. Who is He, this King of Glory? Adonoy of hosts, He is the King of Glory, Selah.

To the Chief Musician a psalm with instrumental music, a Song. May G-d, give us grace & bless us, May He shine His countenance among us – forever. For the world to know Your way, & among all the nations, Your salvation. Peoples [of the world] will thank You, G-d. All the peoples will thank You. The Nations will rejoice & sing [praises] the people [of earth] for you judge the people with righteousness & that You lead the nations of the earth, forever. Peoples [of the world] will thank You, G-d. All the peoples will thank You. The land will have yielded its produce – May You bless us L·rd, our G-d. L·rd bless us & they will fear Him. - from the ends of the earth. (Tehillim / Psalm 67)
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: Hallelujah. I will give thanks unto the LORD with my whole heart, . In the council of the upright, and in the congregation. The works of the LORD are great, Sought out of all them that have delight therein. His work is glory and majesty; And His righteousness endureth for ever. He hath made a memorial for His wonderful works; The LORD is gracious and full of compassion. He hath given food unto them that fear Him; He will ever be mindful of His covenant. He hath declared to His people the power of His works, In giving them the heritage of the nations. The works of His hands are truth and justice; All His precepts are sure. They are established for ever and ever, They are done in truth and uprightness. He hath sent redemption unto His people; He hath commanded His covenant for ever; Holy and awful is His name. The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom; A good understanding have all they that do thereafter; His praise endureth for ever.
paragraphs.note: Exact complete Hebrew passage matched to the bundled Tanakh; no fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: For the Leader. A Psalm of David; when Nathan the prophet came unto him, after he had gone in to Bath-sheba. Be gracious unto me, O God, according to Thy mercy; According to the multitude of Thy compassions blot out my transgressions. Wash me thoroughly from mine iniquity, And cleanse me from my sin. For I know my transgressions; And my sin is ever before me. Against Thee, Thee only, have I sinned, And done that which is evil in Thy sight; That Thou mayest be justified when Thou speakest, And be in the right when Thou judgest. Behold, I was brought forth in iniquity, and in sin did my mother conceive me. Behold, Thou desirest truth in the inward parts; make me, therefore, to know wisdom in mine inmost heart. Purge me with hyssop, and I shall be clean; wash me, and I shall be whiter than snow. Make me to hear joy and gladness; that the bones which Thou hast crushed may rejoice. Hide Thy face from my sins, and blot out all mine iniquities. Create me a clean heart, O God; and renew a stedfast spirit within me. Cast me not away from Thy presence; and take not Thy holy spirit from me. Restore unto me the joy of Thy salvation; and let a willing spirit uphold me. Then will I teach transgressors Thy ways; and sinners shall return unto Thee. . Deliver me from bloodguiltiness, O God, Thou God of my salvation; so shall my tongue sing aloud of Thy righteousness. O Lord, open Thou my lips; and my mouth shall declare Thy praise. For Thou delightest not in sacrifice, else would I give it; Thou hast no pleasure in burnt-offering. The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a broken and a contrite heart, O God, Thou wilt not despise. Do good in Thy favour unto Zion; build Thou the walls of Jerusalem. Then wilt Thou delight in the sacrifices of righteousness, in burnt-offering and whole offering; Then will they offer bullocks upon Thine altar.
paragraphs.note: Complete bundled Tanakh passage aligned at 99.69% normalized Hebrew similarity; only orthographic/punctuation variation accepted.

paragraphs.text: On days when Tachanun is omitted, do not recite this verse.
How long shall there be weeping in Zion and mourning in Jerusalem?
You will arise and have mercy on Zion; You will build the walls of Jerusalem.
Some have the custom to recite 'Our God and God of our ancestors' and the psalm 'When the LORD restored' in order to conclude on a note of comfort (Ben Ish Chai, Vayishlach).

Our God and God of our ancestors, merciful King, have compassion on us. You who are good and do good, turn toward us. Return to us in the abundance of Your mercy, for the sake of the ancestors who did Your will. Build Your House as at first, establish Your Sanctuary upon its foundation, let us see it rebuilt and rejoice in its restoration. Return Your Presence into it; restore the priests to their service and the Levites to their stations, their songs and their music, and restore Israel to their dwellings. There we shall ascend, appear, and bow before You. May it be Your will, Lord our God and God of our ancestors, to bring us joyfully up to our land and plant us within our borders. There we shall offer before You our obligatory offerings, the daily offerings in their proper order and the additional offerings according to their laws.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: A Song of Ascents. When Adonoy brings about the return to Zion we will have been like dreamers. Then will our mouths be filled with laughter, and our tongue with joyous song. Then will they say among the nations: ‘Adonoy has done great things for them.’ Adonoy had done great things for us; we will [then] rejoice. Adonoy! bring back our exiles like springs in the desert. Those who sow in tears will reap with joyous song. [Though] he walks along weeping, carrying the bag of seed, he will return with joyous song carrying his sheaves.
paragraphs.note: Reused from a reviewed near-identical Hebrew Siddur variant (99.76% normalized Hebrew similarity).

paragraphs: Order of Enwrapping with Tzitzit

paragraphs.text: Before wrapping oneself in the tallit gadol, recite the blessing.

paragraphs: Blessed are You, L-rd, Our G-d, King of the Universe, that sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us to enwrap [us] with Tzitzit:

paragraphs.text: Order of putting on tefillin.
Before fastening the arm tefillin, recite the blessing with the intention that it also covers the head tefillin.
Blessed are You, Adonoy our God, King of the Universe, Who sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us to put on tefillin.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: After putting on tefillin, recite these two Torah passages. If unable to recite them then, say them after the service before removing the tefillin.

Adonoy spoke to Moses, saying: “Sanctify unto Me all the firstborn, whatsoever opens the womb among the Children of Israel, both of man and beast is Mine.” And Moses said to the people: “Remember this day on which you came out of Egypt, out of the house of bondage, for with a strong hand Adonoy brought you out from here, and [therefore] you must not eat chametz. This day you are departing, in the month of springtime. And it will be when Adonoy will bring you to the land of the Canaanites and the Hittites, and the Emorites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites, which He swore to your fathers to give you, a land flowing with milk and honey, you shall perform this service in this month. Seven days, you shall eat matzos, and on the seventh day there shall be a festival [dedicated] to Adonoy. Matzos shall be eaten during these seven days, and no chametz and no leaven shall be seen in your possession within all your boundaries. And you shall relate to your son on that day, saying: ‘Because of this Adonoy acted on my behalf when I came out of Egypt. And it shall be for a sign upon your arm and for a reminder between your eyes so that Adonoy’s teaching will be [the words of] your mouth; for with a strong hand Adonoy brought you out of Egypt. And you shall keep this ordinance in its appointed time from year to year.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: And it will be, when Adonoy will bring you to the land of the Canaanites as He swore unto you and to your fathers, and will have given it to you. Then you shall bring to Adonoy every one that opens the womb, and every firstling that is dropped by cattle that belong to you, the males shall belong to Adonoy, The firstling of a donkey you shall redeem with a lamb; and if you do not redeem it, then you must kill it by breaking its neck. You must redeem every firstborn of man among your children. And it will be when your son asks you in future times, saying: ‘What is this?’ You shall say to him: ‘With a strong hand Adonoy brought us out of Egypt, out of the house of bondage. And it was when Pharaoh unyieldingly refused to let us go, that Adonoy killed all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of man, to the firstborn of beast; therefore I sacrifice to Adonoy all that opens the womb that are males, and every firstborn of my sons, I redeem.’ And it shall be a sign upon your arm, and for totafos between your eyes, for with a strong hand, Adonoy brought us out of Egypt.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: Morning Prayer (Shacharit).

For the sake of the unification of the Holy One, Blessed be He, & His Divine Presence – with awe & love & love & awe - to unify of the Name of [letter] Yud, Hei with Vav Hei with a Complete Unity in the name of all Yisrael. Behold we come to pray the Evening Service, that was instituted by Yaakov / Jacob our Patriarch, peace be upon him, with all of the Mitzvot / commandments included in it, to repair the source in a high place, to give serenity to the One Who Formed us and to do the will of our Creator. May the goodwill of our L·rd, our G·d, be upon us. [Oh, G·d] establish our handiwork for us. And our handiwork establish (two times)
paragraphs.note: Previously translated paragraph, Hebrew similarity 98.0%: source and target independently present in source corpus.

paragraphs.text: I hereby accept upon myself the positive commandment to 'love your neighbor as yourself'; I love every one of the children of Israel as my own soul and with all my strength. I prepare my lips to pray before the King of kings, the Holy One, blessed be He.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Our God and God of our fathers, remember us favorably before You and be mindful of us for deliverance and compassion from the eternal high heavens. Remember in our behalf, Adonoy, our God: the love of our ancestors, Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, Your servants; the covenant, the kindness, and the oath which You swore to our father Abraham on Mount Moriah, and the binding of Isaac, his son on the altar, as it is written in Your Torah.
paragraphs.note: Previously translated paragraph, Hebrew similarity 99.3%: source and target independently present in source corpus.

paragraphs.text: After these events, God tested Abraham and said to him, “Abraham!” and he [Abraham] said, “Here I am.” He said, “Please, take your son, your only one, whom you love—Isaac— and go to the land of Moriah, and bring him up as a burnt-offering on one of the mountains which I will designate to you. Abraham awoke early in the morning, saddled his donkey, and took his two attendants with him, and also his son Isaac. He split the wood of the burnt-offering, and rose up, and went to the place that God had designated to him. On the third day, Abraham lifted his eyes and saw the place from afar. Abraham said to his attendants, You stay here with the donkey, and I and the boy will go to that place. We will prostrate ourselves [in worship] and return to you.” And Abraham took the wood of the burnt-offering and placed it on his son Isaac. In his hand he took the fire and the knife, and they both went together. Isaac spoke to Abraham his father and said, “Father,” and he said, “Here I am my son.” He said, “Here are the fire and the wood, but where is the lamb for the burnt-offering?” Abraham said, God Himself will show the lamb for a burnt offering, my son.” And the two of them went together. They came to the place that God had designated to him, and Abraham built the altar there, and arranged the wood, and bound his son Isaac, and placed him on the altar, on top of the wood. Abraham reached out his hand and took the knife to slaughter his son. An angel of Adonoy called to him from heaven and said, “Abraham! Abraham!” and he said, “Here I am.” He [God] said, Do not harm the boy, nor do anything to him; for now I know that you are one who fears God and have not withheld your son, your only one, from Me.” Abraham raised his eyes and beheld a ram after it had been caught in the thicket by its horns; and Abraham went and took the ram, and brought it up as a burnt-offering instead of his son. Abraham called the name of that place, Adonoy will see; as it is said [to] this day On Adonoy’s mountain, He will be seen. An angel of Adonoy called to Abraham a second time from heaven, and said, ‘I have sworn by Myself,’ declares Adonoy, ‘that because you performed this deed, and did not withhold your only son, I will greatly bless you and make your descendants as numerous as the stars of the sky and like the sand on the seashore, and your descendants will inherit the gate of their enemies. All the nations of the world will be blessed Through your children, because you heeded My voice.’” Abraham returned to his attendants, and they rose and went together to Beer Sheva, and Abraham dwelt in Beer Sheva.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text:
(Leviticus 1:11)
And he will slaughter it on the north side of the Altar, before Adonoy; and Aaron’s sons, the Kohanim, will sprinkle its blood all around the Altar.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: Some have the custom to recite the following passage.

May it be Your will, LORD our God and God of our ancestors, to be filled with compassion for us. In Your great mercy remember the binding of our father Isaac, son of our father Abraham, peace be upon them, as though his ashes lay heaped upon the altar. Look upon those ashes and have mercy on us, annul every harsh and evil decree against us, enable us to return before You in complete repentance, rescue us from the evil inclination and every sin and wrongdoing, and prolong our days in goodness and our years in pleasantness.

Master of the universe! Just as our father Abraham restrained his fatherly compassion in order to fulfill Your will with a whole heart, so may Your mercy overcome Your anger, and may compassion prevail over the strictness of Your judgment. Deal with us, Lord our God, through kindness and mercy; treat us beyond the strict letter of the law. In Your great goodness turn the heat of Your anger from Your people, Your city, Your land, and Your inheritance. Fulfill for us, Lord our God, what You promised in Your Torah through Moses Your servant: 'I will remember My covenant with Jacob, and also My covenant with Isaac, and also My covenant with Abraham will I remember; and I will remember the land.' And it is said: 'Yet for all that, when they are in the land of their enemies, I will not reject them or abhor them to destroy them utterly and break My covenant with them; for I am the Lord their God. But I will remember for them the covenant of their forebears whom I brought out of the land of Egypt before the eyes of the nations, to be their God. I am the Lord.' And it is said: 'Then the Lord your God will restore your captivity and have compassion upon you, and will return and gather you from all the peoples where the Lord your God scattered you. Even if your outcasts are at the ends of heaven, from there the Lord your God will gather you, and from there He will take you. The Lord your God will bring you into the land your ancestors possessed, and you shall possess it; He shall deal well with you and multiply you beyond your ancestors.' And through Your prophet it is said: 'Lord, be gracious to us! We wait for You; be our arm every morning, our salvation in the time of trouble.' And it is said: 'It is a time of trouble for Jacob, yet he shall be saved out of it.' And it is said: 'In all their affliction He was afflicted, and the angel of His presence saved them; in His love and pity He redeemed them, lifted them and carried them all the days of old.' And it is said: 'Who is a God like You, forgiving iniquity and passing over transgression for the remnant of His inheritance? He does not retain His anger forever because He delights in mercy. He will again have compassion upon us and subdue our iniquities. You will cast all their sins into the depths of the sea; You will show faithfulness to Jacob, kindness to Abraham, as You swore to our ancestors in the days of old.' And it is said: 'I shall bring them to My holy mountain and make them joyful in My house of prayer. Their burnt offerings and sacrifices shall be acceptable on My altar, for My house shall be called a house of prayer for all peoples.'

paragraphs.text: These are matters without a prescribed measure: leaving the corner of the field for the poor, offering first fruits, appearing before God on the pilgrimage festivals, acts of kindness, and the study of Torah. These are deeds whose fruits a person enjoys in this world while the principal remains for the World to Come: honoring father and mother, acts of kindness, visiting the sick, welcoming guests, attending the synagogue early, making peace between one person and another and between husband and wife. The study of Torah is equal in importance to them all.

A person should always fear Heaven in private as in public, acknowledge the truth and speak truth within his heart. Let him arise early and say: Master of the worlds and Lord of lords! We do not place our supplications before You on account of our righteousness, but on account of Your great mercies. Lord, hear; Lord, forgive; Lord, attend and act, do not delay for Your own sake, my God, for Your name is called over Your city and Your people. Who are we? What is our life, our kindness, our righteousness? What can we say before You, Lord our God and God of our ancestors? The mightiest before You are as nothing; the renowned are as though they never existed, the wise as though without knowledge, the discerning without understanding. Humanity has no advantage over the beasts, for all is vanity, apart from the pure soul that must give an account before the throne of Your glory. All nations are as nothing before You, as it says: 'Behold, the nations are like a drop from a bucket and as dust on the scales; He lifts the islands as a fine grain.' Yet we are Your people, the children of Your covenant, descendants of Abraham who loved You and to whom You swore at Mount Moriah; the seed of Isaac bound upon the altar; the congregation of Jacob Your firstborn, whom You loved and in whom You rejoiced, naming him Israel and Jeshurun.
paragraphs.note: New English working translation reviewed against the Hebrew and available Russian text; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Therefore we are obliged always, every day, to thank You, praise You, glorify and exalt You, and to sing songs of praise and gratitude to Your great name. Happy are we: how good is our portion, how pleasant our lot, and how beautiful our inheritance! Happy are we, who come morning and evening to synagogues and study houses, proclaiming Your oneness each day and saying twice with love:
If the time for reciting the Shema is about to pass, recite the entire Shema here.
HEAR, O ISRAEL: THE LORD OUR GOD, THE LORD IS ONE.
paragraphs.note: Exact complete Hebrew passage matched to the bundled Tanakh; no fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: (Silently) Blessed be the Name of His glorious kingdom forever more.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: You alone were One before You created the world and You alone are One after You created it. You are God in this world and God in the world to come; You and Your years shall never end. Sanctify Your name in Your world among the people who sanctify Your name; by Your salvation, our King, raise and exalt our strength and save us soon for the sake of Your name. Blessed is He who sanctifies His name in public.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: You alone are the Lord God in heaven above and on the earth beneath, in the heavens above and below. You are the First and You are the Last, and besides You there is no god. Gather those who wait for You and are scattered across the four corners of the earth. Let all who enter the world recognize and know that You alone are God over all the kingdoms of the earth. You made heaven and earth, the sea and everything in them. Who among all the works of Your hands, above or below, may say to You: 'What are You doing?' Our Father in heaven, living and enduring, deal kindly with us for the glory of Your great, mighty, and awesome name called upon us. Fulfill for us, Lord our God, what You promised through Your seer Zephaniah, as it is said: 'At that time I will bring you in; at that time I will gather you. I will make you renowned and praised among all the peoples of the earth when I restore your fortunes before your eyes,' says the Lord.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: May it be Your will, LORD our God and God of our ancestors, to have mercy on us, forgive all our sins, atone for all our iniquities and pardon every transgression. Rebuild the Holy Temple speedily in our days, and we shall offer before You the daily sacrifice to atone for us, as You wrote in Your Torah through Moses Your servant:

paragraphs.text: And the LORD spoke unto Moses, saying: Command the children of Israel, and say unto them: My food which is presented unto Me for offerings made by fire, of a sweet savour unto Me, shall ye observe to offer unto Me in its due season. And thou shalt say unto them: This is the offering made by fire which ye shall bring unto the LORD: he-lambs of the first year without blemish, two day by day, for a continual burnt-offering. The one lamb shalt thou offer in the morning, and the other lamb shalt thou offer at dusk; and the tenth part of an ephah of fine flour for a meal-offering, mingled with the fourth part of a hin of beaten oil. It is a continual burnt-offering, which was offered in mount Sinai, for a sweet savour, an offering made by fire unto the LORD. And the drink-offering thereof shall be the fourth part of a hin for the one lamb; in the holy place shalt thou pour out a drink-offering of strong drink unto the LORD. And the other lamb shalt thou present at dusk; as the meal-offering of the morning, and as the drink-offering thereof, thou shalt present it, an offering made by fire, of a sweet savour unto the LORD.
paragraphs.note: Exact complete Hebrew passage matched to the bundled Tanakh; no fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: The preparation of the incense.

[Incense Offering] You are the L·rd, Our G·d, that our Forefathers burned before You the incense spices at the time that the Holy Temple stood – like You commanded them through Moshe, Your Prophet, like it is written in your Torah.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: And the L·rd said to Moshe – Take for yourself spices- balsam sap / Nataf / & onycha / Sh-h'elet & galbanum / H'elbona, spices & pure frankincense / Levona – each shall be of equal weight. And you shall prepare it (the spices) as incense – a compound, the work of a spice mixer, blended (or salted) pure & holy. And you shall grind from it very well, and you shall take from it, before the [tent of] testimony – in the Tent of Meeting - that I shall meet with you there – holy, holy it shall be for you. And it says – and Aharon shall offer as incense, the incense spices each & every morning when he cleans the lamps he shall offer it. And when Aharon Ascends, he shall offer the incense – a regular incense offering before the L·rd – throughout your generations.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: Our Rabbis Taught, The compound of the Incense, how was it done? Three-hundred & Sixty-eight Maneh (a measure) was in it – 365 [maneh] – like the count of the days of the solar year. One Maneh daily – half in the morning and half in the evening and the three extra maneh – where those of which the Chief Kohen entered [the holy of holies] and took from them a full palm-full on the Yom Kippur – he would return them to the grinder on the eve of Yom Kippur, in order to accomplish the mitzvah – in the finest of finest [way] and 11 spices were in it – and these are they:
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: 1) Balsam, 2) onycha, 3) & galbanum 4) frankincense – the weight of 70 maneh each. 5) myrrh, 6) cassia & 7) spikenard & 8) saffron – [each] a weight of 16, 16 maneh. 9) costus – 12 maneh 10) aromatic bark – three [maneh] 11) cinnamon – 9 (maneh) [Added also were] Lye of Carsina – 9 Kavs (a measure), Wine of Cypres – 3 Seahs and 3 kavs- and if one did not find wine of Cypres – he brings old wine. Salt of Sodom – a quarter [of a kav.] An ascension of smoke – a small amount. Rabbi Nathan, the Babylonian, says – even the resin of the Jordan – a bit. If he put in it honey it is invalid and if he omitted one from all of its spices, he is liable for death [penalty].
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: Rabban Shimeon Son of Gamliel says : The Tzorit is sap, that flows from the Balsam tree. The Lye of Karsina, what does it come [to do]? – in order to rub the onycha in order for it to be beautiful. The wine of Cyprus, why is it brought? in order to soak in it the Onycha, in order for it to be sharp. But is not urine – better [to make it sharp] – rather we do not bring in urine into the Sanctuary out of respect.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: We learned in [a Baraita] Rabbi Nathan Says - When he chops – he says “Hadek Heitev, Hetitev Hadek / Chop Well, Well Chop” because the voice is good for spices. The incense compound divided in half is Kosher. For a third or a-quarter we did not hear [the law]. Rabbi Yehuda said “This is the general rule – if it is in the same proportion – it is Kosher for half, & if it lacks one from all of the spices – he is liable for the death penalty.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: Bar Kapara taught once every sixty or seventy years there were remains [of the spices] of half. And Bar Kapparah also taught , if one was to add a Kartov [a measure] of honey a person would not be able to stand because of the fragrance. And why do we not mix in it honey? Because the Torah says “For any leaven or any honey, do not offer incense from it – as a fire offering. L·rd of hosts, is with us. He is our refuge for us the G·d of Yaakov / Jacob forever. L·rd of hosts, happy is the man that has faith in You. L·rd save, the King will answer us on the day we call. And pleasant to the L·rd is the offering of Yehudah / Judah and Yerusalayim / Jerusalem – like the days of old.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: Abbaye listed the order of the [daily] Altar service based on tradition, and according to the opinion of Abba Shaul: the [arranging on the Altar of the] great Pyre precedes the second pyre [from which live coals are taken] for the incense-offering; the second pyre of the incense-offering [is arranged] before the placement of two logs [on the large pyre] the placement of the two logs precedes the removal of the ashes from the inner Altar; the removal of the ashes from the inner Altar precedes the cleaning of five lamps [of the Menorah]; the cleaning of the five lamps precedes [sprinkling] the blood of the daily-offering; the blood of the daily-offering precedes the cleaning of the [remaining] two lamps; the cleaning of the two lamps precedes the incense-offering; the incense-offering precedes [burning] the limbs [of the daily-offering]; burning the limbs [precedes] the meal-offering; the meal-offering [precedes] the baking-pan-offering; the baking-pan-offerings [precede] the wine libations; the wine-libations [precede] the Mussaf-offering; the Mussaf-offering [precedes] the two bowls of frankincense; and the two bowls of frankincense precede the daily afternoon-offering, for it is said, (Leviticus 6:5) And [the Kohein] shall arrange on it the burnt-offering, and burn on it the fat of the peace-offerings. Therewith complete all the offerings [of the day.]

Blessed [is His] Name, Whose glorious kingdom is forever and ever.
