paragraphs.text: The First Shabbat Meal.
After Kiddush, one should promptly wash one’s hands for the meal. Before washing, some recite this declaration of sacred intention cited by the Ben Ish Chai.

For the sake of the unity of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Presence, in awe and love and in love and awe, to unite the letters Yod–Heh with Vav–Heh in perfect unity, in the name of all Israel: to raise the Divine Presence from the dust and exalt the Presence of our strength, I now come to fulfill the positive commandment instituted by the Sages of washing and rubbing my hands carefully before a meal. May this bring pleasure to my Maker, fulfill my Creator's will, and repair the root of this commandment in the supernal realm. May it be Your will, Lord our God and God of our ancestors, that this commandment of washing and rubbing the hands before eating be accounted worthy, accepted, and pleasing before You, as though I had directed my mind to all the intentions appropriate to this commandment.
paragraphs.note: New English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: May it be Your will, Lord our God and God of our ancestors, that through the merit of the blessing we are about to say over washing our hands before the meal, this become a time of favor before You. May an abundance of higher understanding and great lights flow from the Infinite Light to the twelve divine configurations hinted at within the ten encompassing sefirot, themselves symbolized by the ten fingers of our hands. From there may we receive the bounty of the ten blessings, as it is written: 'May God give you of the dew of heaven and the fat places of the earth, and abundance of grain and wine. May peoples serve you and nations bow down to you. Be lord over your brothers, and may your mother's sons bow down to you. Cursed be those who curse you, and blessed be those who bless you.'

It is good to recite the following before the meal:

For the sake of uniting the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shekhinah, in awe and love, love and awe, to unite the letters Yod and Heh with Vav and Heh in a complete unity, in the name of all Israel, to raise the Shekhinah from the dust and exalt the dwelling of our strength: I am ready to fulfill the commandment of the first Sabbath meal and to repair its root in the supernal realm. It corresponds to Isaac, the holy father. By his merit may we be saved from the suffering preceding the Messiah, and may the verse be fulfilled for us: 'I shall cause you to ride upon the heights of the earth.' May the pleasantness of the Lord our God rest upon us; establish the work of our hands for us; yes, establish the work of our hands.

paragraphs.text: Ki Eshmera Shabbat
Words: Rabbi Abraham ibn Ezra. Acrostic: Avraham.
If I keep the Sabbath, God will keep me; it is an everlasting sign between Him and me.
On it one may not pursue one’s affairs or set out on journeys, nor speak about weekday needs, commerce, or even affairs of rulers. I will meditate on God’s Torah, and it will make me wise.

On it I always find rest for my soul. Behold, my Holy One gave it to the first generation as a sign by giving a double portion of bread on the sixth day; so on every sixth day He will double my sustenance.

In God’s law a statute was established for His servants: on it to arrange the showbread before Him. Therefore fasting on it, according to the sages, is forbidden, except on Yom Kippur, when my sin is atoned.
It is an honored day, a day of delight—bread, good wine, meat, and fish. Mourning gives way on it, for it is a day of joy, and You will make me rejoice.

One who profanes it with labor will ultimately be cut off. Therefore on it I will cleanse my heart as with soap, and I will pray to God at evening and morning, at Musaf and also Minchah; He will answer me.
Dror Yikra
Words: Dunash ben Labrat. Acrostic: Dunash in each stanza.
May He proclaim freedom to son and daughter and guard you like the pupil of the eye. May your name be pleasant and never cease. Sit and rest on the Sabbath day.
Seek out my dwelling and my sanctuary, and make with me a sign of salvation. Plant a choice vine within my vineyard; heed the cry of the children of my people.
Tread the winepress in Bozrah, and also Babylon—another reading: Edom—which has grown mighty. Shatter my foes in wrath and fury; hear my voice on the day I call.
God, make the wilderness a mountain of myrtle, acacia, cypress, and plane trees; to the one who warns and the one who heeds, grant peace like the waters of a river.
Crush those who rise against me, living and zealous God; make their hearts melt and break their defense. Then we will open our mouths wide and fill our tongues with song to You.
Know wisdom for your soul, and it will be a crown upon your head. Guard the commandment of your Holy One—another reading: your God—and keep your holy Sabbath.

paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: From evening we prepare every kind of delicacy; while it is still day, fattened chickens are ready. Arrange many dishes, drink fragrant wines, and enjoy delicacies at each of the three meals.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: To delight in pleasures—fowl, quail, and fish.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: He will inherit Jacob's inheritance, an inheritance without bounds. Rich and poor will honor it, and you will merit redemption. If you keep the Sabbath, you will be My treasured people; six days you shall labor, and on the seventh we shall rejoice.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: To delight in pleasures—fowl, quail, and fish.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Your business affairs are forbidden, as is making calculations. Reflection is permitted, as are arranging marriages, teaching a child a book, singing sacred melodies, and studying fine words wherever one may be.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: To delight in pleasures—fowl, quail, and fish.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Let your walking be unhurried; call the Sabbath a delight. Sleep too is praiseworthy, in accordance with the law that restores the soul. Thus my soul longs for you and to rest in affection; enclosed like roses, son and daughter rest on it.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: To delight in pleasures—fowl, quail, and fish.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: A foretaste of the World to Come is the Sabbath day of rest. All who delight in it will merit abundant joy; they will be spared the birth-pangs of the Messiah. May our redemption sprout forth, and sorrow and sighing flee away.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: To delight in pleasures—fowl, quail, and fish.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: My Thoughts Will Praise You
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Words: Rabbi Israel Najara.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: My thoughts will praise You, LORD my Shepherd, on the holy Sabbath, the seventh day.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: The day on which You completed all Your work, I declare that You rule over all besides You. You made works beyond wearing out; hasten to give rest to me, son of Your maidservant.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: You chose the seventh from all numbers and sanctified it in weeks and years. Hasten, You who lifted up the faithful seed, and redeem them from disasters—You know my path and my resting place.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Take pleasure in my rest—this day is a day of rest. On my working days grant me relief, and prepare for my Sabbath a portion and a meal. May joy and gladness be my delight.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Grant me a place in the world that is entirely Sabbath. As Your lamp shines, cast light upon me; bring me again up to the dwelling of Shiloh. Answer me speedily, my Light and my Salvation.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Blessed Is God Most High
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Acrostic: Baruch Hazak.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Blessed is God Most High, who gave rest and redemption to our souls from burden and sighing. He will seek Zion, the banished city. How long will the sighing soul grieve? Whoever keeps the Sabbath—son and daughter—will be pleasing to God like an offering on a griddle.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: He who rides the heavens, King of worlds, arranged pleasant Sabbath rest for His people—with delightful foods, many delicacies, garments of honor, and a family feast. Whoever keeps the Sabbath...
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Fortunate is everyone who waits for double recompense from the One who shelters all and dwells in thick cloud. He will merit an inheritance on mountain and lowland, inheritance and rest when his sun has risen. Whoever keeps the Sabbath...
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Everyone who keeps the Sabbath according to law and does not profane it thereby prepares the beloved holiness as his portion. If he fulfills the duty of the day, fortunate is he; to God, his Maker and Master, it is an offering sent. Whoever keeps the Sabbath...
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: My Rock called it the delight of days; fortunate are the wholehearted if it is guarded. A crown set with gems will be formed upon their heads; the Rock of worlds lets His spirit rest upon them. Whoever keeps the Sabbath...
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Remember the Sabbath day to sanctify it. Its dignity is exalted, a diadem upon its head. Therefore a person should give his soul delight and joy, as an anointing. Whoever keeps the Sabbath...
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: It is holy for you, the Sabbath Queen, entering your homes to place blessing there. In all your dwellings do no work—you, your sons and daughters, servant and maidservant. Whoever keeps the Sabbath...
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: The Sabbath Day
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: There is no day like the Sabbath day; God blessed it and sanctified it.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: From the first day through the sixth my soul longs for the Sabbath, for on the Sabbath I go free, and I call it a day of rest.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Let us rejoice and be glad, for it is good to give thanks and to sing to the Most High for all things. The Sabbath is precious to us; a brutish person does not understand it.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: He commanded us to observe Sabbath according to its law; from Sinai came this ordered commandment. Keeping it is also a royal crown, and glory and splendor will crown the one who guards it.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Those who love it will lengthen their days, and those who taste of it merit life. They will walk on the path of uprightness and seek His testimonies with all their heart.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: The LORD desired us and chose us, and separated us from every tongue. He gave us the holiness of Sabbath as an inheritance; all the seed of Jacob, honor it.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: The Rock, From Whose Food We Ate
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Hymn before Grace After Meals.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: The Rock—from His [store] we have eaten—Bless [Him] my faithful ones. We have satisfied ourselves and we have left over [some food] according to the word of Adonoy.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: He sustains His world, our Shepherd and our Father. We ate of His bread and drank of His wine; therefore we thank His Name and praise Him with our mouths. We said and answered: there is none holy like the LORD.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: With song and a voice of thanksgiving we bless our God for the desirable, good land He gave our fathers as an inheritance, and for food and provisions with which He satisfied our souls. His kindness has prevailed over us, and the truth of the LORD endures.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: In Your kindness have mercy upon Your people, our Rock, upon Zion, the dwelling of Your glory, the abode of our glorious Temple. May the son of David, Your servant, come and redeem us—the breath of our nostrils, the anointed of the LORD.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: May the Temple be rebuilt and the city of Zion be filled; there we will sing a new song and ascend there with rejoicing. May the sanctified Merciful One be blessed and exalted over a full cup of wine, according to the blessing of the LORD.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs: Blessing of the Meal

paragraphs.text: Wash the fingertips after the meal; it is good to recite:

To the Chief Musician a psalm with instrumental music, a Song. May G-d, give us grace & bless us, May He shine His countenance among us – forever. For the world to know Your way, & among all the nations, Your salvation. Peoples [of the world] will thank You, G-d. All the peoples will thank You. The Nations will rejoice & sing [praises] the people [of earth] for you judge the people with righteousness & that You lead the nations of the earth, forever. Peoples [of the world] will thank You, G-d. All the peoples will thank You. The land will have yielded its produce – May You bless us L·rd, our G-d. L·rd bless us & they will fear Him. - from the ends of the earth. (Tehillim / Psalm 67)
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: I shall bless the LORD at all times; His praise shall continually be in my mouth. The end of the matter, when all is heard: revere God and keep His commandments, for this is the whole duty of humanity. My mouth shall speak the praise of the LORD, and all flesh shall bless His holy name forever and ever. But we shall bless the LORD from now until eternity, Hallelujah! And He spoke to me: 'This is the table that is before the LORD.'
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs: If three or more are together say:
The leader says:

paragraphs.text: 'With your permission' (some say: 'Come, let us bless the supreme holy King').

paragraphs: The others respond:

paragraphs.text: Heaven:

paragraphs: The leader says:

paragraphs.text: 'With permission of the supreme holy King and with your permission, let us bless' (with ten or more add 'our God') 'of whose food we have eaten.'

paragraphs: The others respond:

paragraphs.text: Blessed is He (with ten or more add 'our God') of whose food we have eaten, and by whose goodness we live.

paragraphs: The leader responds:

paragraphs.text: Blessed is our God of whose food we have eaten, and by whose goodness we live.

paragraphs: Blessed are You, L·rd, our G·d, King of the universe. The G·d, Who feeds us & the entire world, with His Goodness, with Grace, with Kindness, with Abundance, & with great Mercy. He Provides bread to all flesh – because forever is His kindness. (Psalms 136, 25) And with His great goodness, we continually never lack. And May You never let us lack food continually forever & ever. For He is G·d, Who feeds & provides livelihood to everyone. And His table is set for all. For He prepares sustenance & food for all His creations that He created with His mercy & great kindness. As it says “You Open Your Hand, & You Satiate all the Living with its wants.” (Psalms 145, 16). Blessed are You, L·rd, our G·d, King of the universe Who feeds all.

We thank You, L·rd, our G·d, that You bequeathed to our Forefathers a desirable, good & spacious land, a Covenant & Torah, life & food. And that You took us out from the land of Egypt & that You redeemed us from the house of bondage. And upon the Your Covenant that you stamped upon our flesh. And for Your Torah that You taught us. And upon the laws of Your Will – that You taught us. And upon life, & food that you feed & sustain us.
(On Hanukah & Purim Al HaNissim is recited)...
Upon the miracles and upon the redemption and upon the mighty acts and for salvation and for the wonders and for the comfort that you did for our fathers in those days at this period.

On Hanukkah continue: In the days of Matitya son of Yohanan, The high priest, The Hashmonay and his sons when the Wicked Greek empire arose Against your people Israel To make them forget your Torah, and to remove them from the ordinances of your will and you with your great mercy you stood at the time of their suffering , you battle their battles, you judged their laws, you took vengeance upon their vengeance, you gave up over the mighty into the hands of the weak, and the masses in the hands of the few, and the impure Into the hands of the pure, and the wicked into the hands of the righteous, and the intentional sinners into the hands of those that are engaged in your Torah. To you you made your holy and great name In your world and for your people Israel you made a great salvation and deliverance as you do This day. And the afterwords your children came to the inner chambers of your house cleared your sanctuary and purify it your holy Temple and lit candles In your holy courtyard. And they fixed these eight days of Hanukkah – With complete praise and thanks, and you did for them miracles and wonders and we will thank Your great name, Forever.

On Purim Continue: In the days of Mordekhai & Esther, in Shushan, the Capital (of Ancient Persia) – When Haman, the wicked, stood against them, asking to destroy and kill and annihilate all the Jews – from the Youth to the Elderly, Baby & Women – in a single day – on the 13th of the Twelfth month – which is the month of Adar – and to pillage and take booty and You with Your great mercy – You uprooted his advice & confused his thought & He returned to him his wiles upon his own head – and they hung him & His children upon the gallows. And You did for them miracles and wonders - and we will thank Your great name, Forever.

And Upon all, L·rd, our G·d, do we thank You & bless Your Name. As it says “And you shall eat & be satiated & you shall bless the L·rd, our G·d for the good land that He gave you.” Blessed are You, L·rd, for the land & the food.

Have Mercy L·rd, our G·d upon us & upon Israel Your people & upon Jerusalem, Your city. And upon Mount Tzion – the Tabernacle of Your glory & upon Your sanctuary. And upon Your Abode & upon Your Inner Chamber. And upon the great & holy abode upon which Your Name is called (Temple). Our father, Our Shepherd, Our Feeder, Our Sustainer, Our Provider. Our Deliverer. Deliver us speedily from all our sufferings. And please, let us not need, L·rd, our G·d, from the hands [of others], gifts from flesh & blood. And not from their hands – their loans – rather from Your hand – Full & plentiful, rich & open. May it be Your Will that we will not be embarrassed in this world & we will not be denigrated in the next world. And upon the Kingship of the house of David Your Messiah - restore it in place speedily in our days.
(On Shabbat we add : Retze: Desire & Release … On Rosh Hodesh & Festivals, & Intermediate Holidays we add: Elo-keinu)

May it please You, L·rd our G·d, to give us Rest Hash·m, our G·d from your Commandments & from the commandments of the Seventh day, this Great and Holy Shabbat day, for this day is a great and holy day before you. Let us rest on it and let us have serenity and have pleasure with your commandments – the decrees of Your will. And do not let there be pain and suffering on the day of our rest. And let us see the consolation of Zion speedily in our days. For you are the one that is the master of rest. And even though we ate and drank, the destruction of the of your great and holy house – we did not forget. Do not forget us forever and do not abandon us forever, for you are G-d, a Great and Holy King.
(Rosh Hodesh, Intermed. days Passover & Sukot say)

Our G·d, & G·d of Our forefathers, may it rise, & come, arrive, appear, find favor, & be heard, & be considered, & be remembered & our remembrance, & the remembrance of our Patriarchs, & the remembrance of Jerusalem, Your city, & the remembrance of the Messiah, the son of David, Your servant, & the remembrance of your entire People, the house of Israel before You – for deliverance, for good, for grace, for kindness, & mercy, for a good life, and for peace on this day of
(on Rosh Hodesh) the head of the month
(on Passover) the Holiday of Matzot - On this day of Holy Convocation,

paragraphs.text: For Shavuot: this Festival of Weeks, this holy festival day.
For Rosh Hashanah: this Day of Remembrance, this holy festival day.

paragraphs: (on Sukkot) Holiday of Sukkot.

paragraphs.text: On Shemini Atzeret: “This Eighth-Day Assembly festival, on this holy festival day...”

paragraphs: to have mercy on it (this day) upon us & to save us. Remember L·rd, our G·d, on it for good, & consider us on it with blessing, & deliver us on it for good life, With a pronouncement of deliverance & mercy. Take pity & be gracious to us, & have mercy & be compassionate with us & save us for upon You are our eyes turned, For You are G·d, King, gracious & compassionate....
And build Jerusalem, Your city, speedily in our days. Blessed are You, L·rd, Who builds Jerusalem. (Say Quietly) Amen.

paragraphs.text: If, on Shabbat, one forgot 'Retzeh VeHachalitzenu' and remembers before beginning the blessing 'Who is good and does good,' recite:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who lovingly gave Sabbaths to His people Israel for rest, as a sign and a covenant. Blessed are You, LORD, who sanctifies the Sabbath.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: If one forgot 'Ya'aleh VeYavo' on Rosh Chodesh and remembers before beginning 'Who is good and does good,' recite:
Blessed is He who gave the new months to His people Israel as a remembrance.
If one forgot both 'Retzeh VeHachalitzenu' and 'Ya'aleh VeYavo' on a Shabbat that is also Rosh Chodesh, and remembers after concluding 'Who builds Jerusalem,' recite:

Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who lovingly gave Sabbaths to His people Israel for rest, as a sign and a covenant, and New Moons to His people Israel as a remembrance. Blessed are You, LORD, who sanctifies Shabbat, Israel and the New Moons.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs: Blessed are You, L·rd, our G·d, King of the universe, G·d, our Father, our King, our Glorious One, our Creator, our Redeemer, our Holiness. The Holiness of Jacob, our Shepherd, Shephard of Yisrael. The Good King that does good to all. Every single day He does Good, He causes good, & will do good to us. He bestowed, bestows & will bestow forever grace, & kindness & mercy & bounty & salvation & all good.

The Merciful One, He will Be Praised upon His Throne of GloryThe Merciful One, He will in Heaven & upon the Earth. The Merciful One, He will Be Praised by us each & every generation. The Merciful One, He will raise the horn of His people The Merciful One, He will Be Glorified by us Eternally Forever The Merciful One, He will will give us sustenance with honor & not denigration; with permission & not prohibitions; with tranquility & not with suffering The Merciful One, He will provide peace among usThe Merciful One, He will send blessing & abundance & success in all our handiwork. The Merciful One, He will provide success in our paths. The Merciful One, He will break the yoke of the exile, speedily, from our necks The Merciful One, He will guide us speedily to independence in our land The Merciful One, He will heal us – a complete healing – healing of the soul & healing of the body The Merciful One, He will open for us His Hand of plenty. The Merciful One, He will bless each & every one of us with his Great Name – as were blessed our forefathers - Avraham, Yitzhak & Yaakov – with all, from all of all. Thus may You bless us together – with a complete blessing. And thus, may it be Your Will. And let us say Amen. The Merciful One, He will spread upon us the Shelter of His peace.
* (Shabbat)
The Merciful One, He will bequeath to us a world that is complete rest and serenity for eternity
* (Rosh Hodesh) ...
The Merciful One, He will renew upon us this month for good & blessing.
* (Rosh HaShanna)...
The Merciful One, He will renew upon us this year for good & blessing.
* (Sukkot) ...

The Merciful One, He will give us the merit to sit in the Sukkah of the skin of Leviathan. The Merciful One, He will bestow upon us plentyof holiness and purity- from the seven lofty and holy guests – may there merit protect and shield us. The Merciful One, He will establish for us the Sukkah of David, that is fallen.
* (Holidays) ...
The Merciful One, He will allow us to arrive at other holidays – that come to greet us with peace.
* (Yom Tov) ...
The Merciful One, He will bequeath upon us a day that is completely good. ...
The Merciful One, He will plant His Torah & His love into our hearts. And his awe should be on our faces – without any sin. And all our deeds should be for the sake of heaven....

A guest says: The Merciful One, He will bless this table that we ate upon and set it with all the delicacies in the world, may it be like the table of Abraham our father (may he rest in peace), every hungry person shall eat from it and every thirsty person shall drink from it, and it shall not lack any good, for all eternity, amen. The Merciful one, He will bless the master of this house and the host of this meal, him and his children and his wife and all he owns, with children who will live and assets that will multiply, Bless, Hashem, his substance, And favor his undertakings. and may his possessions and our possessions be successful and near the city. May thoughts of sin and transgression not appear before him and before us. Happy shall he be and glad all his days, with wealth and honor, from here to eternity. He shall not suffer shame in this world, nor humiliation in the World-to-Come. amen, so be itThe Merciful One, He will give us life & merit & approach us to the days of the Messiah & the building of the Holy Temple & life of the World to Come.
At a Seduat Chatan: The merciful one, bless the groom and bridge, with male children for his blessed service:

He makes great (On Shabbat & Holidays days when Musaf (additional prayer service) is said, say instead: He is a tower of) Salvation of His Kingship. And does kindness to his anointed one – to [King] David & his descendants forever. Young lions became needy and starved But, those that seek, the L·rd, did not lack any good. (Psalms 34:11) I was a youth & I also became older, & I did not see a Righteous person abandoned & his children seeking bread. (Psalms 37:25) All day He is graceful & lends & his children are held blessed. (Psalms 37, 26) That that we ate, may it be to satiate. And that which we drank, may it be for healing. And that that we left over, may it be for blessing. As it is written: As it is written: “and he gave it [the food] before them and when they had eaten, they had some left over as [according to] the word of the L·rd. (II Kings 4:44 ) Blessed are you to the L·rd – Who makes the Heaven and Earth. Blessed is the man that will place trust in the L·rd. And the L·rd is his trust. (Jeremiah 17:7 ) The L·rd gives strength to His People. The L·rd will bless his people with peace. (Psalms 29:11) May He Who creates peace in His high places, may He with His mercy, make peace upon us & all His people Israel, & say ye, Amen.

paragraphs.text: The Threefold After-Blessing (Me'ein Shalosh).
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe.
If one ate grain-based foods, say “For sustenance and nourishment.”
If one drank wine, say “For the vine and the fruit of the vine.”
If one ate fruit from the seven species, say: 'for the tree and for the fruit of the tree.'

For the produce of the field and for the desirable, good, and spacious land that You favored and gave as an inheritance to our ancestors, to eat of its fruit and be satisfied with its goodness: have mercy, Lord our God, on us, on Israel Your people, on Jerusalem Your city, on Mount Zion the dwelling of Your glory, on Your altar and on Your Sanctuary. Rebuild Jerusalem, the holy city, speedily in our days. Bring us into it, gladden us in its rebuilding, and we will bless You there in holiness and purity.
paragraphs.note: Original English working translation aligned to the full Hebrew paragraph; specialist review pending.

paragraphs.text: On Shabbat: “Be pleased and grant us rest on this Shabbat day.”
On Rosh Chodesh: Remember us for good on this day of Rosh Chodesh.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: On Rosh Hashanah: Remember us for good on this Day of Remembrance, this holy festival day.
On Passover: Gladden us on this Festival of Unleavened Bread, this holy festival day.
On Shavuot: Gladden us on this Festival of Weeks, this holy festival day.
On Sukkot: Gladden us on this Festival of Booths, this holy festival day.
On Shemini Atzeret: Gladden us on this Eighth Day of Assembly, this holy festival day.
For You are good and do good to all, and we thank You, [LORD our God,] for the land.
If one ate grain foods, say: 'for the sustenance and the nourishment'; for food from the Land of Israel, say: 'for its sustenance and its nourishment.'
If the wine was produced in the Land of Israel, say “And for the fruit of its vine.”
For fruit of the seven species, say: 'for the fruits'; for fruit of the Land of Israel, say: 'for its fruits.'
Blessed are You, LORD, for the land and for its produce.
If one ate grain-based foods, say: 'the sustenance'; for produce of the Land of Israel say: 'her sustenance.'
If one drank wine, say: 'the fruit of the vine'; for wine from the Land of Israel say: 'the fruit of her vine.'
For fruit of the Seven Species say: 'the fruits'; for produce of the Land of Israel say: 'her fruits.'
Blessings for enjoyment.
For a cooked dish made from any of the five grain species, for baked goods made from these grains other than bread, and for rice, recite:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who creates varieties of nourishing foods.
Over wine, recite the blessing:
Blessed are You, Adonoy our God, King of the Universe, Creator of the fruit of the vine.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: Over fruit growing on trees, recite the blessing:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who creates the fruit of the tree.
Over produce of the ground, recite the blessing:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who creates the fruit of the ground.
For foods that do not grow from the ground, such as meat, fish, milk, cheese, and the like, and for water or other beverages except wine, recite:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, by whose word all things came to be.

After eating tree fruits (except the seven species), produce of the earth, or foods that do not grow from the earth (other than wine), if one has eaten an olive-sized quantity within the usual eating time (four minutes; some say eight), or has drunk a revi'it in one continuous drink, recite the following blessing:
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who creates many living beings and their needs, for all the things You have created to sustain the life of every living creature. Blessed is the Life of all worlds.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: For a pleasant scent from trees (meaning plants whose hard stalk remains throughout the year and whose leaves grow from the stem rather than directly from the roots), recite:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who creates fragrant trees.
Over a pleasant fragrance from herbs, recite the blessing:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who creates fragrant herbs.
For a pleasant scent that is neither woody nor herbaceous, or when unsure whether the plant is a tree or an herb, recite:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who creates varieties of fragrant spices.

If someone buys or makes new clothes—or even buys secondhand clothing or receives garments as a gift—and rejoices in them, they recite Shehecheyanu because of that joy. The general rule is that any garment that brings its owner joy warrants this blessing, even if others would not rejoice in it. Conversely, if a wealthy person feels no joy over a purchased garment, that person does not recite Shehecheyanu, even though the same garment would bring a poor person joy (Ben Ish Hai, Re'eh, second year, paragraph 4). The blessing is also recited over a fruit that appears anew each year at a definite season. But for fruit whose older and newer crops cannot be distinguished—such as walnuts, almonds, and apples sold all year—the blessing is not recited merely because one knows a particular item is newly harvested (ibid., paragraph 10). The custom on eating a new seasonal fruit is to recite the fruit blessing first, then Shehecheyanu.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who has kept us alive, sustained us, and brought us to this season.
Shabbat morning service.
Pray as on a weekday morning through 'Let every soul praise the LORD,' after 'The LORD reigns,' then continue here.

For the director of music. A psalm of David. The heavens declare the glory of God; the skies proclaim the work of his hands. Day after day they pour forth speech; night after night they reveal knowledge. They have no speech, they use no words; no sound is heard from them. Yet their voice goes out into all the earth, their words to the ends of the world. In the heavens God has pitched a tent for the sun. It is like a bridegroom coming out of his chamber, like a champion rejoicing to run his course. It rises at one end of the heavens and makes its circuit to the other; nothing is deprived of its warmth. The law of the Lord is perfect, refreshing the soul. The statutes of the Lord are trustworthy, making wise the simple. The precepts of the Lord are right, giving joy to the heart. The commands of the Lord are radiant, giving light to the eyes. The fear of the Lord is pure, enduring forever. The decrees of the Lord are firm, and all of them are righteous. They are more precious than gold, than much pure gold; they are sweeter than honey, than honey from the honeycomb. By them your servant is warned; in keeping them there is great reward. But who can discern their own errors? Forgive my hidden faults. Keep your servant also from willful sins; may they not rule over me. Then I will be blameless, innocent of great transgression. May these words of my mouth and this meditation of my heart be pleasing in your sight, Lord, my Rock and my Redeemer.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: Rejoice in the LORD, O ye righteous, Praise is comely for the upright. Give thanks unto the LORD with harp, Sing praises unto Him with the psaltery of ten strings. Sing unto Him a new song; Play skilfully amid shouts of joy. For the word of the LORD is upright; And all His work is done in faithfulness. He loveth righteousness and justice; The earth is full of the lovingkindness of the LORD. By the word of the LORD were the heavens made; And all the host of them by the breath of His mouth. He gathereth the waters of the sea together as a heap; He layeth up the deeps in storehouses. Let all the earth fear the LORD; Let all the inhabitants of the world stand in awe of Him. For He spoke, and it was; He commanded, and it stood. The LORD bringeth the counsel of the nations to nought; He maketh the thoughts of the peoples to be of no effect. The counsel of the LORD standeth for ever, The thoughts of His heart to all generations. Happy is the nation whose God is the LORD; The people whom He hath chosen for His own inheritance. The LORD looketh from heaven; He beholdeth all the sons of men; From the place of His habitation He looketh intently Upon all the inhabitants of the earth; He that fashioneth the hearts of them all, That considereth all their doings. A king is not saved by the multitude of a host; A mighty man is not delivered by great strength. A horse is a vain thing for safety; Neither doth it afford escape by its great strength. Behold, the eye of the LORD is toward them that fear Him, Toward them that wait for His mercy; To deliver their soul from death, And to keep them alive in famine. Our soul hath waited for the LORD; He is our help and our shield. For in Him doth our heart rejoice, Because we have trusted in His holy name. Let Thy mercy, O LORD, be upon us, According as we have waited for Thee.
paragraphs.note: Exact complete Hebrew passage matched to the bundled Tanakh; no fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: [A Psalm] of David; when he changed his demeanour before Abimelech, who drove him away, and he departed. I will bless the LORD at all times; His praise shall continually be in my mouth. My soul shall glory in the LORD; The humble shall hear thereof, and be glad. O magnify the LORD with me, And let us exalt His name together. I sought the LORD, and He answered me, And delivered me from all my fears. They looked unto Him, and were radiant; And their faces shall never be abashed. This poor man cried, and the LORD heard, And saved him out of all his troubles. The angel of the LORD encampeth round about them that fear Him, And delivereth them. O consider and see that the LORD is good; Happy is the man that taketh refuge in Him. O fear the LORD, ye His holy ones; For there is no want to them that fear Him. The young lions do lack, and suffer hunger; But they that seek the LORD want not any good thing. Come, ye children, hearken unto me; I will teach you the fear of the LORD. Who is the man that desireth life, and loveth days, That he may see good therein? Keep thy tongue from evil, And thy lips from speaking guile. Depart from evil, and do good; Seek peace, and pursue it. The eyes of the LORD are toward the righteous, And His ears are open unto their cry. The face of the LORD is against them that do evil, To cut off the remembrance of them from the earth. They cried, and the LORD heard, And delivered them out of all their troubles. The LORD is nigh unto them that are of a broken heart, And saveth such as are of a contrite spirit. Many are the ills of the righteous, But the LORD delivereth him out of them all. He keepeth all his bones; Not one of them is broken. Evil shall kill the wicked; And they that hate the righteous shall be held guilty. The LORD redeemeth the soul of His servants; And none of them that take refuge in Him shall be desolate.
paragraphs.note: Exact complete Hebrew passage matched to the bundled Tanakh; no fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: A Prayer of Moses the man of God. Lord, Thou hast been our dwelling-place in all generations. Before the mountains were brought forth, Or ever Thou hadst formed the earth and the world, Even from everlasting to everlasting, Thou art God. Thou turnest man to contrition; And sayest: 'Return, ye children of men.' For a thousand years in Thy sight Are but as yesterday when it is past, And as a watch in the night. Thou carriest them away as with a flood; they are as a sleep; In the morning they are like grass which groweth up. In the morning it flourisheth, and groweth up; In the evening it is cut down, and withereth. For we are consumed in Thine anger, And by Thy wrath are we hurried away. Thou hast set our iniquities before Thee, Our secret sins in the light of Thy countenance. For all our days are passed away in Thy wrath; We bring our years to an end as a tale that is told. The days of our years are threescore years and ten, Or even by reason of strength fourscore years; Yet is their pride but travail and vanity; For it is speedily gone, and we fly away. Who knoweth the power of Thine anger, And Thy wrath according to the fear that is due unto Thee? So teach us to number our days, That we may get us a heart of wisdom. Return, O LORD; how long? And let it repent Thee concerning Thy servants. O satisfy us in the morning with Thy mercy; That we may rejoice and be glad all our days. Make us glad according to the days wherein Thou hast afflicted us, According to the years wherein we have seen evil. Let Thy work appear unto Thy servants, And Thy glory upon their children. And let the graciousness of the Lord our God be upon us; Establish Thou also upon us the work of our hands; Yea, the work of our hands establish Thou it.
paragraphs.note: Exact complete Hebrew passage matched to the bundled Tanakh; no fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: O thou that dwellest in the covert of the Most High, And abidest in the shadow of the Almighty; I will say of the LORD, who is my refuge and my fortress, My God, in whom I trust, That He will deliver thee from the snare of the fowler, And from the noisome pestilence. He will cover thee with His pinions, And under His wings shalt thou take refuge; His truth is a shield and a buckler. Thou shalt not be afraid of the terror by night, Nor of the arrow that flieth by day; Of the pestilence that walketh in darkness, Nor of the destruction that wasteth at noonday. A thousand may fall at Thy side, And ten thousand at Thy right hand; It shall not come nigh thee. Only with thine eyes shalt thou behold, And see the recompense of the wicked. For thou hast made the LORD who is my refuge, Even the Most High, thy habitation. There shall no evil befall thee, Neither shall any plague come nigh thy tent. For He will give His angels charge over thee, To keep thee in all thy ways. They shall bear thee upon their hands, Lest thou dash thy foot against a stone. Thou shalt tread upon the lion and asp; The young lion and the serpent shalt thou trample under feet. 'Because he hath set his love upon Me, therefore will I deliver him; I will set him on high, because he hath known My name. He shall call upon Me, and I will answer him; I will be with him in trouble; I will rescue him, and bring him to honour. With long life will I satisfy him, And make Him to behold My salvation.'

paragraphs.text: On a festival, add the psalm associated with that festival here.

A Psalm. Sing to Adonoy, a new song for He has performed wonders; His right hand effected deliverance for Him [as did] His holy arm. Adonoy has made known His deliverance, before the eyes of the nations He has revealed His justice. He remembered His kindliness and faithfulness to the House of Israel; all the ends of the earth have seen the deliverance of our God. Raise your voice unto Adonoy all [inhabitants of] the earth! burst forth into exultation, sing, and play music! Play to Adonoy with a harp, with harp and the sound of music. With trumpets and the sound of the shofar raise your voices before the King, Adonoy. The sea and its fullness, will roar with joy! [also] the world and those who dwell therein. Rivers will clap hands, together, mountains will sing. Before Adonoy when He comes to judge the earth; He will judge mankind with righteousness and peoples with uprightness.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: A Song of Ascents. I will lift up mine eyes unto the mountains: From whence shall my help come? My help cometh from the LORD, Who made heaven and earth. He will not suffer thy foot to be moved; He that keepeth thee will not slumber. Behold, He that keepeth Israel Doth neither slumber nor sleep. The LORD is thy keeper; The LORD is thy shade upon thy right hand. The sun shall not smite thee by day, Nor the moon by night. The LORD shall keep thee from all evil; He shall keep thy soul. The LORD shall guard thy going out and thy coming in, From this time forth and for ever.
paragraphs.note: Exact complete Hebrew passage matched to the bundled Tanakh; no fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: A Song of Ascents; of David. I rejoiced when they said unto me: 'Let us go unto the house of the LORD.' Our feet are standing within thy gates, O Jerusalem; Jerusalem, that art builded as a city that is compact together; Whither the tribes went up, even the tribes of the LORD, as a testimony unto Israel, to give thanks unto the name of the LORD. For there were set thrones for judgment, the thrones of the house of David. Pray for the peace of Jerusalem; May they prosper that love thee. Peace be within thy walls, and prosperity within thy palaces. For my brethren and companions' sakes, I will now say: 'Peace be within thee.' For the sake of the house of the LORD our God I will seek thy good.
paragraphs.note: Exact complete Hebrew passage matched to the bundled Tanakh; no fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: A Song of Ascents. Unto Thee I lift up mine eyes, O Thou that art enthroned in the heavens. Behold, as the eyes of servants unto the hand of their master, As the eyes of a maiden unto the hand of her mistress; So our eyes look unto the LORD our God, Until He be gracious unto us. Be gracious unto us, O LORD, be gracious unto us; For we are full sated with contempt. Our soul is full sated With the scorning of those that are at ease, And with the contempt of the proud oppressors.
paragraphs.note: Exact complete Hebrew passage matched to the bundled Tanakh; no fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: A Song of Ascents; of David. 'If it had not been the LORD who was for us', Let Israel now say; 'If it had not been the LORD who was for us, When men rose up against us, Then they had swallowed us up alive, when their wrath was kindled against us; Then the waters had overwhelmed us, the stream had gone over our soul; Then the proud waters Had gone over our soul.' Blessed be the LORD, who hath not given us as a prey to their teeth. Our soul is escaped as a bird out of the snare of the fowlers; The snare is broken, and we are escaped. Our help is in the name of the LORD, Who made heaven and earth.
paragraphs.note: Exact complete Hebrew passage matched to the bundled Tanakh; no fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: Hallelujah. Praise ye the name of the LORD; Give praise, O ye servants of the LORD, Ye that stand in the house of the LORD, In the courts of the house of our God. Praise ye the LORD, for the LORD is good; Sing praises unto His name, for it is pleasant. For the LORD hath chosen Jacob unto Himself, And Israel for His own treasure. For I know that the LORD is great, And that our Lord is above all gods. Whatsoever the LORD pleased, that hath He done, In heaven and in earth, in the seas and in all deeps; Who causeth the vapours to ascend from the ends of the earth; He maketh lightnings for the rain; He bringeth forth the wind out of His treasuries. Who smote the first-born of Egypt, Both of man and beast. He sent signs and wonders into the midst of thee, O Egypt, Upon Pharaoh, and upon all his servants. Who smote many nations, And slew mighty kings: Sihon king of the Amorites, And Og king of Bashan, And all the kingdoms of Canaan; And gave their land for a heritage, A heritage unto Israel His people. O LORD, Thy name endureth for ever; Thy memorial, O LORD, throughout all generations. For the LORD will judge His people, And repent Himself for His servants. The idols of the nations are silver and gold, The work of men's hands. They have mouths, but they speak not; Eyes have they, but they see not; They have ears, but they hear not; Neither is there any breath in their mouths. They that make them shall be like unto them; Yea, every one that trusteth in them. O house of Israel, bless ye the LORD; O house of Aaron, bless ye the LORD; O house of Levi, bless ye the LORD; Ye that fear the LORD, bless ye the LORD. Blessed be the LORD out of Zion, Who dwelleth at Jerusalem. Hallelujah.
