paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: [May the] L·rd shine His countenance upon you & give you grace. [Cong. Answers : Amen]
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: [May the] L·rd lift His countenance upon you & place peace upon you. [Cong. Answers : Amen]
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: If no kohanim go up to bless the congregation, the prayer leader says:
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: Our God and God of our ancestors, bless us with the threefold blessing in the Torah, written by the hand of Moshe Your servant and spoken from the mouth of Aaron and his sons, the kohanim, Your holy people, as it is said:
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: [May the] L·rd bless you & protect you. [Cong. Answers : Thus, May it Be His Will]
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: [May the] L·rd shine His countenance upon you & give you grace. [Cong. Answers : Thus, May it Be His Will]
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: [May the] L·rd lift His countenance upon you & place peace upon you. [Cong. Answers : Thus, May it Be His Will]
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: Grant peace, goodness, blessing, life, favor, kindness, righteousness and compassion to us and to all Israel Your people. Bless us all together, our Father, by the light of Your face, for by that light You have given us Torah and life, love and kindness, righteousness and compassion, blessing and peace. May it be good in Your sight to bless us and all Your people Israel with abundant strength and peace. On Shabbat Shuvah add: In the Book of Life, blessing and peace, good livelihood, deliverance and comfort, and good decrees, may we and all Your people the house of Israel be remembered and inscribed for a good life and peace. Blessed are You, LORD, who blesses His people Israel with peace. Amen.
Let the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable before Thee, O LORD, my Rock, and my Redeemer.
paragraphs.note: Exact complete Hebrew passage matched to the bundled Tanakh; no fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: My G·d! Guard my tongue from Bad, & my lips from [speaking] deceit. And those that curse me, let my soul be silent. And let my soul be like the dust to all. Open my heart to Your Torah, & after Your Mitzvot (commandments) let my soul pursue, & all that rise against me for bad, quickly nullify their counsel & ruin their thoughts. Do [it] for the sake of Your Name, do [it] for the sake of Your right (mercy), do [it] for the sake of Your Torah, do [it] for the sake of Your Holiness. For the sake of refraining Your beloved (Israel, from sufferance), Your right (mercy) Deliver [us], & answer us.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: It is customary to say here a verse whose first and last letters match the first and last letters of one’s given name.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: Let the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable before Thee, O LORD, my Rock, and my Redeemer.
paragraphs.note: Exact complete Hebrew passage matched to the bundled Tanakh; no fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: He who makes peace in His heights—on Shabbat Shuvah say 'the peace'—may He in His compassion make peace for us and for all His people Israel; and say: Amen.

May it be Your will before You, L·rd, Our G-d and G-d of our fathers – that You build the Holy Temple speedily in our days. And give us our share in Your Torah – to do the laws of Your will and to serve You with a perfect heart.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: After the cantor's repetition some say:

Blessed be the name of the LORD From this time forth and for ever. From the rising of the sun unto the going down thereof The LORD'S name is to be praised. The LORD is high above all nations, His glory is above the heavens. O LORD, our Lord, How glorious is Thy name in all the earth!
paragraphs.note: Every colon-delimited fragment matched a unique near-exact complete Tanakh verse; reviewed orthographic/qere alignment only.

paragraphs.text: The prayer leader recites Kaddish Titkabbal.

Exalted & sanctified be His (G·d's) great Name. [cong. - Amen.] In this world that He created according to His will. May His Kingdom reign, & may he cause His redemption to sprout & may He hasten His Messiah. [cong. - Amen.] In your lifetime & in your days, & in the lifetime of the whole house of Israel, speedily & soon; & say ye, Amen. [cong. - Amen.] Be His great Name blessed forever & throughout eternity. Blessed, lauded, glorified, exalted, extolled & honored, uplifted & supremely exalted, the Name of the Holy One, Blessed be He. [cong. - Amen.] Beyond all blessings, songs, praises & consolations of this world to express; & say ye, [cong. - Amen.]
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur (deterministic preferred wording).

paragraphs.text: May our prayers and supplications be accepted, together with the prayers and supplications of all the House of Israel, before our Father in heaven; and say: Amen. [Amen]

May abundant peace descend from heaven: life, plenty, salvation, consolation, deliverance, healing, redemption, forgiveness, atonement, relief and rescue for us and for all His people Israel; and say: Amen. [Amen]
May the One who makes peace in His heights, in His mercy, make peace for us and for all His people Israel; and say: Amen. [Amen]

All Israel has a share in the World to Come, as it is said: “Your people are all righteous; they shall inherit the land forever—the branch of My planting, the work of My hands, in which I take pride.”
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: Rabbi Judah said: Happy is the person whose labor is in Torah and who gives pleasure to the Creator, growing with a good name and departing the world with a good name. Of such a person Solomon said in his wisdom: 'A good name is better than good oil, and the day of death than the day of birth.' Study much Torah and you shall be given much reward. Know that the reward of the righteous awaits in the world to come.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Rabbi Hananiah son of Akashya said: The Holy One, blessed be He, wished to grant merit to Israel; therefore He gave them an abundance of Torah and commandments, as it is said: 'The LORD desired, for the sake of His righteousness, to magnify and glorify the Torah.'
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: There is none like our God, none like our Lord, none like our King, none like our Savior. Who is like our God, who is like our Lord, who is like our King, who is like our Savior? Let us thank our God, our Lord, our King and our Savior. Blessed is our God, blessed is our Lord, blessed is our King, blessed is our Savior. You are our God, You are our Lord, You are our King, You are our Savior. You will save us; You will rise and show mercy to Zion, for the time to favor her has come, the appointed time has arrived.
The preparation of the incense.

[Incense Offering] You are the L·rd, Our G·d, that our Forefathers burned before You the incense spices at the time that the Holy Temple stood – like You commanded them through Moshe, Your Prophet, like it is written in your Torah.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: And the L·rd said to Moshe – Take for yourself spices- balsam sap / Nataf / & onycha / Sh-h'elet & galbanum / H'elbona, spices & pure frankincense / Levona – each shall be of equal weight. And you shall prepare it (the spices) as incense – a compound, the work of a spice mixer, blended (or salted) pure & holy. And you shall grind from it very well, and you shall take from it, before the [tent of] testimony – in the Tent of Meeting - that I shall meet with you there – holy, holy it shall be for you. And it says – and Aharon shall offer as incense, the incense spices each & every morning when he cleans the lamps he shall offer it. And when Aharon Ascends, he shall offer the incense – a regular incense offering before the L·rd – throughout your generations.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: Our Rabbis Taught, The compound of the Incense, how was it done? Three-hundred & Sixty-eight Maneh (a measure) was in it – 365 [maneh] – like the count of the days of the solar year. One Maneh daily – half in the morning and half in the evening and the three extra maneh – where those of which the Chief Kohen entered [the holy of holies] and took from them a full palm-full on the Yom Kippur – he would return them to the grinder on the eve of Yom Kippur, in order to accomplish the mitzvah – in the finest of finest [way] and 11 spices were in it – and these are they:
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: 1) Balsam, 2) onycha, 3) & galbanum 4) frankincense – the weight of 70 maneh each. 5) myrrh, 6) cassia & 7) spikenard & 8) saffron – [each] a weight of 16, 16 maneh. 9) costus – 12 maneh 10) aromatic bark – three [maneh] 11) cinnamon – 9 (maneh) [Added also were] Lye of Carsina – 9 Kavs (a measure), Wine of Cypres – 3 Seahs and 3 kavs- and if one did not find wine of Cypres – he brings old wine. Salt of Sodom – a quarter [of a kav.] An ascension of smoke – a small amount. Rabbi Nathan, the Babylonian, says – even the resin of the Jordan – a bit. If he put in it honey it is invalid and if he omitted one from all of its spices, he is liable for death [penalty].
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: Rabban Shimeon Son of Gamliel says : The Tzorit is sap, that flows from the Balsam tree. The Lye of Karsina, what does it come [to do]? – in order to rub the onycha in order for it to be beautiful. The wine of Cyprus, why is it brought? in order to soak in it the Onycha, in order for it to be sharp. But is not urine – better [to make it sharp] – rather we do not bring in urine into the Sanctuary out of respect.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: We learned in [a Baraita] Rabbi Nathan Says - When he chops – he says “Hadek Heitev, Hetitev Hadek / Chop Well, Well Chop” because the voice is good for spices. The incense compound divided in half is Kosher. For a third or a-quarter we did not hear [the law]. Rabbi Yehuda said “This is the general rule – if it is in the same proportion – it is Kosher for half, & if it lacks one from all of the spices – he is liable for the death penalty.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: Bar Kapara taught once every sixty or seventy years there were remains [of the spices] of half. And Bar Kapparah also taught , if one was to add a Kartov [a measure] of honey a person would not be able to stand because of the fragrance. And why do we not mix in it honey? Because the Torah says “For any leaven or any honey, do not offer incense from it – as a fire offering. L·rd of hosts, is with us. He is our refuge for us the G·d of Yaakov / Jacob forever. L·rd of hosts, happy is the man that has faith in You. L·rd save, the King will answer us on the day we call. And pleasant to the L·rd is the offering of Yehudah / Judah and Yerusalayim / Jerusalem – like the days of old.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: It was taught in the school of Elijah: Whoever studies halakhot every day is assured a place in the World to Come, as it is said, 'His ways are everlasting.' Read not halikhot ('ways'), but halakhot ('laws'). Rabbi Elazar said in the name of Rabbi Hanina: Torah scholars increase peace in the world, as it is said, 'All your children shall be taught of the LORD, and great shall be the peace of your children.' Read not banayikh ('your children'), but bonayikh ('your builders'). May there be peace within your walls and tranquility in your palaces. For the sake of my brothers and friends, let me speak peace concerning you. For the sake of the house of the LORD our God, I will seek your good. May you see your children's children; peace be upon Israel. Great peace have those who love Your Torah, and they have no stumbling block. The LORD will give strength to His people; the LORD will bless His people with peace.
The congregation recites the “Al Yisrael” Kaddish.

Exalted & sanctified be His (G·d's) great Name. [cong. - Amen.] In this world that He created according to His will. May His Kingdom reign, & may he cause His redemption to sprout & may He hasten His Messiah. [cong. - Amen.] In your lifetime & in your days, & in the lifetime of the whole house of Israel, speedily & soon; & say ye, Amen. [cong. - Amen.] Be His great Name blessed forever & throughout eternity. Blessed, lauded, glorified, exalted, extolled & honored, uplifted & supremely exalted, the Name of the Holy One, Blessed be He. [cong. - Amen.] Beyond all blessings, songs, praises & consolations of this world to express; & say ye, [cong. - Amen.]
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur (deterministic preferred wording).

paragraphs.text: For Yisrael, for the rabbis, for their students, and for all the students of their students, who engage in the holy Torah, whether in this place or in any other place. May there be for us, for them, and for you, grace, kindness, and compassion from the presence of the Master of Heaven and Earth. And say, Amen. [Amen]
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: May there be abundant peace from Heaven, life, satisfaction, salvation, consolation, deliverance, healing, redemption, forgiveness, atonement, relief, and rescue for us and for all His people Israel. And say, Amen. [Amen] He who makes peace in His high places, may He in His mercy make peace upon us and upon all His people Israel. And say, Amen. [Amen]
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: Those reciting Kaddish say: Bless the LORD, who is to be blessed.
The congregation responds: Blessed is the LORD, who is blessed forever and ever.
Aleinu Leshabeah'
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur (deterministic preferred wording).

paragraphs.text: It is [incumbent] upon us to praise the L·rd of all. To bestow Greatness to the Molder of creation, for He did not make us as the nations of the lands, & he did not establish us like the families of the earth, for He did not assign our portion as theirs, & our lot like all the multitudes - for they bow to vanity & emptiness & pray to a god that saves not. And we bow before the King, the King of all Kings, the Holy One, Blessed be He, Who spreads out the heavens & creates the foundation of the earth. And the seat of His precious abode is in Heaven above & the divine presence of his power, is in the highest heights. He is our G·d, & there is no other. Our G·d is true, & no other is beside Him. Like it is written in the Torah - "And you shall know today, & you shall take it to heart, that it is the L·rd (Hash·m), Who is G·d in the heavens above & upon the earth below. There is no other.”
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: Therefore, we will hope to You L·rd, our G·d to see speedily the glory of Your Might - to remove abominable idolatry from the earth & the false gods be utterly terminated, to repair the world with the Kingship of the Al·mighty. And all living flesh will call in Your Name to turn back to You all the wicked of the earth. They will recognize & will know, all the inhabitants of the earth, that to You that every knee shall bow down, & every tongue. Before you they will kneel & bow down & give honor to Your glorious name & they will all accept the yolk of Your Kingship. And Reign upon them speedily forever & ever. For the Kingship, it is Yours. And forevermore reign in glory. Like it is written in your Torah, “The L·rd will reign forever & ever.” And it is said “and it will be the L·rd will Be King upon all of the earth. On that day the L·rd will be One (ie, only He will be worshiped) & His name One.” And in Your Torah, L·rd, Our G·d, it is written saying “Hear Oh Israel, the L·rd is our G·d the L·rd is One.”
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur (deterministic preferred wording).

paragraphs.text: Kiddush for the day.

A Psalm of David. The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want. He maketh me to lie down in green pastures; He leadeth me beside the still waters. He restoreth my soul; He guideth me in straight paths for His name's sake. Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for Thou art with me; Thy rod and Thy staff, they comfort me. Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies; Thou hast anointed my head with oil; my cup runneth over. Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life; And I shall dwell in the house of the LORD for ever.
paragraphs.note: Exact complete Hebrew passage matched to the bundled Tanakh; no fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: If thou turn away thy foot because of the sabbath, From pursuing thy business on My holy day; And call the sabbath a delight, And the holy of the LORD honourable; And shalt honour it, not doing thy wonted ways, Nor pursuing thy business, nor speaking thereof; Then shalt thou delight thyself in the LORD, And I will make thee to ride upon the high places of the earth, And I will feed thee with the heritage of Jacob thy father; For the mouth of the LORD hath spoken it.
paragraphs.note: Every colon-delimited fragment matched a unique near-exact complete Tanakh verse; reviewed orthographic/qere alignment only.

paragraphs.text: The children of Israel shall keep the Sabbath, observing the Sabbath throughout their generations as an everlasting covenant. Between Me and the children of Israel it is a sign forever: in six days the LORD made heaven and earth, and on the seventh day He ceased and rested. Therefore the LORD blessed the Sabbath day and sanctified it.
The person reciting Kiddush says this, even when reciting Kiddush alone:
With your permission, honored ones:
And they respond:
To life!
Blessed are You, Adonoy our God, King of the Universe, Creator of the fruit of the vine.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: Drink a quarter of a log or at least a cheekful and offer some to those present. Then wash the hands while standing, recite the blessing for handwashing, say 'who brings forth bread from the earth,' and break bread over two loaves, as on Friday night.
Before the meal, one should say:

For the sake of uniting the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Presence, in awe and love and in love and awe, uniting the letters Yod–Heh with Vav–Heh in perfect unity in the name of all Israel: I now come to fulfill the commandment of the second meal of the holy Sabbath, associated with Abraham the devout, to repair its root in the highest realm. Through its merit may we be spared the judgment of Gehinnom, and may the verse be fulfilled in us: 'Then shall you delight yourself in the Lord,' and so forth. May the favor of the Lord our God be upon us; establish the work of our hands for us; yes, establish the work of our hands.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Minchah for the holy Sabbath.

For the sake of uniting the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Presence, in awe and love and in love and awe, to unite the letters Yod–Heh with Vav–Heh in perfect unity in the name of all Israel: we now come to recite the Minchah prayer of the holy Sabbath, instituted by our father Isaac, peace be upon him, together with all the commandments included in it, to repair its root in the highest realm, to bring delight to our Maker and carry out our Creator's will. May the favor of the Lord our God be upon us; establish the work of our hands for us; yes, establish the work of our hands.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: To the conductor: [set] on the Gitit (musical instrument from city of Gat) by the sons of Korah – a psalm: How beloved are your dwelling places (The Holy Temple / Beit Hamikdash) L·rd of Hosts. My soul yearns & is consumed [with love] for Your courtyards, oh L·rd, my heart & my flesh sing to [You, oh] Living G·d. Even the bird found a house & a sparrow has its nest – that it places its fledglings (chicks) - upon Your altars - L·rd of hosts – my King & my G·d. Happy are those that dwell in Your house – they will praise You forever more. Happy is the man that finds his strength in You [Hash·m] - whose paths [wishing to travel to Beit Hamikdash] are in their hearts. Those that traverse the valley of tears, will make it a spring & also blessings will enwrap those who taught. They will go from strength to strength & will appear before G·d in Tzion. L·rd, G·d of hosts, hear my prayer & listen G·d of Yaakov forever. See our shield (the Temple), G·d & let us see the face of Your anointed one. For greater is one day in Your courtyard G·d than a 1000 [days in exile], I have chosen [to stand] at the threshold of the house of G·d than to live [in comfort] among tents of the wicked. For a sun & shield [are You] L·rd - my G·d, grace & honor do you give L·rd - You do not withhold good from those that go in simple faith. L·rd of Hosts - Fortunate is the man that trusts in You.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: And the LORD spoke unto Moses, saying: Command the children of Israel, and say unto them: My food which is presented unto Me for offerings made by fire, of a sweet savour unto Me, shall ye observe to offer unto Me in its due season. And thou shalt say unto them: This is the offering made by fire which ye shall bring unto the LORD: he-lambs of the first year without blemish, two day by day, for a continual burnt-offering. The one lamb shalt thou offer in the morning, and the other lamb shalt thou offer at dusk; and the tenth part of an ephah of fine flour for a meal-offering, mingled with the fourth part of a hin of beaten oil. It is a continual burnt-offering, which was offered in mount Sinai, for a sweet savour, an offering made by fire unto the LORD. And the drink-offering thereof shall be the fourth part of a hin for the one lamb; in the holy place shalt thou pour out a drink-offering of strong drink unto the LORD. And the other lamb shalt thou present at dusk; as the meal-offering of the morning, and as the drink-offering thereof, thou shalt present it, an offering made by fire, of a sweet savour unto the LORD.
paragraphs.note: Exact complete Hebrew passage matched to the bundled Tanakh; no fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: Happy are those that dwell in Your house, they will yet praise You forever. Happy is the people for whom this is so, happy is the people that the L·rd is their G·d.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: A praise of David, I will exalt You my G·d, the King, & I will bless Your Name forever & ever. Every day I will bless you, & I will laud Your Name forever & ever. Great is the L·rd & He is greatly lauded, & His Greatness is unfathomable. Generation to generation will praise Your deeds, & Your mighty acts they will relate. The splendorous glory of Your Majesty & Your wondrous acts I shall discuss. And the might of Your awesome acts they will speak & Your greatness, I will relate. A recollection of Your great goodness they will express & Your righteousness they will sing. Gracious & Merciful is the L·rd, Slow-to anger & Great in kindness. The L·rd is good to all & His Mercies are on all His works. All Your works shall thank You, L·rd, & Your pious ones shall bless You. Of the glory of Your Kingdom they will relate, & Your Might they shall speak.To inform human beings of Your Mighty acts & of the glorious Majesty of His Kingdom. Your Kingship is Kingship of all worlds & Your dominion is for all generations.The L·rd supports all those who fall, & He straightens all who are bent over. The eyes of all are [looking] upon You for hope, & You provide them their food in the proper time. * You open Your hand, & You satisfy all the living's wants. Righteous is the L·rd in all His ways, & Pious in all His deeds. The L·rd is close to all who call Him, to all that call upon Him with sincerity. The will of those that fear Him He will do, & their cries He will hear & save them. The L·rd protects all who love Him, & all of the wicked He will destroy. Praise of the L·rd will my mouth speak, & all flesh shall bless His holy Name for ever & ever. And we will bless G·d from now to eternity. [Let us all] Praise G·d!
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: A redeemer shall come to Zion.

A Redeemer shall come to Zion and to those in Jacob who turn from wrongdoing, declares the Lord. 'As for Me, this is My covenant with them,' says the Lord: 'My spirit upon you and My words which I placed in your mouth shall not depart from your mouth, or the mouths of your children or their children, from now and forever.' Yet You are holy, enthroned upon the praises of Israel. And one called to another, saying: 'Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of Hosts; the whole earth is full of His glory!' [The following Aramaic is said quietly:] They receive from one another and say: Holy in the highest heavens, the dwelling of His Presence; holy upon the earth, the work of His might; holy for all ages and for ever and ever: the Lord of Hosts, the whole earth is filled with the radiance of His glory. Then a spirit lifted me, and I heard behind me a great rushing sound: 'Blessed is the glory of the Lord from His place.' The spirit raised me, and I heard behind me a mighty trembling voice praising and saying: 'Blessed is the glory of the Lord from the place of His Presence.' The Lord shall reign for ever and ever; His kingdom stands for all eternity. Lord, God of Abraham, Isaac and Israel our ancestors, preserve forever the inclination of Your people's hearts toward You, and prepare their hearts for You. He, being merciful, forgives wrongdoing and does not destroy; often He turns away His anger and does not stir up all His wrath. For You, Lord, are good and forgiving and abundant in loving-kindness toward all who call on You. Your righteousness is everlasting righteousness, and Your Torah is truth. Show faithfulness to Jacob, kindness to Abraham, as You swore to our ancestors in days of old. Blessed be the Lord day by day, who bears our burden, the God of our salvation, Selah. The Lord of Hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge, Selah. Lord of Hosts, happy is the person who trusts in You. Lord, save! May the King answer us on the day we call.
paragraphs.note: Identical Hebrew passage to edot Uva LeSion paragraph 1; verify typography and liturgical placement.

paragraphs.text: Blessed is our God, who created us for His glory, separated us from those who stray, gave us the Torah of truth, and planted eternal life within us. May He open our hearts to His Torah and place His love and reverence in them, so that we may fulfill His will and serve Him wholeheartedly. May we not labor in vain or bring forth children for terror. May it be Your will, Lord our God and God of our ancestors, that we observe Your laws and commandments in this world and merit to live and inherit goodness and blessing in the world to come. 'That my soul may sing praise to You and not be silent' [pause briefly]; 'Lord my God, I will thank You forever.' The Lord desires, for His righteousness' sake, to magnify the Torah and make it glorious. Those who know Your name will trust You, for You, Lord, have not forsaken those who seek You. Lord our Master, how majestic is Your name in all the earth! Be strong and let your hearts take courage, all who hope in the Lord.
paragraphs.note: Identical Hebrew passage to edot Uva LeSion paragraph 2; verify typography and liturgical placement.

paragraphs.text: (Prayer Leader says H'atzi- Kaddish)
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur (deterministic preferred wording).

paragraphs.text: Exalted & sanctified be His (G·d's) great Name. [cong. - Amen.] In this world that He created according to His will. May His Kingdom reign, & may he cause His redemption to sprout & may He hasten His Messiah. [cong. - Amen.] In your lifetime & in your days, & in the lifetime of the whole house of Israel, speedily & soon; & say ye, Amen. [cong. - Amen.] Be His great Name blessed forever & throughout eternity. Blessed, lauded, glorified, exalted, extolled & honored, uplifted & supremely exalted, the Name of the Holy One, Blessed be He. [cong. - Amen.] Beyond all blessings, songs, praises & consolations of this world to express; & say ye, [cong. - Amen.]
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur (deterministic preferred wording).

paragraphs.text: Before opening the Ark, one says:
And as for me, may my prayer come before You, LORD, at a favorable time. O God, in Your great kindness answer me with Your faithful salvation. Repeat twice.
Open the Ark and recite:

Blessed is the Name of the Master of the universe. Blessed is Your crown and Your place. May Your good will [be] with Your people Israel forever. Show Your people the redemption of Your right hand in Your Holy Temple. Bestow on us Your excellent light, and accept our prayer with compassion. May it be Your will to prolong our lives in well-being. Let me be counted among the righteous, so that You will have compassion on me and protect me and all that is mine, and all that belongs to Your people, Israel. You are He Who nourishes all and maintains all; You are He Who rules over all; You are He Who rules over kings, and the kingdom is Yours. I am a servant of the Holy One, blessed is He, I bow before Him and before the honor of His Torah at all times. Not in man do I put my trust, nor do I rely on any angel; but only in the God of heaven, Who is the true God, Whose Torah is truth, Whose prophets are true, and Who performs many deeds of goodness and truth. In Him I put my trust and to His honored, holy Name I utter praises. May it be Your will to open my heart to Your Torah, and grant me sons who do Your will, and to fulfill the desires of my heart, and of the heart of Your people Israel, for goodness, for life, and for peace.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed parallel passage from the existing English Siddur.

paragraphs.text: The Torah scroll is taken out, and the following is said:
Blessed be the Omnipresent, who gave the Torah to His people Israel; blessed is He. Happy is the people for whom this is so; happy is the people whose God is the LORD.
While carrying the Torah scroll, the cantor says together with the congregation:

O magnify the LORD with me, And let us exalt His name together. Exalt ye the LORD our God, And prostrate yourselves at His footstool; Holy is He. Exalt ye the LORD our God, And worship at His holy hill; For the LORD our God is holy. The LORD will give strength unto His people; The LORD will bless his people with peace.
paragraphs.note: Every colon-delimited Hebrew fragment matched an exact complete bundled Tanakh verse; translations joined without fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: There is none holy as the Lord, for there is none beside You; neither is there any rock like our God. For who is God except the Lord? And who is a rock other than our God? Moses commanded us a Torah, an inheritance of the congregation of Jacob. It is a tree of life to those who take hold of it, and those who support it are happy. Its ways are ways of pleasantness, and all its paths are peace. Great peace have those who love Your Torah; nothing causes them to stumble. The Lord gives strength to His people; the Lord blesses His people with peace. When I proclaim the name of the Lord, ascribe greatness to our God. All of you, give strength to God and honor to the Torah. Let the heavens rejoice and the earth be glad; let them say among the nations: 'The Lord reigns!' Let Mount Zion rejoice, let the daughters of Judah be glad, because of Your judgments.
paragraphs.note: New English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Raise the Torah scroll, show its writing to the congregation, bow, and say:

This is the Torah that Moses set before the children of Israel. Moses commanded us the Torah as the heritage of the congregation of Jacob. The way of God is perfect, and the word of the LORD is refined; He is a shield to all who seek refuge in Him.
Read at least ten verses from the coming weekly Torah portion. Do not recite Half Kaddish; go immediately to “A Psalm, a Song for the Sabbath Day,” and afterward recite “Yehalelu.”

A Psalm, a song for the Shabbos day. It is good to thank Adonoy, and sing praise to Your Name, Most High. To relate Your kindliness in the morning, and Your faithfulness in the nights. Upon a ten-stringed instrument and lute, in meditation upon the harp. For You have given me joy, Adonoy, with Your deeds, at the work of Your hands I sing joyously. How great are Your works, Adonoy; how infinitely profound are Your thoughts. An empty-headed man cannot know, nor does a fool understand this: When the wicked bloom like grass, and all the evildoers blossom— it is so that they may be destroyed forever. But You will remain on high forever Adonoy. For behold, Your enemies, Adonoy; For behold, Your enemies shall perish; dispersed shall be all evildoers. You uplifted my horn like that of a unicorn; I am saturated with fresh oil. My eye has seen [the defeat of] those who spy on me; of the wicked who rise against me, my ears have heard [that they are doomed]. The righteous will blossom like a date palm, like a cedar in Lebanon, he will grow tall. Planted in the House of Adonoy, in the courtyards of our God they will blossom. They will still be fruitful in old age; they will be full of sap and freshness. To declare that Adonoy is upright; He is my Stronghold; in Whom there is no injustice.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: Return the Torah scroll to its place and recite:

Let them praise the name of the LORD, for His name alone is exalted, His splendor above earth and heaven. He has raised the strength of His people, praise for all His faithful ones, for the children of Israel, the people near Him. Hallelujah! The LORD is God, the LORD is God; in heaven above and upon earth below, there is no other. None among the gods is like You, Lord, and none of their deeds is like Yours. Return us to You, LORD, and we shall return; renew our days as of old.
paragraphs.note: Identical unpointed Hebrew source across sections.

paragraphs.text: For I give you a good taking; Forsake ye not my teaching. Let my prayer be set forth as incense before Thee, The lifting up of my hands as the evening sacrifice.

paragraphs.text: The Amidah for Shabbat afternoon prayer (Minchah).
O Lord, open Thou my lips; and my mouth shall declare Thy praise.
paragraphs.note: Exact complete Hebrew passage matched to the bundled Tanakh; no fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: Blessed are You, LORD our God and God of our ancestors, God of Abraham, God of Isaac, and God of Jacob; the great, mighty, and awesome God, God Most High, who bestows loving-kindness, possesses all things, remembers the kindness of the ancestors, and lovingly brings a redeemer to their descendants for His name's sake. On Shabbat Shuvah add: Remember us for life, O King who desires life, and inscribe us in the Book of Life for Your sake, living God. O King, Helper, Savior, and Shield: blessed are You, LORD, Shield of Abraham.
You are mighty forever, my L·rd, You revive the dead - Greatly capable of saving.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur (deterministic preferred wording).

paragraphs.text: (summer) who causes dew to fall (winter) who causes the winds to blow & the rain to fall.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: You sustain the living with kindness and revive the dead in great mercy; You support the fallen, heal the sick, release the bound, and keep faith with those who sleep in the dust. Who is like You, Master of mighty deeds, and who can be compared with You, O King who causes death and restores life and makes salvation spring forth? On Shabbat Shuvah add: Who is like You, merciful Father, who remembers His creatures for life in mercy? You are faithful to revive the dead. Blessed are You, LORD, who revives the dead.
Kedousha (said in repetition of Amida in quorum of 10 men – in prayer alone skip to “You are Holy”)
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: We will sanctify You & revere You, like the pleasant conversation, of the assembly of the holy Serafim (angels) that recite holiness thrice before You. And as it is written by Your prophet: And one calls to the other & says : Holy, Holy, Holy is the L·rd of hosts. the entire world is filled with His glory. Those facing them, give praise & say: Blessed is the honor of the L·rd from His place. And in Your holy words it is written, stating: The L·rd will reign forever, your G·d, oh zion, for every generation, Halleluy·ah. (Praise G·d!)
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: You are holy, and Your name is holy; holy ones praise You every day, selah. Blessed are You, LORD, the holy God. On Shabbat Shuvah conclude instead: the holy King.

You are One and Your name is One; and who is like Your people Israel, one nation on earth? You gave Your people a day of rest and holiness, a glorious crown of salvation and a splendor of greatness. Abraham shall rejoice, Isaac shall sing, and Jacob and his children shall rest upon it: a rest of love and free offering, a rest of truth and faithfulness, a rest of peace, quiet and security—a complete rest that You desire. May Your children recognize and know that their rest comes from You, and may they sanctify Your name through that rest.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Our God and God of our ancestors, be pleased with our rest. Sanctify us with Your commandments, grant us a portion in Your Torah, satisfy us with Your goodness, gladden our souls with Your salvation, and purify our hearts to serve You sincerely. In love and favor, grant us Your holy Shabbat as an inheritance, LORD our God, and may all Israel who sanctify Your name rest upon it. Blessed are You, LORD, who sanctifies Shabbat.
paragraphs.note: Identical unpointed Hebrew source across sections.

paragraphs.text: Find favor, L·rd, our G·d, in Your people Israel, & to their prayers turn, & restore the [divine offering] service to the inner Sanctuary of Your house, & the fires [of the offerings] of Israel & their prayers speedily lovingly accept with favor, & let You continually have satisfaction from the service of Your people Israel.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: Our G·d, & G·d of Our forefathers, may it rise, & come, arrive, appear, find favor, & be heard, & be considered, & be remembered & our remembrance, & the remembrance of our Patriarchs, & the remembrance of Jerusalem, Your city, & the remembrance of the Messiah, the son of David, Your servant, & the remembrance of your entire People, the house of Israel before You – for deliverance, for good, for grace, for kindness, & mercy, for a good life, on this day of
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: to have mercy on it (this day) upon us & to save us. Remember L·rd, our G·d, on it for good, & consider us on it with blessing, & deliver us on it for good life, With a pronouncement of deliverance & mercy. Take pity & be gracious to us, & have mercy & be compassionate with us & save us for upon You are our eyes turned, For You are G·d, King, gracious & compassionate.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur (deterministic preferred wording).

paragraphs.text: And You, with Your great compassion, desire us & let us be dear, & may our eyes see Your return to Zion with compassion. Bless You, L·rd, Who returns His Divine Presence to Zion.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: [Upon Saying "Modim" / "We are Grateful" One Bows]
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: We are grateful to You, that You are He Who is the L·rd, our G·d, & G·d of our fathers forever, & our Rock, the Rock of our lives & You are He Who is a Shield of salvation. For each & every generation, we will thank You & will relate Your praise, upon our lives that are placed in Your Hands, & upon our souls, that are entrusted in Your hands (when we sleep), & upon Your miracles that all day are with us, & all Your wonders & goodness at all times, at night, & morning & afternoon. The Good [One], for Your mercy never ends, The Merciful [One are You], for Your loving-kindness never ceases, forever we have hope in You.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: Thanks Of the rabbis / Said at repetition of Amid (In the repetition Of the standing prayer, when the prayer leader says “Modim”, the congregation says:) We give thanks to You, that You L·rd, are our God and God of our fathers, God of all flesh, our Creator, the creator [of the works] of Genesis. Blessings and thanks to your great and Holy name, that You gave us life and made us exist. Thus, give us life and have mercy upon us, and gather in our exiles to Your holy courtyards, To observe Your ordinances and to do Your will and to serve You with a complete heart, upon that we give thanks to You. Blessed is the Lord of thanks.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: *(Al HaNissim) (on Purim & Hanuka an extra prayer is added here)
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: Upon the miracles and upon the redemption and upon the mighty acts and for salvation and for the wonders and for the comfort that you did for our fathers in those days at this period.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: On Hanukkah continue: In the days of Matitya son of Yohanan, The high priest, The Hashmonay and his sons when the Wicked Greek empire arose Against your people Israel To make them forget your Torah, and to remove them from the ordinances of your will and you with your great mercy you stood at the time of their suffering , you battle their battles, you judged their laws, you took vengeance upon their vengeance, you gave up over the mighty into the hands of the weak, and the masses in the hands of the few, and the impure Into the hands of the pure, and the wicked into the hands of the righteous, and the intentional sinners into the hands of those that are engaged in your Torah. To you you made your holy and great name In your world and for your people Israel you made a great salvation and deliverance as you do This day. And the afterwords your children came to the inner chambers of your house cleared your sanctuary and purify it your holy Temple and lit candles In your holy courtyard. And they fixed these eight days of Hanukkah – With complete praise and thanks, and you did for them miracles and wonders and we will thank Your great name, Forever.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: On Purim Continue: In the days of Mordekhai & Esther, in Shushan, the Capital (of Ancient Persia) – When Haman, the wicked, stood against them, asking to destroy and kill and annihilate all the Jews – from the Youth to the Elderly, Baby & Women – in a single day – on the 13th of the Twelfth month – which is the month of Adar – and to pillage and take booty and You with Your great mercy – You uprooted his advice & confused his thought & He returned to him his wiles upon his own head – and they hung him & His children upon the gallows. And You did for them miracles and wonders - and we will thank Your great name, Forever.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: For all these things may Your name, our King, be blessed, exalted, and raised up always and forever; may every living creature thank You, selah. On Shabbat Shuvah add: Inscribe all the children of Your covenant for a good life. May they praise and bless Your great name in truth forever, for You are good, the God of our salvation and our help, selah, the good God. Bow at 'Blessed' and straighten at the Divine Name: Blessed are You, LORD, the Good One, whose name is good and to whom thanksgiving is fitting.

Grant peace, goodness, blessing, life, favor, kindness, righteousness and compassion to us and to all Israel Your people. Bless us all together, our Father, by the light of Your face, for by that light You have given us Torah and life, love and kindness, righteousness and compassion, blessing and peace. May it be good in Your sight to bless us and all Your people Israel with abundant strength and peace. On Shabbat Shuvah add: In the Book of Life, blessing and peace, good livelihood, deliverance and comfort, and good decrees, may we and all Your people the house of Israel be remembered and inscribed for a good life and peace. Blessed are You, LORD, who blesses His people Israel with peace. Amen.
Let the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable before Thee, O LORD, my Rock, and my Redeemer.
paragraphs.note: Exact complete Hebrew passage matched to the bundled Tanakh; no fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: My G·d! Guard my tongue from Bad, & my lips from [speaking] deceit. And those that curse me, let my soul be silent. And let my soul be like the dust to all. Open my heart to Your Torah, & after Your Mitzvot (commandments) let my soul pursue, & all that rise against me for bad, quickly nullify their counsel & ruin their thoughts. Do [it] for the sake of Your Name, do [it] for the sake of Your right (mercy), do [it] for the sake of Your Torah, do [it] for the sake of Your Holiness. For the sake of refraining Your beloved (Israel, from sufferance), Your right (mercy) Deliver [us], & answer us.

May it be Your will before You, L·rd, Our G-d and G-d of our fathers – that You build the Holy Temple speedily in our days. And give us our share in Your Torah – to do the laws of Your will and to serve You with a perfect heart.

paragraphs.text: On Shabbat Shuvah, recite Avinu Malkeinu ('Our Father, our King') here.
On a day when Tachanun would have been recited at weekday Minchah, stand and recite Tzidkatekha ('Your righteousness').

Thy righteousness is like the mighty mountains; Thy judgments are like the great deep; Man and beast Thou preservest, O LORD. Thy righteousness also, O God, which reacheth unto high heaven; Thou who hast done great things, O God, who is like unto Thee? Thy righteousness is an everlasting righteousness, and Thy law is truth.

Blessed be the name of the LORD From this time forth and for ever. From the rising of the sun unto the going down thereof The LORD'S name is to be praised. The LORD is high above all nations, His glory is above the heavens. O LORD, our Lord, How glorious is Thy name in all the earth!

Hallelujah. I will give thanks unto the LORD with my whole heart, . In the council of the upright, and in the congregation. The works of the LORD are great, Sought out of all them that have delight therein. His work is glory and majesty; And His righteousness endureth for ever. He hath made a memorial for His wonderful works; The LORD is gracious and full of compassion. He hath given food unto them that fear Him; He will ever be mindful of His covenant. He hath declared to His people the power of His works, In giving them the heritage of the nations. The works of His hands are truth and justice; All His precepts are sure. They are established for ever and ever, They are done in truth and uprightness. He hath sent redemption unto His people; He hath commanded His covenant for ever; Holy and awful is His name. The fear of the LORD is the beginning of wisdom; A good understanding have all they that do thereafter; His praise endureth for ever.

paragraphs.text: Aleinu Leshabeah'
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur (deterministic preferred wording).

paragraphs.text: It is [incumbent] upon us to praise the L·rd of all. To bestow Greatness to the Molder of creation, for He did not make us as the nations of the lands, & he did not establish us like the families of the earth, for He did not assign our portion as theirs, & our lot like all the multitudes - for they bow to vanity & emptiness & pray to a god that saves not. And we bow before the King, the King of all Kings, the Holy One, Blessed be He, Who spreads out the heavens & creates the foundation of the earth. And the seat of His precious abode is in Heaven above & the divine presence of his power, is in the highest heights. He is our G·d, & there is no other. Our G·d is true, & no other is beside Him. Like it is written in the Torah - "And you shall know today, & you shall take it to heart, that it is the L·rd (Hash·m), Who is G·d in the heavens above & upon the earth below. There is no other.”
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: Therefore, we will hope to You L·rd, our G·d to see speedily the glory of Your Might - to remove abominable idolatry from the earth & the false gods be utterly terminated, to repair the world with the Kingship of the Al·mighty. And all living flesh will call in Your Name to turn back to You all the wicked of the earth. They will recognize & will know, all the inhabitants of the earth, that to You that every knee shall bow down, & every tongue. Before you they will kneel & bow down & give honor to Your glorious name & they will all accept the yolk of Your Kingship. And Reign upon them speedily forever & ever. For the Kingship, it is Yours. And forevermore reign in glory. Like it is written in your Torah, “The L·rd will reign forever & ever.” And it is said “and it will be the L·rd will Be King upon all of the earth. On that day the L·rd will be One (ie, only He will be worshiped) & His name One.” And in Your Torah, L·rd, Our G·d, it is written saying “Hear Oh Israel, the L·rd is our G·d the L·rd is One.”
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur (deterministic preferred wording).
