paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Tishbite, rescue us from the mouths of lions; announce good tidings to us at the close of Sabbaths; gladden us, children together with fathers. (Elijah...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: The man called the Tishbite: through him grant us success in Torah; let us hear from his mouth good tidings soon; bring us out from darkness into light. (Elijah...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Fortunate is one who saw his face in a dream; fortunate is one who greeted him and received his greeting in return. May the LORD bless His people with peace. (Elijah...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: As it is written: Behold, I am sending you Elijah the prophet before the coming of the great and awesome day of the LORD. He will turn the hearts of fathers to children and the hearts of children to their fathers.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: At the close of Shabbat one should take care to say 'Our God and God of our fathers, with a good sign and good fortune...' This custom is cited in the Jerusalem Talmud, Tur 299, and later authorities.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Our God and God of our fathers, with a good sign and good fortune, begin for us the six coming working days in peace: free from every sin and transgression, cleansed of every iniquity, guilt, and wickedness, attached to Torah study and good deeds, and graced by You with wisdom, understanding, and knowledge. Let us hear in them joy and gladness. Let no jealousy of us rise in another's heart and no jealousy of another rise in ours. Our King and our God, place blessing, abundance, and success in all the work of our hands. Whoever plans good counsel and good intent for us and for Your people, the House of Israel—strengthen, bless, exalt, and sustain him; establish his counsel, as it is said: 'May He grant you according to your heart and fulfill all your counsel,' and: 'You shall decree a thing and it shall stand for you, and light shall shine upon your ways.' Whoever plans counsel that is not good and thoughts that are not good against us or Your people, the House of Israel—destroy, nullify, cut down, and overturn them; frustrate his counsel, as it is said: 'The LORD frustrates the counsel of nations; He foils the plans of peoples,' and: 'Take counsel and it shall be frustrated; speak a word and it shall not stand, for God is with us.' Open for us, LORD our God, in this week and every week:
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Gates of light, gates of blessing, gates of rejoicing, gates of delight, gates of knowledge, gates of glory and splendor, gates of good counsel, gates of song, gates of joy, gates of compassion, gates of grace and kindness, gates of good life, gates of goodness, gates of salvation, gates of atonement, gates of sustenance, gates of Torah study for its own sake, gates of food, gates of pardon, gates of consolation, gates of forgiveness, gates of help, gates of redemption, gates of good livelihood, gates of charity, gates of exultation, gates of upright independence, gates of complete healing, gates of peace, gates of serenity, gates of Torah, gates of prayer, gates of repentance, gates of deliverance.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: As it is written: The salvation of the righteous is from the LORD, their stronghold in time of trouble. The LORD helps them and delivers them; He delivers them from the wicked and saves them, because they take refuge in Him. And: The LORD has bared His holy arm before the eyes of all nations, and all ends of the earth shall see the salvation of our God. And: The voice of your watchmen—they raise their voices, together they sing, for eye to eye they shall see the LORD returning to Zion. Fulfill for us, LORD our God, the verse: How beautiful upon the mountains are the feet of the herald who announces peace, brings good tidings, announces salvation, and says to Zion: Your God reigns.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: This prayer for success, to be said three times on Motzaei Shabbat, is found in the sacred writings of the holy Rabbi Levi Yitzhak of Berditchev, author of Kedushat Levi:
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: God of Abraham, God of Isaac, and God of Jacob, guard and save Your beloved people Israel from every evil for the sake of Your glorious Name. Behold, the beloved holy Sabbath is departing. May it be Your will that the coming week come upon us with complete faith, faith in the sages, love of friends, attachment to the blessed Creator, faith in Your Thirteen Principles, in a near redemption speedily in our days, in the resurrection of the dead, and in the prophecy of Moses our teacher, peace be upon him.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Master of the world, You who give strength to the weary, give strength also to Your beloved children, the Jews, to praise Your Name and serve You alone. May the coming week come upon us with health and good fortune, success, blessing and kindness, with children, life, and sustenance, for us and for all Israel. And let us say: Amen.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Order of Havdalah
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: First to Zion—behold, here they are; and to Jerusalem I will give a herald. Do not rejoice over me, my enemy: though I have fallen, I rise; though I sit in darkness, the LORD is my light. The Jews had light and gladness, joy and honor. David succeeded in all his ways, and the LORD was with him. Noah found favor in the eyes of the LORD. So may we find favor and good understanding in the eyes of God and man.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Arise, shine, for thy light is come, And the glory of the LORD is risen upon thee. For, behold, darkness shall cover the earth, And gross darkness the peoples; But upon thee the LORD will arise, And His glory shall be seen upon thee.
paragraphs.note: Exact complete Hebrew passage matched to the bundled Tanakh; no fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: He takes the cup in his hand and says:
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: I will lift up the cup of salvation, And call upon the name of the LORD.
paragraphs.note: Exact complete Hebrew passage matched to the bundled Tanakh; no fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: Please, LORD, save now—twice.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Please, LORD, grant success now—twice.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Grant us success; make our ways successful, make our studies successful, and send blessing, abundance, and success into all the work of our hands, as it is written: 'He shall receive blessing from the LORD and righteousness from the God of his salvation.' The Jews had light and gladness, joy and honor. And it is written: 'David succeeded in all his ways, and the LORD was with him.' So may He be with us always.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: With your permission, masters. They answer: To life!
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Blessed are You, Adonoy our God, King of the Universe, Creator of the fruit of the vine.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: At the end of a festival that is not also the end of Shabbat, no blessing is made over spices or the flame.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, Creator of fragrant trees (herbs / kinds of spices).
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Curl the fingertips of the right hand into the palm, with the thumb covered beneath them. Hold them bent before the flame opposite the face, look only at the fingernails and not at the inner sides of the fingers, and recite the blessing (Sha'ar HaKavanot).
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, Creator of the lights of fire.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who distinguishes between holy and ordinary, between light and darkness, between Israel and the nations, and between the seventh day and the six days of labor. Blessed are You, LORD, who distinguishes between holy and ordinary.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Drink a revi'it and recite the after-blessing 'Al HaGefen.' If less than a revi'it was drunk, the after-blessing is not said.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, for the vine and the fruit of the vine, for the produce of the field, and for the desirable, good, and spacious land that You desired and gave as an inheritance to our fathers, to eat of its fruit and be satisfied from its goodness. Have mercy, LORD our God, upon us, upon Israel Your people, upon Jerusalem Your city, upon Mount Zion the dwelling of Your glory, upon Your altar, and upon Your Temple. Rebuild Jerusalem, the holy city, speedily in our days; bring us up into it and gladden us in its rebuilding, and there we shall bless You in holiness and purity.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: On Rosh Chodesh: Remember us for good on this day of Rosh Chodesh.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: On Chol HaMoed Pesach: Gladden us on this Festival of Matzot, on this holy convocation day.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: On Chol HaMoed Sukkot: Gladden us on this Festival of Sukkot, on this holy convocation day.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: For You are good and do good to all, and we thank You, LORD our God, for the land and for the fruit of the vine. For wine of the Land of Israel say 'its vine.' Blessed are You, LORD, for the land and for the fruit of the vine.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Motzaei Shabbat Songs
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: He who separates holy from ordinary—may He forgive our sins. May He multiply our children and our wealth like sand and like the stars at night.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: The day turns away like the shadow of a palm tree; I call to God who completes His work for me. On the day when the watchman said: morning comes, and also night. (He who separates...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Your righteousness is like Mount Tabor; pass over and pardon my transgressions. Like yesterday when it passes away, and like a watch in the night. (He who separates...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: The hour of my Minchah has passed. Who will grant me rest? I am weary with my sighing; every night I drench my bed. (He who separates...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Hear my voice; do not let it be cast away. Open for me the exalted gate, for my head is filled with dew, my locks with drops of the night. (He who separates...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Be entreated, awesome and revered One. I cry out—grant redemption at twilight, in the evening of the day, in the darkness of night. (He who separates...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: I called to You, Yah—save me. Make known to me the path of life. From my lowliness rescue me, from day until night. (He who separates...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Cleanse the filth of my deeds, lest those who anger me say: 'Where is the God who made me?' He gives songs in the night. (He who separates...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: We are in Your hand like clay; please forgive both light and grave offenses. Day pours forth speech to day, and night to night. (He who separates...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: God who redeems from every foe, we called to You from the narrow place. Your hand is not too short—not by day and not by night. (He who separates...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Michael, prince of Israel, Elijah and Gabriel—please come with the Redeemer; arise at midnight. (He who separates...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: At our right is Michael, at our left Gabriel, and above our head the Divine Presence of God—every day and every night. (He who separates...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Give us a good week, fresh as a watered garden; may goodness come from the LORD all day and all night. (He who separates...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: May this house be blessed by the word of prophet and seer, for so our God shall command—to guard it by day and by night. (He who separates...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: He who separated water from water—may He revive us after two days. May He show us the goodness of Jerusalem and grant rule by day and by night. (He who separates...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: The LORD said to Jacob: Fear not, My servant Jacob.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: The LORD chose Jacob. The LORD redeemed Jacob. A star has stepped forth from Jacob.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Those who come shall take root—Jacob. One shall have dominion from Jacob. Remember these things, Jacob.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: The joy of the salvations of Jacob. How good are your tents, Jacob. They shall teach Your judgments to Jacob.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: There is no divination in Jacob. He saw no iniquity in Jacob. Who has counted the dust of Jacob?
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: The LORD swore to Jacob. Please forgive the iniquity of Jacob. Now restore the captivity of Jacob.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: The LORD redeemed Jacob. Command the salvations of Jacob. The voice is the voice of Jacob.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Sing aloud with joy for Jacob. The LORD restored the captivity of Jacob. Give truth to Jacob.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Acrostic: Avraham.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: God—Elijah! God—Elijah! By the merit of Elijah the prophet, please bring him.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: With him He will harness His chariot. He wanders in captivity, yet his heart did not lie down, nor did he see sleep. (God—Elijah...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Great is my pain when I see deceit and hatred, outwardly fair and healthy, feeding on flesh. (God—Elijah...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: My Rock, give bitter waters to the foe whose eyes sharpen against us; let my eyes look toward the Holy One, and let Israel turn to Him. (God—Elijah...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: When will You show the sign of salvation? Those who call to God lift their voices to You alone, and they shall sing—another reading: weep. (God—Elijah...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: The redeeming angel, before a poor petitioner—please, God, God of Abraham, cause success now. (God—Elijah...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Words: Rabbi Yosef Hayyim.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Upon this house and those who dwell in it, may Elijah's blessing rest.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Elijah, master of the sign, angel of the LORD of Hosts; he merited and worked wonders—fortunate is the eye that saw him. (Upon this house...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: He clothed himself in zeal among his people, and the LORD was with him. He merited to take unto himself the soul of Nadab and Abihu. (Upon this house...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: His hands were mighty in his zeal; God gave him His covenant—life and peace are with him; the spirit of the LORD guides him. (Upon this house...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: He flies to the four directions, and his home is in the highest heavens. Fortunate is the person who merits seeing him and learning Torah from his mouth. (Upon this house...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Fortunate is one who greets him and receives his greeting in return. If only we might see him in a dream and be satisfied by the light of his face. (Upon this house...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Alive and enduring in the strength of God, he will speak good on behalf of Israel and quickly come with the Redeemer. How beautiful upon the mountains are his feet! (Upon this house...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: May his merit protect us; may he write our merits at the close of our Sabbaths. He sits by the Tree of Life. (Upon this house...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: The voice of Elijah shall be heard; he will sow peace and salvation, for the time of song has arrived. The spirit of Elijah has rested. (Upon this house...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Acrostic: Yaakov Menui Hazak.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: At the close of the day of rest, grant relief to Your people. Send the Tishbite to the sighing people, and grief and sighing shall flee.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: It befits You, my Rock, to gather my scattered people from the hand of a cruel nation that dug a pit for me. (At the close...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Awaken the time of love, God, to rescue the people who ask to behold Your goodness when the Redeemer comes to the scattered sheep. (At the close...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Proclaim salvation to the generous people, God exalted above myriads. May the coming week be for salvation and relief. (At the close...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Daughter of Zion, bereaved and presently rejected—soon she shall again be espoused, a joyful mother of children. (At the close...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Then springs shall flow, the redeemed shall return, and they shall draw from the waters of salvation; distress will be forgotten. (At the close...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Guide Your people like a compassionate father. Let the people who are not widowed chirp joyfully at the faithful word of the LORD when You fulfill the promise. (At the close...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Beloved survivors of earthly frailty will break forth in song with vigor, without breach and without outcry—no going out and no cry. (At the close...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: May this month be as the prophecy of the father of seers, and may there be heard in this house the sound of joy and the sound of gladness. (At the close...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: The Mighty One will fulfill our wishes; the Strong One will grant our request and send into all the work of our hands blessing, abundance, and success. (At the close...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: At the close of the joyful day, awesome in deeds is Your Name. Send the Tishbite to the treasured people—relief, joy, and rest. (At the close...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: A voice of exultation and song—then our lips shall sing. Please, LORD, save now; please, LORD, grant success now. (At the close...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Acrostic: LeSaadia.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: For the candle and the spices my soul longs—if only you give me a cup of wine for Havdalah. (If you give me...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Build roads for me, clear the way for the perplexed; open gates for me, all angels above. (If you give me...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: I lift my eyes to God with a longing heart, the One who provides my needs by day and by night. (If you give me...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Give me what I lack from the treasuries of Your goodness, for Your kindness has neither end nor limit. (If you give me...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: May my joy, my sustenance, and my good be renewed; remove my sorrows, pain, and darkness. (If you give me...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Behold, the working days are continually renewed; may peace and goodness forever be renewed within them. (If you give me...)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Verses of Blessing
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: A segulah for livelihood: on every Motzaei Shabbat recite 'Veyiten Lecha...' It is good for two people to say it together.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: So God give thee of the dew of heaven, And of the fat places of the earth, And plenty of corn and wine. Let peoples serve thee, And nations bow down to thee. Be lord over thy brethren, And let thy mother’s sons bow down to thee. Cursed be every one that curseth thee, And blessed be every one that blesseth thee. And God Almighty bless thee, and make thee fruitful, and multiply thee, that thou mayest be a congregation of peoples; and give thee the blessing of Abraham, to thee, and to thy seed with thee; that thou mayest inherit the land of thy sojournings, which God gave unto Abraham.’ Even by the God of thy father, who shall help thee, And by the Almighty, who shall bless thee, With blessings of heaven above, Blessings of the deep that coucheth beneath, Blessings of the breasts, and of the womb. The blessings of thy father Are mighty beyond the blessings of my progenitors Unto the utmost bound of the everlasting hills; They shall be on the head of Joseph, And on the crown of the head of the prince among his brethren. and He will love thee, and bless thee, and multiply thee; He will also bless the fruit of thy body and the fruit of thy land, thy corn and thy wine and thine oil, the increase of thy kine and the young of thy flock, in the land which He swore unto thy fathers to give thee. Thou shalt be blessed above all peoples; there shall not be male or female barren among you, or among your cattle. And the LORD will take away from thee all sickness; and He will put none of the evil diseases of Egypt, which thou knowest, upon thee, but will lay them upon all them that hate thee. Blessed shalt thou be in the city, and blessed shalt thou be in the field. Blessed shall be the fruit of thy body, and the fruit of thy land, and the fruit of thy cattle, the increase of thy kine, and the young of thy flock. Blessed shall be thy basket and thy kneading-trough. Blessed shalt thou be when thou comest in, and blessed shalt thou be when thou goest out. The LORD will command the blessing with thee in thy barns, and in all that thou puttest thy hand unto; and He will bless thee in the land which the LORD thy God giveth thee. The LORD will open unto thee His good treasure the heaven to give the rain of thy land in its season, and to bless all the work of thy hand; and thou shalt lend unto many nations, but thou shalt not borrow. Happy art thou, O Israel, who is like unto thee? A people saved by the LORD, The shield of thy help, And that is the sword of thy excellency! And thine enemies shall dwindle away before thee; And thou shalt tread upon their high places.
paragraphs.note: Every colon-delimited fragment matched a unique near-exact complete Tanakh verse; reviewed orthographic/qere alignment only.

paragraphs.text: O Israel, that art saved by the LORD with an everlasting salvation; Ye shall not be ashamed nor confounded world without end. And ye shall eat in plenty and be satisfied, and shall praise the name of the LORD your God, that hath dealt wondrously with you; and My people shall never be ashamed. And ye shall know that I am in the midst of Israel, and that I am the LORD your God, and there is none else; and My people shall never be ashamed. And the ransomed of the LORD shall return, And come with singing unto Zion, And everlasting joy shall be upon their heads; They shall obtain gladness and joy, And sorrow and sighing shall flee away. For ye shall go out with joy, And be led forth with peace; The mountains and the hills shall break forth before you into singing, And all the trees of the field shall clap their hands. Behold, God is my salvation; I will trust, and will not be afraid; For GOD the LORD is my strength and song; And He is become my salvation.’ Therefore with joy shall ye draw water Out of the wells of salvation. And in that day shall ye say: ‘Give thanks unto the LORD, proclaim His name, Declare His doings among the peoples, Make mention that His name is exalted. Sing unto the LORD; for He hath done gloriously; This is made known in all the earth. Cry aloud and shout, thou inhabitant of Zion, For great is the Holy One of Israel in the midst of thee.’ And it shall be said in that day: ‘Lo, this is our God, For whom we waited, that He might save us; This is the LORD, for whom we waited, We will be glad and rejoice in His salvation.’ Peace, peace, to him that is far off and to him that is near, Saith the LORD that createth the fruit of the lips; And I will heal him. Then the spirit clothed Amasai, who was chief of the captains: Thine are we, David, And on thy side, thou son of Jesse; Peace, peace be unto thee, And peace be to thy helpers; For thy God helpeth thee. Then David received them, and made them captains of the band. and thus ye shall say: All hail! and peace be both unto thee, and peace be to thy house, and peace be unto all that thou hast. Blessed is the man that trusteth in the LORD, And whose trust the LORD is. The LORD will give strength unto His people; The LORD will bless his people with peace.
paragraphs.note: Joined from the bundled Tanakh edition in the source order; editorial pause marks omitted.

paragraphs.text: Recite 130 times, corresponding to the numerical value 130.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Elijah the prophet, remembered for good.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Fourteen verses of three words each.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Mishma, Dumah, and Massa. Isaac dwelt in Gerar. The famine was severe in the land. The sons of Dan: Hushim. For Your salvation I wait, LORD. Issachar, Zebulun, and Benjamin. You shall not allow a sorceress to live. Make settings of gold. For the leprosy of a garment and a house. For a swelling, a scab, and a bright spot. May the LORD bless you and guard you. And it was after the plague. The sons of Pallu: Eliab. Blessed shall be your basket and your kneading bowl.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed anthology translation; short biblical snippets preserved in source order.

paragraphs.text: And if a man prevail against him that is alone, two shall withstand him; and a threefold cord is not quickly broken. The LORD of hosts is with us; The God of Jacob is our high tower. Selah O LORD of hosts, happy is the man that trusteth in Thee. Save, LORD; Let the King answer us in the day that we call. The LORD will give strength unto His people; The LORD will bless his people with peace. Let the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable before Thee, O LORD, my Rock, and my Redeemer.

paragraphs.text: In the beginning God created the heaven and the earth. and in all the mighty hand, and in all the great terror, which Moses wrought in the sight of all Israel. And Jacob went on his way, and the angels of God met him. And Jacob said when he saw them: ‘This is God’s camp.’ And he called the name of that place Mahanaim. Give ear, ye heavens, and I will speak; And let the earth hear the words of my mouth. My doctrine shall drop as the rain, My speech shall distil as the dew; As the small rain upon the tender grass, And as the showers upon the herb. And it came to pass, when the ark set forward, that Moses said: ‘Rise up, O LORD, and let Thine enemies be scattered; and let them that hate Thee flee before Thee.’ And when it rested, he said: ‘Return, O LORD, unto the ten thousands of the families of Israel.’ and his host, and those that were numbered of them, thirty and five thousand and four hundred; all that were numbered of the camp of Ephraim being a hundred thousand and eight thousand and a hundred, according to their hosts; and they shall set forth third.

paragraphs.text: When the plague of leprosy is in a man, then he shall be brought unto the priest. We will pass over armed before the LORD into the land of Canaan, and the possession of our inheritance shall remain with us beyond the Jordan.’ A prophet will the LORD thy God raise up unto thee, from the midst of thee, of thy brethren, like unto me; unto him ye shall hearken; There is a river, the streams whereof make glad the city of God, The holiest dwelling-place of the Most High. Marvellous things did He in the sight of their fathers, In the land of Egypt, in the field of Zoan. Thou didst lead Thy people like a flock, By the hand of Moses and Aaron. I have perfumed my bed With myrrh, aloes, and cinnamon. The spirit of man is the lamp of the LORD, searching all the inward parts. Thy lips, O my bride, drop honey— Honey and milk are under thy tongue; And the smell of thy garments is like the smell of Lebanon. Flee out of the midst of Babylon, And go forth out of the land of the Chaldeans, And be as the he-goats before the flocks. They were armed with bows, and could use both the right hand and the left in slinging stones and in shooting arrows from the bow; they were of Saul’s brethren of Benjamin.

Just as You spread Your wings over our fathers in the wilderness so that Balaam's evil eye had no power over them, so in Your great mercy spread them over us, that we may be covered and protected by Your holy Names from every evil eye.

Selah Trust ye in the LORD for ever, For the LORD is GOD, an everlasting Rock. The LORD will give strength unto His people; The LORD will bless his people with peace.

paragraphs.text: When thou passest through the waters, I will be with thee, And through the rivers, they shall not overflow thee; When thou walkest through the fire, thou shalt not be burned, Neither shall the flame kindle upon thee. For, O people that dwellest in Zion at Jerusalem, Thou shalt weep no more; He will surely be gracious unto thee at the voice of thy cry, When He shall hear, He will answer thee. For I am the LORD thy God, The Holy One of Israel, thy Saviour; I have given Egypt as thy ransom, Ethiopia and Seba for thee. For I the LORD thy God Hold thy right hand, Who say unto thee: ‘Fear not, I help thee.’ For the nether-world cannot praise Thee, Death cannot celebrate Thee; They that go down into the pit cannot hope for Thy truth. For I will pour water upon the thirsty land, And streams upon the dry ground; I will pour My spirit upon thy seed, And My blessing upon thine offspring; For Thou art our Father; for Abraham knoweth us not, and Israel doth not acknowledge us; Thou, O LORD, art our Father, Our Redeemer from everlasting is Thy name.

paragraphs.text: The LORD bless thee, and keep thee; The LORD make His face to shine upon thee, and be gracious unto thee; The LORD lift up His countenance upon thee, and give thee peace. So shall they put My name upon the children of Israel, and I will bless them.’
paragraphs.note: Joined from the bundled Tanakh edition in the source order; editorial pause marks omitted.

paragraphs.text: A Song of Ascents. I will lift up mine eyes unto the mountains: From whence shall my help come? My help cometh from the LORD, Who made heaven and earth. He will not suffer thy foot to be moved; He that keepeth thee will not slumber. Behold, He that keepeth Israel Doth neither slumber nor sleep. The LORD is thy keeper; The LORD is thy shade upon thy right hand. The sun shall not smite thee by day, Nor the moon by night. The LORD shall keep thee from all evil; He shall keep thy soul. The LORD shall guard thy going out and thy coming in, From this time forth and for ever.

paragraphs.text: Fourth Meal (Melaveh Malkah)
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: A person should always set the table on Motzaei Shabbat with two loaves, even if able to eat only an olive-sized portion. It is good not to remove Shabbat clothing until after the fourth meal. Ideally it should not be delayed beyond four hours into the night; if prevented, it may be fulfilled until midnight.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: The disciples of the Ari wrote: the additional soul does not depart completely until the Motzaei Shabbat meal. Therefore one should not engage in non-food-related labor—or, according to this text, even in another occupation—until after eating the Motzaei Shabbat meal.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Before the fourth meal say:
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Prepare the meal of faith; this is the fourth meal of David, King Messiah.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: For the sake of the unification of the Holy One, blessed is He, and His Presence, in fear and love, love and fear, to unite the Name—Yod-Heh with Vav-Heh—in perfect unity in the name of all Israel: I now come to eat the fourth Sabbath meal, to escort the Queen and to escort the additional soul, the aspect of Hayah within it, which is now departing, and to leave blessing in all our meals during the six weekdays and preserve in them something of the holiness of Sabbath. By the power of this precious practice, guard us like the pupil of the eye; hide us in the shadow of Your wings; save us from the suffering of the grave, and settle our nefesh, ruach, and neshamah in secure dwellings. May the pleasantness of the Lord our God be upon us; establish the work of our hands for us—establish the work of our hands.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs: Rosh Chodesh order

In the morning and evening prayers, one says "go up and come" with "Retzah"; and if one does not say it in the morning, one does not return it - between one day and two days - because the month is not sanctified at night; but if one does not say it in the morning and evening prayers, one returns it. And if one remembers before he begins "Modim", he says it in the place he remembers; and if one remembers after saying "Blessed are you, O Lord", he ends with "Learn from me your laws". Some say that one does not finish "Learn from me your laws", but rather completes the blessing, and then says "go up and come" before "Modim". And if one does not remember until after he begins "Modim": if one remembers before he has completed his prayer, he returns to "Retzah"; and if one does not remember until he says "Let the words of my mouth be pleasing" and is ready to remove his feet, and does not say any more supplications, then it is considered as if he removed his feet and returned to the head. (Ba'ach Shab 2 Leviticus 15)

The recitation of Hallel is performed standing up and on the first day of Chashod and the last six days of Pesach, there is no end to the recitation of Hallel. On the first day of Pesach (and abroad also on the Monday of Pesach), Shavuot, Sukkot, Shemini Atzeret, and Chanukah, a complete Hallel is recited with a blessing at the beginning and end.

paragraphs.text: Hallel for Rosh Chodesh and the festivals.
On days when the full Hallel is recited, the prayer leader says:
With the permission of my teachers and masters. The congregation responds: 'Heaven.'
On days when the full Hallel is recited, the following blessing is said:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who has sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us to complete Hallel.

Hallelujah. Praise, O ye servants of the LORD, Praise the name of the LORD. Blessed be the name of the LORD From this time forth and for ever. From the rising of the sun unto the going down thereof The LORD'S name is to be praised. The LORD is high above all nations, His glory is above the heavens. Who is like unto the LORD our God, That is enthroned on high, That looketh down low Upon heaven and upon the earth? Who raiseth up the poor out of the dust, And lifteth up the needy out of the dunghill; That He may set him with princes, Even with the princes of His people. Who maketh the barren woman to dwell in her house As a joyful mother of children. Hallelujah.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: When Israel came forth out of Egypt, The house of Jacob from a people of strange language; Judah became His sanctuary, Israel His dominion. The sea saw it, and fled; The Jordan turned backward. The mountains skipped like rams, The hills like young sheep. What aileth thee, O thou sea, that thou fleest? Thou Jordan, that thou turnest backward? Ye mountains, that ye skip like rams; Ye hills, like young sheep? Tremble, thou earth, at the presence of the Lord, At the presence of the God of Jacob; Who turned the rock into a pool of water, The flint into a fountain of waters.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: On days when the full Hallel is not recited, omit this passage.

Not unto us, O LORD, not unto us, But unto Thy name give glory, For Thy mercy, and for Thy truth's sake. Wherefore should the nations say: 'Where is now their God?' But our God is in the heavens; Whatsoever pleased Him He hath done. Their idols are silver and gold, The work of men's hands. They have mouths, but they speak not; Eyes have they, but they see not; They have ears, but they hear not; Noses have they, but they smell not; They have hands, but they handle not; Feet have they, but they walk not; Neither speak they with their throat. . They that make them shall be like unto them; Yea, every one that trusteth in them. O Israel, trust thou in the LORD! He is their help and their shield! O house of Aaron, trust ye in the LORD! He is their help and their shield! Ye that fear the LORD, trust in the LORD! He is their help and their shield.
paragraphs.note: Exact complete Hebrew passage matched to the bundled Tanakh; no fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: The LORD hath been mindful of us, He will bless— He will bless the house of Israel; He will bless the house of Aaron. He will bless them that fear the LORD, Both small and great. The LORD increase you more and more, You and your children. Blessed be ye of the LORD Who made heaven and earth. The heavens are the heavens of the LORD; But the earth hath He given to the children of men. The dead praise not the LORD, Neither any that go down into silence; But we will bless the LORD From this time forth and for ever. Hallelujah.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: On days when the full Hallel is not recited, omit this passage.

I love that the LORD should hear my voice and my supplications. Because He hath inclined His ear unto me, Therefore will I call upon Him all my days. The cords of death compassed me, And the straits of the nether-world got hold upon me; I found trouble and sorrow. But I called upon the name of the LORD: 'I beseech thee, O LORD, deliver my soul.' Gracious is the LORD, and righteous; Yea, our God is compassionate. The LORD preserveth the simple; I was brought low, and He saved me. Return, O my soul, unto Thy rest; For the LORD hath dealt bountifully with thee. For thou hast delivered my soul from death, Mine eyes from tears, And my feet from stumbling. I shall walk before the LORD In the lands of the living. I trusted even when I spoke: 'I am greatly afflicted.' I said in my haste: 'All men are liars.'
paragraphs.note: Complete bundled Tanakh passage aligned at 99.83% normalized Hebrew similarity; only orthographic/punctuation variation accepted.

paragraphs.text: How can I repay unto the LORD All His bountiful dealings toward me? I will lift up the cup of salvation, And call upon the name of the LORD. My vows will I pay unto the LORD, Yea, in the presence of all His people. Precious in the sight of the LORD Is the death of His saints. I beseech Thee, O LORD, for I am Thy servant; I am Thy servant, the son of Thy handmaid; Thou hast loosed my bands. I will offer to thee the sacrifice of thanksgiving, And will call upon the name of the LORD. I will pay my vows unto the LORD, Yea, in the presence of all His people; In the courts of the LORD’S house, In the midst of thee, O Jerusalem. Hallelujah.
paragraphs.note: Reused from a reviewed near-identical Hebrew Siddur variant (99.77% normalized Hebrew similarity).

paragraphs.text: O praise the LORD, all ye nations; Laud Him, all ye peoples. For His mercy is great toward us; And the truth of the LORD endureth for ever. Hallelujah.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good; His mercy endures forever.
So let Israel now say, For His mercy endureth for ever,
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: So let the house of Aaron now say, For His mercy endureth for ever.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: So let them now that fear the LORD say, For His mercy endureth for ever.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: Out of my straits I called upon the LORD; He answered me with great enlargement. The LORD is for me; I will not fear; What can man do unto me? The LORD is for me as my helper; And I shall gaze upon them that hate me. It is better to take refuge in the LORD Than to trust in man. It is better to take refuge in the LORD Than to trust in princes. All nations compass me about; Verily, in the name of the LORD I will cut them off. They compass me about, yea, they compass me about; Verily, in the name of the LORD I will cut them off. They compass me about like bees; They are quenched as the fire of thorns; Verily, in the name of the LORD I will cut them off. Thou didst thrust sore at me that I might fall; But the LORD helped me. The LORD is my strength and song; And He is become my salvation. The voice of rejoicing and salvation is in the tents of the righteous; The right hand of the LORD doeth valiantly. The right hand of the LORD is exalted; The right hand of the LORD doeth valiantly. I shall not die, but live, And declare the works of the LORD. The LORD hath chastened me sore; But He hath not given me over unto death. Open to me the gates of righteousness; I will enter into them, I will give thanks unto the LORD. This is the gate of the LORD; The righteous shall enter into it.
paragraphs.note: Complete bundled Tanakh passage aligned at 99.88% normalized Hebrew similarity; only orthographic/punctuation variation accepted.

paragraphs.text: I will give thanks unto Thee, for Thou hast answered me, And art become my salvation. I will give thanks unto Thee, for Thou hast answered me, And art become my salvation. The stone which the builders rejected Is become the chief corner-stone. The stone which the builders rejected Is become the chief corner-stone. This is the LORD’S doing; It is marvellous in our eyes. This is the LORD’S doing; It is marvellous in our eyes. This is the day which the LORD hath made; We will rejoice and be glad in it. This is the day which the LORD hath made; We will rejoice and be glad in it.
paragraphs.note: Every colon-delimited Hebrew fragment matched an exact complete bundled Tanakh verse; translations joined without fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: Please, LORD, save us now! Repeat twice, with the accent on the preceding syllable.
Please, LORD, grant us success now! Repeat twice, with the accent on the final syllable.

Blessed be he that cometh in the name of the LORD; We bless you out of the house of the LORD. Blessed be he that cometh in the name of the LORD; We bless you out of the house of the LORD. The LORD is God, and hath given us light; Order the festival procession with boughs, even unto the horns of the altar. The LORD is God, and hath given us light; Order the festival procession with boughs, even unto the horns of the altar. Thou art my God, and I will give thanks unto Thee; Thou art my God, I will exalt Thee. Thou art my God, and I will give thanks unto Thee; Thou art my God, I will exalt Thee. O give thanks unto the LORD, for He is good, For His mercy endureth for ever. O give thanks unto the LORD, for He is good, For His mercy endureth for ever.

All Your works shall praise You, Lord our God, and Your faithful ones, the righteous who do Your will, and Your people the house of Israel. All shall gratefully sing, bless, praise, and glorify Your glorious name. For it is good to thank You and pleasant to sing to Your name. From everlasting to everlasting You are God. Blessed are You, Lord, King praised in songs of thanksgiving. Amen.

paragraphs.text: The cantor recites Full Kaddish (Titkabbal); on Hanukkah, only Half Kaddish is recited.

Exalted & sanctified be His (G·d's) great Name. [cong. - Amen.] In this world that He created according to His will. May His Kingdom reign, & may he cause His redemption to sprout & may He hasten His Messiah. [cong. - Amen.] In your lifetime & in your days, & in the lifetime of the whole house of Israel, speedily & soon; & say ye, Amen. [cong. - Amen.] Be His great Name blessed forever & throughout eternity. Blessed, lauded, glorified, exalted, extolled & honored, uplifted & supremely exalted, the Name of the Holy One, Blessed be He. [cong. - Amen.] Beyond all blessings, songs, praises & consolations of this world to express; & say ye, [cong. - Amen.]
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur (deterministic preferred wording).

paragraphs.text: May our prayers and supplications be accepted, together with the prayers and supplications of all the House of Israel, before our Father in heaven; and say: Amen. [Amen]

May abundant peace descend from heaven: life, plenty, salvation, consolation, deliverance, healing, redemption, forgiveness, atonement, relief and rescue for us and for all His people Israel; and say: Amen. [Amen]
May the One who makes peace in His heights, in His mercy, make peace for us and for all His people Israel; and say: Amen. [Amen]
It is good to repeat this verse three times after Hallel.
And Abraham was old, well stricken in age; and the LORD had blessed Abraham in all things.
paragraphs.note: Exact complete Hebrew passage matched to the bundled Tanakh; no fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: And then say:
May the LORD protect me and keep me alive; so may it be Your will, living God and eternal King, in whose hand is the soul of every living being. Amen, may it be His will.
Before taking out the Torah scroll, one says:

The LORD our God be with us, as He was with our fathers; let Him not leave us, nor forsake us; Save Thy people, and bless Thine inheritance; And tend them, and carry them for ever. For Thy servant David's sake Turn not away the face of Thine anointed.
paragraphs.note: Every colon-delimited Hebrew fragment matched an exact complete bundled Tanakh verse; translations joined without fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: Open the Ark and recite:

Blessed is the Name of the Master of the universe. Blessed is Your crown and Your place. May Your good will [be] with Your people Israel forever. Show Your people the redemption of Your right hand in Your Holy Temple. Bestow on us Your excellent light, and accept our prayer with compassion. May it be Your will to prolong our lives in well-being. Let me be counted among the righteous, so that You will have compassion on me and protect me and all that is mine, and all that belongs to Your people, Israel. You are He Who nourishes all and maintains all; You are He Who rules over all; You are He Who rules over kings, and the kingdom is Yours. I am a servant of the Holy One, blessed is He, I bow before Him and before the honor of His Torah at all times. Not in man do I put my trust, nor do I rely on any angel; but only in the God of heaven, Who is the true God, Whose Torah is truth, Whose prophets are true, and Who performs many deeds of goodness and truth. In Him I put my trust and to His honored, holy Name I utter praises. May it be Your will to open my heart to Your Torah, and grant me sons who do Your will, and to fulfill the desires of my heart, and of the heart of Your people Israel, for goodness, for life, and for peace.
paragraphs.note: Reviewed parallel passage from the existing English Siddur.

paragraphs.text: Take out the Torah scroll and call four people to read from Parashat Pinchas.

And the LORD spoke unto Moses, saying: Command the children of Israel, and say unto them: My food which is presented unto Me for offerings made by fire, of a sweet savour unto Me, shall ye observe to offer unto Me in its due season. And thou shalt say unto them: This is the offering made by fire which ye shall bring unto the LORD: he-lambs of the first year without blemish, two day by day, for a continual burnt-offering. The one lamb shalt thou offer in the morning, and the other lamb shalt thou offer at dusk; and the tenth part of an ephah of fine flour for a meal-offering, mingled with the fourth part of a hin of beaten oil. It is a continual burnt-offering, which was offered in mount Sinai, for a sweet savour, an offering made by fire unto the LORD. And the drink-offering thereof shall be the fourth part of a hin for the one lamb; in the holy place shalt thou pour out a drink-offering of strong drink unto the LORD. And the other lamb shalt thou present at dusk; as the meal-offering of the morning, and as the drink-offering thereof, thou shalt present it, an offering made by fire, of a sweet savour unto the LORD. And on the sabbath day two he-lambs of the first year without blemish, and two tenth parts of an ephah of fine flour for a meal-offering, mingled with oil, and the drink-offering thereof. This is the burnt-offering of every sabbath, beside the continual burnt-offering, and the drink-offering thereof. And in your new moons ye shall present a burnt-offering unto the LORD: two young bullocks, and one ram, seven he-lambs of the first year without blemish; and three tenth parts of an ephah of fine flour for a meal-offering, mingled with oil, for each bullock; and two tenth parts of fine flour for a meal-offering, mingled with oil, for the one ram; and a several tenth part of fine flour mingled with oil for a meal-offering unto every lamb; for a burnt-offering of a sweet savour, an offering made by fire unto the LORD. And their drink-offerings shall be half a hin of wine for a bullock, and the third part of a hin for the ram, and the fourth part of a hin for a lamb. This is the burnt-offering of every new moon throughout the months of the year. And one he-goat for a sin-offering unto the LORD; it shall be offered beside the continual burnt-offering, and the drink-offering thereof.
paragraphs.note: Public-domain JPS 1917 English aligned with the original Hebrew; any liturgical instructions are supplied by the project.

paragraphs.text: After the reading, the fourth person recites Half Kaddish, and the congregation continues with Ashrei.

Exalted & sanctified be His (G·d's) great Name. [cong. - Amen.] In this world that He created according to His will. May His Kingdom reign, & may he cause His redemption to sprout & may He hasten His Messiah. [cong. - Amen.] In your lifetime & in your days, & in the lifetime of the whole house of Israel, speedily & soon; & say ye, Amen. [cong. - Amen.] Be His great Name blessed forever & throughout eternity. Blessed, lauded, glorified, exalted, extolled & honored, uplifted & supremely exalted, the Name of the Holy One, Blessed be He. [cong. - Amen.] Beyond all blessings, songs, praises & consolations of this world to express; & say ye, [cong. - Amen.]

paragraphs.text: Let Thy mercy, O LORD, be upon us, According as we have waited for Thee.
paragraphs.note: Exact complete Hebrew passage matched to the bundled Tanakh; no fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: Happy are those that dwell in Your house, they will yet praise You forever. Happy is the people for whom this is so, happy is the people that the L·rd is their G·d. A praise of David, I will exalt You my G·d, the King, & I will bless Your Name forever & ever. Every day I will bless you, & I will laud Your Name forever & ever. Great is the L·rd & He is greatly lauded, & His Greatness is unfathomable. Generation to generation will praise Your deeds, & Your mighty acts they will relate. The splendorous glory of Your Majesty & Your wondrous acts I shall discuss. And the might of Your awesome acts they will speak & Your greatness, I will relate. A recollection of Your great goodness they will express & Your righteousness they will sing. Gracious & Merciful is the L·rd, Slow-to anger & Great in kindness. The L·rd is good to all & His Mercies are on all His works. All Your works shall thank You, L·rd, & Your pious ones shall bless You. Of the glory of Your Kingdom they will relate, & Your Might they shall speak.To inform human beings of Your Mighty acts & of the glorious Majesty of His Kingdom. Your Kingship is Kingship of all worlds & Your dominion is for all generations.The L·rd supports all those who fall, & He straightens all who are bent over. The eyes of all are [looking] upon You for hope, & You provide them their food in the proper time. * You open Your hand, & You satisfy all the living's wants. Righteous is the L·rd in all His ways, & Pious in all His deeds. The L·rd is close to all who call Him, to all that call upon Him with sincerity. The will of those that fear Him He will do, & their cries He will hear & save them. The L·rd protects all who love Him, & all of the wicked He will destroy. Praise of the L·rd will my mouth speak, & all flesh shall bless His holy Name for ever & ever. And we will bless G·d from now to eternity. [Let us all] Praise G·d!
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: A redeemer shall come to Zion.

A Redeemer shall come to Zion and to those in Jacob who turn from wrongdoing, declares the Lord. 'As for Me, this is My covenant with them,' says the Lord: 'My spirit upon you and My words which I placed in your mouth shall not depart from your mouth, or the mouths of your children or their children, from now and forever.' Yet You are holy, enthroned upon the praises of Israel. And one called to another, saying: 'Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of Hosts; the whole earth is full of His glory!' [The following Aramaic is said quietly:] They receive from one another and say: Holy in the highest heavens, the dwelling of His Presence; holy upon the earth, the work of His might; holy for all ages and for ever and ever: the Lord of Hosts, the whole earth is filled with the radiance of His glory. Then a spirit lifted me, and I heard behind me a great rushing sound: 'Blessed is the glory of the Lord from His place.' The spirit raised me, and I heard behind me a mighty trembling voice praising and saying: 'Blessed is the glory of the Lord from the place of His Presence.' The Lord shall reign for ever and ever; His kingdom stands for all eternity. Lord, God of Abraham, Isaac and Israel our ancestors, preserve forever the inclination of Your people's hearts toward You, and prepare their hearts for You. He, being merciful, forgives wrongdoing and does not destroy; often He turns away His anger and does not stir up all His wrath. For You, Lord, are good and forgiving and abundant in loving-kindness toward all who call on You. Your righteousness is everlasting righteousness, and Your Torah is truth. Show faithfulness to Jacob, kindness to Abraham, as You swore to our ancestors in days of old. Blessed be the Lord day by day, who bears our burden, the God of our salvation, Selah. The Lord of Hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge, Selah. Lord of Hosts, happy is the person who trusts in You. Lord, save! May the King answer us on the day we call.
paragraphs.note: Identical Hebrew passage to edot Uva LeSion paragraph 1; verify typography and liturgical placement.

paragraphs.text: Blessed is our God, who created us for His glory, separated us from those who stray, gave us the Torah of truth, and planted eternal life within us. May He open our hearts to His Torah and place His love and reverence in them, so that we may fulfill His will and serve Him wholeheartedly. May we not labor in vain or bring forth children for terror. May it be Your will, Lord our God and God of our ancestors, that we observe Your laws and commandments in this world and merit to live and inherit goodness and blessing in the world to come. 'That my soul may sing praise to You and not be silent' [pause briefly]; 'Lord my God, I will thank You forever.' The Lord desires, for His righteousness' sake, to magnify the Torah and make it glorious. Those who know Your name will trust You, for You, Lord, have not forsaken those who seek You. Lord our Master, how majestic is Your name in all the earth! Be strong and let your hearts take courage, all who hope in the Lord.
paragraphs.note: Identical Hebrew passage to edot Uva LeSion paragraph 2; verify typography and liturgical placement.

paragraphs.text: O house of Jacob, come ye, and let us walk In the light of the LORD. For let all the peoples walk each one in the name of its god, But we will walk in the name of the LORD our God for ever and ever. The LORD our God be with us, as He was with our fathers; let Him not leave us, nor forsake us; that He may incline our hearts unto Him, to walk in all His ways, and to keep His commandments, and His statutes, and His ordinances, which He commanded our fathers. And let these my words, wherewith I have made supplication before the LORD, be nigh unto the LORD our God day and night, that He maintain the cause of His servant, and the cause of His people Israel, as every day shall require; that all the peoples of the earth may know that the LORD, He is God; there is none else.
paragraphs.note: Every colon-delimited fragment matched a unique near-exact complete Tanakh verse; reviewed orthographic/qere alignment only.

paragraphs.text: A Song of Ascents; of David. 'If it had not been the LORD who was for us', Let Israel now say; 'If it had not been the LORD who was for us, When men rose up against us, Then they had swallowed us up alive, when their wrath was kindled against us; Then the waters had overwhelmed us, the stream had gone over our soul; Then the proud waters Had gone over our soul.' Blessed be the LORD, who hath not given us as a prey to their teeth. Our soul is escaped as a bird out of the snare of the fowlers; The snare is broken, and we are escaped. Our help is in the name of the LORD, Who made heaven and earth.
paragraphs.note: Exact complete Hebrew passage matched to the bundled Tanakh; no fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: Psalm of the Day.
A psalm for Sunday. Today is the first day of the holy Sabbath week.

A psalm of David: the earth is Adonoy’s and the fullness thereof, the inhabited world and those who dwell in it. For He founded it upon the seas, and established it upon rivers. Who may ascend the mountain of Adonoy, and who may stand in the place of His holiness? The clean of hands and the pure of heart, who has not borne My soul in vain, and has not sworn deceitfully. He will bear Adonoy’s blessing and righteousness from the God of his deliverance. This is the generation of those who seek Him, the seekers of Your Presence, [God of] Jacob, Selah. Lift up your heads, gates, and be uplifted [you] entranceways to eternity, so that the King of Glory may enter. Who is this King of Glory? Adonoy, strong and mighty; Adonoy, the Mighty One in battle. Lift up your heads, gates, and lift, entranceways to eternity, so that the King of Glory may enter. Who is He, this King of Glory? Adonoy of hosts, He is the King of Glory, Selah.
paragraphs.note: Previously translated paragraph, Hebrew similarity 98.1%: source and target independently present in source corpus.

paragraphs.text: A psalm for Monday. Today is the second day of the holy Sabbath week.

A song, a psalm by the sons of Korach. Adonoy is great and highly extolled in the city of our God, the mountain of His Sanctuary. Beautiful in its panoramic vista, the joy of all the earth is Mount Zion, on the northern extremities (of Jerusalem); the city of the great King. God, in its palaces, has become known as a Stronghold. For behold, the kings assembled, they passed by together. They saw and were astounded, they panicked and fled in haste. Trembling siezed them there, like the pangs of a woman in labor. With an east wind You smashed the ships of Tarshish. As we heard, so we saw in the city of Adonoy of hosts, in the city of our God; may God establish it for eternity, Selah. We hoped, God, for Your lovingkindness in the midst of Your Sanctuary. As Your Name, God, so is Your praise— to the ends of the earth; Your right hand is full of righteousness. Let Mount Zion rejoice, let the daughters of Judah exult, because of Your judgments. Rally around Zion and encircle her, count her towers. Consider well her ramparts, raise high her citadels, that you may recount it to future generations. That this is God, our God forever and ever, He will lead us like children.
paragraphs.ref: KAV EN parallel ashkenaz:Song of the Day:6
paragraphs.note: Previously translated paragraph, Hebrew similarity 98.6%: source and target independently present in source corpus.

paragraphs.text: A psalm for Tuesday. Today is the third day of the holy Sabbath week.

A psalm of Assaf God stands in the congregation of the Almighty, in the midst of the judges He gives judgement. How long will you judge lawlessly and show partiality to the wicked forever? Render justice to the lowly and the orphan, deal righteously with the poor and destitute. Rescue the lowly and the needy, save them from the hand of the wicked. They neither know nor understand, they walk along in darkness, all the foundations of the earth are shaken. I had said “You are godlike beings, all of you, sons of the Most High.” Nevertheless, you shall die like men, and fall like one of the princes. Arise, God, judge the earth, for You will inherit all the nations.
A psalm for Wednesday. Today is the fourth day of the holy Sabbath week.

O God of vengeance, LORD, O God of vengeance, shine forth! Rise up, Judge of the earth, and repay the proud as they deserve. How long shall the wicked exult? They utter arrogant words and boast, all workers of iniquity. They crush Your people, LORD, and afflict Your heritage; they slay the widow and the stranger and murder the orphan, saying: “The God of Jacob does not see.” Understand, you senseless among the people: He who planted the ear, shall He not hear? He who fashioned the eye, shall He not see?
A psalm for Thursday. Today is the fifth day of the holy Sabbath week.

To Him Who grants victory— upon the Gittis, a psalm of Assaf: Sing joyously to God, our strength, shout for joy to the God of Jacob. Take up the hymn, sound the drum, the pleasant harp and the lute. Blow the shofar on the Rosh Chodesh, at the appointed time for our festive day. For it is a statute for Israel, a [day of] judgement of the God of Jacob. As a testimony for Yehosef, He ordained it when he went out over the land of Egypt, [where] an unfamiliar language I heard. From the burden, I removed his shoulder, his hands were removed from the cauldron. In distress you called out, and I released you, I answered you [though you called] in secret [I answered you] thunderously; I tested you at the waters of Merivah. Selah. Hear, My people, I will testify about you, Israel, if you would just listen to Me. Let no strange god be within you, nor bow before a foreign god. I am Adonoy, your God, Who brought you up from the land of Egypt, open your mouth wide, and I will fill it. But My people did not heed My voice, and Israel did not want Me. So I sent them to follow their heart’s desires, let them follow their own devices. If only My people would heed Me, if Israel would walk in My ways. I would immediately subdue their enemies, and turn My hand against their tormentors. Those who cause hate of Adonoy deceive [pretend obedience to] Him, but their time (of punishment) will be forever. But He would feed him (Israel) from the cream of the wheat, and from the rock, I would sate you with honey.
paragraphs.ref: KAV EN parallel ashkenaz:Song of the Day:15
paragraphs.note: Previously translated paragraph, Hebrew similarity 98.6%: source and target independently present in source corpus.

paragraphs.text: A psalm for Friday. Today is the sixth day of the holy Sabbath week.

The LORD reigns, clothed in majesty; the LORD has clothed Himself and girded Himself with strength. Indeed the world is established and cannot be moved. Your throne has stood since of old; You are from eternity. The rivers have lifted up, LORD, the rivers have lifted their voices, the rivers lift their crashing waves. Mightier than the thunder of many waters, than the breakers of the sea, is the LORD on high. Your testimonies are exceedingly trustworthy; holiness befits Your house, LORD, for all time. Continue with 'Save us...'.
paragraphs.note: Identical unpointed Hebrew source across sections.

paragraphs.text: After the Psalm of the Day, they say:

Save us, O LORD our God, And gather us from among the nations, That we may give thanks unto Thy holy name, That we may triumph in Thy praise. Blessed be the LORD, the God of Israel, from everlasting even to everlasting, and let all the people say: 'Amen.' Hallelujah. Blessed be the LORD out of Zion, Who dwelleth at Jerusalem. Hallelujah. Blessed be the LORD God, the God of Israel, Who only doeth wondrous things; And blessed be His glorious name for ever; And let the whole earth be filled with His glory. Amen, and Amen.
paragraphs.note: Every colon-delimited Hebrew fragment matched an exact complete bundled Tanakh verse; translations joined without fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: Return the Torah scroll to its place and recite:

Let them praise the name of the LORD, for His name alone is exalted, His splendor above earth and heaven. He has raised the strength of His people, praise for all His faithful ones, for the children of Israel, the people near Him. Hallelujah! The LORD is God, the LORD is God; in heaven above and upon earth below, there is no other. None among the gods is like You, Lord, and none of their deeds is like Yours. Return us to You, LORD, and we shall return; renew our days as of old.
paragraphs.note: Identical unpointed Hebrew source across sections.

paragraphs.text: The cantor recites Half Kaddish, and the tefillin are removed.

Exalted & sanctified be His (G·d's) great Name. [cong. - Amen.] In this world that He created according to His will. May His Kingdom reign, & may he cause His redemption to sprout & may He hasten His Messiah. [cong. - Amen.] In your lifetime & in your days, & in the lifetime of the whole house of Israel, speedily & soon; & say ye, Amen. [cong. - Amen.] Be His great Name blessed forever & throughout eternity. Blessed, lauded, glorified, exalted, extolled & honored, uplifted & supremely exalted, the Name of the Holy One, Blessed be He. [cong. - Amen.] Beyond all blessings, songs, praises & consolations of this world to express; & say ye, [cong. - Amen.]
