paragraphs.text: Musaf for Rosh Chodesh.
If this falls on Shabbat, see the combined Musaf for Rosh Chodesh and Shabbat.
O Lord, open Thou my lips; and my mouth shall declare Thy praise.
paragraphs.note: Exact complete Hebrew passage matched to the bundled Tanakh; no fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: Blessed are You, Lord, our God and God of our ancestors, God of Abraham, God of Isaac, and God of Jacob; the great, mighty, and awesome God, God Most High, who bestows abundant loving-kindness, possesses all things, remembers the kindnesses of the ancestors, and lovingly brings redemption to their children's children for the sake of His name. O King who helps, saves, and shields: blessed are You, Lord, Shield of Abraham.
paragraphs.note: Identical Hebrew passage to reviewed edot Amidah paragraph 2.

paragraphs.text: You are mighty forever, my L·rd, You revive the dead - Greatly capable of saving.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur (deterministic preferred wording).

paragraphs.text: (summer) who causes dew to fall (winter) who causes the winds to blow & the rain to fall.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: You sustain the living with loving-kindness. You revive the dead with great compassion. You support the fallen & heal the ill. And You release those bound. And You fulfill Your faithfulness to those who sleep in the ground. Who is like You, Master of [all] powers, King, Who causes death & gives life & causes salvation to sprout. & You are trustworthy to revive the dead. Blessed are You L·rd, Who revives the dead.
Kedushah in the prayer leader's repetition: recite Kedushah.

A crown will be offered to You, Lord our God, by the hosts of angels above and by Your people Israel assembled below. Together they proclaim Your holiness three times, as spoken through Your prophet: 'And one called to another and said: Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of Hosts; the whole earth is full of His glory.' Opposite them they praise and say: 'Blessed is the glory of the Lord from His place.' And in Your holy writings it is said: 'The Lord shall reign forever, your God, O Zion, throughout all generations. Hallelujah.'
paragraphs.note: Original English working translation aligned to the full Hebrew paragraph; specialist review pending.

paragraphs.text: You are holy and Your Name is holy and holy beings praise You every day, forever. Blessed are You, Adonoy, the Almighty, the Holy One.
paragraphs.note: Exact Hebrew match to a sequence of reviewed Siddur paragraphs; translations joined without fuzzy splitting.

paragraphs.text: You gave New Moons to Your people as a season of atonement through all their generations. They offered before You willing sacrifices and a goat as a sin offering to atone for them: a remembrance for all of them and deliverance for their souls from the hand of an enemy. Establish a new altar in Zion; upon it we shall offer the New Moon burnt offering, bringing a goat with willing hearts. We shall all rejoice in the Temple service, and songs of David Your servant shall be heard in Your city before Your altar. Grant them eternal love, and remember the covenant of the ancestors for their children.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: May it be Your will, Lord our God and God of our ancestors, to bring us joyfully into our land and plant us within our borders. There we shall present the sacrifices we owe, the daily offerings in their order and the additional offerings according to their laws. We shall lovingly offer the additional sacrifice of this New Moon, as You have commanded, as written in Your Torah through Moses Your servant, as it is said:
paragraphs.note: Original English working translation aligned to the full Hebrew paragraph; specialist review pending.

paragraphs.text: On your New Moons you shall bring a burnt offering to the LORD: two young bulls, one ram and seven unblemished year-old lambs, together with their meal offerings and libations as prescribed—three-tenths for each bull, two-tenths for the ram, one-tenth for each lamb, wine for its libation, a goat for atonement and the two daily offerings according to their law.
paragraphs.note: Identical unpointed Hebrew source across sections.

paragraphs.text: Our God and God of our ancestors, renew this month for our good and blessing, for happiness and joy, for deliverance and comfort, for livelihood and sustenance, for a good life and peace, for pardon of sin and forgiveness of iniquity. [In a leap year add: 'and for atonement of transgression.'] May this New Moon be the end of all our troubles and the beginning of the redemption of our souls, for You chose Your people Israel from among all nations and established for them the laws of the New Moons. Blessed are You, Lord, who sanctifies Israel and the New Moons.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Look with favor, LORD our God, upon Your people Israel and attend to their prayers. Restore the service to the inner sanctuary of Your house; receive Israel's offerings and their prayers swiftly, lovingly, and with favor, and may the service of Your people Israel always be acceptable. In Your great mercy, delight in us and accept us; may our eyes behold Your return to Zion in mercy. Blessed are You, LORD, who restores His Presence to Zion.
[Upon Saying "Modim" / "We are Grateful" One Bows]
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: We are grateful to You, that You are He Who is the L·rd, our G·d, & G·d of our fathers forever, & our Rock, the Rock of our lives & You are He Who is a Shield of salvation. For each & every generation, we will thank You & will relate Your praise, upon our lives that are placed in Your Hands, & upon our souls, that are entrusted in Your hands (when we sleep), & upon Your miracles that all day are with us, & all Your wonders & goodness at all times, at night, & morning & afternoon. The Good [One], for Your mercy never ends, The Merciful [One are You], for Your loving-kindness never ceases, forever we have hope in You.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: Thanks Of the rabbis / Said at repetition of Amid (In the repetition Of the standing prayer, when the prayer leader says “Modim”, the congregation says:) We give thanks to You, that You L·rd, are our God and God of our fathers, God of all flesh, our Creator, the creator [of the works] of Genesis. Blessings and thanks to your great and Holy name, that You gave us life and made us exist. Thus, give us life and have mercy upon us, and gather in our exiles to Your holy courtyards, To observe Your ordinances and to do Your will and to serve You with a complete heart, upon that we give thanks to You. Blessed is the Lord of thanks.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: Al HaNisim: on Hanukkah, Al HaNisim is recited here.
Upon the miracles and upon the redemption and upon the mighty acts and for salvation and for the wonders and for the comfort that you did for our fathers in those days at this period.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: On Hanukkah continue: In the days of Matitya son of Yohanan, The high priest, The Hashmonay and his sons when the Wicked Greek empire arose Against your people Israel To make them forget your Torah, and to remove them from the ordinances of your will and you with your great mercy you stood at the time of their suffering , you battle their battles, you judged their laws, you took vengeance upon their vengeance, you gave up over the mighty into the hands of the weak, and the masses in the hands of the few, and the impure Into the hands of the pure, and the wicked into the hands of the righteous, and the intentional sinners into the hands of those that are engaged in your Torah. To you you made your holy and great name In your world and for your people Israel you made a great salvation and deliverance as you do This day. And the afterwords your children came to the inner chambers of your house cleared your sanctuary and purify it your holy Temple and lit candles In your holy courtyard. And they fixed these eight days of Hanukkah – With complete praise and thanks, and you did for them miracles and wonders and we will thank Your great name, Forever.
paragraphs.note: Previously translated paragraph, Hebrew similarity 98.6%: source and target independently present in source corpus.

paragraphs.text: Upon all of these, You are Blessed, You are Exalted & Uplifted (in our mouths) always, Your Name, our King, forever & ever & all the living will praise You evermore. And they will praise, & they will bless Your Great Name truely, constantly, for It is good, the G·d of our Salvation & our Assistance, the Good G·d. Blessed are You L·rd, the Good, Your Name & You are befitting to give thanks.

paragraphs.text: Grant peace, goodness and blessing, life, grace and kindness, righteousness and mercy to us and to all Israel Your people. Bless us, our Father, all together in the light of Your presence. For by the light of Your presence You have given us, Lord our God, Torah and life, love and kindness, righteousness and mercy, blessing and peace. May it be good in Your eyes to bless us and all Israel Your people with abundant strength and peace. Blessed are You, Lord, who blesses His people Israel with peace. Amen.
paragraphs.note: Identical Hebrew passage to reviewed edot Amidah paragraph 49.

paragraphs.text: Let the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable before Thee, O LORD, my Rock, and my Redeemer.
paragraphs.note: Exact complete Hebrew passage matched to the bundled Tanakh; no fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: My G·d! Guard my tongue from Bad, & my lips from [speaking] deceit. And those that curse me, let my soul be silent. And let my soul be like the dust to all. Open my heart to Your Torah, & after Your Mitzvot (commandments) let my soul pursue, & all that rise against me for bad, quickly nullify their counsel & ruin their thoughts. Do [it] for the sake of Your Name, do [it] for the sake of Your right (mercy), do [it] for the sake of Your Torah, do [it] for the sake of Your Holiness. For the sake of refraining Your beloved (Israel, from sufferance), Your right (mercy) Deliver [us], & answer us.

paragraphs.text: May the One who makes peace in His heights, in His mercy, make peace for us and for all His people Israel; and let us say: Amen.

May it be Your will before You, L·rd, Our G-d and G-d of our fathers – that You build the Holy Temple speedily in our days. And give us our share in Your Torah – to do the laws of Your will and to serve You with a perfect heart.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: After the repetition, recite:

Blessed be the name of the LORD From this time forth and for ever. From the rising of the sun unto the going down thereof The LORD'S name is to be praised. The LORD is high above all nations, His glory is above the heavens. O LORD, our Lord, How glorious is Thy name in all the earth!

paragraphs.text: The prayer leader recites Kaddish Titkabbal.

Exalted & sanctified be His (G·d's) great Name. [cong. - Amen.] In this world that He created according to His will. May His Kingdom reign, & may he cause His redemption to sprout & may He hasten His Messiah. [cong. - Amen.] In your lifetime & in your days, & in the lifetime of the whole house of Israel, speedily & soon; & say ye, Amen. [cong. - Amen.] Be His great Name blessed forever & throughout eternity. Blessed, lauded, glorified, exalted, extolled & honored, uplifted & supremely exalted, the Name of the Holy One, Blessed be He. [cong. - Amen.] Beyond all blessings, songs, praises & consolations of this world to express; & say ye, [cong. - Amen.]
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur (deterministic preferred wording).

paragraphs.text: May our prayers and supplications be accepted, together with the prayers and supplications of all the House of Israel, before our Father in heaven; and say: Amen. [Amen]

May abundant peace descend from heaven: life, plenty, salvation, consolation, deliverance, healing, redemption, forgiveness, atonement, relief and rescue for us and for all His people Israel; and say: Amen. [Amen]
May the One who makes peace in His heights, in His mercy, make peace for us and for all His people Israel; and say: Amen. [Amen]
Bless the LORD, O my soul.
They recite the psalm 'Bless the LORD, O my soul.'

Bless my soul L·rd. L·rd - my G·d – You are Very Great – Majesty & splendor You have attired; He enwraps [Himself] with light like a garment, [and] stretches out the heavens like a curtain. He Who roofs with waters His upper chambers. He makes the clouds His chariot – Who walks on the wings of wind. Who makes His Messengers [from] winds – His servants – are flaming fire. He founded the earth upon its firmament – it will not falter forever. The depths, as with a garment He covered them, upon the mountains stand the water. From Your rebuke they flee; from the voice of your Thunder – they rushed away; Ascending mountains and descending to valleys – to this place that you founded for them. A boundary did You establish without letting them pass; without letting them return to cover the earth. He sends streams in the valleys, between the mountains they flow. They (the rivers) irrigate all of the beasts the field, they satiate the wild animals thirst. Near them do birds of the sky dwell, from among the branches they give their voice [in song]. He irrigates mountains from His upper chambers, with the fruits of Your handiwork You satiate the earth. He sprouts grass for the animals and vegetation for the service, for man to extract bread from the earth. And wine gladdens the heart of man – to make the face shine from oil and with bread are the hearts of man satiated. You satiate the trees – L·rd – the cedars of Lebanon – that were planted. Where are birds – You direct the stork with to her house in the junipers. High mountains are for the chamois - rocks a refuge for the rock badgers. He made the moon for the seasons – the sun to know its coming. You spread Darkness and it is night – when all creatures swarm the forest. The Young lions roar upon their prey – and ask from G·d their food. You shine the sun – and gather them and to their dwelling they go to lie. A man goes to his labor and to his work while it is night. How great are Your works, L·rd, all of them with great wisdom did You make them – the earth is full of Your creatures. This is the great ocean – and width of hands – there swarms – and there uncountable small creatures with the large ones. There the ships go – this You created to sail in it. All of them you give sustenance – to give them food in their proper time. You give to them their gatherings, You open your hands and hey are sustained well. You conceal Your face – they are bewildered – You remove their breath and they die and they return to their dust. You send Your spirit – you created them and renew the face of the earth. May the Honor of the L·rd be eternal - let the L·rd rejoice in his creations. He looks to the earth and it trembles, He touches the mountains and they smoke. I will sing to the L·rd while alive, I will chant to my G·d while I still remain [alive]. I will make my conversations pleasant to Him – I will rejoice with the L·rd. Sins will cease from the land and the wicked will be no more – Bless my soul L·rd – Halleluy-a (Tehillim / Psalm 104)
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: The congregation recites the Kaddish beginning “May there be abundant peace.”

Exalted & sanctified be His (G·d's) great Name. [cong. - Amen.] In this world that He created according to His will. May His Kingdom reign, & may he cause His redemption to sprout & may He hasten His Messiah. paragraphs.text: Kaveh — Hope in the LORD.

Hope to Adonoy; be strong and He will give you courage and hope to Adonoy. There is none holy like Adonoy for there is none beside You and there is no stronghold like our God. For who is a god other than Adonoy and who is a stronghold beside our God.

paragraphs.text: There is none like our God, none like our Lord, none like our King, none like our Savior. Who is like our God, who is like our Lord, who is like our King, who is like our Savior? Let us thank our God, our Lord, our King and our Savior. Blessed is our God, blessed is our Lord, blessed is our King, blessed is our Savior. You are our God, You are our Lord, You are our King, You are our Savior. You will save us; You will rise and show mercy to Zion, for the time to favor her has come, the appointed time has arrived.
The preparation of the incense.

[Incense Offering] You are the L·rd, Our G·d, that our Forefathers burned before You the incense spices at the time that the Holy Temple stood – like You commanded them through Moshe, Your Prophet, like it is written in your Torah.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: And the L·rd said to Moshe – Take for yourself spices- balsam sap / Nataf / & onycha / Sh-h'elet & galbanum / H'elbona, spices & pure frankincense / Levona – each shall be of equal weight. And you shall prepare it (the spices) as incense – a compound, the work of a spice mixer, blended (or salted) pure & holy. And you shall grind from it very well, and you shall take from it, before the [tent of] testimony – in the Tent of Meeting - that I shall meet with you there – holy, holy it shall be for you. And it says – and Aharon shall offer as incense, the incense spices each & every morning when he cleans the lamps he shall offer it. And when Aharon Ascends, he shall offer the incense – a regular incense offering before the L·rd – throughout your generations.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: Our Rabbis Taught, The compound of the Incense, how was it done? Three-hundred & Sixty-eight Maneh (a measure) was in it – 365 [maneh] – like the count of the days of the solar year. One Maneh daily – half in the morning and half in the evening and the three extra maneh – where those of which the Chief Kohen entered [the holy of holies] and took from them a full palm-full on the Yom Kippur – he would return them to the grinder on the eve of Yom Kippur, in order to accomplish the mitzvah – in the finest of finest [way] and 11 spices were in it – and these are they:
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: 1) Balsam, 2) onycha, 3) & galbanum 4) frankincense – the weight of 70 maneh each. 5) myrrh, 6) cassia & 7) spikenard & 8) saffron – [each] a weight of 16, 16 maneh. 9) costus – 12 maneh 10) aromatic bark – three [maneh] 11) cinnamon – 9 (maneh) [Added also were] Lye of Carsina – 9 Kavs (a measure), Wine of Cypres – 3 Seahs and 3 kavs- and if one did not find wine of Cypres – he brings old wine. Salt of Sodom – a quarter [of a kav.] An ascension of smoke – a small amount. Rabbi Nathan, the Babylonian, says – even the resin of the Jordan – a bit. If he put in it honey it is invalid and if he omitted one from all of its spices, he is liable for death [penalty].
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: Rabban Shimeon Son of Gamliel says : The Tzorit is sap, that flows from the Balsam tree. The Lye of Karsina, what does it come [to do]? – in order to rub the onycha in order for it to be beautiful. The wine of Cyprus, why is it brought? in order to soak in it the Onycha, in order for it to be sharp. But is not urine – better [to make it sharp] – rather we do not bring in urine into the Sanctuary out of respect.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: We learned in [a Baraita] Rabbi Nathan Says - When he chops – he says “Hadek Heitev, Hetitev Hadek / Chop Well, Well Chop” because the voice is good for spices. The incense compound divided in half is Kosher. For a third or a-quarter we did not hear [the law]. Rabbi Yehuda said “This is the general rule – if it is in the same proportion – it is Kosher for half, & if it lacks one from all of the spices – he is liable for the death penalty.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: Bar Kapara taught once every sixty or seventy years there were remains [of the spices] of half. And Bar Kapparah also taught , if one was to add a Kartov [a measure] of honey a person would not be able to stand because of the fragrance. And why do we not mix in it honey? Because the Torah says “For any leaven or any honey, do not offer incense from it – as a fire offering. L·rd of hosts, is with us. He is our refuge for us the G·d of Yaakov / Jacob forever. L·rd of hosts, happy is the man that has faith in You. L·rd save, the King will answer us on the day we call. And pleasant to the L·rd is the offering of Yehudah / Judah and Yerusalayim / Jerusalem – like the days of old.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: It was taught in the school of Elijah: Whoever studies halakhot every day is assured a place in the World to Come, as it is said, 'His ways are everlasting.' Read not halikhot ('ways'), but halakhot ('laws'). Rabbi Elazar said in the name of Rabbi Hanina: Torah scholars increase peace in the world, as it is said, 'All your children shall be taught of the LORD, and great shall be the peace of your children.' Read not banayikh ('your children'), but bonayikh ('your builders'). May there be peace within your walls and tranquility in your palaces. For the sake of my brothers and friends, let me speak peace concerning you. For the sake of the house of the LORD our God, I will seek your good. May you see your children's children; peace be upon Israel. Great peace have those who love Your Torah, and they have no stumbling block. The LORD will give strength to His people; the LORD will bless His people with peace.

paragraphs.text: It is [incumbent] upon us to praise the L·rd of all. To bestow Greatness to the Molder of creation, for He did not make us as the nations of the lands, & he did not establish us like the families of the earth, for He did not assign our portion as theirs, & our lot like all the multitudes - for they bow to vanity & emptiness & pray to a god that saves not. And we bow before the King, the King of all Kings, the Holy One, Blessed be He, Who spreads out the heavens & creates the foundation of the earth. And the seat of His precious abode is in Heaven above & the divine presence of his power, is in the highest heights. He is our G·d, & there is no other. Our G·d is true, & no other is beside Him. Like it is written in the Torah - "And you shall know today, & you shall take it to heart, that it is the L·rd (Hash·m), Who is G·d in the heavens above & upon the earth below. There is no other.”
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: Therefore, we will hope to You L·rd, our G·d to see speedily the glory of Your Might - to remove abominable idolatry from the earth & the false gods be utterly terminated, to repair the world with the Kingship of the Al·mighty. And all living flesh will call in Your Name to turn back to You all the wicked of the earth. They will recognize & will know, all the inhabitants of the earth, that to You that every knee shall bow down, & every tongue. Before you they will kneel & bow down & give honor to Your glorious name & they will all accept the yolk of Your Kingship. And Reign upon them speedily forever & ever. For the Kingship, it is Yours. And forevermore reign in glory. Like it is written in your Torah, “The L·rd will reign forever & ever.” And it is said “and it will be the L·rd will Be King upon all of the earth. On that day the L·rd will be One (ie, only He will be worshiped) & His name One.” And in Your Torah, L·rd, Our G·d, it is written saying “Hear Oh Israel, the L·rd is our G·d the L·rd is One.”

paragraphs.text: Psalm for Passover.

'O give thanks unto the LORD, for He is good, For His mercy endureth for ever.' So let the redeemed of the LORD say, Whom He hath redeemed from the hand of the adversary; And gathered them out of the lands, From the east and from the west, From the north and from the sea. They wandered in the wilderness in a desert way; They found no city of habitation. Hungry and thirsty, Their soul fainted in them. Then they cried unto the LORD in their trouble, And He delivered them out of their distresses. And He led them by a straight way, That they might go to a city of habitation. Let them give thanks unto the LORD for His mercy, And for His wonderful works to the children of men! For He hath satisfied the longing soul, And the hungry soul He hath filled with good. Such as sat in darkness and in the shadow of death, Being bound in affliction and iron— Because they rebelled against the words of God, And contemned the counsel of the Most High. Therefore He humbled their heart with travail, They stumbled, and there was none to help— They cried unto the LORD in their trouble, And He saved them out of their distresses. He brought them out of darkness and the shadow of death, And broke their bands in sunder. . Let them give thanks unto the LORD for His mercy, And for His wonderful works to the children of men! For He hath broken the gates of brass, And cut the bars of iron in sunder. Crazed because of the way of their transgression, And afflicted because of their iniquities— Their soul abhorred all manner of food, And they drew near unto the gates of death— They cried unto the LORD in their trouble, And He saved them out of their distresses; He sent His word, and healed them, And delivered them from their graves. Let them give thanks unto the LORD for His mercy, And for His wonderful works to the children of men! And let them offer the sacrifices of thanksgiving, And declare His works with singing. They that go down to the sea in ships, That do business in great waters— These saw the works of the LORD, And His wonders in the deep; For He commanded, and raised the stormy wind, Which lifted up the waves thereof; They mounted up to the heaven, they went down to the deeps; Their soul melted away because of trouble; They reeled to and fro, and staggered like a drunken man, And all their wisdom was swallowed up— They cried unto the LORD in their trouble, And He brought them out of their distresses. He made the storm a calm, So that the waves thereof were still. Then were they glad because they were quiet, And He led them unto their desired haven. Let them give thanks unto the LORD for His mercy, And for His wonderful works to the children of men! Let them exalt Him also in the assembly of the people, And praise Him in the seat of the elders. He turneth rivers into a wilderness, And watersprings into a thirsty ground; A fruitful land into a salt waste, For the wickedness of them that dwell therein. He turneth a wilderness into a pool of water, And a dry land into watersprings. And there He maketh the hungry to dwell, And they establish a city of habitation; And sow fields, and plant vineyards, Which yield fruits of increase. He blesseth them also, so that they are multiplied greatly, And suffereth not their cattle to decrease. Again, they are minished and dwindle away Through oppression of evil and sorrow. He poureth contempt upon princes, And causeth them to wander in the waste, where there is no way. Yet setteth He the needy on high from affliction, And maketh his families like a flock. The upright see it, and are glad; And all iniquity stoppeth her mouth. Whoso is wise, let him observe these things, And let them consider the mercies of the LORD.

paragraphs.text: In the Passover Mussaf, continue with the Kaddish beginning “Yehei Shelama” and “Kaveh” to the end.
Psalm for Shavuot.

For the Leader. A Psalm of David, a Song. Let God arise, let His enemies be scattered; And let them that hate Him flee before Him. As smoke is driven away, so drive them away; As wax melteth before the fire, So let the wicked perish at the presence of God. But let the righteous be glad, let them exult before God; Yea, let them rejoice with gladness. Sing unto God, sing praises to His name; Extol Him that rideth upon the skies, whose name is the LORD; And exult ye before Him. A father of the fatherless, and a judge of the widows, Is God in His holy habitation. God maketh the solitary to dwell in a house; He bringeth out the prisoners into prosperity; The rebellious dwell but in a parched land. O God, when Thou wentest forth before Thy people, When Thou didst march through the wilderness; Selah The earth trembled, the heavens also dropped at the presence of God; Even yon Sinai trembled at the presence of God, the God of Israel. A bounteous rain didst Thou pour down, O God; When Thine inheritance was weary, Thou didst confirm it. Thy flock settled therein; Thou didst prepare in Thy goodness for the poor, O God. The Lord giveth the word; The women that proclaim the tidings are a great host. Kings of armies flee, they flee; And she that tarrieth at home divideth the spoil. When ye lie among the sheepfolds, The wings of the dove are covered with silver, And her pinions with the shimmer of gold. . When the Almighty scattereth kings therein, It snoweth in Zalmon. A mountain of God is the mountain of Bashan; A mountain of peaks is the mountain of Bashan. Why look ye askance, ye mountains of peaks, At the mountain which God hath desired for His abode? Yea, the LORD will dwell therein for ever. The chariots of God are myriads, even thousands upon thousands; The Lord is among them, as in Sinai, in holiness. Thou hast ascended on high, Thou hast led captivity captive; Thou hast received gifts among men, Yea, among the rebellious also, that the LORD God might dwell there. Blessed be the Lord, day by day He beareth our burden, Even the God who is our salvation. Selah God is unto us a God of deliverances; And unto GOD the Lord belong the issues of death. Surely God will smite through the head of His enemies, The hairy scalp of him that goeth about in his guiltiness. The Lord said: 'I will bring back from Bashan, I will bring them back from the depths of the sea; That thy foot may wade through blood, That the tongue of thy dogs may have its portion from thine enemies.' They see Thy goings, O God, Even the goings of my God, my King, in holiness. The singers go before, the minstrels follow after, In the midst of damsels playing upon timbrels. 'Bless ye God in full assemblies, Even the Lord, ye that are from the fountain of Israel.' There is Benjamin, the youngest, ruling them, The princes of Judah their council, The princes of Zebulun, the princes of Naphtali. Thy God hath commanded thy strength; Be strong, O God, Thou that hast wrought for us Out of Thy temple at Jerusalem, Whither kings shall bring presents unto Thee. Rebuke the wild beast of the reeds, The multitude of the bulls, with the calves of the peoples, Every one submitting himself with pieces of silver; He hath scattered the peoples that delight in war! Nobles shall come out of Egypt; Ethiopia shall hasten to stretch out her hands unto God. Sing unto God, ye kingdoms of the earth; O sing praises unto the Lord; Selah To Him that rideth upon the heavens of heavens, which are of old; Lo, He uttereth His voice, a mighty voice. Ascribe ye strength unto God; His majesty is over Israel, And His strength is in the skies. Awful is God out of thy holy places; The God of Israel, He giveth strength and power unto the people; Blessed be God.
paragraphs.note: Exact complete Hebrew passage matched to the bundled Tanakh; no fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: Psalm for Sukkot.

For the Leader; Maschil of the sons of Korah. As the hart panteth after the water brooks, so panteth my soul after Thee, O God. My soul thirsteth for God, for the living God: 'When shall I come and appear before God?' My tears have been my food day and night, while they say unto me all the day: 'Where is Thy God?' These things I remember, and pour out my soul within me, how I passed on with the throng, and led them to the house of God, with the voice of joy and praise, a multitude keeping holyday. Why art thou cast down, O my soul? And why moanest thou within me? Hope thou in God; for I shall yet praise Him for the salvation of His countenance. O my God, my soul is cast down within me; therefore do I remember Thee from the land of Jordan, and the Hermons, from the hill Mizar. Deep calleth unto deep at the voice of Thy cataracts; all Thy waves and Thy billows are gone over me. By day the LORD will command His lovingkindness, and in the night His song shall be with me, even a prayer unto the God of my life. I will say unto God my Rock: 'Why hast Thou forgotten me? Why go I mourning under the oppression of the enemy?' As with a crushing in my bones, mine adversaries taunt me; while they say unto me all the day: 'Where is Thy God?' Why art thou cast down, O my soul? And why moanest thou within me? Hope thou in God; for I shall yet praise Him, the salvation of my countenance, and my God.

paragraphs.text: In the Sukkot Mussaf, continue with the Kaddish beginning “Yehei Shelama” and “Kaveh” to the end.
Psalm for Shemini Atzeret.

For the Leader; on the Sheminith. A Psalm of David. Help, LORD; for the godly man ceaseth; For the faithful fail from among the children of men. They speak falsehood every one with his neighbour; With flattering lip, and with a double heart, do they speak. May the LORD cut off all flattering lips, The tongue that speaketh proud things! Who have said: 'Our tongue will we make mighty; Our lips are with us: who is lord over us?' 'For the oppression of the poor, for the sighing of the needy, Now will I arise', saith the LORD; 'I will set him in safety at whom they puff.' . The words of the LORD are pure words, As silver tried in a crucible on the earth, refined seven times. Thou wilt keep them, O LORD; Thou wilt preserve us from this generation for ever. The wicked walk on every side, When vileness is exalted among the sons of men.

paragraphs.text: You have chosen us from all peoples; You have loved us and taken delight in us. You have exalted us above every language and sanctified us through Your commandments. You have drawn us near, our King, to Your service, and You have called Your great and holy name upon us.

You made Your righteous judgments known to us and taught us to perform the decrees of Your will. In love You gave us, Lord our God, just ordinances and true teachings, good statutes and commandments. You granted us seasons of rejoicing, sacred assemblies, and festivals of willing offerings; You caused us to inherit the holiness of Shabbat, the honor of the festival, and the rejoicing of the pilgrimage feast. You distinguished the holiness of Shabbat from that of a festival, and sanctified the seventh day above the six days of labor. You set apart and sanctified Your people Israel with Your holiness.

paragraphs.text: Look with favor, LORD our God, upon Your people Israel and attend to their prayers. Restore the service to the inner sanctuary of Your house; receive Israel's offerings and their prayers swiftly, lovingly, and with favor, and may the service of Your people Israel always be acceptable. In Your great mercy, delight in us and accept us; may our eyes behold Your return to Zion in mercy. Blessed are You, LORD, who restores His Presence to Zion.
[Upon Saying "Modim" / "We are Grateful" One Bows]
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: We are grateful to You, that You are He Who is the L·rd, our G·d, & G·d of our fathers forever, & our Rock, the Rock of our lives & You are He Who is a Shield of salvation. For each & every generation, we will thank You & will relate Your praise, upon our lives that are placed in Your Hands, & upon our souls, that are entrusted in Your hands (when we sleep), & upon Your miracles that all day are with us, & all Your wonders & goodness at all times, at night, & morning & afternoon. The Good [One], for Your mercy never ends, The Merciful [One are You], for Your loving-kindness never ceases, forever we have hope in You.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: Thanks Of the rabbis / Said at repetition of Amid (In the repetition Of the standing prayer, when the prayer leader says “Modim”, the congregation says:) We give thanks to You, that You L·rd, are our God and God of our fathers, God of all flesh, our Creator, the creator [of the works] of Genesis. Blessings and thanks to your great and Holy name, that You gave us life and made us exist. Thus, give us life and have mercy upon us, and gather in our exiles to Your holy courtyards, To observe Your ordinances and to do Your will and to serve You with a complete heart, upon that we give thanks to You. Blessed is the Lord of thanks.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: Upon all of these, You are Blessed, You are Exalted & Uplifted (in our mouths) always, Your Name, our King, forever & ever & all the living will praise You evermore. And they will praise, & they will bless Your Great Name truely, constantly, for It is good, the G·d of our Salvation & our Assistance, the Good G·d. Blessed are You L·rd, the Good, Your Name & You are befitting to give thanks.

paragraphs.text: Grant peace, goodness and blessing, life, grace and kindness, righteousness and mercy to us and to all Israel Your people. Bless us, our Father, all together in the light of Your presence. For by the light of Your presence You have given us, Lord our God, Torah and life, love and kindness, righteousness and mercy, blessing and peace. May it be good in Your eyes to bless us and all Israel Your people with abundant strength and peace. Blessed are You, Lord, who blesses His people Israel with peace. Amen.
paragraphs.note: Original English working translation aligned to the full Hebrew paragraph; specialist review pending.

paragraphs.text: Let the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable before Thee, O LORD, my Rock, and my Redeemer.
paragraphs.note: Exact complete Hebrew passage matched to the bundled Tanakh; no fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: My G·d! Guard my tongue from Bad, & my lips from [speaking] deceit. And those that curse me, let my soul be silent. And let my soul be like the dust to all. Open my heart to Your Torah, & after Your Mitzvot (commandments) let my soul pursue, & all that rise against me for bad, quickly nullify their counsel & ruin their thoughts. Do [it] for the sake of Your Name, do [it] for the sake of Your right (mercy), do [it] for the sake of Your Torah, do [it] for the sake of Your Holiness. For the sake of refraining Your beloved (Israel, from sufferance), Your right (mercy) Deliver [us], & answer us.

paragraphs.text: May the One who makes peace in His heights, in His mercy, make peace for us and for all His people Israel; and let us say: Amen.

May it be Your will before You, L·rd, Our G-d and G-d of our fathers – that You build the Holy Temple speedily in our days. And give us our share in Your Torah – to do the laws of Your will and to serve You with a perfect heart.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: After the repetition, recite:

Blessed be the name of the LORD From this time forth and for ever. From the rising of the sun unto the going down thereof The LORD'S name is to be praised. The LORD is high above all nations, His glory is above the heavens. O LORD, our Lord, How glorious is Thy name in all the earth!
paragraphs.note: Every colon-delimited fragment matched a unique near-exact complete Tanakh verse; reviewed orthographic/qere alignment only.

paragraphs.text: At the evening service on a festival night, after the Amidah, if the festival falls on Shabbat recite Vayechulu, and the prayer leader recites the abridged sevenfold blessing and Kaddish Titkabbal. If it falls on a weekday, recite “May the name [of the LORD be blessed]” and the prayer leader says Kaddish Titkabbal. On the first night of Passover, after the Amidah recite the entire Hallel with blessings before and after it; then the prayer leader says Kaddish Titkabbal. The abridged sevenfold blessing is not recited that night, even when it falls on Shabbat: instead say Vayechulu immediately after the Amidah, and then recite the blessings over Hallel.
After Kaddish Titkabbal, the following psalms are recited:
When the festival falls on Shabbat, this psalm is added:

A Psalm of David. The LORD is my shepherd; I shall not want. He maketh me to lie down in green pastures; He leadeth me beside the still waters. He restoreth my soul; He guideth me in straight paths for His name's sake. Yea, though I walk through the valley of the shadow of death, I will fear no evil, for Thou art with me; Thy rod and Thy staff, they comfort me. Thou preparest a table before me in the presence of mine enemies; Thou hast anointed my head with oil; my cup runneth over. Surely goodness and mercy shall follow me all the days of my life; And I shall dwell in the house of the LORD for ever.
paragraphs.note: Exact complete Hebrew passage matched to the bundled Tanakh; no fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: On Passover, say:

When Israel came forth out of Egypt, The house of Jacob from a people of strange language; Judah became His sanctuary, Israel His dominion. The sea saw it, and fled; The Jordan turned backward. The mountains skipped like rams, The hills like young sheep. What aileth thee, O thou sea, that thou fleest? Thou Jordan, that thou turnest backward? Ye mountains, that ye skip like rams; Ye hills, like young sheep? Tremble, thou earth, at the presence of the Lord, At the presence of the God of Jacob; Who turned the rock into a pool of water, The flint into a fountain of waters.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: For Shavuot, Sukkot, and Shemini Atzeret, say:

A Song of Ascents; of David. I rejoiced when they said unto me: 'Let us go unto the house of the LORD.' Our feet are standing within thy gates, O Jerusalem; Jerusalem, that art builded as a city that is compact together; Whither the tribes went up, even the tribes of the LORD, as a testimony unto Israel, to give thanks unto the name of the LORD. For there were set thrones for judgment, the thrones of the house of David. Pray for the peace of Jerusalem; May they prosper that love thee. Peace be within thy walls, and prosperity within thy palaces. For my brethren and companions' sakes, I will now say: 'Peace be within thee.' For the sake of the house of the LORD our God I will seek thy good.
paragraphs.note: Exact complete Hebrew passage matched to the bundled Tanakh; no fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: The congregation recites the Kaddish beginning “May there be abundant peace.”

Exalted & sanctified be His (G·d's) great Name. [cong. - Amen.] In this world that He created according to His will. May His Kingdom reign, & may he cause His redemption to sprout & may He hasten His Messiah. [cong. - Amen.] In your lifetime & in your days, & in the lifetime of the whole house of Israel, speedily & soon; & say ye, Amen. [cong. - Amen.] Be His great Name blessed forever & throughout eternity. Blessed, lauded, glorified, exalted, extolled & honored, uplifted & supremely exalted, the Name of the Holy One, Blessed be He. [cong. - Amen.] Beyond all blessings, songs, praises & consolations of this world to express; & say ye, [cong. - Amen.]
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur (deterministic preferred wording).

paragraphs.text: May there be abundant peace from Heaven, life, satisfaction, salvation, consolation, deliverance, healing, redemption, forgiveness, atonement, relief, and rescue for us and for all His people Israel. And say, Amen. [Amen] He who makes peace in His high places, may He in His mercy make peace upon us and upon all His people Israel. And say, Amen. [Amen]
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: It is [incumbent] upon us to praise the L·rd of all. To bestow Greatness to the Molder of creation, for He did not make us as the nations of the lands, & he did not establish us like the families of the earth, for He did not assign our portion as theirs, & our lot like all the multitudes - for they bow to vanity & emptiness & pray to a god that saves not. And we bow before the King, the King of all Kings, the Holy One, Blessed be He, Who spreads out the heavens & creates the foundation of the earth. And the seat of His precious abode is in Heaven above & the divine presence of his power, is in the highest heights. He is our G·d, & there is no other. Our G·d is true, & no other is beside Him. Like it is written in the Torah - "And you shall know today, & you shall take it to heart, that it is the L·rd (Hash·m), Who is G·d in the heavens above & upon the earth below. There is no other.”
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: Therefore, we will hope to You L·rd, our G·d to see speedily the glory of Your Might - to remove abominable idolatry from the earth & the false gods be utterly terminated, to repair the world with the Kingship of the Al·mighty. And all living flesh will call in Your Name to turn back to You all the wicked of the earth. They will recognize & will know, all the inhabitants of the earth, that to You that every knee shall bow down, & every tongue. Before you they will kneel & bow down & give honor to Your glorious name & they will all accept the yolk of Your Kingship. And Reign upon them speedily forever & ever. For the Kingship, it is Yours. And forevermore reign in glory. Like it is written in your Torah, “The L·rd will reign forever & ever.” And it is said “and it will be the L·rd will Be King upon all of the earth. On that day the L·rd will be One (ie, only He will be worshiped) & His name One.” And in Your Torah, L·rd, Our G·d, it is written saying “Hear Oh Israel, the L·rd is our G·d the L·rd is One.”
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur (deterministic preferred wording).

paragraphs.text: Musaf for the Three Pilgrimage Festivals.
O Lord, open Thou my lips; and my mouth shall declare Thy praise.
paragraphs.note: Exact complete Hebrew passage matched to the bundled Tanakh; no fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: Blessed are You, Lord, our God and God of our ancestors, God of Abraham, God of Isaac, and God of Jacob; the great, mighty, and awesome God, God Most High, who bestows abundant loving-kindness, possesses all things, remembers the kindnesses of the ancestors, and lovingly brings redemption to their children's children for the sake of His name. O King who helps, saves, and shields: blessed are You, Lord, Shield of Abraham.
paragraphs.note: Identical Hebrew passage to reviewed edot Amidah paragraph 2.

paragraphs.text: You are mighty forever, my L·rd, You revive the dead - Greatly capable of saving.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur (deterministic preferred wording).

paragraphs.text: (summer) who causes dew to fall (winter) who causes the winds to blow & the rain to fall.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: You sustain the living with loving-kindness. You revive the dead with great compassion. You support the fallen & heal the ill. And You release those bound. And You fulfill Your faithfulness to those who sleep in the ground. Who is like You, Master of [all] powers, King, Who causes death & gives life & causes salvation to sprout. & You are trustworthy to revive the dead. Blessed are You L·rd, Who revives the dead.
During the cantor's Mussaf repetition on a festival or on a Shabbat that is also a festival, recite this Kedushah:

The multitudes of angels on high, together with Your people Israel assembled below, offer You a crown, Lord our God. Together all of them proclaim Your holiness three times, as Your prophet said: 'And one called to another and said: Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hosts; the whole earth is full of His glory.' His glory fills the world, and His ministers ask [on Shabbat, when saying 'Where', intend to receive the additional Shabbat soul]: 'Where is the place of His glory, that we may revere Him?' In response they praise and say: 'Blessed is the glory of the Lord from His place.' From His place may He turn in mercy to His people who declare His oneness each evening and morning, twice every day, with love: 'Hear, Israel: the Lord is our God, the Lord is One.' He is our God, He is our Father, He is our King, He is our Savior. He will save and redeem us a second time, and in His mercy make all living beings hear: 'Behold, I have redeemed you at the end as at the beginning, to be your God; I am the Lord your God.' And in Your holy words it is written: 'The Lord shall reign for ever, your God, O Zion, from generation to generation. Hallelujah!'
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: During the prayer leader's repetition of Musaf on Chol HaMoed, say:

The angels and heavenly hosts shall offer You a crown, Lord our God, together with Your people Israel gathered below. All of them together shall proclaim Your holiness threefold, as spoken by Your prophet: 'And one called to another and said: Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of hosts; the whole earth is full of His glory.' Facing them they offer praise and say: 'Blessed is the glory of the Lord from His place.' In Your sacred words it is written: 'The Lord shall reign forever, your God, Zion, from generation to generation. Hallelujah!'
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: You are holy and Your Name is holy and holy beings praise You every day, forever. Blessed are You, Adonoy, the Almighty, the Holy One.
paragraphs.note: Exact Hebrew match to a sequence of reviewed Siddur paragraphs; translations joined without fuzzy splitting.

paragraphs.text: You have chosen us from all peoples; You have loved us and taken delight in us. You have exalted us above every language and sanctified us through Your commandments. You have drawn us near, our King, to Your service, and You have called Your great and holy name upon us.
You gave us, LORD our God, with love (on Shabbat add 'Sabbaths for rest, and') festivals for rejoicing, holidays and appointed times for gladness, this day of ...
On Shabbat: “This Shabbat day, and the day of...”
On Passover: 'this Festival of Unleavened Bread, this (on a festival add 'holy') day of sacred assembly, the season of our freedom.'
On Shavuot: 'this festival of Shavuot, this holy festival day, the season of the giving of our Torah.'
On Sukkot: 'this Festival of Booths, this (on a festival add 'holy') day of sacred assembly, the season of our rejoicing.'
On Shemini Atzeret: 'this festival of the Eighth Day of Assembly, this holy festival day, the season of our rejoicing.'
With love, a holy convocation, in remembrance of the Exodus from Egypt.

Our God and God of our ancestors, because of our sins we were exiled from our land and driven far from our soil. We are unable to go up, appear, and bow before You in the house You have chosen, the dwelling of Your splendor, the great and holy house upon which Your name is called, because a hostile hand was stretched out against Your Sanctuary.
paragraphs.note: Original English working translation aligned to the full Hebrew paragraph; specialist review pending.

paragraphs.text: May it be Your will, Lord our God and God of our ancestors, merciful King, that You return and have mercy on us and on Your Sanctuary in Your abundant compassion; rebuild it speedily and magnify its glory. Our Father, our King, our God, reveal the glory of Your kingdom over us soon. Appear and be exalted above us before the eyes of all living beings. Draw our scattered people near from among the nations, gather our dispersed ones from the far ends of the earth, and bring us, Lord our God, to Zion Your city in song and to Jerusalem, the city of Your Sanctuary, in everlasting joy. Please, our God, there let us offer our obligatory offerings before You, the daily offerings in their order and the additional offerings according to their laws.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: The additional offering (on Shabbat: 'the additional offerings of this Sabbath day') and the day of ...
For Passover: the Festival of Unleavened Bread.
For Shavuot: the Festival of Weeks.
On Sukkot: the Festival of Booths.
For Shemini Atzeret: the Festival of the Eighth Day of Assembly.

This day—and on a festival add: “this good day, a holy convocation”—we shall prepare and bring offerings before You in love, according to Your will, as You wrote in Your Torah through Moses Your servant.

Our God and God of our ancestors, merciful King, have compassion on us. You who are good and do good, turn toward us. Return to us in the abundance of Your mercy, for the sake of the ancestors who did Your will. Rebuild Your House as at first, establish Your Sanctuary on its foundation; let us see its rebuilding and rejoice in its restoration. Return Your Presence into it, restore the priests to their service and the Levites to their platforms, their song and their music; restore Israel to their dwellings. There we shall ascend and appear and bow before You on the three pilgrimage occasions each year, as it is written in the Torah: 'Three times a year all your males shall appear before the Lord your God at the place He will choose, at the Festival of Unleavened Bread, at the Festival of Weeks, and at the Festival of Booths. They shall not appear before the Lord empty-handed, but each according to what he can give, according to the blessing of the Lord your God that He has given you.'
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Bestow upon us, LORD our God, the blessing of Your festivals for life, joy, and peace, as You have desired and promised to bless us; so bless us always.
On Shabbat, some add:
Our God and God of our ancestors, be pleased with our rest.

Sanctify us through Your commandments, give us a share in Your Torah, satisfy us with Your goodness, gladden our souls in Your salvation, and purify our hearts to serve You in truth. Let us inherit, Lord our God, [on Shabbat: with love and favor] with joy and rejoicing [on Shabbat: Your Sabbaths and] Your holy festivals. May all Israel who sanctify Your name rejoice in You. Blessed are You, Lord, who sanctifies [on Shabbat: the Sabbath,] Israel, and the festivals.

On an intermediate festival day, after Full Kaddish, recite the psalm for that festival, then Kaddish Yehei Shelama and 'Hope in the LORD' to the end.
Hanukkah.
Order of lighting the Hanukkah candles.

For the sake of uniting the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Presence, in awe and love and in love and awe, uniting the letters Yod–Heh with Vav–Heh in perfect unity in the name of all Israel: we now come to fulfill the commandment of lighting the Hanukkah lights, as our sages of blessed memory ordained, together with all the commandments included in it, to repair its root in the highest realm, to bring delight to our Maker and fulfill our Creator's will. May this act be reckoned before Him, blessed be He, as though we had directed all the intentions appropriate to this commandment. May the favor of the Lord our God be upon us; establish the work of our hands for us; yes, establish the work of our hands.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us to light the Hanukkah candle.
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who performed miracles for our ancestors in those days, at this season.
On the first night, this blessing is also recited:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who has kept us alive, sustained us, and brought us to this season.
After lighting one candle, one says:

We kindle these lights for the miracles, acts of salvation, and wonders You performed for our ancestors through Your holy priests. Throughout the eight days of Hanukkah these lights are sacred, and we have no permission to use them, but only to look at them, in order to give thanks to Your name for Your miracles, wonders, and saving acts.
paragraphs.note: Original English working translation aligned to the full Hebrew paragraph; specialist review pending.

paragraphs.text: A Psalm, a song for the inauguration of the Temple, by David. I will exalt You, Adonoy, for You have upheld me, and not let my foes rejoice over me. Adonoy, my God, I cried out to You, and You healed me. Adonoy, You have raised my soul from the lower world. You have kept me alive, lest I descend to the Pit. Sing to Adonoy, [you,] His pious ones, and give thanks to His holy Name. For His anger lasts only a moment, but there is [long] life, in His conciliation. In the evening, one retires weeping, but in the morning there is [a cry of] joy! I said, in my serenity, I would never be moved. [But,] Adonoy, it was Your will [alone] that established my mountain as a stronghold. When You concealed Your Presence, I was terrified. To You, Adonoy, I called, and my Master I beseeched. What gain is there in [the shedding of] my blood? In my going down to destruction? Will the dust acknowledge You? Will it proclaim Your truth? Hear [me] Adonoy, and be gracious to me, Adonoy, be a help to me. You have turned my mourning into dancing, You have loosened my sackcloth and supported me with joy. In order that my soul might sing to You and not be stilled, Adonoy, my God, forever will I thank You.

paragraphs.text: Morning prayer for Hanukkah.
Laws of Shacharit for Hanukkah.

Pray the weekday service. Recite Al HaNissim in the thanksgiving blessing, complete Hallel, and say Half Kaddish. Take out a Torah scroll; Berikh Shemeh is not recited. Three people are called to the Torah from Parashat Naso. On the first day of Hanukkah, the kohen reads to 'the Tabernacle,' the Levite to 'dedication of the altar,' and the third reader to 'Amminadab.' On the second day, the kohen reads to 'filled with incense,' the Levite to 'son of Tzuar,' and the third reader repeats 'on the second day.' On each subsequent day of Hanukkah read that day's offering. After the reading, say Half Kaddish. Do not recite Ya'anekha or A Prayer of David. When announcing 'Today is the [number] day of the holy Sabbath week,' omit 'the song which the Levites used to say,' and after Hoshi'enu say Psalm 30, 'A psalm, a song for the dedication.' Conclude the prayers as on other weekdays.

paragraphs.text: Reading for the first day.

On the first day of Hanukkah, three people are called to the Torah for the portion Naso, through “Nahshon son of Amminadab.” The kohen reads until “before the Tabernacle,” the Levite until “the dedication of the altar,” and the Israelite until “Nahshon son of Amminadab.”

And the LORD spoke unto Moses, saying: ’Speak unto Aaron and unto his sons, saying: On this wise ye shall bless the children of Israel; ye shall say unto them: The LORD bless thee, and keep thee; The LORD make His face to shine upon thee, and be gracious unto thee; The LORD lift up His countenance upon thee, and give thee peace. So shall they put My name upon the children of Israel, and I will bless them.’ And it came to pass on the day that Moses had made an end of setting up the tabernacle, and had anointed it and sanctified it, and all the furniture thereof, and the altar and all the vessels thereof, and had anointed them and sanctified them; that the princes of Israel, the heads of their fathers’houses, offered—these were the princes of the tribes, these are they that were over them that were numbered. And they brought their offering before the LORD, six covered wagons, and twelve oxen: a wagon for every two of the princes, and for each one an ox; and they presented them before the tabernacle. And the LORD spoke unto Moses, saying: ’Take it of them, that they may be to do the service of the tent of meeting; and thou shalt give them unto the Levites, to every man according to his service.’ And Moses took the wagons and the oxen, and gave them unto the Levites. Two wagons and four oxen he gave unto the sons of Gershon, according to their service. And four wagons and eight oxen he gave unto the sons of Merari, according unto their service, under the hand of Ithamar the son of Aaron the priest. But unto the sons of Kohath he gave none, because the service of the holy things belonged unto them: they bore them upon their shoulders. And the princes brought the dedication-offering of the altar in the day that it was anointed, even the princes brought their offering before the altar. And the LORD said unto Moses: ‘They shall present their offering each prince on his day, for the dedication of the altar.’ And he that presented his offering the first day was Nahshon the son of Amminadab, of the tribe of Judah; and his offering was one silver dish, the weight thereof was a hundred and thirty shekels, one silver basin of seventy shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary; both of them full of fine flour mingled with oil for a meal-offering; one golden pan of ten shekels, full of incense; one young bullock, one ram, one he-lamb of the first year, for a burnt-offering; one male of the goats for a sin-offering; and for the sacrifice of peace-offerings, two oxen, five rams, five he-goats, five he-lambs of the first year. This was the offering of Nahshon the son of Amminadab.

On the eighth day Gamaliel the son of Pedahzur, prince of the children of Manasseh: his offering was one silver dish, the weight thereof was a hundred and thirty shekels, one silver basin of seventy shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary; both of them full of fine flour mingled with oil for a meal-offering; one golden pan of ten shekels, full of incense; one young bullock, one ram, one he-lamb of the first year, for a burnt-offering; one male of the goats for a sin-offering; and for the sacrifice of peace-offerings, two oxen, five rams, five he-goats, five he-lamb of the first year. This was the offering of Ahiezer the son of Ammishaddai. On the eleventh day Pagiel the son of Ochran, prince of the children of Asher: his offering was one silver dish, the weight thereof was a hundred and thirty shekels, one silver basin of seventy shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary; both of them full of fine flour mingled with oil for a meal-offering; one golden pan of ten shekels, full of incense; one young bullock, one ram, one he-lamb of the first year, for a burnt-offering; one male of the goats for a sin-offering; and for the sacrifice of peace-offerings, two oxen, five rams, five he-goats, five he-lambs of the first year. This was the offering of Pagiel the son of Ochran. On the twelfth day Ahira the son of Enan, prince of the children of Naphtali: his offering was one silver dish, the weight thereof was a hundred and thirty shekels, one silver basin of seventy shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary; both of them full of fine flour mingled with oil for a meal-offering; one golden pan of ten shekels, full of incense; one young bullock, one ram, one he-lamb of the first year, for a burnt-offering; one male of the goats for a sin-offering; and for the sacrifice of peace-offerings, two oxen, five rams, five he-goats, five he-lambs of the first year. This was the offering of Ahira the son of Enan. This was the dedication-offering of the altar, in the day when it was anointed, at the hands of the princes of Israel: twelve silver dishes, twelve silver basins, twelve golden pans; each silver dish weighing a hundred and thirty shekels, and each basin seventy; all the silver of the vessels two thousand and four hundred shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary; twelve golden pans, full of incense, weighing ten shekels apiece, after the shekel of the sanctuary; all the gold of the pans a hundred and twenty shekels; all the oxen for the burnt-offering twelve bullocks, the rams twelve, the he-lambs of the first year twelve, and their meal-offering; and the males of the goats for a sin-offering twelve; and all the oxen for the sacrifice of peace-offerings twenty and four bullocks, the rams sixty, the he-goats sixty, the he-lambs of the first year sixty. This was the dedication-offering of the altar, after that it was anointed. And when Moses went into the tent of meeting that He might speak with him, then he heard the Voice speaking unto him from above the ark-cover that was upon the ark of the testimony, from between the two cherubim; and He spoke unto him. And the LORD spoke unto Moses, saying: ’Speak unto Aaron, and say unto him: When thou lightest the lamps, the seven lamps shall give light in front of the candlestick.’ And Aaron did so: he lighted the lamps thereof so as to give light in front of the candlestick, as the LORD commanded Moses. And this was the work of the candlestick, beaten work of gold; unto the base thereof, and unto the flowers thereof, it was beaten work; according unto the pattern which the LORD had shown Moses, so he made the candlestick.

paragraphs.text: Rosh Chodesh Tevet when it falls on a weekday.

Pray the weekday service, adding Ya'aleh VeYavo in the Avodah blessing and Al HaNissim in the thanksgiving blessing, and complete Hallel. After Hallel say Kaddish Titkabbal and take out two Torah scrolls. From the first, three people read the Rosh Chodesh section: the kohen to 'a quarter of a hin'; the Levite to 'and its libation'; and the third reader to the end of the Rosh Chodesh reading. Do not say Kaddish yet. From the second scroll, the fourth reader reads the day's offering from the section of the tribal leaders. Say Half Kaddish, then Ashrei, Uva LeTzion, Beit Yaakov, the Song of the Day and Hoshi'enu. Return the scrolls and say Half Kaddish. Pray the Rosh Chodesh Mussaf, adding Al HaNissim in thanksgiving. After Mussaf say Kaddish Titkabbal, Psalm 104 (Barekhi Nafshi), Psalm 30 (the dedication psalm), Kaddish Yehe Shelama, Kaveh El Hashem, Kaddish Al Yisrael and Aleinu.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Shabbat Hanukkah.

Pray as on other Sabbaths, adding Al HaNissim to the thanksgiving blessing, completing Hallel, and reciting Kaddish Titkabbal. Take out two Torah scrolls. From the first, seven people read the weekly portion, and after the concluding aliyah say Half Kaddish. From the second, the maftir reads the day's offering from the section of the tribal leaders and says Half Kaddish. Read the Haftarah beginning 'Sing and rejoice' (Zechariah 2). If Hanukkah contains two Sabbaths, on the second Sabbath read the Haftarah beginning 'And Hiram made' up to 'for the golden sanctuary' (1 Kings 7). Continue with the usual Sabbath service, adding Al HaNissim in thanksgiving during Mussaf.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Shabbat, Rosh Chodesh, and Hanukkah.

Pray as on other Sabbaths, adding Ya'aleh VeYavo to the Avodah blessing and Al HaNissim to thanksgiving, and complete Hallel. Say Kaddish Titkabbal and take out three Torah scrolls. From the first, six people read the weekly portion, without Kaddish afterward. From the second scroll, the seventh reader reads the Rosh Chodesh section beginning 'And on the Sabbath day'; say Half Kaddish. Read the Haftarah 'Sing and rejoice,' adding the first and final verses of the Shabbat Rosh Chodesh Haftarah, 'Thus says the Lord: Heaven is My throne.' Continue the usual Sabbath prayers. Pray the Mussaf for Shabbat and Rosh Chodesh, adding Al HaNissim in thanksgiving, and conclude as on other Sabbaths.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Purim.
Shabbat Zachor.
On Shabbat Zachor, before taking out the Torah scroll, it is customary to recite the piyyut 'Mi Kamocha.' Some recite it after the Torah reading (see Kaf HaChayim, section 68).
Who is like You? There is none like You. Who resembles You? No one resembles You.
In alphabetical order.
Master, may Your lovingkindness never cease; Your truth is a strong fortress and tower, for You have been a refuge to the poor, a refuge to the needy in distress.
In the days of my youth, long ago, the spirit of the LORD spoke within me; and today, though my sins have driven me away, my Beloved is mine and I am His.
He has bestowed goodness upon me from of old, evident and known to hearts. Even when troubles draw near, happy are all who wait for Him.
I will scatter the blood of those who rise against me and raise my banner as the seers foretold: Behold, this is our God; we waited for Him.
Today I shall utter ancient riddles of things foretold; wondrous is He who understands hidden secrets, my Creator, who formed me in the womb to be His servant.
And it came to pass in the days of Ahasuerus: a king rose up like a towering cypress, exalted above every prince and chief, and the LORD allowed him to reign.
In the third year of his reign, he assembled people to display his magnificence to all his servants; precious stones gleamed in his land, and gold dust was his.
He gave a portion to all the people of Shushan and invited his guests as a bridegroom, in the courtyard of the garden of the palace that he had chosen for his dwelling.
He wished to fulfill the desire and pleasure of each person; no one was forced to drink wine, and everyone asking was given what he lacked.
All the invited guests gathered; Queen Vashti also made a feast for the women, and the women’s feast lasted seven days like that of the men.
When the king’s heart was merry with wine, he ordered the beautiful queen brought before him, but she boldly refused his command and said no.
He asked his counselors, who sat close to him, and Memucan advised him—Haman, destined for calamity, whose heart was filled with wrongdoing.
The decrees issued on his advice, though prescribed by law, concealed a remedy for my people; without those first letters, no remnant would have survived.
He advised gathering all the people to bring every beautiful young woman before the king; whoever pleased him would swiftly become his bride.
A shoot of Jair shone forth and rose like a strong man running his course: before the blow, a flower of healing bloomed, for the LORD set apart one faithful to Him.
With him was faithful, innocent Hadassah, Esther his cousin, bright as the sun; when her father and mother died, Mordecai took her into his care.
She found favor and went forth; Esther was taken to the king’s house by heavenly decree, while Mordecai instructed her as she departed.
She wore righteousness in her royal station. Esther did not reveal her people or her birth, and the king loved her and honored her increasingly, for this came from the LORD.
Mordecai, like a sachet of myrrh, listened carefully to the king’s officers charged with guarding him, and heard that they planned to attack the king.
Esther told the king the matter in Mordecai’s name, and it was written in the book; an inquiry was made and the matter was confirmed before the king.
The two conspirators were hanged on a tree, for Mordecai heard their secret counsel: they had intended to poison the king to bring about his death.
This act of rescue was kept for a later generation and written in the book of remembrance, so that Mordecai might one day receive a reward from the king.
Acrostic: 'I am the young Judah Halevi, son of Rabbi Samuel Halevi.'
After these events, Ahasuerus raised Haman and exalted him above all the officials, giving him towering power.
Mordecai refused to bow to the wicked man, a descendant of Amalek who had sinned from his youth; Haman added rebellion to his sins, and the LORD would not forgive him.
When all the king’s servants bowed to Haman, Mordecai continued walking in his integrity. Haman sought a quarrel against a poor and wandering people, meddling in a dispute not his own.
Haman contrived painful schemes, and in his arrogance he considered it beneath him to strike Mordecai alone; he scorned what would lead to his ruin.
He offered silver and gold without limit, saying in his heart that this was the moment to rejoice, and devised plots from afar to seize what was not his.
He cast the pur, the lot, and saw that Moses, the father of the Torah, had died in Adar. But he forgot that Adar was also the month of his birth; the pains of birth would come upon Haman.
His thoughts counseled him like a lurking bear. He made a request of his master, bearing teeth like a lion and the jaws of a lioness.
“There is a people scattered and estranged; their laws differ from those of others, and they do not keep your laws.” They sow the wind and will reap the whirlwind.
“I have prepared money to bring into your treasury so this detested nation may be destroyed”—the people who would not bow to Baal or kiss him.
“I will bring ten thousand talents of silver into the royal treasury and strike down every soul of the House of Joseph, once and for all.”
The king answered him: “Keep your silver, and take my signet ring upon your hand. Do with this people as seems good to you.” Thus he decreed their end without help.
The royal scribes were summoned and wrote all that Haman instructed; couriers rode out to every people and province bearing the king’s commands.
The order was urgent: to cut down the entire vineyard in a single day, the thirteenth of Adar, and bring the destruction to an end.
Mordecai tore his clothes before God and cried bitterly over the exile of Israel. “Has Israel no children, no one to inherit?”
“The remnant of my people is torn to pieces! Who has given Jacob over to spoilers and Israel to plunderers? Was it not the LORD, against whom we sinned?”
Esther’s attendants told her: “We heard a cry like ostriches in the wilderness, and Mordecai walked in sackcloth. We do not know what has happened to him.”
She sent clothes for him to wear, but in his bitter grief he would not accept them. She sent Hathach to question him and learn what should be done.
Mordecai poured out his heart to Hathach, explained the silver involved, sent a copy of the decree, and charged Esther to go before the king and plead with him.
Esther replied: “Know that anyone who enters without being summoned is sentenced to death, except the one to whom the king extends his golden scepter.”
When the noble one heard Hadassah's words, he cried: 'Alas, there is no escape! I bear the LORD's anger, for I have sinned against Him.'

paragraphs.text: He sent her word: 'Do not imagine you will escape in the royal palace more than all my people. You may perish, but my people, though sold, will find redemption.'

paragraphs.text: From another place He will send His deliverance; He who makes peace in His heights, whose mercies are not exhausted. Therefore I shall hope in Him.

paragraphs.text: She answered him: 'Go, gather all who await redemption, and fast for me three days, night and day. Seek mercy from the awesome and fearsome God; give Him no rest.'

paragraphs.text: On the third day she clothed herself in grace and went; she became very precious in the king's eyes. He offered all that he ruled, all that he possessed.

paragraphs.text: To the fairest among women, a lovely sapling, he said: 'What is your request? Everything is ready.' She answered: 'Let the king and Haman come to the banquet I have prepared for him.'

paragraphs.text: She called them again the next day to a secret gathering. Haman departed that day glad and delighted; he boasted among kings, and princes were his sport.

paragraphs.text: His friends and his wife Zeresh came, and he told them of his honor and dominion. Yet a decree stood against him: woe to one who multiplies what is not his.

paragraphs.text: They advised him to erect a gallows fifty cubits high, to hang upon it the holy man; craftsmen were to prepare it as he desired, and a skillful artisan was sought for him.

God inspected His flock in the morning and drove sleep from the king until he had the records searched. In the Book of Remembrance, as morning came, the LORD recognized those who were His.

paragraphs.text: When he found Mordechai's deed written plainly, he asked what honor and dignity had been bestowed on him. They answered that none had been recorded: what should be done for him?

paragraphs.text: The king brought the matter to Haman's ear: 'What shall be done for a man whom the king desires to honor?' Haman answered and was caught by his own words; a fool's mouth is his ruin.

paragraphs.text: He spoke of royal ornaments and of a prince walking before the honored man. Yet his own thoughts wandered in darkness, and he had no light.
