paragraphs.text: The king replied: 'You have spoken well. Do everything you have said for Mordechai the Jew.' You yourself have pronounced your sentence; this very judgment shall be done to you.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Mordechai returned to his duty, while Haman hurried home. His friends and his wife Zeresh gathered to mourn with him.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: The wise remembered the seed of Jeshurun: 'If Mordechai, before whom you have begun to fall, is of that people, you cannot prevail against him.'
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: While his advisers were still speaking, the king's attendants hurried him away. He did not see that his day was drawing near; the Lord would laugh at him.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Before the wine banquet ended, the king said to the beautiful-eyed queen: 'Ask, for all is as nothing beside your request.' She wept and pleaded with him.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: 'Let my life be granted at my petition, my people at my request, my lord the king, for we were sold to an enemy who is not of my covenant. You have granted the desire of his heart.'
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: 'What more could I desire after this grief? Weapons of battle were set at the gate. Does a lion roar in the forest when he has no prey?'
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: He said to her: 'Who among my men is this? Which of those who would drive you out? What creditor is there to whom I sold you?'
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Quickly she answered: 'It is Haman, this evil man, who has inflicted calamities on a righteous nation.' Woe to the wicked man, for the work of his own hands will be done to him.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: The king was filled with rage and rose to his garden. On returning he saw Haman falling upon the couch; heaven would reveal his guilt, and earth would rise against him.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: One of the attendants revealed his crime: 'Behold, he made a gallows for Mordechai at his house.' The king ordered him hanged on the very gallows he had prepared.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Esther stood to plead for her people, that the letters of wrath and fury be revoked. For the LORD relented from the terrible blow, turned back and healed His people.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: The decree was written that the Jews might stand ready against their enemies, because fear of Mordechai had fallen on the rebels, and peace came to him.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Mordechai gave orders to a people not abandoned, whose Savior is great, steadfast and faithful. He was placed over Haman's household and all that Haman possessed.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: I prepared an altar for my enemies and slaughter for his sons because of the guilt of their murderous father; these are the names of his children:
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Parshandatha, Dalphon, Aspatha, Poratha, Adalia, Aridatha, Parmashta, Arisai, Aridai and Vaizatha were struck down; even a burial place was denied him.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: I took the plunder and cried out, for the desperate pauper's plea had risen; the poor escaped from the mighty one, and the orphan from him who had no helper.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Let this be written for a later generation and remembered by the children of our children. All who recall it shall sing: Happy is the people for whom it is so.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Acrostic: Ani Yehudah.
Eat, friends, drink and rejoice; keep the days of Purim in happiness. Amid your joy remember the poor, and send portions to those who have none prepared.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: The miracles of God have carried me since of old; He brought me through the depths of the sea. Therefore my heart chastens me: Be still before the LORD and wait for Him.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: When Pharaoh pursued me to devour my flock like a lion, the waters of the breakers stood up as a wall, raging as His anger burned.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: The enemy pursued His holy people; the Rock sent His cloud to separate them, to shade their heads and deliver them.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: He led them over dry land and terrified their foes; He separated them from their pursuers and cast the enemy down to the depths, while making a dwelling in the rock for His engraved ones.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: When the sea returned to its strength, Pharaoh and all his multitude drowned. The sea overwhelmed his proud chariots, and he saw that he could not prevail.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: The horsemen fell amid the mighty waters and sank like lead. Those who seek the LORD praised His name and sang to Him with the ten-stringed harp.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: He showed us His wondrous hand, awesome upon the seashore. I will sing to the LORD, for He is greatly exalted; with songs we shall cheer Him.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: The tribes crossed on dry land, and before them went God, awesome in holiness. Then they sang a new song: 'Who is like You among the mighty, O LORD?'
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: The Torah scroll is brought out, and the weekly portion is read; for the maftir, read the passage of Zachor. If “Mi Khamokha” was recited after the Torah reading, then say “Ashrei” and complete the service as on any Shabbat.

Remember what Amalek did to you on the way, as you came out of Egypt! How he encountered you on the way, and he cut off all the weak ones [who were straggling] behind you, when you were weary and exhausted; and he did not fear God. When Adonoy, Your God, will relieve you from all your enemies around you, in the land which Adonoy, your God, gives you as a possession to inherit; you shall eradicate the memory of Amalek from beneath the heavens. Do not forget.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: The month of Nisan.
Order of the Blessing of the Trees.
Before reciting the blessing, it is good to say this 'For the sake of the unification' declaration, cited in Lashon Chachamim, volume one.

For the sake of the unity of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Shekhinah, in awe and love, in love and awe, to unite the letters Yod and Heh with Vav and Heh in perfect unity in the name of all Israel and in the name of all souls, spirits and higher souls bound to the roots of our souls, spirits and higher souls, their garments and those close to them, together with the totality of the worlds of Atzilut, Beriah, Yetzirah and Asiyah and all their individual levels: behold, we are ready to perform the commandment of the blessing instituted by the Sages of blessed memory upon seeing flowering trees. May it be before You, Lord our God and God of our ancestors, as though we had concentrated on every fitting intention and every mystery of this blessing. May it be considered important, accepted and pleasing before You, so that through it every spark of holiness mingled with the vegetable world and every soul, spirit and higher soul passing through incarnations in it may be separated and raised up. And You, God, in Your goodness and great mercy, shine the light of Your face upon them and complete their purification and restoration. Bless them, cleanse them, and always bestow upon them the mercy of Your righteousness.
paragraphs.note: New English working translation reviewed against the Hebrew and available Russian text; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: May it be Your will, Lord our God and God of our ancestors, that through the merit of this blessing we recite, the verse be fulfilled in us: 'See, the scent of my son is like the scent of a field which the Lord has blessed.' May we receive the abundance of the ten blessings, as written: 'May God give you of the dew of heaven' (Wisdom), 'and the richness of the earth' (Understanding), 'and abundance of grain' (Knowledge), 'and wine' (Kindness); 'May peoples serve you' (Strength), 'and nations bow down to you' (Beauty); 'Be lord' (Victory), 'over your brothers' (Splendor), 'and may your mother's sons bow down to you' (Foundation); 'Cursed be those who curse you, and blessed be those who bless you' (Kingship). May the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable before You, Lord, my Rock and my Redeemer.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: And let the graciousness of the Lord our God be upon us; Establish Thou also upon us the work of our hands; Yea, the work of our hands establish Thou it.
paragraphs.note: Exact complete Hebrew passage matched to the bundled Tanakh; no fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who has left nothing lacking in His world, and has created good creatures and good trees for human beings to enjoy.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: After the blessing, this supplication is recited:

May it be Your will, Lord our God and God of our ancestors, to bring us joyfully to our land and plant us within our borders, so that we may observe there the commandments of separating terumah, the tithes, and all the other commandments dependent upon the land You gave our ancestors as an inheritance, the land flowing with milk and honey: 'A land of streams of water, springs and depths flowing from valleys and hills; a land of wheat and barley, vines and fig trees and pomegranates, a land of olive trees and honey,' as You commanded us in Your Torah through Moses Your servant. Lord, for the sake of Your great name, multiply Your mercy upon us and fulfill the promise given through Moses Your servant: 'I shall give your rains in their season, the land shall yield its produce and the trees of the field shall yield their fruit. Your threshing shall reach the vintage and your vintage shall reach the sowing; you shall eat your bread to the full and dwell securely in your land.' Fulfill for us the promise through Your prophet Isaiah: 'On that day the branch of the Lord shall be beautiful and glorious, and the fruit of the land shall be splendid and glorious for the survivors of Israel.' And it says: 'They shall build houses and inhabit them; they shall plant vineyards and eat their fruit.' Fulfill the promise given through Your prophet Amos: 'Behold, days are coming, says the Lord, when the plowman shall overtake the reaper and the treader of grapes the sower; the mountains shall drip sweet wine and all the hills shall melt. I shall restore the fortunes of My people Israel; they shall rebuild desolate cities and inhabit them, plant vineyards and drink their wine, make gardens and eat their fruit.' And fulfill what was promised through Your prophet Ezekiel: 'I shall multiply the fruit of the trees and the produce of the fields, so that you shall no longer bear the reproach of famine among the nations.' And it says: 'On the bank of the river on both sides shall grow every tree for food; their leaves shall not wither and their fruit shall not fail. Every month they shall bear fresh fruit, because the waters flow from the Sanctuary; their fruit shall be for food and their leaves for healing.'
paragraphs.note: New English working translation reviewed against the Hebrew and available Russian text; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Our God and God of our ancestors, merciful King, have compassion on us. You who are good and do good, turn toward us. Return to us in the abundance of Your mercy, for the sake of the ancestors who did Your will. Rebuild Your House as at first, establish Your Sanctuary on its foundation; let us see its rebuilding and rejoice in its restoration. Return Your Presence into it, restore the priests to their service and the Levites to their platforms, their song and their music; restore Israel to their dwellings. There we shall ascend and appear and bow before You on the three pilgrimage occasions each year, as it is written in the Torah: 'Three times a year all your males shall appear before the Lord your God at the place He will choose, at the Festival of Unleavened Bread, at the Festival of Weeks, and at the Festival of Booths. They shall not appear before the Lord empty-handed, but each according to what he can give, according to the blessing of the Lord your God that He has given you.'
paragraphs.note: Reviewed parallel passage from the existing English Siddur.

paragraphs.text: May You, LORD our God, soon reign over all Your works on Mount Zion, the dwelling place of Your glory, and in Jerusalem, Your holy city, as it is written in Your sacred words: 'The LORD shall reign forever, your God, O Zion, from generation to generation. Hallelujah!'
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: A Song of Ascents; of David. I rejoiced when they said unto me: 'Let us go unto the house of the LORD.' Our feet are standing within thy gates, O Jerusalem; Jerusalem, that art builded as a city that is compact together; Whither the tribes went up, even the tribes of the LORD, as a testimony unto Israel, to give thanks unto the name of the LORD. For there were set thrones for judgment, the thrones of the house of David. Pray for the peace of Jerusalem; May they prosper that love thee. Peace be within thy walls, and prosperity within thy palaces. For my brethren and companions' sakes, I will now say: 'Peace be within thee.' For the sake of the house of the LORD our God I will seek thy good.
paragraphs.note: Every colon-delimited fragment matched a unique near-exact complete Tanakh verse; reviewed orthographic/qere alignment only.

paragraphs.text: Then recite Petichat Eliyahu ('Elijah's Discourse'); it is also appropriate to say the prayer for the elevation of departed souls.
Order of study for the month of Nisan.

On the first day of Nisan (in the year 2449 from Creation), the Tabernacle was erected, and the tribal leaders brought their offerings for the dedication of the altar, one leader on each day. Therefore it is customary, beginning on the first of Nisan, to read each day's passage of the tribal leaders, as arranged in the reading order for the dedication. Some also read the passage 'They brought the Tabernacle' and the passage 'On the day Moses finished,' along with Ezekiel chapter 37 and a selection from the Zohar, in the order given here. However, the essential reading is the passage of that day's tribal leader. One who lacks time, or attends a synagogue whose worshippers hurry to work, may say: 'Our help is in the name of the Lord, Maker of heaven and earth'; 'When I proclaim the name of the Lord, ascribe greatness to our God'; 'Moses commanded us the Torah, an inheritance for the congregation of Jacob'; 'Blessed are You, Lord; teach me Your statutes'; and 'Hear, O Israel, the Lord our God, the Lord is One.' Then read the tribal leader's passage and the psalm 'A Song of Ascents of David: I rejoiced,' and recite Kaddish Yehe Shelama. Nothing further is required. Such is also the custom of the holy community of Tunis, may the Most High protect it.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: And they brought the tabernacle unto Moses, the Tent, and all its furniture, its clasps, its boards, its bars, and its pillars, and its sockets; and the covering of rams’skins dyed red, and the covering of sealskins, and the veil of the screen; the ark of the testimony, and the staves thereof, and the ark-cover; the table, all the vessels thereof, and the showbread; the pure candlestick, the lamps thereof, even the lamps to be set in order, and all the vessels thereof, and the oil for the light; and the golden altar, and the anointing oil, and the sweet incense, and the screen for the door of the Tent; the brazen altar, and its grating of brass, its staves, and all its vessels, the laver and its base; the hangings of the court, its pillars, and its sockets, and the screen for the gate of the court, the cords thereof, and the pins thereof, and all the instruments of the service of the tabernacle of the tent of meeting; the plaited garments for ministering in the holy place; the holy garments for Aaron the priest, and the garments of his sons, to minister in the priest’s office. According to all that the LORD commanded Moses, so the children of Israel did all the work. And Moses saw all the work, and, behold, they had done it; as the LORD had commanded, even so had they done it. And Moses blessed them. And the LORD spoke unto Moses, saying: ’On the first day of the first month shalt thou rear up the tabernacle of the tent of meeting. And thou shalt put therein the ark of the testimony, and thou shalt screen the ark with the veil. And thou shalt bring in the table, and set in order the bread that is upon it; and thou shalt bring in the candlestick, and light the lamps thereof. And thou shalt set the golden altar for incense before the ark of the testimony, and put the screen of the door to the tabernacle. And thou shalt set the altar of burnt-offering before the door of the tabernacle of the tent of meeting. And thou shalt set the laver between the tent of meeting and the altar, and shalt put water therein. And thou shalt set up the court round about, and hang up the screen of the gate of the court. And thou shalt take the anointing oil, and anoint the tabernacle, and all that is therein, and shalt hallow it, and all the furniture thereof; and it shall be holy. And thou shalt anoint the altar of burnt-offering, and all its vessels, and sanctify the altar; and the altar shall be most holy. And thou shalt anoint the laver and its base, and sanctify it. And thou shalt bring Aaron and his sons unto the door of the tent of meeting, and shalt wash them with water. And thou shalt put upon Aaron the holy garments; and thou shalt anoint him, and sanctify him, that he may minister unto Me in the priest’s office. And thou shalt bring his sons, and put tunics upon them. And thou shalt anoint them, as thou didst anoint their father, that they may minister unto Me in the priest’s office; and their anointing shall be to them for an everlasting priesthood throughout their generations.’ Thus did Moses; according to all that the LORD commanded him, so did he. And it came to pass in the first month in the second year, on the first day of the month, that the tabernacle was reared up. And Moses reared up the tabernacle, and laid its sockets, and set up the boards thereof, and put in the bars thereof, and reared up its pillars. And he spread the tent over the tabernacle, and put the covering of the tent above upon it; as the LORD commanded Moses. And he took and put the testimony into the ark, and set the staves on the ark, and put the ark-cover above upon the ark. And he brought the ark into the tabernacle, and set up the veil of the screen, and screened the ark of the testimony; as the LORD commanded Moses. And he put the table in the tent of meeting, upon the side of the tabernacle northward, without the veil. And he set a row of bread in order upon it before the LORD; as the LORD commanded Moses. And he put the candlestick in the tent of meeting, over against the table, on the side of the tabernacle southward. And he lighted the lamps before the LORD; as the LORD commanded Moses. And he put the golden altar in the tent of meeting before the veil; and he burnt thereon incense of sweet spices; as the LORD commanded Moses. And he put the screen of the door to the tabernacle. And the altar of burnt-offering he set at the door of the tabernacle of the tent of meeting, and offered upon it the burnt-offering and the meal-offering; as the LORD commanded Moses. And he set the laver between the tent of meeting and the altar, and put water therein, wherewith to wash; that Moses and Aaron and his sons might wash their hands and their feet thereat; when they went into the tent of meeting, and when they came near unto the altar, they should wash; as the LORD commanded Moses. And he reared up the court round about the tabernacle and the altar, and set up the screen of the gate of the court. So Moses finished the work. Then the cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle. And Moses was not able to enter into the tent of meeting, because the cloud abode thereon, and the glory of the LORD filled the tabernacle.— And whenever the cloud was taken up from over the tabernacle, the children of Israel went onward, throughout all their journeys. But if the cloud was not taken up, then they journeyed not till the day that it was taken up. For the cloud of the LORD was upon the tabernacle by day, and there was fire therein by night, in the sight of all the house of Israel, throughout all their journeys.— [Translator’s note: The Hebrew source marks a pronunciation detail in the final verse.]

The LORD spoke to Moses, saying: Speak to Aaron and his sons, saying: Thus shall you bless the children of Israel; say to them: 'May the LORD bless you and protect you. May the LORD shine His face upon you and be gracious to you. May the LORD lift His face toward you and grant you peace.' Thus they shall place My name upon the children of Israel, and I shall bless them.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: And it came to pass on the day that Moses had made an end of setting up the tabernacle, and had anointed it and sanctified it, and all the furniture thereof, and the altar and all the vessels thereof, and had anointed them and sanctified them; that the princes of Israel, the heads of their fathers’houses, offered—these were the princes of the tribes, these are they that were over them that were numbered. And they brought their offering before the LORD, six covered wagons, and twelve oxen: a wagon for every two of the princes, and for each one an ox; and they presented them before the tabernacle. And the LORD spoke unto Moses, saying: ’Take it of them, that they may be to do the service of the tent of meeting; and thou shalt give them unto the Levites, to every man according to his service.’ And Moses took the wagons and the oxen, and gave them unto the Levites. Two wagons and four oxen he gave unto the sons of Gershon, according to their service. And four wagons and eight oxen he gave unto the sons of Merari, according unto their service, under the hand of Ithamar the son of Aaron the priest. But unto the sons of Kohath he gave none, because the service of the holy things belonged unto them: they bore them upon their shoulders. And the princes brought the dedication-offering of the altar in the day that it was anointed, even the princes brought their offering before the altar. And the LORD said unto Moses: ‘They shall present their offering each prince on his day, for the dedication of the altar.’
paragraphs.note: Exact complete Hebrew passage matched to the bundled Tanakh; no fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: And he that presented his offering the first day was Nahshon the son of Amminadab, of the tribe of Judah; and his offering was one silver dish, the weight thereof was a hundred and thirty shekels, one silver basin of seventy shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary; both of them full of fine flour mingled with oil for a meal-offering; one golden pan of ten shekels, full of incense; one young bullock, one ram, one he-lamb of the first year, for a burnt-offering; one male of the goats for a sin-offering; and for the sacrifice of peace-offerings, two oxen, five rams, five he-goats, five he-lambs of the first year. This was the offering of Nahshon the son of Amminadab.
paragraphs.note: Exact complete Hebrew passage matched to the bundled Tanakh; no fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: Some have the custom to add this supplication:

May it be Your will, Lord our God and God of our ancestors, that our reading from the Torah of the offering of the tribal leader Nahshon son of Amminadab of the tribe of Judah, corresponding to kingship, offered for the dedication of Your holy altar, be reckoned before You as pleasing and accepted, as though we had attained all the mysteries and sacred names arising from the initial and final letters of these holy verses, thus fulfilling the offering of our lips in place of bulls. May all the sparks of holiness and all the sacred lights contained in the sanctity of this tribe illuminate us and all our brothers and sisters of the house of Israel. May we be clothed in the holiness of this tribe, gaining understanding and discernment in Your Torah and reverence of You—the reverence of Your exalted greatness—so that we, our children and our children's children may do Your will as You desire, all the days of our lives.
paragraphs.note: Complete tribal offering prayer: common Hebrew clauses translated, tribal and kabbalistic names checked individually; independent proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: As in this month You delivered Your people, the tribes of Your inheritance, from Egypt's iron furnace, and lovingly remembered the names of their ancestral tribes for glory, honor and splendor, through the wonders, redemption, mighty deeds and salvation You performed for them, so now, Lord our God and God of our ancestors, look mercifully upon Your flock. Remember Your ancient love for the tribes of God amid this painful exile, and the tribulations and suffering of the tribe of Judah. As in the exodus from Egypt, when in Judah's merit they gave thanks to the Lord for His mercy, so may we thank You, Lord our God, for our deliverance and redemption of our souls through the merit of Judah, ruler among his brothers. May the scepter never depart from Judah nor the lawgiver from among his descendants; his seed shall endure forever and his throne shall stand like the sun before You. May our eyes behold the King in His beauty and our hearts rejoice. Reign soon, Lord our God, over all Your works on Mount Zion, the dwelling of Your glory, and in Jerusalem, the city of Your Temple, as it is written in Your holy words: 'The Lord will reign forever, your God, Zion, from generation to generation. Hallelujah!' And it is said: 'For the kingdom is the Lord's, and He rules over the nations.' 'Deliverers shall ascend Mount Zion to judge Mount Esau, and the kingdom shall be the Lord's.' 'The Lord shall be King over all the earth; on that day the Lord shall be One and His name One.' May the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable before You, Lord, my rock and my redeemer. Accept our prayer and hear our cry, You who know what is hidden.
paragraphs.note: New English working translation reviewed against the Hebrew and available Russian text; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Ezekiel chapter 37.

And the word of the LORD came unto me, saying: ’And thou, son of man, take thee one stick, and write upon it: For Judah, and for the children of Israel his companions; then take another stick, and write upon it: For Joseph, the stick of Ephraim, and of all the house of Israel his companions; and join them for thee one to another into one stick, that they may become one in thy hand. And when the children of thy people shall speak unto thee, saying: Wilt thou not tell us what thou meanest by these? say into them: Thus saith the Lord GOD: Behold, I will take the stick of Joseph, which is in the hand of Ephraim, and the tribes of Israel his companions; and I will put them unto him together with the stick of Judah, and make them one stick, and they shall be one in My hand. And the sticks whereon thou writest shall be in thy hand before their eyes. And say unto them: Thus saith the Lord GOD: Behold, I will take the children of Israel from among the nations, whither they are gone, and will gather them on every side, and bring them into their own land; and I will make them one nation in the land, upon the mountains of Israel, and one king shall be king to them all; and they shall be no more two nations, neither shall they be divided into two kingdoms any more at all; neither shall they defile themselves any more with their idols, nor with their detestable things, nor with any of their transgressions; but I will save them out of all their dwelling-places, wherein they have sinned, and will cleanse them; so shall they be My people, and I will be their God. And My servant David shall be king over them, and they all shall have one shepherd; they shall also walk in Mine ordinances, and observe My statutes, and do them. And they shall dwell in the land that I have given unto Jacob My servant, wherein your fathers dwelt; and they shall dwell therein, they, and their children, and their children’s children, for ever; and David My servant shall be their prince for ever. Moreover I will make a covenant of peace with them—it shall be an everlasting covenant with them; and I will establish them, and multiply them, and will set My sanctuary in the midst of them for ever. My dwelling-place also shall be over them; and I will be their God, and they shall be My people. And the nations shall know that I am the LORD that sanctify Israel, when My sanctuary shall be in the midst of them for ever.’

A Song of Ascents; of David. I rejoiced when they said unto me: 'Let us go unto the house of the LORD.' Our feet are standing within thy gates, O Jerusalem; Jerusalem, that art builded as a city that is compact together; Whither the tribes went up, even the tribes of the LORD, as a testimony unto Israel, to give thanks unto the name of the LORD. For there were set thrones for judgment, the thrones of the house of David. Pray for the peace of Jerusalem; May they prosper that love thee. Peace be within thy walls, and prosperity within thy palaces. For my brethren and companions' sakes, I will now say: 'Peace be within thee.' For the sake of the house of the LORD our God I will seek thy good.
paragraphs.note: Exact complete Hebrew passage matched to the bundled Tanakh; no fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: Zohar, Bamidbar, folio 118b.

Each person beneath his banner with his signs: These are the four camps of the Congregation of Israel, the twelve tribes, twelve divisions surrounding Her. Everything corresponds to the pattern above, as it is written: 'There the tribes went up, the tribes of the LORD.' 'There the tribes went up'—these are the twelve tribes, the twelve divisions below.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: 'The tribes of the Lord': it has already been explained that the name Yah is indeed a testimony for Israel. Thus, in the names 'the Reubenite' and 'the Simeonite' the letters of Yah are present. And this is truly so: the supernal holy Tree stamped them with its seals. They explained the verse: 'The likeness of their faces was a human face, and a lion's face on the right,' and so forth. The human likeness is included in all their images. Their faces turn toward the four directions of the world and differ in appearance, yet all are included in the human image.
paragraphs.note: New English working translation reviewed against the Hebrew and available Russian text; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Michael is on the right, Gabriel on the left, Uriel before them and Raphael behind; the Divine Presence is above them. Two are on this side and two on that, with Her in the center. In the same way on the earth below, two on this side and two on that, with the Divine Name between them.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: When two banners set forth on their journey, what is written? 'Then the Tent of Meeting shall set forward, the camp of the Levites,' and so on, followed by the two remaining camps. The four camps correspond to the four quarters of the world and together comprise twelve. Thus everything below follows the pattern of what is above. 'The standard of the camp of Judah shall set forward first': opposite the camp of Uriel. The camp of Reuben is opposite the camp of Michael; one stands to the south and the other to the east. So too the altar has a southeastern corner. The camp of Dan is to the north and the camp of Ephraim toward the sea. The camp of Dan corresponds to Gabriel's camp, and Ephraim's camp in the west to Raphael's camp. So too the altar has a northwestern corner. Everything is joined to everything else until all rise and unite in the holy Name, the beginning of everything, above everything, holier than everything; all is contained in it. Yod is east, the beginning of light; it moves, spreads out and brings forth the south, and the south emerges and depends on the eastern beginning. Heh is south, from which south proceeds into the world. Yod enters the beginning of the east and brings it forth.
paragraphs.note: New English working translation reviewed against the Hebrew and available Russian text; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: From the letter heh depend south and north and that which is between them. Yod is the east; south and north depend upon Yah. Vav is in the middle, and this is the male child, for he stands between north and south. This is what we learned: one who places his bed between north and south is blessed with sons, because that male child is situated between north and south. North and south depend upon the upper heh, and the son between them is the mystery of the union Yod–Vav–Heh. The final heh signifies the west.
paragraphs.note: New English working translation reviewed against the Hebrew and available Russian text; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Therefore the south is joined to the east, where the sun begins its course, and depends upon it. Thus we have learned: from the side of the Father comes the highest lovingkindness, and from the side of the Mother comes might. In this way, everything is joined together.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: The corners of the altar also turn in this order: one approaches the southeastern corner, for the south draws strength from the east, the beginning of the sun. The sun's power rests at its rising. Then the northeastern corner: when the south takes strength from the east, it illuminates the north, and north is included in south, for the left is included in the right.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: 'Northwest': the west, corresponding to the final heh of the divine Name, draws strength from the north; hence north turns toward west. 'Southwest': the west moves to unite with the south, just as the south is joined to the east and its power is revealed at the beginning. Thus the west longs to be united with the south, as it is said: 'His right hand embraces me.' That right hand is the south. The west, therefore, receives nourishment from two sides, north and south. Of this it is written: 'His left hand is beneath my head, and his right hand embraces me.' The left hand is north; the right hand is south.
paragraphs.note: New English working translation reviewed against the Hebrew and available Russian text; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: We have learned this secret: the Holy One, blessed be He, placed His bed between north and south and united it with that Son. Therefore human beings too should set their beds between north and south. Thus my father taught me: sons will then be granted them, because a person directs himself toward complete supernal faith and the perfection of everything—to the Holy One, blessed be He, who dwells between north and south, and to the Assembly of Israel whose light shines between north and south. Then sons will surely be born to him.
paragraphs.note: New English working translation reviewed against the Hebrew and available Russian text; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: In every action one must show a pattern corresponding to what is above: as an action is performed below, so it awakens a response above, as the sages explained. Rabbi Pinchas heard this, kissed Rabbi Elazar, wept and smiled, and said: 'Fortunate is my portion in this world and in the world to come.'
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Then, each day, recite this prayer after the passage about the tribal leader, for the elevation of departed souls:

May it be Your will, Lord our God and God of our ancestors, that today You illuminate with the radiance of Your abundant compassion the holy souls standing in the three rows of Eden. Their voices are like the singing of birds; with their whole being they praise God and extol the greatness of Your glorious name, our King. They seek for us, Your beloved children, a crown of life and peace. We implore You, for the great power of Your mercy, incline Your ear to them and graciously receive their prayer, to turn away from us and from all the house of Israel every burning anger, destroyer and calamity. Prolong our days in goodness and our years in joy. Grant a life of peace, a life of tranquility, a life of grace, a life of blessing, a life with honorable sustenance, a life of renewed strength, a life of reverence for sin, a life free of shame and humiliation, a life of abundance and honor with which to serve You, and a life of love for the Torah for its own sake. May all the good desires of our hearts be fulfilled.
paragraphs.note: New English working translation reviewed against the Hebrew and available Russian text; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: May Your compassion rest upon these holy souls, and may a favorable remembrance of them rise, come, reach, appear, be accepted, be heard, be recalled and be preserved before the throne of Your glory. May they find rest, and may their souls be bound in the Holy of Holies, in the place no eye has seen except Yours, O God. Satisfy their souls with the goodness of heaven; let them drink from the abundance of Your house and let them drink of the river of Your delights. Grant us a portion with them, that we may merit life, goodness and blessing in the world to come. As for the souls that are cast off and wander in the air of the world, those who died before their time and have not yet been placed under the care of Dumah, and those concealed in the earth who must grow again like grass but have not yet found rest: You, God who mercifully illumines the earth and its inhabitants, shine the light of Your face upon them, cover their sins and transgressions, and command the angel appointed over them to lighten the weight of their judgment, sentence and suffering. May the Lord grant them true rest, each in their appointed place, in peace, quiet and safety forever. May they dwell in the shadow of the Almighty beneath the wings of the cherubim, ascending from level to level and height to height. And to one who has no merit with which to ascend, grant grace as an unearned gift, as it is said: 'I will make all My goodness pass before you and proclaim the name of the Lord before you; I will be gracious to whom I will be gracious, and show mercy to whom I will show mercy.' 'May the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be pleasing before You, Lord, my rock and my redeemer.'

paragraphs.text: On the second day of the month of Nisan.

On the second day Nethanel the son of Zuar, prince of Issachar, did offer: he presented for his offering one silver dish, the weight thereof was a hundred and thirty shekels, one silver basin of seventy shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary; both of them full of fine flour mingled with oil for a meal-offering; one golden pan of ten shekels, full of incense; one young bullock, one ram, one he-lamb of the first year, for a burnt-offering; one male of the goats for a sin-offering; and for the sacrifice of peace-offerings, two oxen, five rams, five he-goats, five he-lambs of the first year. This was the offering of Nethanel the son of Zuar.
paragraphs.note: Exact complete Hebrew passage matched to the bundled Tanakh; no fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: Some also recite each day 'And the word came ...', 'A Song of Ascents ...', and the Zohar passage, as printed above for the first day of Nissan.
Some have the custom to add this supplication:

May it be Your will, Lord our God and God of our ancestors, that our reading from the Torah of the offering of the tribal leader Nethanel son of Zuar of the tribe of Issachar, corresponding to the endurance aspect of kingship, offered for the dedication of Your holy altar, be reckoned before You as pleasing and accepted, as though we had attained all the mysteries and sacred names arising from the initial and final letters of these holy verses, thus fulfilling the offering of our lips in place of bulls. May all the sparks of holiness and all the sacred lights contained in the sanctity of this tribe illuminate us and all our brothers and sisters of the house of Israel. May we be clothed in the holiness of this tribe, gaining understanding and discernment in Your Torah and reverence of You—the reverence of Your exalted greatness—so that we, our children and our children's children may do Your will as You desire, all the days of our lives.
paragraphs.note: Complete tribal offering prayer: common Hebrew clauses translated, tribal and kabbalistic names checked individually; independent proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: As in this month You delivered Your people, the tribes of Your inheritance, from Egypt's iron furnace and lovingly remembered the names of their fathers' tribes for glory and honor through the wonders, redemption, might and salvation You did for them, so now, Lord our God and God of our ancestors, mercifully remember Your flock and Your ancient love for the tribes of God amid this harsh exile. Just as You multiplied the reward of our ancestors in those days through the merit of Issachar and 'afterward they went out with great possessions,' so, Lord, grant a good reward to Your afflicted and dispersed people in this present exile, to all who sincerely hope in Your name. May we never be ashamed, for we trust in You and await Your salvation every day, through the merit and blessing of Issachar: 'He saw that rest was good and the land pleasant.' 'Look upon Zion, the city of our appointed feasts; your eyes shall see Jerusalem, a peaceful dwelling, a tent whose stakes shall never be pulled up and none of whose cords shall be broken.' 'Lord of Hosts, cause Your face to shine, and we shall be saved!' 'Bless them, purify them; always grant them the mercy of Your righteousness.' May the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable before You, Lord, my rock and my redeemer. After this one recites the prayer for the elevation of souls.

paragraphs.text: As You redeemed our ancestors from Egypt and caused Your Presence to dwell among them in the House of Your habitation through the merit of Zebulun, so now, Lord our God and God of our ancestors, remember the congregation You acquired of old amid this bitter, fleeting exile. Through Zebulun's merit return Your Shekhinah to the House of Your glorious dwelling. Dwell in Jerusalem, Your city, as You promised, and speedily establish there the throne of David. Tend this vine that suffers daily and show us Your greatness for good. 'Save us, Lord our God, and gather us from among the nations, that we may give thanks to Your holy name and glory in Your praise.' Fulfill for Your servants Zebulun's blessing: 'They shall call peoples to the mountain; there they shall offer sacrifices of righteousness, for they shall draw upon the abundance of the seas and treasures hidden in the sand.' 'The Lord of Hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our refuge. Selah.' 'Mighty and Holy One, in Your abundant goodness guide Your congregation.' May the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable before You, Lord, my rock and my redeemer. After this one recites the prayer for the elevation of souls.

paragraphs.text: Just as in those days You saw in Egypt the affliction of Your people Israel, the sheep of Your pasture, through the merit of Reuben, so now, Lord our God and God of our ancestors, look upon and see our humiliation in this bitter exile. Through Reuben's merit behold our troubles, defend us, and swiftly grant us complete redemption. 'We implore You, by the power of the greatness of Your right hand, release those who are bound.' 'Rise to our aid and redeem us for Your kindness' sake.' 'Make wondrous Your lovingkindnesses, Savior of those who seek refuge in Your right hand from those who rise against them.' 'Let Your mercy, Lord, rest upon us, as we have hoped in You.' 'May the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable before You, Lord, my rock and my redeemer.' After this one recites the prayer for the elevation of the souls of the departed.

paragraphs.text: As You heard the groaning of the children of Israel, Your people, in Egypt in those days and at that time through the merit of Simeon, so now, Lord our God and God of our ancestors, visit us with salvation and mercy in this bitter and heavy exile. Through Simeon's merit accept Your people's song; strengthen and purify us, O Awesome One! Hear our voice and graciously receive the prayer of those groaning from the pit of exile and the land of captivity. God, look upon us: our honor is brought low among the nations, who detest us as something impure. How long shall Your strength be in captivity and Your glory in the enemy's hands? May they see and be ashamed, and tremble at their own powerlessness. Awaken Your might and save us for Your name's sake. 'The Lord shall go forth like a mighty man; like a warrior He shall stir His zeal; He shall cry out and raise the battle shout, and show Himself strong against His enemies.' 'May the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable before You, Lord, my rock and my redeemer.' Then the prayer for the elevation of the souls of the departed is recited.

paragraphs.text: As at the exodus of Israel from Egypt You brought down manna for them from the heights of heaven, like coriander seed—gad—through the merit of the tribe of Gad, so now, Lord our God and God of our ancestors, Mighty and Holy One, in Your abundant goodness guide Your congregation through this harsh exile. Open for us the treasuries of the supernal white dew from the two mazalot, Notzer and Nakeh, through the palate and throat to Abba and Imma, from Abba and Imma to Zeir Anpin, and from him to the field of holy apples. From there comes supernal nourishment, from the millstones which grind manna for the righteous. Sustain the whole world with Your goodness; send dew and rain as a blessing for the whole earth from the heavenly abundance of dew and from the deep that lies below. Through the merit of Gad, linked to the level of the five hod powers of Your Malkhut, 'Be as dew to Israel; he shall blossom like a lily, strike his roots like Lebanon, spread out his branches, and his beauty shall be as the olive tree, and his scent like Lebanon.' May our king be exalted by Your salvation; may the strength of the Messiah, son of David Your servant, be exalted, and grant him Your glory. 'Great is his honor through Your salvation; majesty and splendor You have laid upon him.' May the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable before You, Lord, my rock and my redeemer. After this one recites the prayer for the elevation of souls.

paragraphs.text: Some have the custom to add this supplication:

May it be Your will, Lord our God and God of our ancestors, that our reading in the Torah describing the offering of the prince Elishama son of Ammihud of the tribe of Ephraim, associated with the crown of Yesod of Zeir Anpin, which he brought for the dedication of Your holy altar, may be worthy and accepted. May it be counted for us as though we had understood all the mysteries and all the holy Names arising from the first and last letters of the sacred verses, and as though we had offered You the fruit of our lips instead of bulls. May all sparks of holiness and holy lights belonging to this tribe shine upon us and upon all our brothers of the house of Israel. May we be clothed in the holiness of this tribe, so as to understand and grasp Your Torah, to experience reverent awe of Your majesty and fulfill Your will all the days of our life—we, our children and our descendants. 'One, exalted, turn toward Your people who remember Your holiness.' 'Before Ephraim, Benjamin and Manasseh, stir up Your strength and come to save us.' Speedily establish in Jerusalem the royal throne of the Messiah, son of Ephraim. May no calamity or sorrow accompany our redemption; may the Messiah son of Ephraim, who is to begin comforting us and raise our banner over the nations, not fall by the hand of the wicked Armilus. 'He asked You for life, and You gave him length of days forever and ever.' And may the blessing be fulfilled: 'His firstborn bull has majesty, his horns are the horns of the wild ox; with them he shall gore the peoples together to the ends of the earth. These are the ten thousands of Ephraim and the thousands of Manasseh.'

paragraphs.text: Through the merit of Ephraim, whose seal is in the crown of Yesod of Zeir Anpin, remember, Lord, the children of Edom on the day of Jerusalem, when they said: 'Raze it, raze it to its very foundation!' Cut off every horn of the wicked, and may the horn of the righteous be raised. 'For You bless the righteous, Lord; You surround him with favor as with a shield.' 'You will arise and have mercy upon Zion, for the time to favor her has come, the appointed time has come.' May the One who redeemed our ancestors at Israel's exodus from Egypt return to redeem their children. 'Let Israel rejoice in his Maker; let the children of Zion be glad in their King.' 'The envy of Ephraim shall cease, and those who harass Judah shall be cut off; Ephraim shall not envy Judah, and Judah shall not oppress Ephraim.' 'May the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable before You, Lord, my rock and my redeemer.' Afterward the prayer for the elevation of the souls of the departed is recited.

paragraphs.text: As You caused Israel to forget all its burdens and removed the load from its shoulders in Egypt in those days and at that time through the merit of Manasseh, so now, Lord our God and God of our ancestors, do not forget us in this harsh exile. Look upon Your great people; do not become to them like a creditor in a land of forgetfulness; bring my soul out of prison to give thanks to Your name. Thus we hope in You, Lord our God, to behold soon the splendor of Your might when You remove the idols from the earth and the false gods utterly vanish, so as to perfect the world under the kingdom of the Almighty. 'Let Mount Zion rejoice and the daughters of Judah be glad because of Your judgments.' 'Of Zion it shall be said: This and that man was born in her, and the Most High Himself shall establish her.' 'Before Ephraim, Benjamin and Manasseh, stir up Your strength and come to save us.' 'May the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable before You, Lord, my rock and my redeemer.' paragraphs.text: As You exacted vengeance for the children of Israel upon the Egyptians and came out to save Your people with Your great power—'Your right hand, Lord, is glorious in power; Your right hand, Lord, has shattered the enemy,' 'You stretched out Your right hand and the earth swallowed them'—through the merit of righteous Benjamin, so now, Lord our God and God of our ancestors, in this bitter exile, 'May Your hand find all Your enemies; may Your right hand find those who hate You.' 'The right hand of the Lord is lifted high; the right hand of the Lord acts valiantly.' 'Look down from heaven and see; visit this vine planted by Your right hand and the son You made strong for Yourself.' 'Bring them in and plant them on the mountain of Your inheritance, the place You fashioned for Your dwelling, Lord, the Sanctuary which Your hands established,' within Benjamin's inheritance, as it is said: 'Of Benjamin he said: The beloved of the Lord shall dwell securely beside Him; He shelters him all the day long and dwells between his shoulders.' Establish the foundations of Zion, upon which You once poured Your anger and whose foundations the fire consumed. Come forth to save Your people, to deliver Your anointed. 'You have crushed the head of the wicked house, baring its foundation to the neck. Selah.' 'Of Zion it shall be said: This and that man was born in her, and the Most High Himself shall establish her.' 'One, exalted, turn toward Your people who remember Your holiness.' May the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable before You, Lord, my rock and my redeemer. After this the prayer for the elevation of souls is recited.
paragraphs.note: New English working translation reviewed against the Hebrew and available Russian text; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: On the tenth day of the month of Nisan.

On the tenth day Ahiezer the son of Ammishaddai, prince of the children of Dan: his offering was one silver dish, the weight thereof was a hundred and thirty shekels, one silver basin of seventy shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary; both of them full of fine flour mingled with oil for a meal-offering; one golden pan of ten shekels, full of incense; one young bullock, one ram, one he-lamb of the first year, for a burnt-offering; one male of the goats for a sin-offering; and for the sacrifice of peace-offerings, two oxen, five rams, five he-goats, five he-lambs of the first year. This was the offering of Ahiezer the son of Ammishaddai.
paragraphs.note: Exact complete Hebrew passage matched to the bundled Tanakh; no fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: Some have the custom to add this supplication:

May it be Your will, Lord our God and God of our ancestors, that our reading from the Torah of the offering of the tribal leader Ahiezer son of Ammishaddai of the tribe of Dan, corresponding to the lower division of the glory aspect of kingship, offered for the dedication of Your holy altar, be reckoned before You as pleasing and accepted, as though we had attained all the mysteries and sacred names arising from the initial and final letters of these holy verses, thus fulfilling the offering of our lips in place of bulls. May all the sparks of holiness and all the sacred lights contained in the sanctity of this tribe illuminate us and all our brothers and sisters of the house of Israel. May we be clothed in the holiness of this tribe, gaining understanding and discernment in Your Torah and reverence of You—the reverence of Your exalted greatness—so that we, our children and our children's children may do Your will as You desire, all the days of our lives.
paragraphs.note: Complete tribal offering prayer: common Hebrew clauses translated, tribal and kabbalistic names checked individually; independent proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: As You aided Your people Israel in their hour of distress in the land of Egypt, judged their cause and passed righteous judgment through the merit of Dan, so now, Lord our God and God of our ancestors, exalt the strength of the Messiah son of David, Your servant, among whose maternal ancestors were leaders of the tribe of Dan. 'He will judge among the nations among the fallen; He will shatter heads over a wide land.' 'He shall judge the poor with righteousness and decide with fairness for the afflicted of the earth; He shall strike the earth with the rod of his mouth and slay the wicked with the breath of his lips.' 'Rise up, Judge of the earth; render recompense to the proud.' 'To bind their kings with chains and their nobles with fetters of iron, to execute upon them the judgment written.' 'Deliverers shall ascend Mount Zion to judge Mount Esau, and the kingdom shall be the Lord's.' 'There stood thrones of judgment, the thrones of the house of David.' 'The Lord shall cause His majestic voice to be heard and shall display the descent of His arm.' 'Lord God of Hosts, restore us, cause Your face to shine, and we shall be saved!' May the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable before You, Lord, my rock and my redeemer. After this the prayer for the elevation of souls is recited.
paragraphs.note: New English working translation reviewed against the Hebrew and available Russian text; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: On the eleventh day of the month of Nisan.

On the eleventh day Pagiel the son of Ochran, prince of the children of Asher: his offering was one silver dish, the weight thereof was a hundred and thirty shekels, one silver basin of seventy shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary; both of them full of fine flour mingled with oil for a meal-offering; one golden pan of ten shekels, full of incense; one young bullock, one ram, one he-lamb of the first year, for a burnt-offering; one male of the goats for a sin-offering; and for the sacrifice of peace-offerings, two oxen, five rams, five he-goats, five he-lambs of the first year. This was the offering of Pagiel the son of Ochran.
paragraphs.note: Exact complete Hebrew passage matched to the bundled Tanakh; no fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: Some have the custom to add this supplication:

May it be Your will, Lord our God and God of our ancestors, that our reading from the Torah of the offering of the tribal leader Pagiel son of Ochran of the tribe of Asher, corresponding to the heel of the endurance aspect of kingship, offered for the dedication of Your holy altar, be reckoned before You as pleasing and accepted, as though we had attained all the mysteries and sacred names arising from the initial and final letters of these holy verses, thus fulfilling the offering of our lips in place of bulls. May all the sparks of holiness and all the sacred lights contained in the sanctity of this tribe illuminate us and all our brothers and sisters of the house of Israel. May we be clothed in the holiness of this tribe, gaining understanding and discernment in Your Torah and reverence of You—the reverence of Your exalted greatness—so that we, our children and our children's children may do Your will as You desire, all the days of our lives.
paragraphs.note: Complete tribal offering prayer: common Hebrew clauses translated, tribal and kabbalistic names checked individually; independent proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: As You redeemed Your people, the house of Israel, from Egypt's iron furnace in those days and at that time, making Your name glorious to this day, and those who heard called us happy, saying, 'Happy is the people for whom it is thus,' through the merit of Asher, so now, Lord our God and God of our ancestors, bring the end of our exile near and show us a sign for good, a sign of salvation and a token of mercy. May those who hate us see and be ashamed, and our enemies see and be confounded, because You, Lord, have helped and comforted us. 'Then shall they say among the nations, The Lord has done great things for them.' 'Happy are you, Israel! Who is like you, a people saved by the Lord?' 'Happy is the people whose God is the Lord, the nation He has chosen for His inheritance.' May the power of David Your servant increase, and may the lamp of the son of Jesse, Your anointed one, shine soon in our days. May he be blessed upon earth and 'have dominion from sea to sea and from the River to the ends of the earth.' 'Those who dwell in the wilderness shall bow before him, and his enemies shall lick the dust.' 'The kings of Tarshish and the islands shall bring tribute, the kings of Sheba and Seba shall offer gifts.' 'All kings shall bow before him and all nations shall serve him.' 'His name shall endure forever; as long as the sun endures his name shall continue, and all families shall bless themselves by him; all nations shall call him happy.' 'God of Hosts, restore us, cause Your face to shine, and we shall be saved!' May the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable before You, Lord, my rock and my redeemer. Then the prayer for the elevation of souls is recited.
paragraphs.note: New English working translation reviewed against the Hebrew and available Russian text; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: On the twelfth day of the month of Nisan.

On the twelfth day Ahira the son of Enan, prince of the children of Naphtali: his offering was one silver dish, the weight thereof was a hundred and thirty shekels, one silver basin of seventy shekels, after the shekel of the sanctuary; both of them full of fine flour mingled with oil for a meal-offering; one golden pan of ten shekels, full of incense; one young bullock, one ram, one he-lamb of the first year, for a burnt-offering; one male of the goats for a sin-offering; and for the sacrifice of peace-offerings, two oxen, five rams, five he-goats, five he-lambs of the first year. This was the offering of Ahira the son of Enan.
paragraphs.note: Exact complete Hebrew passage matched to the bundled Tanakh; no fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: Some have the custom to add this supplication:

May it be Your will, Lord our God and God of our ancestors, that our reading from the Torah of the offering of the tribal leader Ahira son of Enan of the tribe of Naphtali, corresponding to the lower division of the endurance aspect of kingship, offered for the dedication of Your holy altar, be reckoned before You as pleasing and accepted, as though we had attained all the mysteries and sacred names arising from the initial and final letters of these holy verses, thus fulfilling the offering of our lips in place of bulls. May all the sparks of holiness and all the sacred lights contained in the sanctity of this tribe illuminate us and all our brothers and sisters of the house of Israel. May we be clothed in the holiness of this tribe, gaining understanding and discernment in Your Torah and reverence of You—the reverence of Your exalted greatness—so that we, our children and our children's children may do Your will as You desire, all the days of our lives.
paragraphs.note: Complete tribal offering prayer: common Hebrew clauses translated, tribal and kabbalistic names checked individually; independent proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: As at Israel's exodus from Egypt You chose us from all nations and taught us the Torah and commandments, sweeter than honey and the honeycomb, through the merit of Naphtali, so now, Lord our God and God of our ancestors, sanctify us with Your commandments and give us a share in Your Torah amid this harsh exile, for the Torah shall not be forgotten from the mouths of our descendants. Make, Lord our God and God of our ancestors, the words of Your Torah sweet in our mouths and in the mouths of all Your people, the house of Israel. Give our hearts understanding to know, listen, study and teach, preserve, perform and observe all the words of Your Torah's teaching with love. Enlighten our eyes through its study and open our hearts to understand wisdom—the treasure of salvation, wisdom and knowledge—so that the words of Torah may be like honey upon our lips, sweet to the soul and healing to the body. Look upon Your people and have mercy on Your inheritance. 'A shoot shall come forth from the stock of Jesse, and a branch shall grow from his roots. The spirit of the Lord shall rest upon him, a spirit of wisdom and understanding, counsel and might, knowledge and fear of the Lord.' 'For out of Zion shall go forth Torah, and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.' 'God of Hosts, turn again, look down from heaven and see; visit this vine.' May the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable before You, Lord, my rock and my redeemer. Then the prayer for the elevation of souls is recited.
paragraphs.note: New English working translation reviewed against the Hebrew and available Russian text; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: On the thirteenth day of the month of Nisan.

And the LORD spoke unto Moses, saying: ’Speak unto Aaron, and say unto him: When thou lightest the lamps, the seven lamps shall give light in front of the candlestick.’ And Aaron did so: he lighted the lamps thereof so as to give light in front of the candlestick, as the LORD commanded Moses. And this was the work of the candlestick, beaten work of gold; unto the base thereof, and unto the flowers thereof, it was beaten work; according unto the pattern which the LORD had shown Moses, so he made the candlestick.
paragraphs.note: Exact complete Hebrew passage matched to the bundled Tanakh; no fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: ’Sing and rejoice, O daughter of Zion; for, lo, I come, and I will dwell in the midst of thee, saith the LORD. And many nations shall join themselves to the LORD in that day, and shall be My people, and I will dwell in the midst of thee’; and thou shalt know that the LORD of hosts hath sent me unto thee. And the LORD shall inherit Judah as His portion in the holy land, and shall choose Jerusalem again. Be silent, all flesh, before the LORD; for He is aroused out of His holy habitation.
paragraphs.note: Complete bundled Tanakh passage aligned at 99.73% normalized Hebrew similarity; only orthographic/punctuation variation accepted.

paragraphs.text: And he showed me Joshua the high priest standing before the angel of the LORD, and Satan standing at his right hand to accuse him. And the LORD said unto Satan: ‘The LORD rebuke thee, O Satan, yea, the LORD that hath chosen Jerusalem rebuke thee; is not this man a brand plucked out of the fire?’ Now Joshua was clothed with filthy garments, and stood before the angel. And he answered and spoke unto those that stood before him, saying: ‘Take the filthy garments from off him.’ And unto him he said: ‘Behold, I cause thine iniquity to pass from thee, and I will clothe thee with robes.’ And I said: ‘Let them set a fair mitre upon his head.’ So they set a fair mitre upon his head, and clothed him with garments; and the angel of the LORD stood by. And the angel of the LORD forewarned Joshua, saying: ’Thus saith the LORD of hosts: If thou wilt walk in My ways, and if thou wilt keep My charge, and wilt also judge My house, and wilt also keep My courts, then I will give thee free access among these that stand by. Hear now, O Joshua the high priest, thou and thy fellows that sit before thee; for they are men that are a sign; for, behold, I will bring forth My servant the Shoot. For behold the stone that I have laid before Joshua; upon one stone are seven facets; behold, I will engrave the graving thereof, saith the LORD of hosts: And I will remove the iniquity of that land in one day. In that day, saith the LORD of hosts, shall ye call every man his neighbour under the vine and under the fig-tree. And the angel that spoke with me returned, and waked me, as a man that is wakened out of his sleep. And he said unto me: ‘What seest thou?’ And I said: ‘I have seen, and behold a candlestick all of gold, with a bowl upon the top of it, and its seven lamps thereon; there are seven pipes, yea, seven, to the lamps, which are upon the top thereof; and two olive-trees by it, one upon the right side of the bowl, and the other upon the left side thereof.’ And I answered and spoke to the angel that spoke with me, saying: ‘What are these, my lord?’ Then the angel that spoke with me answered and said unto me: ‘Knowest thou not what these are?’ And I said: ‘No, my lord.’ Then he answered and spoke unto me, saying: ‘This is the word of the LORD unto Zerubbabel, saying: Not by might, nor by power, but by My spirit, saith the LORD of hosts. Who art thou, O great mountain before Zerubbabel? thou shalt become a plain; and he shall bring forth the top stone with shoutings of Grace, grace, unto it.’

May it be Your will, Lord our God and God of our ancestors, that our reading from the Torah of the section of the lamps, which You lovingly granted to Aaron, Your holy servant, prince of the tribe of Levi, corresponding to the beauty aspect of kingship, be reckoned before You as pleasing and accepted, as though we had attained all the mysteries and sacred names arising from the initial and final letters of these holy verses, thus fulfilling the offering of our lips in place of bulls. May all the sparks of holiness and all the sacred lights contained in the sanctity of this tribe illuminate us and all our brothers and sisters of the house of Israel. May we be clothed in the holiness of this tribe, gaining understanding and discernment in Your Torah and reverence of You—the reverence of Your exalted greatness—so that we, our children and our children's children may do Your will as You desire, all the days of our lives.
paragraphs.note: Complete tribal offering prayer: common Hebrew clauses translated, tribal and kabbalistic names checked individually; independent proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: As You saw the affliction of Your people, the flock of Your pasture, in Egypt's iron furnace and were with them through all their troubles in the burning bush through the merit of Levi, so now, Lord our God and God of our ancestors, 'I Am Who I Am': we implore You, Mighty One, guard those who strive for unity with You like the apple of Your eye amid this harsh exile. By Your abundant goodness may the flame of Your anger turn away from Your people, Your city, Your land and Your inheritance. Fulfill for us the promise given through Moses Your servant: 'I Am Who I Am,' help in times of trouble. And it is said: 'Yet for all that, when they are in the land of their enemies, I will not reject or abhor them to destroy them utterly and to break My covenant with them; for I am the Lord their God.' And it is said: 'In all their affliction He was afflicted; the angel of His presence saved them. In His love and pity He redeemed them; He lifted them and carried them all the days of old.' Return the priests to their service, the Levites to their song, and Israel to its place of prayerful standing, that they may join themselves to You and serve You.
paragraphs.note: New English working translation reviewed against the Hebrew and available Russian text; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Therefore we hope in You, Lord our God, that we may soon behold the beauty of Your strength. As it is said: 'She will place upon your head a graceful garland; she will bestow upon you a beautiful crown.' 'Awake, awake, put on your beautiful garments, Jerusalem, holy city'; and 'you shall be a crown of beauty in the hand of the Lord, and a royal diadem in the palm of your God.' For Your people, the house of Israel, fulfill Your word: 'He will set you high above all the nations that He has made, for praise, fame and glory.' For You are the glory of their strength, and by Your favor our horn shall be exalted. May the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable before You, Lord, my Rock and my Redeemer.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Various blessings and prayers.
Order of betrothal and marriage.
With your permission, masters. They answer: To life!
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Blessed are You, Adonoy our God, King of the Universe, Creator of the fruit of the vine.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who sanctified us through His commandments and commanded us concerning forbidden unions. He prohibited to us women merely betrothed, and permitted to us our wives through the marriage canopy and kiddushin. Blessed are You, LORD, who sanctifies His people Israel through the marriage canopy and kiddushin.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: The person reciting the blessing drinks, followed by the groom and the bride.
Before placing the ring on the bride's finger, the groom says:
Behold, you are consecrated to me by this ring (if betrothing with money say 'by this') in accordance with the law of Moses and Israel.
Order of the Seven Wedding Blessings.
With your permission, masters. They answer: To life!
paragraphs.note: Reviewed project translation added in Siddur coverage pass 4.

paragraphs.text: Blessed are You, Adonoy our God, King of the Universe, Creator of the fruit of the vine.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who created everything for His glory.
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who fashions humankind.

Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who created humankind in His image, in the image of His likeness and form, and fashioned from him an everlasting structure. Blessed are You, LORD, Creator of humankind.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Let the barren one rejoice and exult as her children are speedily gathered back to her in joy. Blessed are You, LORD, who gladdens Zion with her children.
Bring great joy to the beloved companions as You gladdened Your creature in the Garden of Eden in ancient times. Blessed are You, LORD, who gladdens the groom and bride.

Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the universe, who created joy and gladness, groom and bride, rejoicing, song, delight and exultation, love and fellowship, peace and friendship. May there soon be heard, Lord our God, in the towns of Judah and the streets of Jerusalem the sound of joy and the sound of gladness, the voice of the groom and the voice of the bride, the jubilant voices of grooms from their wedding canopies and of young people from their musical feasts. Blessed are You, Lord, who gladdens groom and bride. [And grants success.]
paragraphs.note: Original English working translation aligned to the full Hebrew paragraph; specialist review pending.

paragraphs.text: They taste the wine, and afterward say:
May celebrations increase in Israel, and may this be a good omen!
The groom breaks a glass in remembrance of Jerusalem and says:
If I forget thee, O Jerusalem, Let my right hand forget her cunning. Let my tongue cleave to the roof of my mouth, If I remember thee not; If I set not Jerusalem Above my chiefest joy.
paragraphs.note: Every colon-delimited fragment matched a unique near-exact complete Tanakh verse; reviewed orthographic/qere alignment only.

paragraphs.text: Order of the circumcision ceremony (brit milah).
Prayer to be recited before the circumcision.

For the sake of the unity of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Presence, in awe and love and in love and awe, to unite the letters Yod–Heh with Vav–Heh in perfect unity, in the name of all Israel: I now come to circumcise this child [the father says: 'to circumcise my son'], to fulfill the positive commandment as it is said: 'This is My covenant, which you shall keep, between Me and you and your descendants after you: every male among you shall be circumcised.' May he be brought into the covenant of our father Abraham and into the good portion of the Holy One, blessed be He, as it is written: 'The righteous one is an everlasting foundation.' May the Holy One favor this offering and accept it; may the child merit the ten canopies prepared for the righteous in the world to come, as it is said: 'Happy is the man whom You choose and bring near, that he may dwell in Your courts; we shall be satisfied with the goodness of Your house, the holiness of Your Temple.' But now, because of our sins, our city is destroyed, our sanctuary desolate, and we have no sacrifices to atone for us. May the blood of this covenant be reckoned as though I had built an altar and offered upon it burnt offerings and sacrifices. May the words of my mouth and the meditation of my heart be acceptable before You, Lord, my rock and my redeemer.
paragraphs.note: New English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Prayer for the sandak.

For the sake of the unity of the Holy One, blessed be He, and His Presence, in awe and love and in love and awe, to unite the letters Yod–Heh with Vav–Heh in perfect unity, in the name of all Israel: I now come to serve as the sandak, to be as a chair and an altar upon my knees for the circumcision. May it be Your will, Lord our God and God of our ancestors, that this be as an altar of atonement, and that You atone for all my sins, wrongdoings and transgressions, especially what I have impaired through my limbs and the sign of the holy covenant. May this deed be accounted as though we had directed our minds to every proper intention and restored the root of the commandment in the supernal realm, bringing delight to our Maker and fulfilling the will of our Creator. May the favor of the Lord our God be upon us, and establish the work of our hands for us; establish the work of our hands.
