paragraphs.note: New English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: When the baby is brought into the synagogue, the entire congregation stands and says:
Blessed is the one who comes in the name of the LORD.
When the father takes the child in his hands, he says:

I rejoice at Thy word, As one that findeth great spoil. The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a broken and a contrite heart, O God, Thou wilt not despise. Do good in Thy favour unto Zion; build Thou the walls of Jerusalem. Then wilt Thou delight in the sacrifices of righteousness, in burnt-offering and whole offering; Then will they offer bullocks upon Thine altar.
paragraphs.note: Every colon-delimited fragment matched a unique near-exact complete Tanakh verse; reviewed orthographic/qere alignment only.

paragraphs.text: Afterward, the father of the child says:
Happy is the one You choose and draw near to dwell in Your courts.
Those present answer:
We shall be satisfied with the goodness of Your house, the holiness of Your Temple.
In the Land of Israel, it is customary to add these verses:
If I forget thee, O Jerusalem, Let my right hand forget her cunning. Let my tongue cleave to the roof of my mouth, If I remember thee not; If I set not Jerusalem Above my chiefest joy.
paragraphs.note: Every colon-delimited fragment matched a unique near-exact complete Tanakh verse; reviewed orthographic/qere alignment only.

paragraphs.text: Afterward, say:
HEAR, O ISRAEL: THE LORD OUR GOD, THE LORD IS ONE.
paragraphs.note: Exact complete Hebrew passage matched to the bundled Tanakh; no fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: The LORD is King; the LORD has reigned; the LORD will reign forever and ever. Repeat twice.
Please, LORD, save us now. (Twice.)
Please, LORD, grant us success now. (Twice.)
The child's father says:
With the permission of my teachers and rabbis:
Recite the blessing while standing:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us to bring him into the covenant of our father Abraham.
The congregation and the circumciser say:
As you have brought him into the covenant, so may you merit to bring him to Torah, commandments, marriage, and good deeds.
The sandak sits in the chair and places the baby on his knees, and the mohel says:
This is the chair of Elijah the prophet, the angel of the covenant, remembered for good.
Before performing the circumcision, the circumciser recites this blessing:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us concerning circumcision.
After the circumcision, the father blesses as follows:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who has kept us alive, sustained us, and brought us to this season.
The circumciser or another person takes a cup of wine and blesses:
With your permission, honored teachers! The congregation replies: To life!
Blessed are You, Adonoy our God, King of the Universe, Creator of the fruit of the vine.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: Afterward, he takes a myrtle branch and recites this blessing:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who creates fragrant trees.

Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who sanctified the beloved one from the womb, placed a statute upon his flesh and sealed his descendants with the sign of the holy covenant. Therefore, in reward for this, the living God, our portion and our Rock, commands that the beloved offspring of our holy kin be saved from corruption for the sake of the covenant placed in our flesh. Blessed are You, LORD, who establishes the covenant.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Our God and God of our fathers, preserve this child [my son] for his father [for me] and his mother, and let his name in Israel be called [name]. May the father rejoice in the fruit of his loins [when the father recites this blessing, he says: 'May it be Your will that I rejoice in the fruit of my loins']; and may the mother rejoice in the fruit of her womb, as it is said: 'Let your father and your mother be glad, and let her who bore you rejoice.' And it is said: 'I passed by you and saw you wallowing in your blood, and I said to you: In your blood, live!' [The officiant places a finger dipped in wine in the child's mouth; he does so again when the words are repeated:] 'And I said to you: In your blood, live!' And it is said: 'He has remembered His covenant forever, the word He commanded to a thousand generations; the covenant that He made with Abraham, and His oath to Isaac; and He established it to Jacob as a statute, to Israel as an everlasting covenant.' 'Give thanks to the Lord, for He is good, for His mercy endures forever.' May God make this little child [name] grow; just as he has entered the covenant, so may he enter into Torah, the commandments, marriage, and good deeds. So may it be His will; and let us say: Amen.
paragraphs.note: New English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: A Song of Ascents. Happy is every one that feareth the LORD, That walketh in His ways. When thou eatest the labour of thy hands, Happy shalt thou be, and it shall be well with thee. Thy wife shall be as a fruitful vine, in the innermost parts of thy house; Thy children like olive plants, round about thy table. Behold, surely thus shall the man be blessed That feareth the LORD. The LORD bless thee out of Zion; And see thou the good of Jerusalem all the days of thy life; And see thy children's children. Peace be upon Israel!
paragraphs.note: Every colon-delimited fragment matched a unique near-exact complete Tanakh verse; reviewed orthographic/qere alignment only.

paragraphs.text: They recite the Kaddish beginning 'May there be abundant peace.'

paragraphs: Blessing for a Mezuzah

It is a positive commandment from the Torah to affix a mezuzah. And one must affix it to the right of one walking in through the space of the opening, in the handbreadth adjacent to the outside, at the beginning of the highest third of the height of the entrance (going upwards). And it should be erect lengthwise. Before he affixes it, he should recite the blessing:

For the sake of the Union of the Holy One, blessed be He, with His Divine Presence, with fear and love, and love and fear, to unite the name the Name of Yod Hay with Vav Hay in complete unity in the name of all Israel - behold I have come to fulfill the positive commandment from the Torah to affix a mezuzah, as it is written (Deuteronomy 6:19), "And you shall write them upon the doorposts of your house and upon your gates." May the pleasantness of my Master, our God, be upon us, and the work of our hands establish for us and the work of our hands may He establish.
Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the Universe, who sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us to affix a mezuzah.
And after he has affixed it, he should kiss it and say:
This is the gate of the Lord, the righteous shall come through it! (Psalms 118:20)
Order of Hafrishat H'allah – Separating a Portion from Bread Dough (Challah)

paragraphs.text: 1. Today, since challah is forbidden for priests to eat because of ritual impurity, it is not given to priests but burned. Only a small amount is separated; no fixed minimum portion is required.

The hallah portion that is separated must be burned; it may not be discarded as ordinary rubbish or treated disrespectfully. Only after burning may it be thrown away, since its commandment has been fulfilled. If burning is impossible, wrap the portion twice in paper and put it in the bin.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: 3. It is preferable to wait until kneading is finished and the dough has become one mass before separating challah. If challah was not separated from the dough and it has already been baked, separate it from the bread afterward.

4. The obligation to separate challah applies to dough intended for baking. From dough prepared for cooking or frying, challah is separated without a blessing. If some of it will be baked, separate challah with a blessing.

The minimum flour quantity for separating hallah with a blessing is 1,560 grams. As an act of piety, it is preferable to separate hallah without a blessing starting from approximately 1.5 kilograms of flour (Hazon Ovadia responsa, p. 518). According to the Hazon Ish's ruling, the quantity is 2,250 grams.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: Before separating the challah portion, she recites the blessing:

paragraphs: Blessed are You, L·rd, our G·d, King of the Universe, Who has sanctified us with His commandments & commanded us to separate h'allah [Terumah]."
Detach h'allah & say:
Harei Zo H'allah / Behold this is H'allah
The Blessing in Lightning and Thunder
The custom is to bless without mentioning Hashem's name

On lightning one blesses 
Blessed are You (Hashem, King of the world,) Maker of the works of creation.
On thunder one blesses
Blessed are You (Hashem, King of the world,) whose strength and might fill the world.

paragraphs.text: Prayer for someone taking medicine.

paragraphs: ...Before Taking Medicine or Medical Procedure Say Personal Prayer & Text Below...
May it be Your Will, L·rd, Our G·d that this Endeavor bring healing, for You are the Free Doctor

paragraphs.text: The Traveler's Prayer.

When setting out on a journey that will last seventy-two minutes outside the city, recite this prayer with God’s name and kingship. If the travel outside the city is shorter, omit the name and kingship. Recite it after leaving the city; ideally join it to the concluding blessing after eating, drinking, or a similar act.

May it be Your will, LORD our God and God of our ancestors, to lead us in peace, guide our steps in peace, direct our way in peace, and bring us in peace to our desired destination. If returning on the same day add: “and return us in peace.” Rescue us from every enemy and ambush along the road, bless the work of our hands, and grant us grace, kindness, and compassion in Your eyes and in the eyes of all who see us. Hear our supplications, for You are the God who hears prayer and entreaty. Blessed are You, LORD, who hears prayer.
Some also add these verses for protection.
Jacob went on his way and angels of God met him. When Jacob saw them, he said: 'This is God's camp,' and called that place Mahanaim. Repeat three times.
paragraphs.note: New source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading outstanding.

paragraphs.text: And they journeyed; and a terror of God was upon the cities that were round about them, and they did not pursue after the sons of Jacob. I wait for Thy salvation, O Lord.
paragraphs.note: Every colon-delimited fragment matched a unique near-exact complete Tanakh verse; reviewed orthographic/qere alignment only.

paragraphs.text: “May the LORD bless you and keep you; may the LORD make His face shine upon you and be gracious to you; may the LORD lift up His countenance toward you and grant you peace.” Recite three times.
Behold, I am sending an angel before you, to guard you on the road and bring you to the place I have prepared. Repeat three times.

the angel who hath redeemed me from all evil, bless the lads; and let my name be named in them, and the name of my fathers Abraham and Isaac; and let them grow into a multitude in the midst of the earth.’
paragraphs.note: Reviewed near-exact Hebrew Tanakh alignment (genesis 48:16, similarity 0.961); orthographic/qere differences only.

paragraphs.text: Fasts and mourning observances.
Selichot for the Fast of Gedaliah.
After the Amidah repetition, the confession and Tachanun are recited; then say:

Through Your abundant mercy forgive us, our Father, for in our great folly we have gone astray. Pardon us, our King, for our sins are many. You are a God slow to anger, and You have shown us the path of repentance. Remember today the greatness of Your mercy and kindness to the descendants of those You love. Turn toward us in compassion, for You are the Master of mercy. We come before You with supplication and prayer, as You revealed long ago to the humble one. Turn back from Your burning anger, as is written in Your Torah. Let us take refuge and dwell in the shadow of Your wings, as on the day when the Lord descended in the cloud. Pass over transgression and pardon guilt, as on the day when He stood there with him. Hear our plea and favorably receive our words, as on the day when He proclaimed the name of the Lord. And there it is said:
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: The LORD passed before him and proclaimed: “LORD, LORD, God compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, abundant in kindness and truth; preserving kindness for thousands, forgiving iniquity, transgression, and sin, and cleansing.”
paragraphs.note: Kavvanah reviewed Siddur translation (2026).

paragraphs.text: My soul mourns and my brightness is darkened; the House of my glory was burned by the lion-like foe. Even the survivors who remained of my remnant perished on the third of Tishrei. The raging waters swept over us in their onslaught; enemies trampled my sanctuary and plundered its share. The elders of the remnant who escaped the day of vengeance were struck down today together with Gedaliah son of Ahikam. The poor people of the land were torn apart; what the cutting locust left, the swarming locust consumed. The vineyard keepers and farmers appointed by the governor of the land were gathered away; none remained to build the wall or stand in the breach. What can I recount? My sighs are immense, my soul is weary, my assemblies are sorrowful. My survivors, spared the sword and fury, had scarcely established themselves when the walls were broken again. How long will You hide Your face from us? Hear our cries, release our bonds. Holy One, look upon our poverty, for we have none to crown us. Behold our lowliness as we offer praise before You. We have been plundered from generation to generation, through every appointed season; a serpent's root has stung us. Mighty One, awaken in judgment and rouse Yourself; atone for our sins and decree that the end of exile draw near. Let Your mercies stir for the people few among the nations; exalt them by Your kindness before all peoples. Show them Your wonders, Dweller on High, God and King enthroned upon the throne of mercy.
paragraphs.note: New English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: God, King, Who sits upon a throne of mercy and conducts Himself with kindness, forgiving the iniquities of His people and removing each first transgression in turn; Who increases forgiveness for sinners and pardon for transgressors; Who acts charitably toward every creature of flesh and spirit and does not repay them according to their evil. God, You taught us to recite the Thirteen Attributes. Remember for us today the covenant of the Thirteen, as You made known long ago to the humble one. And so it is written in Your Torah: “The LORD descended in the cloud and stood with him there, and he called upon the Name of the LORD.” And there it says:

The LORD passed before him and proclaimed: “LORD, LORD, God compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, abundant in kindness and truth; preserving kindness for thousands, forgiving iniquity, transgression, and sin, and cleansing.”
paragraphs.note: Kavvanah reviewed Siddur translation (2026).

paragraphs.text: In alphabetical order.

People of faith have vanished, those who came with the strength of their deeds; mighty ones who stood in the breach and turned decrees aside. They were a wall for us and a refuge on the day of wrath. Even with a whisper they rebuked anger; with their cry they restrained fury. Before they called to You, You answered them; they knew how to plead and appease. Like a father You had compassion for their sake and did not send them away empty-handed. Because of our many sins we have lost them; through our sins they have been taken from us. They have gone to their rest and left us to sigh. Those who fenced the breach are gone; those who turned back wrath have ceased. There is none to stand in the breach; those worthy to appease You are no more. We have wandered to the four corners and found no remedy. We return to You with shame on our faces, seeking You, O God, at the time of our forgiveness.
paragraphs.note: Previously translated paragraph, Hebrew similarity 98.8%: source and target independently present in source corpus.

paragraphs.text: God, King, Who sits upon a throne of mercy and conducts Himself with kindness, forgiving the iniquities of His people and removing each first transgression in turn; Who increases forgiveness for sinners and pardon for transgressors; Who acts charitably toward every creature of flesh and spirit and does not repay them according to their evil. God, You taught us to recite the Thirteen Attributes. Remember for us today the covenant of the Thirteen, as You made known long ago to the humble one. And so it is written in Your Torah: “The LORD descended in the cloud and stood with him there, and he called upon the Name of the LORD.” And there it says:

The LORD passed before him and proclaimed: “LORD, LORD, God compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, abundant in kindness and truth; preserving kindness for thousands, forgiving iniquity, transgression, and sin, and cleansing.”
paragraphs.note: Kavvanah reviewed Siddur translation (2026).

paragraphs.text: In reverse Hebrew alphabetical order.

We are bewildered by evils; our strength has failed from troubles. We have sunk very low; we have been humbled to the dust. Compassionate One, such is our nature: stiff-necked and rebellious are we. With our mouths we cried, “We have sinned,” while our hearts are twisted and crooked. Most High, Your mercy is from eternity; forgiveness is with You. Relent concerning the evil; incline toward kindness. Do not hide Yourself at a time such as this, for we are in great distress. Let Your goodness and kindness toward us be known in the sight of all. Seal the mouth of the Accuser; let him not accuse us. Rebuke him and let him be silent. Let a good advocate stand to justify us and declare our uprightness. Your ways of compassion and grace You revealed to the faithful one of Your house; when he pleaded before You, You made Your faithfulness known to him.
paragraphs.note: Kavvanah reviewed Siddur translation (2026).

paragraphs.text: God, King, Who sits upon a throne of mercy and conducts Himself with kindness, forgiving the iniquities of His people and removing each first transgression in turn; Who increases forgiveness for sinners and pardon for transgressors; Who acts charitably toward every creature of flesh and spirit and does not repay them according to their evil. God, You taught us to recite the Thirteen Attributes. Remember for us today the covenant of the Thirteen, as You made known long ago to the humble one. And so it is written in Your Torah: “The LORD descended in the cloud and stood with him there, and he called upon the Name of the LORD.” And there it says:

The LORD passed before him and proclaimed: “LORD, LORD, God compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, abundant in kindness and truth; preserving kindness for thousands, forgiving iniquity, transgression, and sin, and cleansing.”
paragraphs.note: Kavvanah reviewed Siddur translation (2026).

paragraphs.text: When Israel sinned in the wilderness, Moses stood before You in prayer and asked mercy for Your people Israel. Thus he prayed: “Please forgive the iniquity of this people according to the greatness of Your kindness, as You have forgiven this people from Egypt until now.” And You answered him in Your goodness, bringing him good tidings and saying: “I have forgiven according to your word.”

Daniel, greatly beloved, said before You: 'Incline Your ear, my God, and hear; open Your eyes and behold our desolations and the city upon which Your name is called. For we do not cast our supplications before You because of our own righteousness, but because of Your great mercies. O Lord, hear! O Lord, forgive! O Lord, attend and act; do not delay for Your own sake, my God, for Your name is called upon Your city and Your people.' And to Jerusalem, Your city, You said: 'I shall contend with you because you say, I have not sinned.' We are ashamed of our deeds and embarrassed by our transgressions; we have no mouth with which to answer and no boldness to raise our heads.
paragraphs.note: New English working translation reviewed against the Hebrew and available Russian text; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: In the Atbash alphabetical pattern.

Our God and God of our fathers, do not bring us to destruction; hold back Your hand in judgment. When accusation comes before You, do not erase our name from Your record. When You approach to examine and chastise, let Your mercy precede Your anger. When You behold the poverty of our deeds, bring Your own righteousness near. Teach us when we cry to You; command our salvation through the intercessor. Restore the captivity of the tents of the innocent; see how their entrances lie desolate. Remember what You declared: the testimony shall not be forgotten from the mouth of his descendants. Unseal the sealed testimony; place Your secret among those You teach. The navel, the rounded bowl—may the mixed wine never be lacking. O Yah, acknowledge Israel who know You; cast down the nations who do not know You. For You will return the captives to the stronghold, prisoners of hope.
paragraphs.note: Kavvanah reviewed Siddur translation (2026).

paragraphs.text: We are more guilty than any people; we are more ashamed than any nation. Gladness has departed from us; our hearts are sick through our sins. Our dwellings are laid waste and our splendor torn away. The abode of our Sanctuary is destroyed because of our wrongdoing. Our stronghold is desolate; the beauty of our land is given to strangers, our strength to foreigners. They robbed our labor before our eyes; we are dragged and plucked away. They laid their yoke upon us, and we bore it on our shoulders. Servants ruled over us, and there was none to deliver us from their hands. Many troubles surrounded us; we called upon You, Lord our God. Through our sins You became distant from us; we turned back from following You, wandered like sheep and were lost. Still we have not turned back from our wandering. How then can we dare to set our faces and stiffen our necks, to say before You, Lord our God and God of our ancestors, 'We are righteous and have not sinned'?
paragraphs.note: New English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Ezra the scribe said before You: 'My God, I am ashamed and blush to lift my face to You, my God, for our iniquities have multiplied over our heads, and our guilt has grown to the heavens.' Yet You are a God of pardons, gracious and merciful, slow to anger and abundant in kindness, and You did not forsake them. Do not abandon us, our Father; do not forsake us, our King; do not forget us, our Creator; do not destroy us utterly in our exile. Fulfill for us, Lord our God, the promise You made through Jeremiah Your seer, as it is said: 'In those days and at that time, says the Lord, the iniquity of Israel shall be sought and there shall be none, and the sins of Judah, and they shall not be found; for I will pardon those whom I leave as a remnant.' Do not let any sin or wrongdoing hinder our prayer before You. Forgive and pardon all our iniquities, for You are a God who is good and forgiving.
paragraphs.note: New English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: What can we say before You, Who sits on high, and what can we recount before You, Who dwells in the heavens? Surely You know what is hidden and what is revealed. You know the mysteries of the world and the concealed secrets of every living being. You search all the chambers within and see the kidneys and the heart. Nothing is hidden from You, and nothing is concealed from before Your eyes.
paragraphs.note: Kavvanah reviewed Siddur translation (2026).

paragraphs.text: May it be Your will, LORD our God and God of our fathers, that You forgive us all our sins, atone for all our iniquities, and pardon and forgive all our transgressions. Forgive our iniquity and our sin, and take us as Your inheritance. Forgive us, our Father, for we have sinned; pardon us, our King, for we have transgressed. For You, Lord, are good and forgiving, abundant in kindness to all who call upon You. For the sake of Your Name, LORD, forgive my iniquity, for it is great. For the sake of Your Name, LORD, preserve me alive; in Your righteousness bring my soul out of distress. The LORD of Hosts is with us; the God of Jacob is our stronghold, Selah. LORD of Hosts, happy is the person who trusts in You. LORD, save! May the King answer us on the day we call. Return us to You, LORD, and we shall return; renew our days as of old.
paragraphs.ref: KAV EDOT VIDUI 25, KAV EDOT VIDUI 26
paragraphs.note: Kavvanah reviewed Siddur translation (2026).

paragraphs.text: He is compassionate; He forgives iniquity and does not destroy. Many times He turns His anger away and does not arouse all His wrath. You, LORD, do not withhold Your compassion from me; may Your kindness and truth always preserve me. Save us, LORD our God, and gather us from among the nations, to give thanks to Your holy Name and glory in Your praise. If You, Yah, should keep account of iniquities, Lord, who could stand? But forgiveness is with You, so that You may be revered. He has not dealt with us according to our sins, nor repaid us according to our iniquities. Though our iniquities testify against us, LORD, act for the sake of Your Name. Remember, LORD, Your compassion and Your kindness, for they are from of old. May the LORD answer you on the day of distress; may the Name of the God of Jacob protect you. LORD, save! May the King answer us on the day we call. Our Father, our King, be gracious to us and answer us, for we have no deeds to our credit. Deal with us charitably according to Your abundant mercy, and save us for the sake of Your Name.

And now, O Lord our God, who brought Your people out of Egypt with a mighty hand and made Yourself a name as it is today, we have sinned and acted wickedly. O Lord, according to all Your righteousness, turn Your anger and wrath away from Jerusalem, Your city and Your holy mountain; because of our sins and the iniquities of our fathers, Jerusalem and Your people have become a reproach to all around us. And now, our God, hear Your servant's prayer and supplications; for Your own sake, Lord, cause Your face to shine upon Your desolate sanctuary. Incline Your ear and hear, my God; open Your eyes and behold our desolations and the city called by Your name. We present our pleas before You not because of our righteousness but because of Your abundant compassion. Lord, hear! Lord, forgive! Lord, attend and act; do not delay, for Your own sake, my God, for Your name is called upon Your city and Your people. Our Father, merciful Father, show us a sign for good and gather our scattered ones from the four corners of the earth. Let all the nations know that You, Lord, are our Father: we are clay, You are our potter, and all of us are the work of Your hand. Our Father, our King, our Rock and our Redeemer, spare Your people, Lord, and do not deliver Your inheritance to disgrace, so that the nations should rule over it. Why should the peoples say, 'Where is their God?' We know, Lord, that we have sinned, and none can plead for us except Your great name, which is our aid in distress. As a father shows compassion to children, have mercy on us; spare Your people and pity Your inheritance. In the multitude of Your mercies spare us; have mercy on us, our King, and answer us. Righteousness belongs to You, Lord, who works wonders at all times. Look down and save the sheep of Your pasture; let anger not prevail over us, for salvation is Yours, Lord, and our hope rests in You. Forgiving God, we beseech You: forgive us, for You are a good and forgiving God.
paragraphs.note: New English working translation reviewed against the Hebrew and available Russian text; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Please, compassionate and gracious King, remember and look upon the covenant between the pieces. Let the binding of the only son appear before You. For the sake of Israel our father, do not forsake us, our Father; do not abandon us, our King; do not forget us, our Former; and do not bring us to destruction in our exile. For You are God, a gracious and compassionate King.
paragraphs.note: Previously translated paragraph, Hebrew similarity 99.3%: source and target independently present in source corpus.

paragraphs.text: There is none like You, gracious and compassionate, our God. There is none like You, God slow to anger and abundant in kindness and truth. Save us and have mercy on us; rescue us from trembling and wrath. Remember Your servants Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Do not turn toward the stubbornness of this people, nor toward its wickedness and sin. Turn from Your fierce anger and relent concerning the evil against Your people. Remove from us the plague of death, for You are compassionate; for it is Your way to show unearned kindness in every generation. Please, LORD, save now. Please, LORD, grant success now. Please, LORD, answer us on the day we call. For You, LORD, we have hoped; for You, LORD, we have waited; for You, LORD, we yearn. Do not be silent—answer us. For the nations have said that their hope is lost. Every knee shall bend to You, and every upright form shall bow before You.

You Who open a hand in repentance to receive transgressors and sinners: our soul is shaken by the greatness of our sorrow. Do not forget us forever; arise and save us. Do not pour Your wrath upon us, for we are Your people, children of Your covenant. God, look! Our honor is diminished among the nations, and they have treated us as the impurity of a menstruant. How long will Your strength be in captivity and Your splendor in the hand of the foe? They shall see, be ashamed, and be broken from their might. Awaken Your might and save us for the sake of Your Name. Let our hardships not seem small before You; may Your mercy quickly come before us in our time of distress. Act not for our sake but for Yours, and do not destroy the memory of our remnant. For our eyes hope toward You, for You are God, a gracious and compassionate King. Remember our testimony, which every day, continually, we recite twice with love: Hear, Israel: the LORD is our God, the LORD is One.
paragraphs.note: Previously translated paragraph, Hebrew similarity 99.6%: source and target independently present in source corpus.

paragraphs.text: The prayer leader says Half Kaddish, the Torah scroll is brought out and three people are called up for the Vayechal reading printed at the end of the Siddur. The service then concludes as on other weekdays. After “Save Us,” Psalm 83 (“A song, a psalm of Asaph: O God, do not keep silent”) is said, as given above in Shacharit.
Selichot for the Tenth of Tevet.
After the Amidah repetition, the confession and Tachanun are recited; then say:

My stature sank to the earth and my wound grew grievous. I sit desolate, for the day the lion drew near against Zion, my city, the beauty of the holy mountain. Therefore I lament and mourn in the tenth month. In the tenth month the lion came up in fury; on the tenth day he raised a siege wall against me. He and all his people came to take vengeance on my people and prepared for war against them. O my stronghold and savior, turn war against my enemy and oppressor; let him drink the mixed cup filled to the brim. Rise early, Lord my Shepherd, my Shield and horn of salvation.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: In the tenth month an enemy pursued me with the sword; on the tenth day he prepared an ambush against me. For this I lament, and my joy is mingled with bitterness. Woe to us, for the day declines and evening shadows lengthen. Turn evening into morning and do not let traitors triumph. Have mercy upon Your people and bring healing to their suffering. Remember for me the covenant of the ancestors as I spread out my hands before You: You who kill and bring to life, who cast down to the grave and raise up.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: In the tenth month the wolf of the wilderness roared against my people; on the tenth day he encamped with his troops against them. Whoever ventured forth was torn apart, and a leopard lay in wait at their cities. Their cities were burned with fire amid mounting tribulations. Rise, Lord, in Your power and bring desolation upon the arrogant. May they be ashamed when You perform a sign of goodness for us, Holy One of Israel, Lord of hosts.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: In the tenth month the enemy grasped shield and buckler; on the tenth day he prepared as a warrior against the faithful city. Therefore put on sackcloth, O delicate congregation; cut off your crown, cast it away, and raise a lament on the hilltops. Your people utter mourning before You on this day, and our eyes flow with tears over the destruction of Your house. Stir a day of judgment against the enemies clamoring in Your house. Make Your ways known to me, Lord, and teach me Your paths.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: In the tenth month my oppressors piled siege works against my city; on the tenth day my crown was cast down and my glory fell. Those who dealt me a grievous wound surrounded me, and my innermost being was in anguish. On this day I shall plead before the One revered in the great assembly of the holy, beseeching Him to forgive transgression and guilt. Do not regard our wickedness; blot out our recorded sin. Return us to You, Lord, and we shall return.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Through Your abundant mercy forgive us, our Father, for in our great folly we have gone astray. Pardon us, our King, for our sins are many. You are a God slow to anger, and You have shown us the path of repentance. Remember today the greatness of Your mercy and kindness to the descendants of those You love. Turn toward us in compassion, for You are the Master of mercy. We come before You with supplication and prayer, as You revealed long ago to the humble one. Turn back from Your burning anger, as is written in Your Torah. Let us take refuge and dwell in the shadow of Your wings, as on the day when the Lord descended in the cloud. Pass over transgression and pardon guilt, as on the day when He stood there with him. Hear our plea and favorably receive our words, as on the day when He proclaimed the name of the Lord. And there it is said:
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: The LORD passed before him and proclaimed: “LORD, LORD, God compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, abundant in kindness and truth; preserving kindness for thousands, forgiving iniquity, transgression, and sin, and cleansing.”
paragraphs.note: Kavvanah reviewed Siddur translation (2026).

paragraphs.text: In alphabetical order.

When the day of visitation came upon the Valley of Vision and the Lord's anger flashed like sparks of fire, He disclosed to the prophet, the son of Buzi: 'Write down the name of this day, this very day.' In the fire of My zealous wrath I spoke of destruction to the rebellious house: behold, I shall come against it in anger and a stormy whirlwind and make it a proverb, a mockery, and a disgrace. 'Set on the pot, set it on.' Terrible trembling seized Zion and her palaces; her spirit failed and her strength melted away. Her heart was torn when she heard the command, 'Gather its pieces into it.' I shall give her enemies spoil and captives; priests and those who compounded the incense mixtures are led into a lifelong exile, without a savior. 'Take the choicest of the flock.' They held dominion over you and laughed, O mistress of nations; then they proclaimed you infamous and hateful among the peoples. Your accusers spoke against you, saying, 'Woe to the city of blood!' It transgressed the law, broke God's covenant, committed evil, and descended into the deepest pit. It cried aloud, but God did not heed the weeping, for its blood remained in its midst. Hear the voice of those oppressed and call their oppressors to account; do not turn away their cries of anguish unanswered. Repay those who harmed them sevenfold for their deeds, as it is said: 'A righteous man falls seven times and rises again.' Through our own fault we have strayed, great and awesome God; although our transgressions grew strong, Your compassion was stronger. You pitied us when wrath had almost consumed us. 'Distress and sorrow I found; then I called upon the name of the Lord.' Let Your mercy stir toward the small one among the nations; in kindness raise it before all peoples. Reveal to them Your wonders, Rock who dwells on high, God and King who sits upon the throne of mercy.
paragraphs.note: New English working translation reviewed against the Hebrew and available Russian text; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Attend, Most High, to the voice of the poor and do not despise his supplication. Bitter was his heart on the day the prophet, the son of Buzi, was told: 'Write down the name of this day, this very day.' Lord of Hosts, remember the afflictions by which I was so grievously struck. Under the constellation of Capricorn three calamities converged against me. On that day the rejected tribes were struck; on that day a blasphemer of Your name came against the city of their delight; on that day Ezra the priest, leader of the congregation, departed this life. All these befell me, and many more misfortunes like them. On that day the lion rejoiced and aimed an arrow against my city; on the tenth day of the tenth month it rose to destroy the last sons of the tenth generation, to ruin the entire fruit of the cluster and gather the grapes of my consecration. I remain shackled by Assyria, standing at my doors. Cut off, I do not know which loss to bewail. Your people were besieged on the tenth day: the lion surrounded the beautiful, holy city. Hear its cry and wipe away its sins on the tenth day of the month. Renew the anointed kingdom as in ancient days. Sanctify Your name among us, Lord, to be praised as at the beginning. Break all who hate and oppress us by the power of Your anger; let them be seized and destroyed, as in the days of Barak, in the holy city. Return, Most High, to Zion's city, that we may behold You face to face; then with joyful words we shall say, 'Behold our God!'
paragraphs.note: New English working translation reviewed against the Hebrew and available Russian text; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: You who dwell in heaven, hear those who have passed through fire and water; have mercy on a people punished twice for its sins. On the day the enemy began the siege of the city, the delight of our encampments, the king of Babylon came up against Jerusalem. You who answer in distress, do not despise the prayer of the poor; on the fast of the tenth month behold our affliction. On that day You commanded the son of Buzi, the prophet: 'Write down the name of this day, this very day.' On that day the lion and leopard lay in wait at our doors; the palace of the glorious inheritance was besieged, and calamity began among those who covered themselves with dust. On that day Ezra the priest and scribe also passed away. The hearts of the inhabitants of the city of the Book became like water: the king of Babylon came up against Jerusalem.
paragraphs.note: New English working translation reviewed against the Hebrew and available Russian text; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Continue with “God, King” and “Men of Faith” above, and complete the service as on the Fast of Gedaliah. Bring out the Torah scroll, call three readers for the Vayechal passage, and conclude as on an ordinary weekday. After “Save Us,” say Psalm 83, “A song, a psalm of Asaph: O God, do not keep silent.”
Penitential prayers for the Fast of Esther.
After the Amidah repetition, the confession and Tachanun are recited; then say:

Through Your abundant mercy forgive us, our Father, for in our great folly we have gone astray. Pardon us, our King, for our sins are many. You are a God slow to anger, and You have shown us the path of repentance. Remember today the greatness of Your mercy and kindness to the descendants of those You love. Turn toward us in compassion, for You are the Master of mercy. We come before You with supplication and prayer, as You revealed long ago to the humble one. Turn back from Your burning anger, as is written in Your Torah. Let us take refuge and dwell in the shadow of Your wings, as on the day when the Lord descended in the cloud. Pass over transgression and pardon guilt, as on the day when He stood there with him. Hear our plea and favorably receive our words, as on the day when He proclaimed the name of the Lord. And there it is said:
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: The LORD passed before him and proclaimed: “LORD, LORD, God compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, abundant in kindness and truth; preserving kindness for thousands, forgiving iniquity, transgression, and sin, and cleansing.”
paragraphs.note: Kavvanah reviewed Siddur translation (2026).

paragraphs.text: When the descendant of Agag plunged into wicked designs and plotted to destroy and annihilate the holy people, the descendant of Benjamin called weeping to the Rock who dwells on high, for 'the Lord will not forsake His people.' The Agagite planned to exterminate Israel's remnant and cast the pur, the lot, to destroy us all on the appointed day; but the Benjaminite neither rose nor moved before him, for 'one who trusts in the Lord is surrounded by mercy.' Arrogance drove the Agagite to a mad decision; he hastened to offer ten thousand talents of silver for the ruin of the scattered flock. The Benjaminite purified his heart with fasting and the congregation's prayer, for 'the Lord is good, a stronghold in the day of trouble.' The Agagite left the banquet house rejoicing and raised a gallows upon which to hang the faithful man. The Benjaminite was clothed with favor and trusted the One clothed in majesty, the Father of orphans and Judge of widows. The Agagite hastily summoned his wise men and his wife's advisers; to his shame they counseled him, 'You will surely fall before him.' The Benjaminite revealed the secret to Hadassah; she clothed herself in royal dignity and undertook her vow. When the Agagite came to the festive feast, she opened her mouth with wisdom, gentle and gracious. The Benjaminite rejoiced to see Haman's fall, for God is 'greatly feared in the council of the holy ones.' O Holy One praised by the seraphim above, let the congregation of Your faithful sing Your majesty: 'For Your salvation I wait, O Lord!' 'So may all Your enemies perish, O Lord!' Let Your mercy stir toward the small one among the nations; lift it up in Your goodness before all peoples; show them Your wonders, Rock who dwells on high, God and King enthroned in mercy. Your servants hoped in the visions You recorded in Scripture: that You would show them favor before their captors, speak to their hearts and heal their pain: 'Yet even when they are in the land of their enemies...' Then the lion crushed me, tore me from the fruitful vine, exiled me, and carried me into a land of darkness; but beforehand You established four men of wisdom in the Torah: Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. One was delivered from lions, the others from flames. The ram and the swine hastened to sow turmoil and destruction; my light was almost put out, the sun's brightness almost hidden. Yet You upheld the hands of Benjamin's descendant and Hadassah, and the arrows aimed at me returned to the hearts of those who shot them. Because of my transgressions a mad villain rose against me, opening his mouth wide like a wild boar; but You had already prepared defenders of faith for me at the city gates. And now I rejoice in their insight and in their words: 'Yet even when they are in the land of their enemies...'
paragraphs.note: New English working translation reviewed against the Hebrew and available Russian text; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: And yet for all that, when they are in the land of their enemies, I will not reject them, neither will I abhor them, to destroy them utterly, and to break My covenant with them; for I am the LORD their God. then will I remember My covenant with Jacob, and also My covenant with Isaac, and also My covenant with Abraham will I remember; and I will remember the land. Out of my straits I called upon the LORD; He answered me with great enlargement. The LORD is for me; I will not fear; What can man do unto me? The LORD is for me as my helper; And I shall gaze upon them that hate me. It is better to take refuge in the LORD Than to trust in man. It is better to take refuge in the LORD Than to trust in princes. All nations compass me about; Verily, in the name of the LORD I will cut them off. Thou didst thrust sore at me that I might fall; But the LORD helped me.
paragraphs.note: Every colon-delimited Hebrew fragment matched an exact complete bundled Tanakh verse; translations joined without fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: In every generation arrogant enemies rose up, yet God preserved me. First the lion came and scattered me in every direction; after him an orphaned bear arose and sold me to those who struck from behind. 'You pushed me hard so that I might fall, but the Lord helped me.' When I came out of exhausting bondage, the serpent slithered out to confront me on the road, to frighten me when I was weary and weak. Yet You broke it and crushed it from thigh to shin; on the day my oppressors lifted their hands, You granted me victory over them. 'You pushed me hard so that I might fall, but the Lord helped me.' When Haman the Agagite rose like a sea monster to swallow me, he wrote a slanderous decree to wipe me out in a single day. Yet God sent salvation from heaven, delivered me, preserved my life, and sustained me with strength and salvation. 'You pushed me hard so that I might fall, but the Lord helped me.' Your name is the tower of my hope, O God, who brought me forth from my mother's womb. You delivered my soul from death and destruction, my eyes from tears and my feet from stumbling. In the land of my exile, O God, You made me numerous. 'You pushed me hard so that I might fall, but the Lord helped me.'
paragraphs.note: New English working translation reviewed against the Hebrew and available Russian text; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Thou didst thrust sore at me that I might fall; But the LORD helped me. The LORD is my strength and song; And He is become my salvation. The voice of rejoicing and salvation is in the tents of the righteous; The right hand of the LORD doeth valiantly. The right hand of the LORD is exalted; The right hand of the LORD doeth valiantly. I shall not die, but live, And declare the works of the LORD. The LORD hath chastened me sore; But He hath not given me over unto death. Open to me the gates of righteousness; I will enter into them, I will give thanks unto the LORD. This is the gate of the LORD; The righteous shall enter into it. I will give thanks unto Thee, for Thou hast answered me, And art become my salvation. A Song of Ascents; of David. 'If it had not been the LORD who was for us', Let Israel now say;
paragraphs.note: Includes JPS 1917 public-domain biblical readings with translated liturgical additions; specialist proofread pending.

paragraphs.text: How strangers, cruel as swarming bees, surrounded us when Haman arose! Then they plundered us like a demon of desolation. Through our many offenses we were made to drink a poisoned cup for which there was no remedy. 'Had the Lord not been with us, they would have swallowed us alive.' How they plotted together and devised in their hearts a plan to destroy the people! They conspired to annihilate the daughter of Israel, a people unique, and resolved to wipe it from the earth as though it had never been. As if caught between furnace and flame, the waters swept over us. 'Had the Lord not been with us, they would have swallowed us alive.' An oppressor arose and stirred up hostility and hatred against me. He issued a decree and appointed a day to destroy the Almighty's congregation, His inheritance. Yet the Rock took pity, bestowed goodness, and showed His might, destroying the enemy and his sons who oppressed us. In the hour of distress the enemy conceived evil and cast his pur, his lot; but the Rock heard and returned the punishment upon his own head. In the month of Adar the majestic God revealed His strength to His congregation and struck with everlasting ruin those who struck us. 'Had the Lord not been with us, they would have swallowed us alive.'
paragraphs.note: New English working translation reviewed against the Hebrew and available Russian text; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: A Song of Ascents; of David. 'If it had not been the LORD who was for us', Let Israel now say; 'If it had not been the LORD who was for us, When men rose up against us, Then they had swallowed us up alive, when their wrath was kindled against us; Then the waters had overwhelmed us, the stream had gone over our soul; Then the proud waters Had gone over our soul.' Blessed be the LORD, who hath not given us as a prey to their teeth. Our soul is escaped as a bird out of the snare of the fowlers; The snare is broken, and we are escaped. Our help is in the name of the LORD, Who made heaven and earth.

O Lord, hear! O Lord, forgive! O Lord, listen and act; do not delay, for Your own sake, my God, because Your name is called upon Your city and Your people. Bring us back to You, LORD, and we shall return; renew our days as of old.

Continue with “God, King” and “Men of Faith” as printed for the Fast of Gedaliah, and conclude as on that fast. Bring out the Torah scroll and call up three readers for Vayechal at the end of the Siddur. Finish the service as on a weekday. After “Save Us,” say Psalm 22, “For the leader; upon Ayelet HaShachar,” as printed above in Shacharit.
Selichot for the Seventeenth of Tammuz.

Five calamities occurred on the seventeenth of Tammuz: the first Tablets were broken, the regular daily offering ceased (at the First Temple), the city walls were breached (in the Second Temple period), the wicked Apostomos burned the Torah, and an idol was erected in the Sanctuary. One should weep bitterly over these calamities and pray for the rebuilding of Jerusalem.
After the Amidah repetition, the confession and Tachanun are recited; then say:

My height was brought low to the earth on the day the wicked plotted to subdue me. The joy of my heart ceased, and I was cast out of my house of repose. My gateways mourned and grieved when my noble protector and deliverer was taken away. Therefore I lament from year to year in the fourth month.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: In the fourth month troubles and sighs surrounded me; on its seventeenth day I grew weary from my groaning and found no rest. I cried aloud in weeping, and every head was shorn, for on this day the tablets were shattered. When the tablets were taken from me, tribulations beset me, and the hand of my enemy grew strong and scattered me on every side. Turn toward those awaiting the wondrous end and defend them, for the Lord of hosts is a sun and a shield.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: In the fourth month I thought to rise from the miry clay, but no one upheld me; on the seventeenth I became prey for plunder, destruction and ruin. I found no repose; my pain was continually before me, because on that day the daily offering was suspended. When the continual offering was removed, my wailing grew like the cry of Eglaim, and my mourning doubled like the mourning at Hadad-Rimmon. Turn now, God who dwells in heaven, and awaken our sleepers to life; after two days revive us.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: In the fourth month I bore the Rock's indignation, and His wrath burned within me. On the seventeenth terror seized me and a storm shook me. I forgot all good things, and my soul was cast far from peace through the assault of Seir, for on that day the city walls were breached. When the city was breached and Teman and Magdiel arose against it, my strength failed and I found no power. Turn toward the remnant of Ariel and sanctify them, and may they sanctify the Holy One of Jacob, the God of Israel.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: In the fourth month came a day of woe, a day of rebuke and wrath. On the seventeenth my glory went into exile and my splendor was taken away. My fracture has no healing, my wound is grievous and my spirit is broken, for on that day Apostomos burned the Torah. When the Torah was burned, my sorrows were renewed; the elders and aged disappeared from the holy city. Turn and show favor through Your might to the congregation of Your faithful, granting the spirit of knowledge and fear of the Lord.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: In the fourth month the foreigner measured out my punishment and consumed everything. On the seventeenth an alien desolated my dwelling and devoured Jacob. Year upon year I eat bitterness on that day, for then an idol was placed in the Sanctuary. When the abominable image of jealousy was set up, my spirit was wounded and my hope disappointed. Turn now and heal Your people's turning away; love them freely. Return us, Lord, to You, and we shall return.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Through Your abundant mercy forgive us, our Father, for in our great folly we have gone astray. Pardon us, our King, for our sins are many. You are a God slow to anger, and You have shown us the path of repentance. Remember today the greatness of Your mercy and kindness to the descendants of those You love. Turn toward us in compassion, for You are the Master of mercy. We come before You with supplication and prayer, as You revealed long ago to the humble one. Turn back from Your burning anger, as is written in Your Torah. Let us take refuge and dwell in the shadow of Your wings, as on the day when the Lord descended in the cloud. Pass over transgression and pardon guilt, as on the day when He stood there with him. Hear our plea and favorably receive our words, as on the day when He proclaimed the name of the Lord. And there it is said:
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: The LORD passed before him and proclaimed: “LORD, LORD, God compassionate and gracious, slow to anger, abundant in kindness and truth; preserving kindness for thousands, forgiving iniquity, transgression, and sin, and cleansing.”
paragraphs.note: Kavvanah reviewed Siddur translation (2026).

paragraphs.text: In alphabetical order.

Then, because of my faithlessness, says the One who dwells on high, when sin entangled me and my burden grew unbearable, the foreigner gained power over me to strike me; in anger He tore at me and turned against me. I abandoned the ways He had taught me, and so He stirred up anger, fury, and indignation against me. He poured His wrath upon me, loosed His arrows, and made me His target. Five calamities befell me that day; beasts of prey tore me apart and reduced me to ruins. My soul was spent almost to death; I bent low at what I heard and trembled at what I saw. Whenever I recall it, my sighs awaken and fire devours me, burning body and inward parts. I shall deepen my bitter lament and cast away joy, for on this day the tablets were shattered. The stranger and all his multitude mustered against me; they surrounded me like waters, and I was drowning with no helper. Therefore I shall weep aloud and never cease my dirges: on this day the regular tamid offering ceased. My oppressors roared like a flood; they cast me into the pit of my life, handed me over to be devoured, and appointed a day of disaster against me. My people became orphaned, for on this day an idol was set up in the Temple. O city crowded with people! A foreign enemy shattered its gates and opened them to desecration; he turned my vine into a wilderness on the day of anger and fury. The foreigner saw the spoil he coveted and prevailed with a mighty hand, for on this day Apostomus burned the Torah.
paragraphs.note: New English working translation reviewed against the Hebrew and available Russian text; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: The wicked gnashed their teeth on the day when the Lord's anger rose against me. The cruel foreigner spared neither old nor young. His fury burned against me, and his flames engulfed me, for on this day the city wall was breached. Have mercy, Lord, and speak words of comfort to the hearts of mourners: on the seventeenth day of the month they sit stunned. O God, send down to them from above an abundance of Your mercies—God and King enthroned upon the throne of compassion.
paragraphs.note: New English working translation reviewed against the Hebrew and available Russian text; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Look upon the captive, delivered into the hands of Babylon and the ruler of the city. Long has he wept and pleaded before You like a little child. Before You, O Rock, his inward being churns within a subdued heart: 'On the day the enemy grew strong and the city was breached.' Therefore I shall bend down and wring my hands on the day when five calamities befell me. Because of the calf I lost the tablets; a foreigner captured the fortress and bound me in captivity. He put an end to the perpetual tamid offering and deprived me of its service; an idol was installed in the perfected Temple, and a foreigner burned Your Torah in the fire. I became desperately weak and shook on the day the Almighty exposed my shame. The northern serpent flooded over me like a deluge, took the beautiful land captive, and rolled me up like a ball. On the dark day when the heavenly light was dimmed, it thrust me into Persia's hands, gave me suffering to drink, and laid me waste. I shall lift up this lament: 'Will Your anger, my Rock, smoke against me forever?' Close my breaches for the sake of the son of the one who first broke forth; gather the lily among thorns. Open Your eyes and receive my prayer as the rich fat of an offering. Rebuild the house of the heavenly dwelling; restore the borders of Carmel and Bashan. Judge those who use violence; then shall the one who grazes in another's field and sets it aflame pay for his deed.
paragraphs.note: New English working translation reviewed against the Hebrew and available Russian text; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: God of our salvation, turn toward our cry and behold our ruins and the length of our exile. Year after year, as we recall our sorrow on the day when five calamities befell our fathers, we pray: God of spirits, You who search the hidden depths of the soul, turn toward the rejected flock scattered to the four winds. Each year at this time they groan, for on the day of our downfall the tablets were broken; throughout all our years we mourn our affliction. Lift those sunk in muddy mire, who have nowhere to stand. Behold the flocks You have given over to be devoured, plundered, and destroyed! Year after year sorrow encloses us on this day, when the foreigner's hand grew strong and the daily tamid offering ceased because our transgressions multiplied and our sins became heavy. Lord, with whom all things are possible, redeem from death and destruction out of the hands of the stubborn madman who devoured the last descendants of Jacob. Each year on this day our food turns bitter, for a foreigner set an idol in the Temple before our eyes, and in all our suffering our tears flow. How terrible is our ruin, for we turned away from reverence! Radiant One, clothed in light, who teaches what is good: year after year on this day we seek words of grief, for Apostomus burned the Torah. Therefore we lie ashamed over the plundering of the house of our glory. The Merciful One forgives iniquity and does not awaken all His anger; quickly deliver the scattered flock, the small nation, from Esau's hand. Year after year on this day our inward parts are wrung with grief: on that day foreigners prevailed and breached the city walls, and we became a laughingstock to our neighbors. Merciful One, return in compassion to humbled Zion! Hasten to bring the promised consolation to her who mourns; then shall we sing again when You rebuild the ruins, gather our scattered ones, and bring us home from exile.
paragraphs.note: New English working translation reviewed against the Hebrew and available Russian text; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Continue with “God, King” and “Men of Faith” as for the Fast of Gedaliah, and finish the service accordingly. Bring out the Torah scroll; three people read Vayechal as printed at the end of the Siddur. Finish the weekday service. After “Save Us,” say Psalm 79, “A psalm of Asaph: O God, the nations have entered Your inheritance,” as printed above.
Mourning.
One who is obligated to mourn a deceased person should tear their garment while standing; before doing so recite:
Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, the true Judge.
Acceptance of the Divine Judgment.

Righteous are You, Lord, and upright are Your judgments. Righteous is the Lord in all His ways, and gracious in all His deeds. Your righteousness is everlasting righteousness, and Your Torah is truth. The judgments of the Lord are true and righteous altogether. Where the word of a king is sovereign, who may say to him: 'What are you doing?' He is of one mind, and who can turn Him? What His soul desires, He does. Small and great are there alike, and the servant is free from his master. Behold, He puts no trust in His servants and charges His angels with error; how much less mortal man, who is a maggot, and the son of man, who is a worm. The Rock, His work is perfect, for all His ways are justice; a faithful God without injustice, righteous and upright is He. The true Judge, who judges with righteousness and truth: blessed is the true Judge, for all His judgments are righteous and true.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: He will swallow up death forever, and the Lord GOD will wipe away tears from every face and remove His people’s disgrace from the whole earth, for the LORD has spoken. Your dead shall live; my dead bodies shall rise. Awake and sing, you who dwell in the dust, for Your dew is a dew of light, and the earth shall bring forth the departed. He is merciful: He forgives iniquity and does not destroy; again and again He turns aside anger and does not awaken all His wrath. LORD, save; may the King answer us when we call. The comforters say: May you be comforted from heaven.
When the mourning period is over, one says to the mourner:

Your sun shall no more set, nor shall your moon withdraw, for the LORD shall be your everlasting light, and your days of mourning shall end. And it is written: “As a man whom his mother comforts, so shall I comfort you; and you shall be comforted in Jerusalem.”
Grace After Meals for mourners.
With three people, say: 'Let us bless'; with ten, add: 'our God, who comforts mourners, of whose food we have eaten.'
They respond: Blessed is He (with ten: 'our God') who comforts mourners, of whose food we have eaten, and through whose great goodness we have lived.
The leader repeats: Blessed is He (with ten: 'our God') who comforts mourners, of whose food we have eaten, and through whose great goodness we have lived.

Blessed are You, L·rd, our G·d, King of the universe. The G·d, Who feeds us & the entire world, with His Goodness, with Grace, with Kindness, with Abundance, & with great Mercy. He Provides bread to all flesh – because forever is His kindness. (Psalms 136, 25) And with His great goodness, we continually never lack. And May You never let us lack food continually forever & ever. For He is G·d, Who feeds & provides livelihood to everyone. And His table is set for all. For He prepares sustenance & food for all His creations that He created with His mercy & great kindness. As it says “You Open Your Hand, & You Satiate all the Living with its wants.” (Psalms 145, 16). Blessed are You, L·rd, our G·d, King of the universe Who feeds all.
paragraphs.ref: KAV EN parallel edot:Post Meal Blessing:15
paragraphs.note: Previously translated paragraph, Hebrew similarity 99.6%: source and target independently present in source corpus.

paragraphs.text: We thank You, L·rd, our G·d, that You bequeathed to our Forefathers a desirable, good & spacious land, a Covenant & Torah, life & food. And that You took us out from the land of Egypt & that You redeemed us from the house of bondage. And upon the Your Covenant that you stamped upon our flesh. And for Your Torah that You taught us. And upon the laws of Your Will – that You taught us. And upon life, & food that you feed & sustain us.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: On Hanukkah and Purim, add Al HaNissim here. If it was omitted and remembered before pronouncing the Divine Name in the blessing over the land, return and recite it; if remembered afterward, do not go back.

For everything, LORD our God, we thank You and bless Your name, as it is said: “You shall eat and be satisfied, and bless”—when saying the word “the,” pour the cup—“the LORD your God for the good land that He has given you.” Blessed are You, LORD, for the land and for the food.

Have Mercy L·rd, our G·d upon us & upon Israel Your people & upon Jerusalem, Your city. And upon Mount Tzion – the Tabernacle of Your glory & upon Your sanctuary. And upon Your Abode & upon Your Inner Chamber. And upon the great & holy abode upon which Your Name is called (Temple). Our father, Our Shepherd, Our Feeder, Our Sustainer, Our Provider. Our Deliverer. Deliver us speedily from all our sufferings. And please, let us not need, L·rd, our G·d, from the hands [of others], gifts from flesh & blood. And not from their hands – their loans – rather from Your hand – Full & plentiful, rich & open. May it be Your Will that we will not be embarrassed in this world & we will not be denigrated in the next world. And upon the Kingship of the house of David Your Messiah - restore it in place speedily in our days.
paragraphs.note: Reused from an identical reviewed Hebrew paragraph elsewhere in the bundled Siddur.

paragraphs.text: Comfort, LORD our God, the mourners of Zion and Jerusalem, and those who mourn in this bereavement. Comfort them in their grief and gladden them in their sorrow, as it is said: “As a man whom his mother comforts, so shall I comfort you; and in Jerusalem you shall be comforted.” Blessed are You, LORD, who comforts Zion through the rebuilding of Jerusalem. Amen. May the city of Zion be rebuilt in our days, and the Temple service reestablished in Jerusalem.

Blessed are You, Lord our God, King of the universe, the eternal God, our Father, our King, our Mighty One, our Redeemer and Holy One, the Holy One of Jacob; the living King, good and doing good, God of truth, Judge in righteousness, who takes souls and rules His world according to His will. We are His people and servants, and must thank and bless Him for everything. He who repairs breaches, may He in mercy repair this breach affecting us and His people Israel. May He who makes peace in His heights mercifully make peace upon us and all His people Israel, and let us say: Amen.
paragraphs.note: Source-aligned English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Memorial prayer for a man.

May the One who has mercy on all His creatures have compassion, pity and mercy upon the nefesh, ruach and neshamah of [name], son of [mother’s name], who departed this world with a good name. May the spirit of the LORD bring him to rest in the Garden of Eden with all the children of Israel who rest there, among the mercies and forgivenesses. So may it be His will, and let us say: Amen.
For a person outstanding in wisdom and reverence for Heaven, recite this memorial prayer:

But wisdom, where shall it be found? And where is the place of understanding? Happy is the man that findeth wisdom, And the man that obtaineth understanding. Oh how abundant is Thy goodness, which Thou hast laid up for them that fear Thee; Which Thou hast wrought for them that take their refuge in Thee, in the sight of the sons of men! How precious is Thy lovingkindness, O God! And the children of men take refuge in the shadow of Thy wings. They are abundantly satisfied with the fatness of Thy house; And Thou makest them drink of the river of Thy pleasures. A good name is better than precious oil; And the day of death than the day of one’s birth. The end of the matter, all having been heard: fear God, and keep His commandments; for this is the whole man. Let the saints exult in glory; Let them sing for joy upon their beds.
paragraphs.note: Every colon-delimited fragment matched a unique near-exact complete Tanakh verse; reviewed orthographic/qere alignment only.

paragraphs.text: May a fitting rest in the lofty assembly, among the holy and pure who shine and sparkle like the radiance of the firmament, with renewal of strength, atonement of guilt, removal of transgression, the drawing near of salvation, compassion and grace from the One who dwells on high, and a good portion in the world to come, be the portion, place and dwelling of the soul of [name, child of name], may the spirit of the Lord rest him in the Garden of Eden, who departed this world by the will of God, Master of heaven and earth. May the King of kings in His mercy pity and have compassion on him; may He shelter him beneath His wings and within His tent, so that he may behold the beauty of the Lord and visit His Temple. At the end of days may He raise him, let him drink of the stream of His delights, bind his soul in the bond of life, and establish his rest in honor. The Lord is his portion; may peace accompany him, and peace be upon his resting place, as it is written: 'He shall enter into peace; they shall rest upon their beds, each walking in his uprightness.' May he and all the children of Israel resting with him be included in mercy and forgiveness. So may it be His will; and let us say: Amen.
paragraphs.note: New English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Memorial prayer for a woman.
Before the memorial prayer, it is customary to say these verses:

A woman of valour who can find? For her price is far above rubies. Grace is deceitful, and beauty is vain; But a woman that feareth the LORD, she shall be praised. Give her of the fruit of her hands; And let her works praise her in the gates.
paragraphs.note: Every colon-delimited fragment matched a unique near-exact complete Tanakh verse; reviewed orthographic/qere alignment only.

paragraphs.text: May the One who has mercy on all His creatures have compassion, pity and mercy upon the nefesh, ruach and neshamah of [name], daughter of [mother’s name], who departed this world with a good name. May the spirit of the LORD bring her to rest in the Garden of Eden with all the daughters of Israel who rest there, among the mercies and forgivenesses. So may it be His will, and let us say: Amen.
For an esteemed and important woman, this memorial prayer is recited:

A woman of valour who can find? For her price is far above rubies. Grace is deceitful, and beauty is vain; But a woman that feareth the LORD, she shall be praised. Give her of the fruit of her hands; And let her works praise her in the gates.
paragraphs.note: Every colon-delimited Hebrew fragment matched an exact complete bundled Tanakh verse; translations joined without fuzzy alignment.

paragraphs.text: May the Merciful One, whose nature is mercy and by whose word the worlds were created, this world and the world to come—where He has stored up the righteous and faithful women who did His will—through His word, glory and power cause the memory of the soul of the honorable, modest, and esteemed woman [name, daughter of name] to be brought before Him. May the spirit of the Lord grant her rest in the Garden of Eden. She departed this world according to the will of God, Master of heaven and earth. May the King in His mercy pity and have compassion on her; may peace accompany her and rest upon her resting place, as it is written: 'He shall enter into peace; they shall rest upon their beds, each walking in his uprightness.' May she and all the daughters of Israel who rest with her be included in mercy and forgiveness. So may it be His will; and let us say: Amen.
paragraphs.note: New English working translation; specialist proofreading pending.

paragraphs.text: Blessing at a cemetery.

Blessed are You, LORD our God, King of the universe, who formed you in judgment, created you in judgment, fed you in judgment, sustained you in judgment, gave you life in judgment, and brought you death in judgment. He knows the number of you all in judgment, and He will uncover the dust from your eyes to revive and raise you in the resurrection of the dead in judgment. Blessed are You, LORD, who revives the dead.
Pirkei Avot
Chapter One

All Israel has a share in the World to Come, as it is said: “Your people are all righteous; they shall inherit the land forever—the branch of My planting, the work of My hands, in which I take pride.”

Moshe received the Torah from Sinai and transmitted it to Yehoshua; Yehoshua to the Elders; the Elders to the Prophets; and the Prophets transmitted it to the Men of the Great Assembly. They said three things: Be deliberate in judgment, raise many students, and make a protective fence around the Torah.
Shimon the Righteous was among the last members of the Great Assembly. He would say: The world stands on three things—on Torah, on the service of God, and on acts of loving-kindness.

Antigonos of Sokho received the tradition from Shimon the Righteous. He would say: Do not be like servants who serve the master in order to receive a reward; rather, be like servants who serve the master not for the sake of receiving a reward, and let the awe of Heaven be upon you.

Yose ben Yoezer of Tzeredah and Yose ben Yochanan of Jerusalem received the tradition from them. Yose ben Yoezer says: Let your home be a meeting place for sages; sit in the dust of their feet, and drink their words thirstily.

Yose ben Yochanan of Jerusalem says: Let your home be open wide; let the poor be members of your household; and do not engage in excessive conversation with a woman. They said this even concerning one’s own wife, and all the more concerning another man’s wife. From this the Sages said: Whoever engages in excessive conversation with women brings harm upon himself, neglects words of Torah, and in the end inherits Gehinnom.
Yehoshua ben Perachyah and Nittai of Arbel received the tradition from them. Yehoshua ben Perachyah says: Make for yourself a teacher, acquire for yourself a friend, and judge every person favorably.
Nittai of Arbel says: Keep far from a bad neighbor, do not associate with a wicked person, and do not despair of punishment.

Yehudah ben Tabbai and Shimon ben Shetach received the tradition from them. Yehudah ben Tabbai says: Do not make yourself like the advocates. When the litigants stand before you, regard them both as liable; and when they leave you after accepting the judgment, regard them both as innocent.
Shimon ben Shetach says: Examine the witnesses thoroughly, and be careful with your words, lest they learn from them how to lie.
Shemayah and Avtalyon received the tradition from them. Shemayah says: Love work, hate mastery, and do not become overly familiar with the authorities.

Avtalyon says: Sages, be careful with your words, lest you incur the penalty of exile and be exiled to a place of harmful waters; the students who follow you may drink and die, and the Name of Heaven will thereby be desecrated.
Hillel and Shammai received the tradition from them. Hillel says: Be among the disciples of Aaron—loving peace and pursuing peace, loving people and bringing them close to Torah.

He would say: One who seeks to spread his name loses it; one who does not increase his learning causes it to cease; one who does not study deserves death; and one who makes personal use of the crown of Torah passes away.
He would say: If I am not for myself, who will be for me? But when I am only for myself, what am I? And if not now, when?
Shammai says: Make your Torah study a fixed practice; say little and do much; and receive every person with a pleasant countenance.
Rabban Gamliel says: Make for yourself a teacher and remove yourself from doubt, and do not frequently tithe by estimation.
Shimon his son says: All my days I grew up among the sages, and I found nothing better for the body than silence. Study is not the main thing, but action; and whoever multiplies words brings sin.
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says: The world endures on three things—on justice, on truth, and on peace, as it is said: “Judge truth and the judgment of peace in your gates.”

Rabbi Hanania ben Akashya says: The Holy One, blessed be He, wished to grant merit to Israel; therefore He gave them abundant Torah and commandments, as it is said: “The Lord desired, for the sake of His righteousness, to magnify Torah and make it glorious.”

All Israel has a share in the World to Come, as it is said: “Your people are all righteous; they shall inherit the land forever—the branch of My planting, the work of My hands, in which I take pride.”
Chapter Two
paragraphs.note: Reviewed Pirkei Avot translation completed for Kavvanah Siddur.

paragraphs.text: Rabbi Yehudah HaNasi says: Which is the right path that a person should choose? One that is honorable for the one who follows it and brings honor from others. Be as careful with a minor commandment as with a major one, for you do not know the reward of the commandments. Weigh the loss involved in fulfilling a commandment against its reward, and the gain of a transgression against its loss.
